General information about OneNote notebooks

OneNote is an electronic notebook and as such it should support you, e.g. while preparing of meetings; in researching; or in gathering ideas. Please note: OneNote is not suitable as a mass storage or as a storage for business relevant data.


Structure of OneNote 

OneNote consists of notebooks. These notebooks consist of sections and within the sections the various pages store the information.

This structure is important because there are properties that are linked to certain parts of the notebook. For example, it is possible to create only one page of a notebook. You can then insert content into this page - but it will not contain a trash can or versions of the page.

The wastepaper basket belongs to each notebook.

OneNote Limitations

Maximum values must be observed when using OneNote notebooks on the Windows PC and iOS device:
Microsoft recommends a maximum size of a notebook of 2 GB, a section should not exceed a size of 300 MB.

If a section exceeds 200 MB in size, the user should split the contents of the section into several other (smaller and newly created) sections and remove all unneeded data

We strongly recommend not copying large files in one section, as the contents have to be sent to the server and problems may occur during synchronisation.
We do not recommend inserting e-mails into notebooks.

Our OneNote best practices and recommendations:

  • Avoid having a lot of large content in the same section, including file printouts, images, and attached files. Large content makes synchronization slower because the content must be sent/received over the internet. Below are the options to reduce large content in one section:
    1. Instead of mounting files, upload them to a common location (such as OneDrive or OneDrive for Business) and add a link to them.
    2. Delete unnecessary pages with large content.
    3. Try to break down large pieces of content into multiple sections instead of packing them into a single section.
    4. Try to divide content into different notebooks. Store archived notes that you don't need to access every day in different notebooks and keep archived notebooks closed. You can reopen these notebooks at any time if you need them from the “More Notebooks” option.
    5. If there is content that you want to continue to access daily, split it into different sections within the same notebook.

  • If the notebook is stored on OneDrive, is used by multiple users in different locations around the world and the pages are usually edited at the same time, there may be a conflict.
    If there is a conflict with changes you are making at the same time as another user, you should receive a message allowing you to select the version you want to merge for the cloud. In this case, select which final version of the page should be updated.

  • Make sure that the notebook does not exceed the size of 2 GB per file, which is the limit for syncing OneDrive/SharePoint files: Restrictions and limitations in OneDrive and SharePoint (microsoft.com).

  • Avoid that the sections of the notebook have a content of more than 300 MB; in case they are approaching this size, you should create a new section.
  • f notebooks have been moved to OneNote/SharePoint, it is important to ensure that these files are moved properly through the app so that the correct structure of the OneNote file (notebook) is maintained: OneNote syncing best practices (microsoft.com)
  • In case you encounter a sync issue, and you think there is a difference between your local copy and the cloud file, you can open the notebook in the browser and compare between the local and cloud file. Any content that is missing from the browser file will also be missing from all users who have opened the notebook in question using the OneNote client. To open a notebook in the browser, just right-click on the notebook in the client -> click on "Copy link to notebook" -> paste the link into the notepad and copy the first line -> paste the link into the browser's address bar and press Enter. If this link does not take you to the notebook, it could indicate that the notebook has been moved, deleted, or that you cannot access it (possible communication, authentication or permission problems, etc.)

Important instructions for using OneNote

OneNote is intended as a tool for quickly collecting and structuring information. A OneNote notebook is neither a filing system nor a documentation system. 
Business-critical data must not be stored in a OneNote notebook.

Most synchronisation problems result from the inappropriate use of OneNote:

  • OneNote notebooks are misused and used as file storage, i.e. entire files are stored in a notebook
    We strongly advise against saving files in a notebook. This leads to a significant increase in the size of the notebook and can result in 

o    Different versions of files being in circulation. 
o    The notebook cannot be synchronised without errors

We therefore recommend saving files in SharePoint and linking to these files in OneNote. These files can be opened and edited quickly via this link.

  • OneNote notebooks are stored on network drives and not in a SharePoint library..

    OneNote notebooks stored in a SharePoint library are less vulnerable to errors as OneNote has been optimised for use with SharePoint.
    For example, only the changed part of the notebook needs to be synchronised for changes. This reduces the load on the network and minimises the potential for errors. 
    It is also possible to resolve synchronisation conflicts. 
    Another advantage is that you can see directly in OneNote who is authorised for the notebook.

    You can find a guide to moving a notebook under How to move a Notebook in the docupedia Office


Suitable storage locations for OneNote notebooks

Based on the Storage Guide the following considerations will be applied to OneNote notebooks:

Default notebook location

The presetting for the default notebook location was C:.

 It is not recommended to store data on 'C', because backup of data is not guaranteed -> risk of data loss!
     Please keep in mind: C: will be deleted in case of a new installation of your computer!

As of May, 2017:
The default notebook location has been set to the variable %homedrive%\OneNote for new installations.
This variable refers to the folder 'OneNote' on the users home drive (in Germany U:\OneNote, in America H:\OneNote, e.g)

 Tipp: Please find further information about the default notebook location and how it can be changed in the 'Office FAQ (EN) in the section OneNote

Notebook on SharePoint/OneDrive

  • SharePoint
    • Sharing and co-editing with other Bosch users is possible
    • Access management in SharePoint by the site owner
    • Full OneNote functionality
    • Synchronization enables offline access
    • Backup is guaranteed

-> SharePoint suits ideally for teamwork and projects; so for notebooks, which are used and edited by a team 

    • User guide SharePoint on premises
    • User guide SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
    • Sharing and co-editing with other Bosch users is possible
    • Access management by the OneDrive owner
    • Full OneNote functionality
    • Synchronization enables offline access
    • Backup is guaranteed

-> OneDrive suits for notebooks, which contain personal notes, e.g. preparation of business trips, improvement suggestions and so on, which should be shared from time to time with other users  

Microsoft recommends to store OneNote notebooks on SharePoint or OneDrive.

Notebook on network drive

  • Department share / project share
    • Co-editing with other Bosch users is possible (Please note: the synchronization takes place time-delaid) 
    • Access management via Active Directory user groups, can not be done by the notebook owner
    • Full OneNote functionality not guaranteed by Microsoft
    • Off-line access is only possible, if the notebook is integrated into the client version of OneNote
    • Backup is guaranteed

-> Network drives can be used for notebooks, which are used by a certain user group

  • Personal network drive (e.g. U: or H:)
    • No sharing or co-editing
    • Therefore, is not given full functionality
    • Off-line access is only possible, if the notebook is integrated into the client version of OneNote
    • Backup is guaranteed

-> the personal network drive suits for notebooks, which contains exclusively personal notes and which should not be shared with other users 


Access rights for shared notebooks

... on SharePoint

All users, who have access to the SharePoint site, can read or edit the entire notebook, according to their access rights. In SharePoint, the access management is done by the site owner.

If a notebook is shared with single users via the 'Share' option, these users are able to access the Notebook, without having access to the complete SharePoint site. In this case, the notebook can only be opened in the Web App. For the integration of notebooks into the OneNote client, access rights for the complete SharePoint site are necessary.

... on OneDrive

Individual users can read or edit the entire notebook, according to their access rights. The access management is done by the owner of the notebook.

... on a network drive

All users, who have access to the network drive, can read or edit the entire notebook, according to their access rights on the specific directory. The access management is done by the IT Partner.

How to move a Notebook

  Please note

  • It is not possible to move notebooks from SharePoint sites or from OneDrive with the function 'Send to' in the 'Files' menu
  • Do not just move single .one files to SharePoint. It won´t work, because .one files only represent a single notebook section, not a complete Notebook!
  • It is not recommended, to move folders, which contains .one-files, via Window Explorer to OneDrive. Synchronization problems may result

A few steps need be followed before moving:

For notebooks that are edited together with others, no more changes must be made and all users, except the one performing the move, must close the notebook in OneNote.  This ensures that there are no multiple versions of the same notebook.
It is recommended to coordinate the appointment with all affected persons in advance or at least to inform them about it.

The following needs also to be checked

    1. Is there a recycle bin, and if so, can it be cleared?
    2. Is versioning activated? If so, please make sure to check whether existing versions can be deleted. Versioning should be switched off before exporting 

Finally, the notebook should be optimised to keep the required storage space to a minimum. To do this, go to the FILE Options menu, select the item "Save and backup" and click on the "Optimise all files now" button.

This may take some time, as all notebooks in OneNote are optimised.

The entire notebook can now be exported:.

  • The notebook you want to move is selected in OneNote. 
  • Go to FILE and select "Export". 
  • Under "1. Export current" click on "Notebook", under "2. Select format” select the file type "OneNot package /ONEPKG file) and click on Export 


  • Select the desired storage location and click on "Save"
    This export can also be saved and kept as a backup.

  • This exported notebook can then be opened again in OneNote by double-clicking on it. When you open it, you will be asked for a name for the notebook and the new storage location. Enter the location to which you want to move your notebook.



    To avoid confusion, the name of the notebook should be different from the original notebook. Enter a completely new name or add a _SP if you have moved the notebook to SharePoint, for example 

  • The new moved notebook can now be shared with all participants again

  • Close the original notebook in OneNote 

    Right-click on the notebook and select "Close notebook

    Important: The original notebook is still available in the old storage location and should be deleted there. We recommend that you wait some time before deleting it permanently until you are sure that everyone is working with the new notebook and all changes have been applied.

    Inform the other users of the notebook about the new storage location and the new name.


How to delete a notebook 

Always close OneNote notebooks in OneNote first and then delete them directly from the storage location:  If the notebook is stored on SharePoint/OneDrive, start SharePoint, navigate to the notebook and delete it there.

If it is stored on a file share: start the Windows Explorer, navigate to the Notebook and delete it there.

Before you delete the notebook files on the drive, SharePoint or Onedrive, it is recommended that you first close the notebook in OneNote (see screenshot in the previous section). If you are using the notebook on an iOS device, you should also close it there.

Prerequisite: You need delete permissíons on the storage location, 

  • on a SharePoint site, you need the appropriate access rights or the support of the site owner
  • on a network drive you also need the appropriate access rights or the support of someone who has it
  • in OneDrive you are able to delete the notebook by yourself: Select the notebook, then click twice on the three points for the context menu and click 'Delete'. Confirm with 'OK'.

It is also possible that the deleted notebook is still listed for a time in the "recent notebook", e.g. when you open notebooks. This entry can be removed manually by right-clicking on it, and "Remove From List" option.

OneNote offers a list of the notebooks in the notebook pane, which were opened in the OneNote client version by now. According to personal preference or use case, the notebook pane can be covered or can be visible permanently:

  • Notebook pane is covered, i.e. the notebook pane is not visible, but the working area in OneNote is larger.

    Just click on the small black arrow  beside the notebook name, to make the...

  • Notebook pane is visible permanently (pinned)

Replacement of the computer or new installation

In general, the list of notebooks is deleted during a new installation (re-installation, installation of a new Office version), i.e. existing notebooks need to be integrated manually (File - Open). On a new computer, the list is not available.

In order to have the integrated notebooks available again quickly, we recommend saving the list of notebooks used. To do this, use the "Save & restore settings" function in the IT Workplace Toolkit. The description can be found in the docupedia Windows Platform - SCCM and IT Workplace Toolkit - End User Information - Save and Restore Settings

IMPORTANT: Locally stored notebooks need to be moved to a network drive or a SharePoint Site or to your OneDrive before changing computers or reinstalling the entire computer, otherwise they will be lost. You can find a description of this under How to move a Notebook in this Docupedia

Note: Notebooks should generally not be saved locally, as company data may only be saved on the network.

On the new computer (or after reinstallation), use the IT Workplace Toolkit to restore the list of notebooks (see Back up and restore settings link).

In the list of notebooks, the entry for previous locally saved notebooks is no longer valid. There are two ways to correct this:

  • Either close the local notebook by clicking the right mouse button and open it from the new location. The notebook then appears in the list of open notebooks and can be edited as usual

  • Alternatively, you can create the exact same directory locally on the new computer as on the old computer and move the previously backed up notebook there. Editing is then also possible as usual.

What to do in a nutshell:

  1. On old computer
    • Back up settings
    • Move local notebooks
  2. On  new computer
    • Restore settings
    • Either open the moved notebooks from the new storage location or move them to the new computer

Requirements

The basic requirements for using the Enterprise Search are a current Windows and browser installation (as centrally distributed by BD). In order to use the full NGW functionality the user needs Microsoft Office 2013 Professional Plus or Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, Skype for Business or Microsoft Teams, SharePoint and OneNote.


Contents: Enterprise Search User Guide

Features and Benefits

The Enterprise Search provides the following features and benefits for users: 

  • User-friendly and intuitive user interface
  • Quick response time for search queries
  • Search in different sources: Bosch Connect, BGN, SharePoint, Docupedia, People, MyHR, SOCOS, NormMaster, eLibrary, Bosch Tube...
  • Search in Everything generates hits from all the sources with the following exceptions (due to technical reasons):
    • People & Expertise results have their own tab
    • eLibrary and Bosch Tube appear only in the Media tab
    • SharePoint Online also has a separate tab
    • My Mail
  • Automatic suggestion list appears when entering a search term
  • Result blocks enhance the search experience
  • Refiners are displayed dynamically based on the results, e.g. Result type and Modified date

  • Browser Plugin enables to search directly from the input window / address bar

  • Document preview and interaction using a hover panel

  • Direct navigation to document location via 'View Library' function

  • Ability to send a document link using the email function

  • Duplicates displayed if existing

  • People & Expertise Search provides information on associates: cost center, NT-ID, BGN location page and location on Google Maps

  • People & Expertise Search allows to interact directly via business card elements (phone, chat, email, meeting)

  • Advanced search functionality (e.g. Boolean search and search for documents by file name)

  • The App Starter allows to start applications or to find forms in WorkOn or IT Service Portal

  • Search results are only displayed if the user has at least 'read access' to the document


Please note:

There is a Use Case Training that covers both the Enterprise Search and the M365 Search - if you would like to have a guided introduction, feel free to sign up: https://connect.bosch.com/wikis/home?lang=en#!/wiki/W28a4d914c7f7_491a_9502_8a0b6dbb3c17/page/Use%20Case%2023%20-%20Search%2C%20find%20and%20share%20information%20with%20Microsoft%20365

 


Search Everything

Type in a search term and click on the magnifying glass or hit the return key to start the search.

By default it will search Everything. This means the following internal sources:

  • BGN pages including Bosch Zünder Online
  • MyHR
  • Docupedia
  • Bosch Connect 
  • SharePoint 2019
  • Bosch Acronym Wiki (in grey result block)
  • Sponsored Links / Promoted Results (in grey result block)
  • NormMaster
  • Applications & Services (WorkOn, IT Service Portal, Application list)
  • Central Directives and Guidelines (SOCOS)
  • R&D-Reports (FEBER)

To make it easier for you to recognize which of these sources are included in Everything, they have been indented in the list of content sources (the last three items in the list are only available after expanding the list and have therefore not been indented to avoid confusion).

Further sources will  be searched if this source is explicitly selected:

  • Employee Directory (People & Expertise)
  • Expertise Locator (People & Expertise)
  • Bosch Tube and eLibrary within Media
  • SharePoint Online
  • Learning Portal
  • My Mail

With the menu on the left hand side you can choose one of the listed sources in advance to concentrate your search on one category. You can always return to searching all sources by clicking on Everything.

Please note that NormMaster and the Acronym Wiki both are not shown in the menu but are an inherent part of the Search!


Please note:

When using the default setting Everything you will get a mixed result set from all available sources with the most relevant ones standing on top.

An overview how different kinds of search results can be found is provided in the Search Guide: https://connect.bosch.com/wikis/home?lang=de-de#!/wiki/W62210e629477_48ae_ae3c_52239b0630fe/page/OVERVIEW

As Everything, People & Expertise and Media cover the most frequent use cases, these are also available below the search window and can be selected there as well.

 



Result List

When you enter a search term and start the search process, the result page will open. Search results are listed in the central column.

If you have not found the relevant result on the first page, you can either have a look at the following pages or you can try to refine your search by using filters or by being more specific with respect to the words you enter in the search window. You can also use the Advanced Search.


Please note:
When results are displayed within a grey result block, the number of suggested results is limited. If you would like to get more results form this source, click on SHOW MORE in the top right corner of the result block.



At a glance you can see:

  • Document icon (showing the file type, e.g. pdf, ppt, docx)
  • Document title (by clicking on the document title the document will open)
  • Storage location (e.g. BGN, Docupedia, SharePoint)
  • Document summary
  • URL/document path (clicking on the path will allow to copy it to the clipboard)


Number of search results

The search provides an approximate number of search results at the top of your search results page.

Refining Search Results and Searching with Quick Links

Content Sources and Refiners / Filters

The search results can be narrowed down by using dedicated verticals for content sources and filter options - multiple filters can be combined. To apply the filter, click on the corresponding item.

  • Content Sources: Pre-select a source space, like People, BGN pages, MyHR, Docupedia, SharePoint or Bosch Connect if you already know in which system your desired result can be found.
  • Filter / Refiner: Refiners (filters) categorize the top documents in search results into groups that allow users to filter their results. So, if you are looking for something specific, you can use them to limit the search results with respect to specific attributes.
    • Modified date: With this filter you can narrow down the search results by filtering for documents modified in a selected time period; please use the sliders at each end of the timeline to define the desired period.
    • Result type: With this filter you can narrow down the search results by selecting one or more file format(s) such as Word, Excel or PowerPoint (for more information please see below).
    • Dynamic refiners (filters): These are based on result set - different source systems can have different refiner (filter) options, e.g. BGN pages can be filtered according to business unit.

Filters can be reset individually or all in one go by clicking on 'Reset all filters'.


Quick Links


In addition there are three Quick Links at the top right hand side:

  • ASK! Bosch
  • eLibrary
  • ePLM Navigator

ASK! Bosch is just a link to this application. eLibrary forwards your search request directly to the corresponding sites where the results are shown.


Selecting URL/Document Path

When clicking on a link it will be marked automatically.

Now you can copy it easily by just pressing CRTL+C or via the right mouse click context menu.  

Extended and Interactive Preview

If the document is in BGN, SharePoint or Docupedia you’ll see an extended preview of the content.

You can rest the pointer over a search result to preview and interact with the document or site without having to leave the result page.

Hovering over one of the search results shows you more information about the entry and offers interaction options - depending on the document type:

  • Document title or page name
  • File type (PDF, Microsoft Word) or document source (e.g. BGN, SharePoint)
  • Last modified date
  • Author/last modifier
  • Context menu with options - depending on source:
    • Open - opens the file/page in the application or web browser
    • Edit - allows you to edit the document in the application or web browser
    • Send - opens a new email in Outlook with the file name as the subject and a link to the document in the text
    • View duplicates - the Enterprise Search detects duplicates automatically (e.g. versions of the same document), only one duplicate is shown in the results list, clicking on 'View duplicates' will allow you to see the others
    • View library - if you would like to find out where the document is stored, click on 'View library' (if you have access)


Please note:

The preview has to be activated (downloaded) once per session. Then it is used for the Office Web Apps during the same session. If you clear your cache it has to be reloaded.

For some content sources, you need to have logged in at least once before to be able to see the preview.

People & Expertise Search

Searching for People

The Enterprise Search makes it easy to find Bosch associates and to directly interact with them right from the result list.

You can search by name, by NT-Id, by department or combine all three.


Please note:
  • Pictures shown in People Search are those you have provided on Bosch Connect.
  • The People Search is also a good way to identify a user when you only have the NT-Id!

The search process can be executed with the default set Everything or within the content source People & Expertise.

When searching for an associate the result page displays:

  • Everything
    • Documents / pages with the searched name within the content
    • Documents / pages created or modified by the respective associate
  • People
    • A group of Bosch People Results in case there is more than one possible associate who matches the search criteria
    • A profile picture with contact data of the corresponding person (if the user has uploaded a photo in Bosch Connect)
    • Colleagues who have been working closely together with the associates (as Expertise Search results)

Working with People Results


The results contain the following information:

  • Name and department (with a link to the Bosch Connect profile)
  • Office (with location and building code)
  • Local time at the office
  • Postal address


When hovering over the contact data of a person a context menu opens on the right side.
There you can see details like NT-Id, cost center, department, location, email address, telephone number, Teams chat link, a direct link to the Bosch Connect profile and the organizational chart.

Clicking on one of the details starts an interaction, e.g.:

  • opening the Bosch Connect profile
  • creating an new email
  • showing the Bosch location page in BGN (if a location page is available)

Click on the detailed address next to the picture to open Google Maps, which will locate the address (Google Maps might not be available for all countries).


Department Search


In everyday business it is a common use case to get in contact with colleagues from other divisions or departments. The People Search provides information about the department of a colleague as well as organization charts for Bosch group to see the structure of a department or group.

Just move your mouse over the search hit and a hover panel will pop up. Then you can click the link of the department name.

This will automatically start a search in the BGN and you will get the organizational BGN page listed among the top results.


Organization Chart


Just move your mouse over the search hit and a hover panel will pop up. Then you can click on the link of the organization chart.

The link will automatically guide you to an organization chart where you can see the structure of your colleague's department or group. Both the tree view on the left hand side and the tile view in the center can be browsed.

You can find further information on the organization unit, like e.g. all members of the group as well as the manager, the cost center number and so on.

Searching for Associates with Expertise

You can use the People & Expertise Search also to find associates with know-how in specific areas. When you enter a corresponding search term, you will be provided with the four most likely experts straight away.

Clicking on SHOW MORE will open a separate page where further associates are listed.

When you mouse over one of the results, a hover panel will appear containing the contact data as well as an indication why these associates have been listed with expertise – for example, if they are official BEO experts, if they have created blog posts and comments on a topic and so on.

If you want to know more about how expertise is determined, you can find more information and support in the Bosch Expertise Search Community.

Media Search

Overview

The Media Search has the aim to provide Bosch users with easy access to different media available, like videos, books, articles and images. We have not yet reached the full scope of what we would like to include here, but significant progress has been made so far - we have been able to cover centrally purchased stock photos, Bosch Tube and eLibrary!

When you enter a search term and go to Media, you will be provided with three result blocks, one for the Image Search, one for Bosch Tube and one for eLibrary. These result blocks contain the most relevant pictures, videos or publications matching your search. The Image Search block covers stock photos that have been centrally purchased for use within Bosch. The block for Bosch Tube will provide you with videos for easy access to topics, recorded events and so on, whereas the eLibrary offers specialist literature on a wide range of topics.

If the result blocks do not yet offer you a satisfying result, you can click on SHOW MORE - this will lead you to auxiliary pages for Image Search, Bosch Tube or eLibrary where more results are available.

In order for you to access the Media Search more easily, it remains visible directly under the search slot just like the People & Expertise Search. Of course you can also access it in the list of content sources on the left.

Image Search


If you already know you are looking for a picture, you can start your search directly within Media as described above.

If you would like to see more suggestions, click on SHOW MORE within the image results block in the Media Search, and you will be directed to the Image Search auxiliary page. Here, you can browse through further available content.



When you have found a picture you would like to use, click on the three dots below the thumbnail image. This will open a panel that contains further metadata as well as a link to the download options in the Media Asset Management (MAM) system.


Usually, different formats are available.
To choose one, click on the arrow next to the download button, set a checkmark for the selected format and click on Download.

You will need to confirm the terms and conditions and then you are ready to use the image in your presentations, blogs or other materials!

Please note:
  • The images are available for unrestricted use for Bosch purposes, but not for usage by third parties for their own purposes.
    If you are in doubt, you can find the overall terms and conditions here.
  • The Corporate Communications Team will continually expand the image catalog — so have a look from time to time to find new pictures!



Bosch Tube

If you already know you are looking for a video, you can start your search directly within Media as described above. If this already shows the desired result, simply click on the video title to open the corresponding page in Bosch Tube.

If you would like to see more suggestions, click on SHOW MORE within the Bosch Tube results block in the Media Search, and you will be directed to the Bosch Tube auxiliary page. Here, you can browse through up to three pages of suggested videos from Bosch Tube.

You can do further searches here or return to the standard Enterprise Search pages by clicking on Everything or any of the other content sources, either below the search slot or in the list on the left.

Each suggested result for Bosch Tube contains

  • A thumbnail image
  • The video title (with a link to the Bosch Tube site)
  • The number of views and likes
  • A short description
  • The duration of the video
  • Tags assigned to the video




Please note:
  • The Media Search only offers Bosch Tube videos, no vlogs or streams.
  • For data security reasons, the Enterprise Search will only suggest videos with no access restrictions, that is, no videos that are unlisted, private or contained in access-restricted channels.

eLibrary


If you already know you are looking for a specialist book or article, you can start your search directly within Media as described above. If this already shows the desired result, simply click on the title to open the page containing the corresponding publication.

If you would like to see more suggestions, click on SHOW MORE within the eLibrary results block in the Media Search, and you will be directed to the eLibrary auxiliary page. Here, you can browse through up to five pages of publications suggested via eLibrary.


Please note:

By default, all suggested books and articles are already licensed for Bosch and can be directly accessed. If you want to broaden the search, you can remove the filter checkmark. This might mean, however, that you might have to obtain a license before being able to access the publication.


You can do further searches here or return to the standard Enterprise Search pages by clicking on Everything or any of the other content sources, either below the search slot or in the list on the left.

Each suggested result for eLibrary contains

  • A thumbnail image of the title page (if not available: default image)
  • The publication title (with a link to the publication site)
  • Authors
  • Publication date / Edition (for magazines)
  • Tags assigned
  • Licensing information (either 'Full Text Online' for licensed items or 'Request License' when a license needs to be obtained)

The hover panel additionally provides a short content description (where available).

Searching for Central Directives

The SOCOS Corporate Regulation Database is integrated into the Enterprise Search. Here you easily are able to find various sorts of documents such as Bosch Central Directives, Forms, Guidelines, Notifications, Process Descriptions etc.


Just enter your search term and if there is a related SOCOS document, it will be shown in the results list. The two most relevant SOCOS-C documents even get their own result block. Searching in NormMaster

Please note:

Searching in Bosch Overflow

Bosch Overflow is a question-and-answer forum with a strong emphasis on community collaboration and transparent information sharing. 

In order to make the collected know-how easier to access, the Bosch Overflow data is included in the Enterprise Search. You can find the results in Everything and in Bosch Overflow, the dedicated page for this kind of search results.


Please note:

Searching in SharePoint

Please note:

There is a Baseline Search functionality which can be accessed via the link offered in the bottom right corner of the respective pages of the Enterprise Search. You can also access the Baseline Search by going directly to https://search.bosch.com/Pages/BoschIlmresults.aspx


Please note:
You can find out more about ILM and baselines here: https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/JITEvQ

Searching in your Mailbox

While searching for specific information, you can also check whether it can be found in your mailbox. To do so, click on 'My Mail' in the list of content sources on the left. If this option is not visible, click on SHOW MORE to expand the list.

If you are not logged in to Microsoft 365 already, a login window will appear for a few seconds and you will be logged in automatically.

The results contain

  • the subject line as header
  • an indication who sent the mail
  • the date and time when it was sent 
  • a short preview of the text 

Clicking on a search result will open the e.mail in the Outlook web client.


Please note:
  • You will only be able to see content if you have access rights, this means that you will not see the contents of other associates' mailboxes and they in turn will not see the content of yours!
  • For encrypted mails, only the title will be searchable, but nothing contained in the mail text can be found.
  • The search results in the My Mail search should be the same as in Outlook — they are added to the Enterprise Search so you do not have to switch to a different tool to continue your search activities. 
  • Another way to search through your e.mails is the M365 Search: https://www.microsoft365.com/search/conversations?auth=2 — this will also include Teams chats and posts (cf. our user guide for the M365 search for more information).

Searching for APIs

Searching with the Enterprise Search Teams Add-in

The Enterprise Search Teams Add-in will allow you to search for information and documents stored in Bosch on-premise systems like Docupedia, Bosch Connect, MyHR, BGN and many more without leaving the Microsoft Teams client. This can help you avoid interruptions in your work.


In order to get the Add-in, open the Apps list in your Microsoft Teams client by clicking on the tile in the left-hand menu. Search for 'Enterprise Search' (you might have to scroll down a bit in the results).

Once you have found the right Add-in, click on 'Open' and then, in the details view of the Add-in, choose 'Add'.






The Enterprise Search Add-in will appear as entry in the left-hand menu. If you want to keep it there, right-click on the entry and choose 'Pin'.
This will make sure the tile is available next time you open Teams. (If you want to remove it again, just right-click and select 'Unpin'.)

You can now search for content very much in the same way as using the Enterprise Search in the browser.



Please note:
  • Due to technical restrictions, there are some minor limitation to the functionality in comparison with the browser version of the Enterprise Search.
    For example, the search assistant will not work properly and you might see results in MyHR that are not relevant for you.
  • If you are searching for files stored in SharePoint Online, mails or Teams messages and posts, please continue to use the search slot at the top of your Teams window.

Searching with the Search Assistant

In the Help & Service area at the top right hand side you can find the Enterprise Search Assistant. When you are searching for a specific document type (e.g. a blog post or HR information), it provides support in finding the right result page.

The bot offers you different result types to choose from, sometimes narrowing down the selection with a second or third question. Once you have chosen a result type, the Search Assistant will execute a search for your current search term in a page of the Enterprise Search (or other tools) that focuses on this result type.

For example, if you have chosen 'regulations > central regulations' as result type, it will guide you to SOCOS where a search for you current search term has already been executed for you.


Please note:
By clicking on the text above the Search Assistant window and keeping the mouse button pressed, you can drag and drop the window to a more convenient position if required.

Advanced Search

The Enterprise Search allows complex operations with Operators and Boolean functions as described below.

If you do not comfortable using these, you can go to the Advanced Search instead. It can be found in the Help & Service area at the top right hand side.

With the Advanced Search you can search for content that contains:

  • All of these words
  • The exact phrase
  • Any of these words
  • None of these words


Please note:

A combination of the fields above can be used.
The relation between those fields will be AND.

You can add parameter restrictions by selecting and combining items from the drop down menus at the bottom. Selecting one or more properties like Author, Name, Last Modified By ... and conditions like Contains / Does not contain or Equals / Does not equal, you can create complex queries.



After executing the search process the result page is displayed in Everything including the search string with the operators.


Please note:

Wild cards * (used to replace a string of characters) are permitted. However, they only work at the end of a string and not at the beginning or in the middle!

If you are familiar with the search syntax, you can of course directly enter a complex query directly into the search window.

Operators and Boolean Functions

Operators and Functions

Examples:

Double quotes " "


Only results which match exactly the terms between the quotes are displayed

"monthly reports"



Placeholder (*)


The star (*) replaces one or more individual characters at the end of a string (not at the beginning or in the middle!)

Hamburg* displays Hamburg, Hamburger, Hamburgerin



Symbol (+)


The term with (+) must be included in the result list

monthly reports +error displays monthly or reports and in any cases error



Symbol (-)


The term with (-) is excluded in the result list

monthly reports -error displays monthly or reports and in no case error



AND


Only results with both terms will be displayed

monthly AND reports displays only results which contain monthly and reports



OR


Results with one (either/or) both of the terms will be displayed

monthly OR reports displays results which contain monthly or reports (or both terms)



( )


Brackets enable you to assemble or structure your searches

(pump OR sparkplug) AND (plant 1 OR plant 3) displays results for pump or sparkplug only in conjunction with plant1 or plant3



NEAR(x)


Only results will be displayed where the terms in the documents are equal or closer than x words in distance.

Default value is eight.

"EV6" NEAR(5) "chrom" displays search hits where the terms in which the two terms are not more apart than 5 words. The term order can be EV6 Chrom or Chrom EV6.



ONEAR(x)


Only results will be displayed where the terms in the documents are equal or closer than x words in distance and must be in the defined order.

Default value is eight.

"EV6" ONEAR(5) "chrom" displays search hits where the terms in which the two terms are not more apart than 5 words. The term order is EV6 Chrom.

Chrom EV6 will be suppressed.



Words(x, y)


Words indicates the search algorithm that both terms are equivalent. Using words(x, y) influences the ranking of the result list. Thus the result list can be influenced positively.

Words(screen, monitor) uprates (more important) documents with one of the particular terms in the result list.

Without the words(x,y) parameter documents with both parameters would be ranked higher and documents with only one single search term will be listed later in the result list.


Please note:

A colon ( : ) is interpreted as part of the search syntax. A search sting like
          author:Wagner
will provide a list of search results where 'wagner' is in the author property / metadata.
If you are looking for a string that contains a colon, put it into quotation marks like this:
          "author:Wagner"
and you will get a list of search results where this string is contained.

Person-Related Data Used

For some of the functions of the Enterprise Search, we use person-related data:

  • Determine access rights:
    • NT User name is required to check whether the use has access to potential search results
  • People search results:
    • Display data from the Active Directory (name, NT User name, contact details) within the results of the People Search
    • Display the pictures of users in the People Search if they have uploaded one into Bosch Connect
    • Display RB organizational data (e.g. user belongs to a team, is manager of an organizational unit...)
  • Search results meta data:
    • Data taken from Bosch systems,( e.g. file has been created by, wiki page was last modified by...)
  • Images, videos etc. as part of the search results → ensuring that no data protection laws are infringed is in the responsibility of the source systems!
  • Application Monitoring for troubleshooting and improvement; data is aggregated
    • Location of the users (via IP address) → ensuring that performance is good for all locations
    • Number of users per day, over time ... → identify load peaks
    • Browsers used → checking whether further browsers need to be supported by the Enterprise Search
  • Determining number of licenses required:
    • NT User name is required to ensure legality with respect to licensing

Please note:

No sensitive person-related data is used.

Once person-related data is deleted from source systems, it will also disappear from the Enterprise Search index.

Data for Application Monitoring is deleted after three months.

Accessibility

I am an 'External'. Why can't I access search results from Bosch Connect?

Users with 'external' accounts do not have access to Bosch Connect and therefore won't see search results from this system. Enterprise Search only displays search results from sources for which an external has the access rights.

Why are File Shares not a standard part of the Search?

Due to cost and effort reasons a File Shares Search based on Enterprise Search will only be set up in rare cases.


SharePoint

Why are there separate lists for the on-premise SharePoint environment and for SharePoint Online?

See SharePoint User Documentation


How long will the SharePoint result lists have to be searched separately?

See SharePoint User Documentation


How can I get to SharePoint or OneDrive?

For SharePoint on-premises, see the SharePoint Quick Start Guide (EN)

Once you have been onboarded to M365, the easiest way to access SharePoint Online or One Drive will then to go to www.office.com and click on the appropriate button in the left-hand ribbon.


Why is my document / list entry not found?

There are several possible causes if documents or list entries are not found:

  • Access rights - make sure you have access to the element you expect to be returned as a search result
  • Indexing schedule - depending on where you have stored the data, it can take a few hours until it is included in the search index
  • The library / list is too large to be handled properly - if there are many search results (which is more likely for large libraries/lists), the search results might be incomplete, missing or both, this is due to some SharePoint list limitations that should prevent negative impact on response times of SharePoint
  • The document itself is too large to be handled properly - for very large documents the indexing will abort at some point and it can happen that your search term is contained in the non-indexed part of the document, so that document will not turn up as search result even though it contains the search term


Media Search

Why do I not see the video / article / book I was searching for?

There are different possibilities:

  • For data security reasons, the Enterprise Search will only suggest videos with no access restrictions, that is, no videos that are unlisted, private or contained in access-restricted channels. Please make sure that the video you have been looking for does not fall into one of these categories. In that case you would have to search in Bosch Tube directly.
  • As a default, the Enterprise Search will only suggest eLibrary publications where a license is already available. If you want to include further results, click on SHOW MORE in the eLibrary result box in Media. This will direct you to the auxiliary eLibrary page where you can remove the checkmark for licensed content only for this search.
  • If you are looking for a video that has been uploaded as webcast and not as video, this will not be found.
  • Please check whether you are using the correct search term (maybe singular instead of plural) - the Media search is not very fuzzy.

Why do I not see any streams from Bosch Tube?

The Media Search only offers Bosch Tube videos, no vlogs or streams. If you are looking for this kind of content, please open the Bosch Tube directly (e.g. by searching for 'Bosch Tube' and opening the sponsored link).

Why do I only get 30 results within the Bosch Tube page?

In order not to affect overall performance, the interface between the Enterprise Search and Bosch Tube will only deliver 30 results at a time. Experience shows, that users tend to specify their search rather than scroll through different pages, so that would be our recommendation if you have not found the appropriate video within the 30 results provided.

How long does it take to index a modified or new document?

Your documents can usually be seen only a few hours after uploading or changing them.


Which formats are indexed?

Miscellaneous

My photo isn't shown? How can I upload it?

  • Go to https://connect.bosch.com
  • At the top choose My Page (or go directly to https://connect.bosch.com/profiles/html/editMyProfileView.do?tab=photo)

Is an advanced search available?

For advanced users the 'Advanced Search' button can be found within the 'Help & Service' area in the top right hand corner. For more information on the Advanced Search, please see the Enterprise Search User Guide.

There are some file formats I can`t find with the Search. Why?

Make sure that the file type of the document you are searching for is on the list of Indexed File Formats.


How do I get better search results?

Start searching with more than one keyword. The search results will be considerably improved when using multiple keywords with the first search query.
For example, if your search keyword is 'Bosch', it will display thousands of results. Instead, your search keyword should be specific e. g. 'Product Catalogue'.


Search queries with special characters can be problematic - how do I deal with this?


Sometimes your search queries can contain special characters, e.g. when you search for a filename that contains an underscore. Unfortunately this will cause issues. The reason for this is the behavior of the indexing in comparison with the query. When indexing a document, special characters are usually removed, but this does not happen for the queries. So, if you enter a query that contains special characters, the search will not be able to recognize the connection to the indexed data.

What can you do to deal with this:

  • Use the search queries without special characters (except * - see next bullet point) - do not search for 2019-04_User_Statistics but instead for User Statistics 2019 (and maybe use the date filter if there are too many results)
  • Use * at the end of a partial term as a wildcard to get further results ('connect*' will give results for 'connection', 'connectivity', 'connect', 'connected'...); the wildcard will only work at the end of the word, not at the start or in the middle!


After getting my search results - is there a chance to refine them?

Use the filter options whenever possible to refine your search results. After your initial search request you can refine the search results by using the filter options 'Language', 'Result Type' or 'Modified Date'. For more information please have a look at the User Guide.


Sometimes the People Search does not show a map for a business location that belongs to a user profile. Why is that so?


Every map for a business location has to be added manually. In some cases we just did not receive a map for the particular location.
More information you can find here:  Add Location Map


Why are changes in my user profile not shown immediately and can not be found through the People Search?

Due to technical reasons it sometimes may take a while until the data has been transferred. But it will not take any longer than just a couple of days until the new information can be seen. If the data is still not updated after a few days, please create a IT Sevice Desk ticket so we can look into it.


What does the 'Quick link' search function provide?

'ePLM Navigator' and 'eLibrary' forward your search request directly to the corresponding sites. Here the results are shown.

'Ask! Bosch' is just a link to this application.


What do the various Icons in the search results stand for?

If you want to have further information as to which file types are grouped, please see the information on indexed file formats.

When using the Enterprise Search with Firefox sometimes you will be asked for a login:

If this occurs, there is an issue with your Firefox profile. In order for this to be remedied, please call the IT Service Desk and ask for a new user profile to be generated. The colleagues there will perform the required steps to provide you with the new profile including, for example, migrating your bookmarks.


Preview in SharePoint Online search

Due to the current access management for SharePoint Online, you will see a login prompt before you are able to see a preview of the document analogously to to the other result sources (cf. User Guide: Extended and Interactive Preview).

Please note:

The preview only works in Firefox, for other browsers (Chrome, Edge, ...) the login will have no effect.

Technically, there are different domains and the login to see the preview will only be valid for one domain at a time, so you might see a preview for some results but not for others.

Each time you close the browser, the login information is lost, so you will need to repeat the login.


Preview for LeanIX and other systems not available

For most content sources, hovering over a corresponding search result will open a hover panel with a preview of the document / page. For some content sources, however, a preview will only be available if you have logged in to the system at least once before.

The preview will be lost again if you clear the cached login data, so you will have to log in again to see the preview.


Access for IDE clients not working for all constellations

We have identified some constellations where IDE clients are not able to access the Enterprise Search properly:

  • Virtual IDE machine with Edge client
  • Firefox: when the token expires after one day, a new two-factor authentication is required

Should you encounter further access issues, please let us know: Operations.insideEnterpriseSearch@bosch.com

Question
 Description/Answer
Can I make an emergency call using Skype for Business?

Together with the SfB Public Telephony rollout at your location, Skype will be configured for emergency calls according to your location concept. Once you have received your phone number in SfB, you can use your SfB client for emergency calls. Until then, please use your usual telephony solution or mobile phone instead. 

Please note:

  • If you are not at the Bosch location, (homeoffice, business travel,…), you must not use the SfB softclient to do emergency calls. In this case, the emergency call would be routed via your home Bosch location.
  • For users of `+49 711 805 xxx` numbers, please note that these numbers are not configured for emergency calls. The test numbers do not replace your regular office phone. Please use your usual telephony solution or mobile phone instead (e.g. if you are working in Fe location but you are currently in homeoffice, your emergency call would reach the Fe plants fire and rescue department, not the public emergency response for your home location).

 For users in Feuerbach, check the information in the BGN.

What do I have to enter when the "Edit Location" window pops up?

If this window pops up, you do not need to enter anything. Click on Cancel to close the window. Information written there does not affect the routing in the background. For emergency calls, please follow the instructions in the FAQ above.

 

Where can I find an overview about all information related to Skype for Business?

With the new SfB Flyer you can find the most important information at a glance.

Click here for a short training session. Click on File and select the desired representation (text instructions, picture sequence or video in the right column).
How can I contact the CI Hotline using Skype?

Using SfB at the moment, the CI-Hotline can only be contacted by already SfB Public Telephony enabled users. With SfB Public Telephony, users get an own telephony number to also make external calls, including the CI Hotline Call Center.

The SfB Public Telephony rollout is still ongoing. More information about SfB Public Telephony can be found in the Guide and FAQs. Besides the Public Telephony rollout, we are working on an integration in the Next Generation Support and Services project (NGS).

Can I chat/call with a normal Skype user?
No, it is not possible to communicate with a normal Skype user.
How can I hear notification sounds for incoming calls via speakers although a headset is connected?

I want to hear notification sounds for incoming calls via speakers, so that I can notice incoming calls immediately although I did not put on a headset.

The following configurations have to be set:

  1. Open the Skype for Business Client options by clicking on the gear wheel symbol in the top right corner.
  2. Click on Audio Device and select Also ring (Speaker) and Unmute when my phone rings. Confirm with "OK".
  3. With a right click on the loudspeaker symbol in the taskbar, you can open Playback Devices. Set "Default Device" for the PC Speaker and "Default Communications Device" for the headset.
  4. Afterwards, right click on the loudspeaker symbol in the windows taskbar again. Click on "Open Volume Mixer".
  5. Here you can adjust the volume of the Skype for Business sounds to any level you like.
    You should check the volume level of your speakers too. If they are muted, you will hear no sound when you receive a call, although you did the settings as described above.
  6. You are done. Now you can hear incoming calls also via speakers.
This procedure does not apply to notifications sounds for incoming instant messages (IM). However, you will receive not only a notification via email but also in the Skype for Business client by clicking on Missed Conversations.

Why haven't calls been ringing since I got a new HDMI-monitor?

If you connect your HDMI-screen it can happen that Skype uses the monitor as the secondary ringer instead of the laptop speakers. But this monitor audio do not have sound.

If you use a new monitor please check whether the monitor is set as secondary ringer. If yes, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Skype for Business App
  2. Select settings on the right side
  3. Go to the audio device settings
  4. Check if your Laptop is set as secondary ringer

For instructions, please refer to this page.

Is the Busy-on-Busy function available in SfB? 

This function is not available in SfB. Please use the following workaround:

  • Send the user to your voicemail by clicking on Options and on Voice Mail
     
  • You will see that you missed a call as shown in the FAQ below.
  • If the user left a voice mail you will see it in your Outlook inbox. 

More information about the voice mail can be found here.

Further hints: By clicking on Options you can also

  • send the user to your mobile phone if you can shortly answer the call there in parallel
  • answer the user with a reply by IM (chat message) if he also has SfB
  • set your status to Do not Disturb. If you do that, the caller will also be forwarded to your voice mail. The same happens if your status is already set to Do not Disturb
Where do I see missed calls?

There are to possibilities to see missed calls:

  1. SfB client
    Open SfB and click on the clock symbol. If you have any missed calls you will see a small orange number next to the clock symbol. Click on "MISSED" and you can see your missed calls.

2. Outlook
In Outlook you will get an e-mail as soon as you miss a call. You can see all your conversations in the conversation history.

How do I know if someone has a Skype for Business account or not?

If you search for a name in Skype for Business you will find all contacts that are available in the corporate directory.

From the colour of the bar on the left hand side of the profile picture you can see if the person has a Skype for Business account (bar = grey) or not (bar = white). Another indication is the Presence information: If it says "presence unknown" the person does not have a Skype for Business account.

How can I change the privacy relationship to specific contacts and which information do I share exactly?

Have a look at the learning nugget. Click on File and select the desired representation (text instructions, picture sequence or video in the right column)

Is it possible to hide the participants list  for internals and for externals?

No, this is not possible. However you can change your personal view.

Click on this icon while you are in a meeting:

Now you do not see the participants list anymore.

Can I do a bulk import of contacts (e.g. from CSV file) in Skype for Business?

Bulk import of contacts is not possible in Skype for Business. Alternatively, you can quickly add many contacts by adding already defined distribution lists.

To do so, simply search for the distribution list in Skype for Business (similar to adding a single person). Distribution list can be identified by the group icon.

How can I create a group and add contacts?

Have a look at the learning nugget. Click on File and select the desired representation (text instructions, picture sequence or video in the right column)

Why is the option to move a contact to a group greyed out?

All groups in which the contact already exists will be greyed out at the “Move Contact To” function.

How should I handle my contacts?
  • Bosch contacts:
    It is not recommended to store your Bosch contacts again in SfB or in Outlook as these are always local copies. This means they are not updated in case of any change (e.g. department name, mail address (marriage, fixed-term, ...), number). You can open the Bosch global address book on your mobile phone as well as in Outlook. So it is not needed to store them separately.
  • External contacts:
    It is recommended to store external contacts in Outlook (instead of SfB). Doing so, you can add the number as well as the mail address. This contact will then automatically be visible in SfB and synchronised to your iPhone.
  • External contacts with Federation
    If you want to use the advantages of federation with your external partner, you need to add him/her to your SfB contact list. More infromation about SfB Federation and how to use it can be found here.
Why are some names displayed twice in the contact list?

This happens if there is more than one contact entry in Outlook for one person (e.g. one from AD and one from your personal contacts). You can see where SfB gets the contact information from by opening the extended contact card of that person (View Source).

By clicking on "Link Contacts..." another window opens and shows contact sources. (see Screenshot)

>> Please unlink all contact entries except (Address Book) & Skype for Business Contacts. Afterwards, the contact should be displayed correctly.

We strongly recommend to clean up your manual Outlook contacts and only leave externals as manual contacts. By doing so, you ensure having the latest contact information since it is taken from AD. See FAQ above.

Why shouldn't  I create contacts in SfB?
We strongly recommend not to create contacts in SfB as there might occur synchronization problems with other applications and services like Outlook or Mobile PIM. For example, the first name of your contact appears twice or the contact will be duplicated.
How can I configure the iPhone not to sync/ display contacts twice? (duplicated contacts)
If your iPhone displays contacts that were created by SfB and that were synced to your smartphone but you want to remove them because they appear twice (duplicated), please follow the instructions below:

On the iPhone, you need to go to the "Contacts" App, select "Groups" in the upper left corner and deselect all contact groups in the section "BOSCH" except the one called "Kontakte" or "Contacts". After doing so, you'll find only synced contacts from Outlook.

     
Are there any keyboard shortcuts I can use for Skype for Business to improve the practice?

Yes, of course. In order to learn the most useful shortcuts please refer to Tips & Best Practices - SfB Keyboard Shortcuts.

How do I change my photo in Skype for Business?

You can change your photo in Skype for Business (SfB) by going to the Exchange OWA settings: https://rb-owa-portal2.emea.bosch.com/owa/#path=/mail.



Please login and click the gear icon in the right upper corner:

In Options please click "Edit information" and then "Photo":


Click on the Picture in the right upper corner.

And click on Change button:



Please note that your photo displayed in SfB is not synchronised with Bosch Connect.

Additional information

Uploading a photo to be displayed in SfB is voluntary. If you do not want to upload a photo, your account will be displayed like this:

When choosing a photo please consider the following:

  • the picture must not be protected by copyright and / or be discriminatory
  • we recommend using a photo of yourself (e.g. passport photo, BGN photo,..)
Which size, format, etc. should my photo have?

  • File format: JPEG

  • Image file size: up to 20 MB
  • Image resolution: 648 x 648 pixels (If you upload a photo with another image resolution it will be adapted by the system. This might lead to inferior quality.)
  • Color depth: 24-bit
Who can see my photo?
The photo is visible to all Bosch associates, but not to externals. Even in a Skype meeting externals will not see your photo.
How can I remove my photo?

First, click on your profile picture in your SfB client.


Now, your Skype for Business Options will open. "My Picture" is automatically selected. Please click on Edit or Remove Picture.


Outlook Web App will open. Enter your user name and password and click on Sign in.

Previous OWA versionNew OWA version

Afterwards, click on Change, your profile picture will be deleted. Click on Save.


Click the Picture in the right upper corner and click on the Change button

Please click on the Delete symbol and your profile picture will be deleted immediately.


Please note

Icon

The synchronization between Exchange and the Skype for Business client takes some time.

After you clicked save once, the button will be greyed out. It is necessary to wait some time (approximately one day), quit the client and restart it in order to see changes (deleted profile picture).


You will be redirected to your SfB options. Click on Ok to save your changes.

Why do certain accounts not automatically have an SfB account?

All users with BCD account and at least one email-id ending with @bosch.com will automatically have a SfB account.

In case the SfB account is not automatically created, please contact your IDM admin or CI-Hotline. They can add the resource Skype for Business.

Where can I find my Sign-in data (e.g. SIP address)?

Usually, you should be logged on automatically when you start Skype for Business. If that doesn't happen, your sign-in address might be faulty.

Please always use your email address with the suffix "@bosch.com" (e.g. firstname.lastname@bosch.com).

ETAS users: Please use your email address with the suffix "@ucc-service.com"

You can also check your Outlook properties for the right sign-in address (SIP-Address).

If there is no SIP address being displayed in your Outlook Properties, you do not have a Skype for Business account yet.

Why is my SIP address WFA-xx?

Your SfB account is in the process of creation, you should have the account ready in the next 1-2 days.

Why is my SIP address NBA-xx and I cannot login?  

This shows that you do not have an "@bosch.com SMTP address", please inform your IT Partner / CI-Hotline to fix the issue.

Why do I not have a SIP address?

The defined user groups in the questions above should have a SIP account created automatically. However, there are some exceptions:

  • Issues with your user data:
    • Your user data should look like this (1)
    • The field "Department" (2) and / or "Country / Region" (3) must not be empty

    • If you have multiple @bosch.com SMTP address, you should have an @bosch.com SMTP address, which corresponds with the user part of your primary email-id (e.g. SMTP: john.doe@us.bosch.com; smtp: john.doe@bosch.com)  


      Example how it should not look like: sometimes with and sometimes without a prefix like `fixed-term`

    •  If your user data is not correct, please inform your IT Partner / CI-Hotline to fix the issue. 

  • Locations with NC2 or NC3 connection

  • @bcn.bosch.com users

Why did my SIP address change?

a)     Your SIP address is defined based on your @bosch.com email address. If the only existing @bosch.com email address has been updated, your SIP address will be changed automatically to your new email address.

b)    If you are changing from Fixed-Term / External to permanent employee, and your outlook account have been added a new email address with @bosch.com without the Fixed-Term/External prefix, your SIP address will be changed automatically to the new address.

c)     If a new @bosch.com email address has been added and your old email address @bosch.com remains, your SIP address will not change. If there is a need for a change, please write to CI-Hotline using this template.

What to do when my SIP address changes?

a)     Please logon to Skype using your new SIP address. Check the FAQ above for more information: "Where can I find my sign-in data?".

b)    When the SIP address changes, it invalidates all meetings. Please cancel all your Skype meetings, and send out new invites.

Please inform all your Skype contacts to remove you as a contact and add again, otherwise they will not be able to see your presence correctly.

Also good to know:

Question
 Description/Answer
How can I add additional participants to an online meeting?

Have a look at the learning nugget. Click on File and select the desired representation (text instructions, picture sequence or video in the right column)

How to invite meeting participants in blind copy (BCC)?
  1. Create a Skype for Business or Microsoft Teams meeting in Outlook

  2. Insert an invitation text, incl. all relevant information for the participants. Do not insert the participants’ names.
  3. Do not send the invitation! Instead, just save it in your calendar:
  4. In your calendar, click on the meeting
  5. Press CTRL + C
  6. Open a new e-mail message
  7. In the e-mail, press CTRL + V. The appointment is now attached to your e-mail:
  8. Insert all recipients in the BCC field:
    To show the BCC field click on Options > BCC in your e-mail message
  9. Insert a text and click on Send


Important hints

💡 Do not delete the original meeting from your calendar. Otherwise, it’s also deleted for all your recipients.

💡 Please note that you cannot update the meeting invitation afterwards. If you need to reach out to your BCC recipients again, write another e-mail with everyone in BCC.

💡 If participants want to stay anonymous during the meeting, they can participate via the Skype for Business WebApp. If this is the case, please let the participants know in the e-mail invitation.

Can I use Drag and Drop to add call participants?

Yes you can:

Have a look at the learning nugget. Click on File and select the desired representation (text instructions, picture sequence or video in the right column)

What is music on hold and can I change the default music?

Music on hold is available for all Win10 users. If a short break is required during a one-to-one Skype call  and you click the "hold" button, music is played to make the wait more pleasant while keeping the call connected. The music is standardized and set by default, no action is required. It is not allowed to change the music due to legal reasons.

How do I find out which version of Skype for Business is installed on my device?

In order to check the version of your Skype for Business client

  • go to: C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Office\Office16\lync.exe
  • Right click on lync.exe and select Properties
  • Click on Details
