Wi-Fi Calling


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

 A German version can be found here.

Please note: This service is not yet released at every location. 

Wi-Fi Calling

General information

What is Wi-Fi Calling?   

Wi-Fi Calling is a mobile telephony service over Wi-Fi. In this case, the call is placed over the Wi-Fi access points instead of mobile operator's radio network and thereby users will be able to make and receive calls, also at locations where there is no sufficient mobile coverage. If your smartphone is connected to a Wi-Fi network, it establishes a connection to the operators core network. Your smartphone remembers already known Wi-Fi networks. If you are in the vicinity, it connects automatically and you make calls via Wi-Fi depending on the priority given by your operator. Some operator prioritizes Wi-Fi Calling over normal calls and some vice versa.

Can I use Wi-Fi Calling?

Usage of Wi-Fi Calling varies due to the terms of local operators, therefore we cannot give a clear answer. Please contact your local mobile telephony responsible who can be found here.
Wi-Fi Calling is released in Australia, Germany, UK and USA so far. If you are located one of these countries you can use Wi-Fi Calling by activating it on your phone.

What are the advantages of Wi-Fi calling?

  • Ability to make calls where there is poor or no mobile coverage by using Wi-Fi. E.g. in areas with thick concrete walls and special glass facades.
  • Fast call setup times.
  • HD-Voice quality.
  • Same call behaviour: with default smartphone dialer and phone number.
  • No app is required (such as Skype, Facetime, WhatsApp).

Can I use MSW for Wi-Fi Calling?

Yes, you can use MSW (Mobile Services WLAN) to make Wi-Fi calls at Bosch premises. QoS is implemented in MSW for Wi-Fi Calling, therefore it will be prioritized over other Internet applications.

Does my conversation partner also need to use Wi-Fi Calling? 

No, Wi-Fi Calling works independently of what your conversation partner uses.  

How is Wi-Fi Calling being charged?

There is no extra cost. Wi-Fi Calling is already included in your mobile tariff.   

Can Wi-Fi Calling be used for private calls? 

In general, you can also use it private calls. 

What are the pre-requisites for Wi-Fi Calling?  

  • The latest iOS version: For Wi-Fi Calling you need at least the iOS version iOS 10.2. Please update your smartphone to the latest software version released for Intune. You see your current version by clicking on Settings > General > Info > Version. If necessary, update your iOS by clicking on Settings > General > Software update.
  • An updated network operator version: Your network operator settings need to be updated at least to the version 27.1. You can find them under Settings > General > Info > Network operator.

How can I activate and deactivate Wi-Fi Calling?

Turn on  (iOS)Turn off (iOS)

Click on Settings > Phone > Wi-Fi Calling. Switch on Wi-Fi Calling on your iPhone. Please restart your smartphone before your first Wi-Fi Call.

Hint: If Wi-Fi Calling is activated, you directly place your calls via Wi-Fi, as soon as you are connected  to a Wi-Fi network.  You can turn on or off Wi-Fi Calling at any time.

Tipp: Have a look at the short video

Click on Settings > Phone > Wi-Fi Calls. Turn off Wi-Fi Calls on your iPhone.

Instructions for Samsung Smartphones can be found here.  

How will I know if I am using Wi-Fi Calling? 

You recognize you use Wi-Fi Calling when there is a sign or text on the upper corner on your main screen.

  • For example with Vodafone Germany, you see "Vodafone WiFi Calling" in the upper left corner and "Vodafone WiFi Calling" is selected as carrier in the Settings.
  • In UK, you will see O2 WiFiCall.

How can I place calls with Wi-Fi Calling?

You can place Wi-Fi Calls the same way as you do today. Dial a number or choose a contact and click on the green phone button.

What happens in case I have a call via Wi-Fi-Calling and I leave the Wi-Fi area?

It depends on whether you have LTE- connection or not:

  • If you have a LTE connection, your call will not be interrupted. It also works the other way round. You take your call from the LTE-network to the Wi-Fi network without any interruption. You do not need data for this. Wi-Fi Calling in the LTE-area is charged with normal voice minutes which are already included in your flat rate.
  • If you are in the 2G- and 3G-network, you need to re-start your call. 

What do I need to consider when placing emergency calls via Wi-Fi Calling?

  • In Australia: You can make emergency calls. Emergency calls are also carried by other cellular carriers if their coverage is available.
  • In Germany: Due to German regulations, emergency calls cannot be placed via Wi-Fi Calling because location information cannot be retrieved from Wi-Fi Network. Emergency calls will be placed over mobile network automatically. So you need mobile network coverage.
  • In UK: You can still make emergency calls. Please note that if you are in an area with absolute no coverage, your operator will ask where you're calling from as they cannot get location information from Wi-Fi network.
  • In USA: 911 calls will always try cellular service in the local market first even when device is in Airplane mode or cellular service is off. If cellular service isn't available but Wi-Fi calling is set up, the 911 call will route using the registered address. Always remember to keep your location information up-to-date.

Are there any known restrictions or problems?

Yes, currently there are still restrictions which are listed in the following list.

  • Wi-Fi calling is not possible via routers with integrated SIM card. Even if you use a smartphone as a hotspot, WiFi calling is unfortunately not possible.
  • You can send but cannot receive SMS via Wi-Fi where there is no mobile coverage.
  • Emergency calls:
    • Due to German regulations, emergency calls cannot be made via Wi-Fi calling. The smartphone automatically switches to the mobile phone network. Therefore you need a mobile phone coverage. Vodafone alerts you to these restrictions when setting up the emergency call.
  • SMS
    • In Germany, you can send but you cannot receive SMS. In Australia, UK and USA, SMS is not available over Wi-Fi.
  • Wi-Fi Calling Abroad:
    • In Germany and UK, Wi-Fi Calling cannot be used abroad. There your roaming agreement will apply. However, for USA and Australia, Wi-Fi Calling can also be used abroad.

How do I get support?

Please call first your operator's hotline. If the issue occurred due to Wi-Fi problem, please open a ticket to CI-Hotline with the keyword "Wi-Fi Calling".


Information for local mobile telephone responsibles 

Wi-Fi Calling is currently available in several countries. Please follow the steps below if you also want to provide Wi-Fi Calling for your country. Get in contact with your local mobile network provider and clarify the following questions. Then you can come back to us and we will release Wi-Fi Calling also in your country.

  • Is VoLTE supported? VoLTE is important for seamless handover between Wi-Fi Calling and VoLTE.
  • How does Wi-Fi Calling work in your home country? Which one operator prioritizes, Wi-Fi Calling or Call over mobile network when user is connected to Wi-Fi?
  • What are the technical requirements of the operator? Any specific technical specification which we need to be careful with?
  • Is Wi-Fi Calling only supported in the home country or abroad as well?
  • How does SMS work when there is zero cell coverage but there is good Wi-Fi? Does “receive & send” both work?
  • What about emergency calls? Is it supported over Wi-Fi? Is there any problem with your home country's regulators? If emergency call is supported, how?
  • Is there any dependency on tariff options? Can anybody use Wi-Fi Calling today?
  • What will happen when user has a problem? Will operator’s hotline give support?
  • Is Wi-Fi Calling free of charge?
  • How do we see if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on the display of the phone? Is there any sign on the display?
  • Is there a list of the supported devices? What is the baseline for Android and iOS version?

Information for eRoom partners

1.1.1.

Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site.




Tip: For BSH Partners: For any eRoom further information please get in contact with Pasek Marcin (BSH GDS-SEP) and Bulirsch Robert (BSH COS-RE).
     

How to get eRoom at your location

If you are responsible for your location, please create a ticket with the service "eRoom" and script "eRoom_request location_EN" (For BSH responsibles 4444, servicedesk@bshg.com) with the following information:

  • Location with Bosch short name included: e.g. Feuerbach (Fe)
  • Street: e.g. Borsigstrasse 4
  • Site Responsible: The person that will take over the Go Live process

eRoom Team will create a dedicated Teams channel for the handling of the whole Go Live process.

Further information for site managers

1.1.2. General Information for eRoom Set-Up

1.1.2.1.1. eRoom Demo

The demo city is available for all Users. Please open: World→ Europe → Demo City 

1.1.2.1.2. Procedur for the introduction of eRoom
1.1.2.1.2.1. FCM
  1. If your site wants to implement eRoom, contact your locale UCC VT responsible, he will support you in the Golive Process.
  2. Site data, like graphics, room details and contact persons will be needed (CAD-specifications)


1.1.2.1.2.2. UCC VT
  1. The UCC-site-responsible agrees with the site manager/plant manager, local FCM contact (FCM leader), local DSO and local workers council to implement eRoom.
    Result: The site manager/plant manager and the FCM manager agree to the rollout and secure sufficient capacity and resources.

  2. In coordination with the local FCM-management, the eRoom team will enter the location in the activity calendar. The eRoom team creates the location in eRoom system and authorizes the SMR partner to edit this location.
    Result: The rollout at the site is scheduled in the activity calendar. The local SMR partner has the required administration rights in eRoom.

  3. The local FCM and the SMR partner identify all bookable meeting rooms:
    1. Meeting rooms in FCM responsibility
    2. Meeting rooms in responsibility of other departments
    Result: The location, the buildings and their floors are defined. All rooms at the location are known and which department is room owner.

  4. For all meeting rooms under the responsibility of departments, the FCM/SMR partners will clarify the further steps with the department:
    1. Spaces are the responsibility of FCM
    2. Rooms remain the responsibility of departments
    If restrictions are required for bookable meeting rooms or authorization groups, corresponding object groups (containers) must be defined. Such object groups are assigned to  rooms that can be booked by an authorization group.
    Result: All eRoom bookable meeting are defined and grouped according to the local authorization matrix. The corresponding object groups are named according to the eRoom team regulation.

  5. The SMR partner records all bookable rooms, technology and, if necessary, catering in the Excel template, provided by eRoom team.
    Result: All required master data are recorded.

  6. The SMR partner creates all buildings and associated levels in eRoom below the location created in point 2.
    Result: The structure for the location is shown in eRoom.

  7. FCM adapts the existing location plan according to the CAD specifications and provides this as a PNG file. The SMR partner imports the graphic file into eRoom. The buildings belonging to this location are automatically displayed as hotspots. The task now is to move these hotspots to the right position in the graphics.
    Result: The location plan including hotspots is stored in eRoom.

  8. The FCM provides a building view as a PNG file for each multi-floor building. The SMR partner imports the building view as a graphics file in eRoom. The floor levels, belonging to this building, are automatically displayed as hotspots. The task now is to move these hotspots to the right position in the graphics.
    Result: The building sections including hotspots are stored in eRoom.

  9. The SMR partner creates the meeting rooms in eRoom and maintains their master data, source point 7.
    eRoom: https://rb-eroom.de.bosch.com/
    eRoom APAC: https://rb-eroom.apac.bosch.com/
    Result: All bookable rooms, including their master data, are entered in eRoom.

  10. The SMR partner imports the floor graphics, generated in point 11, into eRoom. The bookable meeting rooms that belong to this level are automatically displayed as hotspots. The task is, to move these hotspots to the right position in the graphics.
    Result: Result: Floor plans, including hotspots, are created in eRoom.

  11. The SMR partner clarifies with the location, whether and for which rooms room displays or overview displays are required. eRoom team recommends installing such displays only for representative rooms. Other displays may be used. Test displays - agreed with eRoom team - must be provided by the site itself.
    Result: The number of room or overview displays is fixed. After provisioning, the necessary URLs for connection to eRoom are created by eRoom team.

  12. SMR partner carries out the acceptance test at the location.
    Result: Acceptance has taken place.

  13. After acceptance, the location and eRoom team set the Go Live Date. For a description of a "Go Live" please read the following chapter "Go Live guide for eRoom".
    Result: Go Live can start.

Requirement for Go Live: Successful acceptance tests by SMR-partner.

  1. Clarify whether room mailboxes in Outlook are available for rooms that should be bookable in eRoom in the future. (Please note: eRoom communicates with Outlook via the eRoom add-in, but it does not use room mailboxes)

  2. Clarify whether booking need to be migrated to eRoom, please note the advantages and disadvantages of migration and additional costs may be incurred. If "No" points 5 to 8 can be omitted.

  3. Roll out the SCCM package for the outlook add-in “RBCM2013” at the location.

  4. Inform User/Location about the Go Live and the deactivation of the room mailboxes (at least 2 weeks before).

  5. Check the reservations in the room mailboxes, if they are still valid and if the organizers are still available. Mailboxes must not be ‘hidden’.

  6. Create the room list (eRoom room name with the corresponding NT-account and primary SMTP address) and send it to eRoom team (A dedicated channel for the GoLive will be created by the eRoom team).

  7. eRoom team will export the bookings from the rooms of the room list.

  8. An external service provider (Gingco) will import the data in eRoom.

  9. The SMR-partner has to test the data (objects) and gives the GO for the go live.

  10. eRoom team will activate the location in eRoom (Go Live).

  11. The SMR-partner has to test the location in eRoom.

1.1.3.2.3. Availability

Determines whether the object can be booked. The existing bookings are not affected if the room is marked as "not available". However, no new bookings can be made and existing ones cannot be changed. Attention: if the room is set to "generally unavailable", all other availability settings disappear and may need to be redone. If the settings should be preserved, better disable the room.

Minimum Booking Notice

If you need extensive preparatory work before using the room, you can prevent it from being booked too soon.

Max. Booking Series

Between 1 (no series booking is possible) and 30 (global setting and maximum value) possible.

Booking Duration

Can be set between 1 min. and 24h.

Disable maximum Booking Duration

To book more than one day, you can disable the maximum booking duration.

The room is not available during certain periods or on specific days of the week.

1.1.3.11. Maintenance of booking permissions

In most of the cases, it is not necessary to assign the permissions manually. The administrator allocates the permissions by using rules. These rules evaluate the AD attributes cost center, department, location and (e-mail-)domain and ensure that new users are authorized automatically.
On the other hand it is necessary, that the eRoom partner communicates in advance any changes of cost centers or department names etc to eRoom team, as long as they have effect on the permissions in eRoom. WOM and DL are not supported.

Examples:

Cost center: 425698, 425*

Department: BD/PWS2, BD/*

Location (City): Waiblingen

(E-mail-)domain:  @etas.com

(groups will be limited by object groups and locations)

- Standard booking permission

1.1.3.11.2. Manual assignment

In exceptional cases it can be necessary or desirable to maintain the booking permissions manually. This will be described below.

Booking permissions are organized in "right groups", each right group can be seen as a collection of individual rights, such as the right to book or the right to change a booking. It´s only possible to grant the rights (right groups) that you have yourself – including the site manager rights.
If you need an additional right group, please raise a ticket.

Important: Never use right groups, that are reserved for automatic assignment, recognizable by a suffix in brackets, i.e. (Default), (Userimport), (nur IdM)

Only at your own location, you can grant and revoke permissions. On other locations, the permissions are greyed out and can´t be changed.


Manual assignment of user permissions

Permissions in eRoom are user-related. The basic principle are the permission groups: Each group corresponds to a list of individual rights for which a meaningful name has been defined. For example, the group “Booker” contains individual single rights for booking.

Only administrators can create and modify right groups.

To set permissions for a user, choose the user (System – User – User Settings) and click the “Rights & Right Groups” tab. By using the “+” sign you can add right groups, to revoke right groups please use the “-” sign.
For standard booking permissions we recommend the use of the right group "Bosch booker special rooms" (without Userimport!). If this group is not available for you, contact eRoom team

Please specify the scope of the rights under “Right limitations”.

User group: At the moment we only use “Robert Bosch Ltd. User”
Object group: A summary of rooms and equipment for which special permissions are to apply.
Location: For which location should the permission apply? This could be one of the following: Country, City, Bosch Location, a building or a single floor.

1.1.4. Statistics

Under Statistics you can generate a report about the use of capacity and revenues of a room.

1.1.4.1. Filter Options

There are several filter options in the “Statistics” section to run the required report:

  • Location Filter: Limit your report to one or a number of specified locations only. Open the pop up with a click on the magnifying glass and select the location(s) needed.
  • Category Filter/Object Types: Limit your report to one or several object types or categories to receive a more sophisticated result.
  • Evaluation Period: The exact evaluation period can be set here. Also you can select weekdays to be excluded from the report.
  • Time Grouping/Object Grouping: The list of results can be sorted chronologically and by object attributes.

1.1.4.2. Utilisation Report Options

The utilisation report offers the following additional filter options:

  • Evaluation Period: The evaluation period can be limited to specified times of the day.
  • Data to View: The report can be issued in percent or in hours.
  • Calculation Type: You can distinguish between a ‘Relative’ and an ‘Absolute’ calculation type, which means that you can define if the objects have been booked directly or if they have been booked indirectly, i.e. through a room combination.
  • Furthermore, the handling of permanent assignments, set up times, opening hours, and other options can be included in the report result.

1.1.4.3. Revenue Filter Options

The revenue filter offers the following additional options: · Cost types: Different cost types can be selected (object costs, seating costs, seating upgrade costs, cancellation costs).

1.1.4.4. Calculation of Utilisation / Revenues

Only those objects are included in the statistics that a user is authorized to report. Also the total sum is limited to these objects.

For the average calculation only the actually evaluated time period is considered. This means for example, if the weekend is excluded from the calculation, the average calculation is also done for business days only.

The maximum number of ‘unlimited’ objects cannot be specified, which means that their utilisation can only be calculated to a certain extend. All bookings for these objects are summarised into one, so that the utilisation can also amount up to 100%.

Average values are calculated proportionately if, for example, the output is grouped by weeks, but the end of the time period is not the end of the week. The grouping by weeks complies to ISO 8601.

1.1.5. Exports

This section explains the export options in eRoom. Each department (FCM, Catering, ...) has to decide by their own which export is the right one for them.

1.1.5.1. Booking Export

Under ‘Management > Booking Export’ a user with the appropriate rights can export an Excel sheet with detailed booking. The export can be limited to a specified time period and location as well as to a specific booking status.

1.1.5.2. Booking Overview

Management → Bookings → Booking Overview

Export all bookings of a specific location to an excel or pdf file.

 


1.1.5.3. Delivery Notes

Management → Delivery Notes

Delivery notes can be created for everything in the selected location or selected for technology, catering or service with a separate page for each order.

 


1.1.5.4. Order List

Management → Order List

The order list shows items that the technician or caterer has to deliver in a certain period of time. To export the order list, it is necessary to select a location and the mailing list under “order to”.

 

1.1.5.5. Day List

Management → Day List

In the Day List you will find all events of a day, sorted by time, with the ordered equipment. Since the version 2.14.0.37 the standard seating will be displayed for better differentiation.

 


1.1.6. Confirmation List

Bookings that require a confirmation - perhaps for security reasons or to manage costs - are listed under ‘Management > Confirmation List’. Note that you need the right to see and access this list.

Objects that require a confirmation can be booked as any other object. The booking confirmation e-mail informs the user that the status of his/her booking is ‘unconfirmed’ and that it has to be approved first.

The person in charge of booking confirmations is notified if booking for an object has been made that he/ she manages. The ‘Confirmation List’ displays all unconfirmed bookings, which can be approved or declined with the buttons next to each booking.

If more booking details are needed to confirm or decline a booking, or if a booking has to be amended first, the confirmation manager can double click to open a booking. The buttons ‘Accept confirmation’ and ‘Refuse confirmation’ can be used within the Booking Details. Meeting participants and external service providers are notified of the booking by e-mail once it is confirmed. In case a booking is rejected, only the meeting host receives a notification.

How to Send Pictures/Videos from Mobile to your Computer with Ad hoc Data Exchange

Prerequisite: You need access to Ad hoc Data Exchange

Step 1:  Create an Ad hoc Data Exchange external account for yourself

The internal login link (https://rb-wam.bosch.com/...) allows SSO (Single Sign On), but unfortunately this is not accessible from Bosch mobile devices.
The login-link for external business partners differs from the link for internals, but it allows access from mobile devices (including Bosch mobile devices). The 'trick' is, to send files from your internal 'Ad hoc' account (using your notebook or computer) to an e-mail, which is treated as external user by Ad hoc Data Exchange.

  1. Go to the Ad hoc Data Exchange Site on your computer and Press the “Log in” Button.


  2. Select the “Send Files” Button.

  3. Either type in any private e-mail address (you have access to on your mobile device) or type in your Bosch e-mail address 'a little bit modified', namely with just the "@bosch.com" domain (without any country abbreviation like "de", "en", etc.)  at the end, e.g. max.mustermann@bosch.com. You don't need to fill in the phone number as you will get your password via email. Click on the next button


  4. Enter some text as a message if your require. Then click the "next" button

  5. Drag and Drop a (dummy) file into the designated area on the screen or select the file.

  6. Then select the "Send Files" Button.


Step 2:  Login to your Ad hoc Data Exchange external account on your mobile and send pictures to your computer

  1. Now you should receive some mails through to your email. Browse to the Mail on your phone and it should look something like this below.
     
  2. Select the Web app Link and you will be brought to a page like below.
  3. You will also have received another 2 additional mails regarding an account being created, one of them will have the password.
    Copy this info from your mails to the webpage on your phone for the relevant password field and log in. (The username field will be filled out automatically)
    You will get a screen like below
  4. At this point you can select whether or not you want to send files or download files, in this case it will be send files.

page_name: Login Failure - Error message: "Forbidden - error code 0x38cf0427"
html_content:
Login Failure - Error message: "Forbidden - error code 0x38cf0427"

Issue when logging into Ad hoc Data Exchange


You are getting thies error message because you don't have the permission to access Ad hoc Data Exchange.  

Please follow the instructions here to be granted access to Ad hoc Data Exchange.

page_name: I haven't received any e-mail notifying me of my business partner's password
html_content:
I haven't received any e-mail notifying me of my business partner's password

1st Cause: Please check the spam folder of your e-mail system. This e-mail might have been detected as SPAM. If this is the case, please submit a ticket to the IT Service Desk, solution group "Internet Mail". Insert the affected e-mail and forward it to "IT Service Desk". For contact details see here.

2nd Cause: Accounts of business partners are valid for 7 days. No new user names and passwords will be generated as long as the accounts are still valid: If you have sent files and you haven't received any e-mail (from Ad hoc Data Exchange) informing you of your business partner's password, it  might be that your business partner's account is still valid. 

3rd Cause: Your business partner might have received files from other Ad hoc Data Exchange users. In this case the password has been already shared. Your business partner must have already received an e-mail notification with the subject “Account created….”. That e-mail contains the login information and the original sender who initiated the account creation. He is the one who should forward the password to the business partner.

4th Cause: It is also possible, that meanwhile your business partner has an Ad hoc  Data Exchange access for internal users (like you). In these case, no password is required.

page_name: Why has my business partner not received any email notification,  although I have sent him data with Ad hoc Data Exchange?
html_content:
Why has my business partner not received any email notification, although I have sent him data with Ad hoc Data Exchange?

1st reason Please ask your business partner to check the spam folder of his/her email system. If his/her email account is configured to receive emails only from trusted senders, it might be that emails from Ad hoc Data Exchange are marked as spam and therefore they are moved into the spam folder. 

2nd reason You might have entered a wrong email address while sending your files.
Please make sure that you have entered the correct email address.

page_name: My business partner cannot login to Ad hoc Data Exchange - Missing or invalid credentials
html_content:
My business partner cannot login to Ad hoc Data Exchange - Missing or invalid credentials

1st reason The account of your business partner is valid for 7 days only.
His/her credentials (user name and password) might not be valid any more. Please ask your business partner to check, when he/she last received an e-mail from Ad hoc Data Exchange informing him/her of his/her user name (e-mail subject “Account created…”). Please make sure that you have forwarded the latest current password to your business partner, in case your business partner is not able to get his password via voice call message. In case this e-mail is older than 7 days and meanwhile he/she did not receive any new files, then his/her credentials are not valid any more!

2nd reason Your business partner might have confused user name and password: A user name begins with “adhoc….” and consists of letters and numerals. A password consists of numerals only (0-9).

3rd reason Your business partner might not have used the correct login link. The correct link for business partners begins with https://webapp.....

4th reason Your business partner might have entered his/her e-mail inside the field "user name". E-mail is not the user name. More inofrmation about user names, see above.

How can your business partner find his credentials?

  • User names can be found in e-mail notifications (sent to your business partner) with the subject “Account created...”
  • In case of password, there are two options:

    1. When you send data to your business partner, you will receive an email informing you of your business partner’s password. For security reasons, DO NOT forward the password e-mail to your business partner. Share the password via phone call only!
      Optionally, you can enter your business partner’s phone number and in this case his/her e-mail notification (with the subject “Account created..”) will also contain a link to initiate a voice call that will provide the password additionally. For security reasons the voice call-link will expire after calling it up.

    2. In case your business partner has forgotten his/her password, please forward him/her the password (you must have received a relevant e-mail). In case you do not know your business partner's password either, use this link to initiate a user name and password reset: https://rb-wam.bosch.com/adhoc/internal/selfservice/resetpartnersaccount.jsf .
      By clicking on the above link, new credentials (user name and password) are generated for your business partner.  You will be informed of your business partners password via e-mail. Please forward him/her this new password. Your business partner will receive a new e-mail notification that will contain his/her user name.

page_name: My business partner is not able to initiate a voice call or did not get a voice call (although I have entered his/her phone number)
html_content:
My business partner is not able to initiate a voice call or did not get a voice call (although I have entered his/her phone number)

1st reason You might have typed a wrong phone number.

2nd reason Please note that, for security reasons the voice call link (in the e-mail) for business partners will expire after its first use. Therefore your business partner will not be able to initiate a voice call once again, using the same link.

page_name: If I send multiple files to my business partner, does he have to download each file separately?
html_content:
If I send multiple files to my business partner, does he have to download each file separately?

As soon as more than two files are available for download, Ad hoc Data Exchange automatically creates a zip-file.

The recipient (either internal or external) will be able to download multiple files at a single click.

page_name: What file types does Ad hoc Data Exchange support?
html_content:
What file types does Ad hoc Data Exchange support?

With Ad hoc Data Exchange you can exchange any file type.

page_name: What is the maximum number of files and overall max size in a single transfer?
html_content:
What is the maximum number of files and overall max size in a single transfer?

  • Max. number of files in a single transfer is 999.
  • Maximum number of files per day is 10000.

  • Maximum single file size is 20 GB. 

  • Overall max. size in a single transfer is 50 GB.

  • 50 GB is also the overall max. size you are allowed to transfer within 24 hours.



Note

Nevertheless, we recommend you send smaller file sizes if possible. (e.g.  just split the files before uploading them)

Keep in mind the larger the file, the more time it takes to transfer it and therefore the greater the chance of issue.

page_name: Is it possible to see what files have been uploaded/sent, and to which recipients?
html_content:
Is it possible to see what files have been uploaded/sent, and to which recipients?

Data transfer is being logged. The log files can be viewed by the Ad hoc Data Exchange administrators only and will be deleted automatically after 90 days.

Only in case of legal issues, the log files can be provided to the user via a ticket at IT Service Portal (Ad hoc Data Exchange order form).

page_name: Is it possible to send the same file(s) to multiple recipients at the same time via Ad hoc Data EXchange?
html_content:
Is it possible to send the same file(s) to multiple recipients at the same time via Ad hoc Data EXchange?

Via Ad hoc Data Exchange, it is not possible to send files to multiple recipients.

For this, you have to use OpenDXM.

page_name: Why is the password for business partners being sent via voice message and NOT via SMS?
html_content:
Why is the password for business partners being sent via voice message and NOT via SMS?

Many business partners do not have a business mobile phone at their disposal and they do not want to use their private mobile phone in order to get SMS.

page_name: Charging for Ad hoc Data Exchange
html_content:
Charging for Ad hoc Data Exchange

Ad hoc Data Exchange is not charged directly to the Ad hoc Data Exchange users but to all Bosch IT users, since Ad hoc Data Exchange (Service Code (LASL): 221G06) is part of the "Standard IT User" accounting.

The charges of the "Standard IT User" bundle many CI services, e. g. Portal, Connect, SfB, SharePoint, SCCM, Ad hoc Data Exchange etc.

page_name: Is it possible to send files of security class C-SC3 with Ad hoc Data Exchange?
html_content:
Is it possible to send files of security class C-SC3 with Ad hoc Data Exchange?

In general, we recommend that you use OpenDXM for exchanging data of security class C-SC3.

With Ad hoc Data Exchange, it is also possible to send data that are security class C-SC3 by encrypting your file(s).
See https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/QL0lRw 


Instructions on how to encrypt with 7-Zip

Bitte folgen Sie den Anweisungen hier, um Zugang zum Ad hoc Data Exchange zu erhalten.

page_name: Ich habe keine E-Mail erhalten, die mich über das Passwort meines Geschäftspartners informiert
html_content:
Ich habe keine E-Mail erhalten, die mich über das Passwort meines Geschäftspartners informiert

Grund 1: Bitte überprüfen Sie den Spam-Ordner Ihres E-Mail-Systems. Evtl. ist diese E-mail als SPAM erkannt worden. Ist dies der Fall, eröffnen Sie bitte ein Ticket beim IT Service Desk, Lösergruppe "Internet Mail". Fügen Sie die betroffene E-Mail ein, und leiten Sie sie an "IT Service Desk" weiter. Kontaktdaten siehe hier.

Grund 2: Die Zugänge der Geschäftspartner sind 7 Tage gültig. Es werden keine neuen Benutzernamen und Passwörter generiert, solange die Zugänge noch gültig sind. Wenn Sie Dateien versendet haben und keine E-Mail (von Ad hoc Data Exchange) erhalten haben, die Sie über das Passwort Ihres Geschäftspartners informiert, dann liegt es daran, dass der Zugang Ihres Geschäftspartners weiterhin gültig ist. Bitte beachten Sie auch, dass, sollten Sie während dieser Zeit weitere Dateien schicken, bereits gültige Accounts vom System um weitere 7 Tage verlängert werden.

Grund 3: Ihr Geschäftspartner hat möglicherweise Dateien von anderen Ad hoc Data Exchange Benutzern erhalten. In diesem Fall wurde das Passwort bereits mitgeteilt. Ihr Geschäftspartner muss bereits eine E-Mail-Benachrichtigung mit dem Betreff "Account created..." erhalten haben. Diese E-Mail enthält die Anmeldeinformationen und den ursprünglichen Absender, der die Erstellung des Zugangs veranlasst hat. Er ist derjenige, der das Passwort an den Geschäftspartner weiterleiten soll.

Grund 4: Es ist auch möglich, dass Ihr Geschäftspartner zwischenzeitlich einen Ad hoc Data Exchange Zugang für interne Benutzer (wie Sie) hat. In diesem Fall ist kein Passwort mehr erforderlich.

page_name: Mein Geschäftspartner hat keine E-Mail-Benachrichtigung erhalten! Was ist der Grund dafür?
html_content:
Mein Geschäftspartner hat keine E-Mail-Benachrichtigung erhalten! Was ist der Grund dafür?

1. Grund: Bitte fragen Sie Ihren Geschäftspartner, ob er den Spam-Ordner seines E-Mail-Systems überprüft hat. Wenn sein E-Mail-Account so konfiguriert ist, dass E-Mails nur von vertrauenswürdigen Absendern empfangen werden dürfen, kann es sein, dass E-Mails von Ad hoc Data Exchange als Spam markiert werden und somit in den Spam-Ordner verschoben werden.

2. Grund: Sie haben beim Versenden Ihrer Dateien möglicherweise eine falsche E-Mail-Adresse eingegeben. Bitte überprüfen Sie, ob Sie die richtige E-Mail Adresse eingegeben haben,

page_name: Mein Geschäftspartner kann sich nicht anmelden - Fehlende oder ungültige Zugangsdaten
html_content:
Mein Geschäftspartner kann sich nicht anmelden - Fehlende oder ungültige Zugangsdaten

1. Grund:  Der Zugang Ihres Geschäftspartners ist für 7 Tage gültig. Es könnte sein, dass dessen Zugangsdaten (Benutzername und Passwort) nicht mehr gültig sind. Bitte weisen Sie Ihren Geschäftspartner darauf hin zu überprüfen, wann er zuletzt eine E-Mail von Ad hoc Data Exchange erhalten hat, die ihn über seine Zugangsdaten informiert (E-Mail Betreff  "Account created/ Benutzer angelegt..."). Sollte diese E-Mail älter als 7 Tage sein, und Ihr Geschäftspartner hat seitdem keine neuen Dateien erhalten, dann sind seine Zugangsdaten nicht mehr gültig!

2. Grund:  Ihr Geschäftspartner hat Benutzername und Passwort verwechselt: Ein Benutzername beginnt mit "adhoc..." und besteht aus Buchstaben und Ziffern. Ein Passwort besteht nur aus Ziffern (0-9).

3. Grund:  Ihr Geschäftspartner hat möglicherweise nicht den korrekten Login-Link verwendet. Der richtige Link für Geschäftspartner beginnt mit https://webapp.....

4. Grund:  Ihr Geschäftspartner hat unter Umständen seine E-Mail im Feld "Benutzername" eingegeben. E-Mail ist nicht der Benutzername. Mehr Informationen zu Benutzernamen, siehe oben.


Wie kann Ihr Geschäftspartner seine Zugangsdaten finden?

  1. Benutzernamen finden Sie in E-Mail-Benachrichtigungen (an Ihren Geschäftspartner) mit dem Betreff "Account created/ Benutzer angelegt..."
  2. Bei Passwort gibt es zwei Möglichkeiten:
    1. Wenn Sie Daten an Ihren Geschäftspartner senden, erhalten Sie eine E-Mail mit dem Passwort Ihres Geschäftspartners. Aus Sicherheitsgründen dürfen Sie das Passwort NICHT per E-Mail an Ihren Geschäftspartner weiterleiten. Geben Sie das Passwort nur per Telefonanruf weiter! Optional können Sie die Telefonnummer Ihres Geschäftspartners eingeben und in diesem Fall enthält seine E-Mail-Benachrichtigung (mit dem Betreff "Account created/ Benutzer angelegt...") auch einen Link zum Initiieren einer telefonischen Sprachnachricht, die das Passwort zusätzlich mitteilt. Aus Sicherheitsgründen erlischt die Sprachverbindung nach dem Aufruf.
    2. Falls Ihr Geschäftspartner sein Passwort vergessen hat, senden Sie ihm bitte das Passwort zu (Sie müssen eine entsprechende E-Mail erhalten haben). Falls Ihnen das Passwort Ihres Geschäftspartners auch nicht bekannt ist, können Sie über diesen Link einen Benutzernamen und ein Passwort Reset initiieren: https://rb-wam.bosch.com/adhoc/internal/selfservice/resetpartnersaccount.jsf Durch Klick auf den obigen Link werden neue Zugangsdaten (Benutzername und Passwort) für Ihren Geschäftspartner generiert.  Das Passwort Ihres Geschäftspartners wird Ihnen per E-Mail mitgeteilt. Bitte senden Sie ihm dieses neue Passwort zu. Ihr Geschäftspartner erhält eine neue E-Mail-Benachrichtigung mit seinem Benutzernamen.

page_name: Mein Geschäftspartner kann keinen Sprachanruf iniziieren bzw. er hat keinen Sprachanruf erhalten (obwohl ich seine Telefonnummer eingegeben habe)
html_content:
Mein Geschäftspartner kann keinen Sprachanruf iniziieren bzw. er hat keinen Sprachanruf erhalten (obwohl ich seine Telefonnummer eingegeben habe)

1. Grund:  Sie haben vielleicht eine falsche Telefonnummer eingegeben.

2. Grund:  Bitte beachten Sie, dass aus Sicherheitsgründen der Sprachanruf-Link (in der E-Mail) für Geschäftspartner nach der ersten Nutzung abläuft. Daher kann Ihr Geschäftspartner über den gleichen Link keinen weiteren Anruf mehr initiieren.

page_name: Wenn ich mehrere Dateien an meinen Geschäftspartner sende, muss er dann jede Datei einzeln herunterladen?
html_content:
Wenn ich mehrere Dateien an meinen Geschäftspartner sende, muss er dann jede Datei einzeln herunterladen?

Sobald mehr als zwei Dateien zum Download bereitstehen, erstellt Ad hoc Data Exchange automatisch eine Zip-Datei.

Der Empfänger (intern oder extern) kann mehrere Dateien mit einem Klick herunterladen!

Welche Dateitypen werden unterstützt?

Mit Ad hoc Data Exchange können Sie beliebige Dateitypen austauschen.

page_name: Wie hoch ist die maximale Anzahl der Dateien und die maximale Gesamtgröße bei einer einzelnen Übertragung?
html_content:
Wie hoch ist die maximale Anzahl der Dateien und die maximale Gesamtgröße bei einer einzelnen Übertragung?

  • Die maximale Anzahl der Dateien in einer einzelnen Übertragung beträgt 999.
  • Die maximale Anzahl der Dateien pro Tag beträgt 10000.
  • Die maximale Datenmenge in einem Transfer beträgt 50 GB.

  • Die maximale Größe einer einzelnen Datei beträgt 20 GB.

  • Die maximal erlaubte zu transferierende Datenmenge pro Tag beträgt 50 GB.

    Note

    Dennoch empfehlen wir Ihnen, nach Möglichkeit kleinere Dateigrößen zu verwenden. (z.B. einfach die Dateien vor dem Hochladen splitten)

    Denken Sie daran, je größer die Datei ist, desto mehr Zeit benötigt sie für die Übertragung und desto größer ist die Wahrscheinlichkeit von Problemen.

page_name: Ist es möglich zu sehen, welche Dateien hochgeladen/gesendet wurden und an welche Empfänger?
html_content:
Ist es möglich zu sehen, welche Dateien hochgeladen/gesendet wurden und an welche Empfänger?

Die Datenübertragung wird protokolliert. Die Logdateien können nur von den Ad hoc Administratoren eingesehen werden und werden nach 90 Tagen automatisch gelöscht.

Nur bei rechtlichen Fragen können die Logfiles dem Anwender über ein Ticket beim IT Service Desk zur Verfügung gestellt werden.

page_name: Ist es möglich, die gleichen Dateien an mehrere Empfänger gleichzeitig zu senden?
html_content:
Ist es möglich, die gleichen Dateien an mehrere Empfänger gleichzeitig zu senden?

Dies ist nicht möglich, dafür müssen Sie OpenDXM benutzen.

page_name: Warum wird das Passwort für Geschäftspartner per Sprachnachricht und NICHT per SMS versendet?
html_content:
Warum wird das Passwort für Geschäftspartner per Sprachnachricht und NICHT per SMS versendet?

Viele Geschäftspartner haben kein Geschäftshandy zur Verfügung und möchten nicht ihr privates Mobiltelefon benutzen, um SMS zu erhalten.

page_name: Ist es möglich, mit Ad hoc Data Exchange Dateien der Schutzklasse C-SC3 zu versenden?
html_content:
Ist es möglich, mit Ad hoc Data Exchange Dateien der Schutzklasse C-SC3 zu versenden?

Generell empfehlen wir Ihnen, OpenDXM für den Austausch von C-SC3 Daten zu verwenden.

Mit Ad hoc Data Exchange ist es auch möglich, C-SC3-Daten zu senden, indem Sie Ihre Datei(en) verschlüsseln.
Siehe https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/QL0lRw 


Anleitung zur Verschlüsselung mit 7-Zip

Ad hoc Data Exchange Kosten

Ad hoc Data Exchange wird nicht direkt an die Ad hoc Anwender sondern an alle Bosch IT-User verrechnet, da  Ad hoc Data Exchange (LASL: 221G06) Bestandteil der Verrechnung des "Standard IT User" ist.

Die Kosten des "Standard IT User" bündeln viele CI-Services, z. B. Portal, Connect, SfB, SharePoint, SCCM, Ad hoc Data Exchange etc.

page_name: Ist Ad hoc Data Exchange konform mit DSGVO?
html_content:
Ist Ad hoc Data Exchange konform mit DSGVO?

Ad hoc Data Exchange ist konform mit DSGVO (Datenschutz-Grundverordnung).

Informationen dazu finden die Geschäftspartner auf der Anmeldeseite von Ad hoc Data Exchange (für Geschäftspartner)

page_name: Does Ad hoc Data Exchange conform with the GDPR?
html_content:
Does Ad hoc Data Exchange conform with the GDPR?

Ad hoc Data Exchange conforms with the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation).
Your business partner can find further information on the login page of Ad hoc Data Exchange for business partners:

Automated File Transfer with OpenDXM

Automated File Transfer is a term used to describe the programmatic movement of files.

With OpenDXM, you can automate your repetitive file transfers in the following ways:

  • Automated transfer of received (incoming) files to a user's specific share
       

  • Automated file transfers to or from business partners 
     

  • Automated file uploads via OpenDXM REST APIs

.

.

Do you have a requirement to automate your current data transfers?

If so and you’d like to find out more about the automated file transfer use cases of OpenDXM, contact us on OpenDXM Team.

page_name: Automated transfer of received files to a user's specific share with OpenDXM
html_content:
Automated transfer of received files to a user's specific share with OpenDXM

Received (incoming) files for internal users (Bosch Group) can be transferred automatically to their specific file share.

From that share, the recipient (a OpenDXM user) can process the data automatically.
You can apply for an OpenDXM user for existing regular AD (Active Directory) users or for so called "COMMUNICATION"/"Shared Mailbox" users (if you want the files to be routed to your file share only; without the need to send files or log onto OpenDXM interactively). "COMMUNICATION"/"Shared Mailbox" can also be applied via ITSP as a user type of "resource users" under the topic "Manage Resource Accounts".

The following requirements must be met.

  1. The file share must be:

    • located inside BCN (Bosch Corporate Network)
    • an NFS (Network File System) share

    Please follow the instructions at the following link on how to order a Fileshare with NFS:

    https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/UrlzU

    !! Please make sure that the following fields are filled out correctly, as shown below:


    As “File Share Name” and “DFS Folder Name”: enter your project name (e.g. “lsp_data”).
    Please do not use any blanks or special characters apart from ‘_’ or ‘-‘.


    "Transport Encryption" is always checked by default when the prompt for "security class"  is C-SC2.
    Please note: Do not select the checkbox "2-Factor Authentication" as NFS file shares do not support 2FA


    "NFSv4 with Kerberos (krb5p) authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" has to be selected.

    (If  the option"NFSv3 with sys authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" or "NFSv4 with sys authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" is selected, then the additional section Exports with the field ‘Add Export’ is displayed and you have to add @dxmserver to the “Exports. See also here, section 5.1 
    Explanation: "@dxmserver" ist a so called netgroup and contains the productive OpenDXM servers that require access to your share. The current server referenced via "@dxmserver" are: fe-138szzc146.de.bosch.com, si-138szzc146.de.bosch.com, fe-610lc330.de.bosch.com, si-610lc330.de.bosch.com)



    For “Members and visitors”, select your own users/groups who should be able to access this share.

     Add OpenDXM with the user name “de\dxm” as a “Member” of your share (see screenshot below):


    Select “location”: Fe or Si (for better performance)

    Finally, submit the request. As a next step, the MoR (Master of Role, usually your manager) has to approve this request.

    Some Business units might have their own requesting processes:

    e.g. ED, AE, CP,.. use "easy2order": https://rb-easy2order.bosch.com/

    Please note: In the case, you request for an NFS share via other services, you have to ensure that the service user “de\dxm” gets change permissions (read, write, create, delete) on this share.”


    Background information: Why do you need an NFS share? 

    NFS share is a multiprotocol share, that means two different operating systems (UNIX and Windows) can have access to the share.

    This is required due to the following reasons:

    • The OpenDXM service runs under the operating system UNIX

    • The customer's operating system is mainly Windows based.


    If you want to use an existing multiprotocol share, please notify us of the share name.


    Instructions on how to verify that your share is an NFS share:

    • Click with the right mouse button on your share.


    • Select "CI File Service" and then "Share Management"


    • Select "File Share Info":


    • If the tab "Unix" exists, it means that your share is an NFS share:

    In the tab "Unix", you can find further information on your NFS share (version, automounter path...).



    Another method to check your file share is this tool: https://www.intranet.bosch.com/app/fileservice/cihotlinehelper/#/Access-Rights-Checker



  2. OpenDXM access is required

    Due to license related reasons only employees of Robert Bosch GmbH or of a regional / subsidiary in which the Robert Bosch GmbH holds the majority (> 50%) are allowed to use OpenDXM to exchange data with business partners worldwide  (internal/external business partners, customers, suppliers..)

    In order for a Bosch Group employee to be able to use OpenDXM, the Application/Resource DXM has to be assigned to the user in IdM system (Identity Management system) and be approved by the line manager.

    To do this, there are two options:


    1. Go to  the OpenDXM Order form on IT Service Portal.

    2. Click Order (for your own request)  or  Order For Others (for your colleagues' request):

    3. Click the radio Button "INTERNAL User", then "Request access" and submit your request:


    Description of the registration process

    After the OpenDXM order has been submitted on ITSP, the required roles (role  "tam-dxm-allow" of the Application/Resource WAM and the role "internal-users" of the Application/Resource DXM) will be automatically assigned to the user in the IdM-System. 

    As soon as  the application/resource DXM has been assigned, the user account is automatically created in OpenDXM.

    After approval by the OpenDXM Support Team, the user will be granted the download right in OpenDXM (i.e. the user will be able to receive data only) and will receive an email notification with all information needed to access OpenDXM.

    Finally, the IdM request/workflow will be sent automatically to the user's line manager for approval.

    Once the IdM request has been approved by the line manager, the user is granted upload rights in OpenDXM (i.e. the user will be able to select recipients and send data) and is notified by e-mail.


    OR 


    Brief description:

    Please request the following roles:

    ApplicationRole
    WAMtam-dxm-allow
    DXMinternal-users


    Detailed description:

    Go to Launchpad: https://inside.bosch.com/irj/portal/fiori#Shell-home&/appFinder/catalog

    Search for IdM Start Page and start IdM

    Select the tab User "Self Service" and search for "WAM"

    Click on "WAM"

     

    Select the tab Find access rights and search for tam-dxm-allow

    Click on the  button to add the role to the shopping cart

    From the tab "User self service" search for "DXM" and click on DXM:

    Select the tab Find access rights and search for internal-users


    Click on the  button to add the role to the shopping cart

    Click on the Shopping cart button

    Enter a reason for requesting access and then click on the Submit cart button.


    Your request to access OpenDXM will not be completed until your line manager approves the request in the IdM system.

    Please confirm with your line manager that the approval of your request has been granted.



    In case of questions or issues please contact the OpenDXM Support Team.



  1. Make sure you have created the folder in in your NFS share (see here for further details)

  2. Your business partner(s) send files to your (batch) user via their OpenDXM account

  3. The received files will be stored automatically on your NFS share, in the folder "in", where subfolders will be created automatically.
    The name of these subfolders is the sender's email address.

    If the received files are very large, the copying process may take longer.
    To prevent the files from being further processed while they are still being copied on the folder, OpenDXM creates "trigger" files (file ending: .rdy) for each file once the copy process is completed. This indicates the end of the file copy.
    Trigger files have the same names as the source files, but in additional .rdy as file ending (e.g. source file: test.txt ; Trigger file: test.txt.rdy)
    Please make sure to process the received files only after the corresponding rdy file has been created.

  4. The files are now available on you NFS share for further processing

    a. Please make sure that the file names of the received files are unique. Otherwise you run the risk that a later file will overwrite an earlier one with the same filename.
    To do this,  we recommend that your business partner (sender) create unique file names using a date/time stamp as part of the filename (YYYYmmddHHMMSS).  

    b. We do not delete any files on your share - you are the master of the data and thus it is your own responsibility to delete files when you no longer need them.

page_name: How to order an NFS (Network File System) share?
html_content:
How to order an NFS (Network File System) share?

Please follow the instructions at the following link on how to order a Fileshare with NFS:

https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/UrlzU

!! Please make sure that the following fields are filled out correctly, as shown below:


As “File Share Name” and “DFS Folder Name”: enter your project name (e.g. “lsp_data”).
Please do not use any blanks or special characters apart from ‘_’ or ‘-‘.


"Transport Encryption" is always checked by default when the prompt for "security class"  is C-SC2.
Please note: Do not select the checkbox "2-Factor Authentication" as NFS file shares do not support 2FA


"NFSv4 with Kerberos (krb5p) authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" has to be selected.

(If  the option"NFSv3 with sys authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" or "NFSv4 with sys authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" is selected, then the additional section Exports with the field ‘Add Export’ is displayed and you have to add @dxmserver to the “Exports. See also here, section 5.1 
Explanation: "@dxmserver" ist a so called netgroup and contains the productive OpenDXM servers that require access to your share. The current server referenced via "@dxmserver" are: fe-138szzc146.de.bosch.com, si-138szzc146.de.bosch.com, fe-610lc330.de.bosch.com, si-610lc330.de.bosch.com)



For “Members and visitors”, select your own users/groups who should be able to access this share.

 Add OpenDXM with the user name “de\dxm” as a “Member” of your share (see screenshot below):


Select “location”: Fe or Si (for better performance)

Finally, submit the request. As a next step, the MoR (Master of Role, usually your manager) has to approve this request.

Some Business units might have their own requesting processes:

e.g. ED, AE, CP,.. use "easy2order": https://rb-easy2order.bosch.com/

Please note: In the case, you request for an NFS share via other services, you have to ensure that the service user “de\dxm” gets change permissions (read, write, create, delete) on this share.”


Background information: Why do you need an NFS share? 

NFS share is a multiprotocol share, that means two different operating systems (UNIX and Windows) can have access to the share.

This is required due to the following reasons:

  • The OpenDXM service runs under the operating system UNIX

  • The customer's operating system is mainly Windows based.


If you want to use an existing multiprotocol share, please notify us of the share name.


Instructions on how to verify that your share is an NFS share:

  • Click with the right mouse button on your share.


  • Select "CI File Service" and then "Share Management"


  • Select "File Share Info":


  • If the tab "Unix" exists, it means that your share is an NFS share:

In the tab "Unix", you can find further information on your NFS share (version, automounter path...).



Another method to check your file share is this tool: https://www.intranet.bosch.com/app/fileservice/cihotlinehelper/#/Access-Rights-Checker

page_name: Automated File Transfer to or from Business Partners with OpenDXM
html_content:
Automated File Transfer to or from Business Partners with OpenDXM

This file transfer automation is recommended NOT for single users but for groups of users or for systems.

Automated file transfer (or batch transfer) allows users to automate repetitive file transfer tasks or high-volume file transfers to or from business partners (both internal and external) worldwide.

To do this, follow the steps below:

Step 1:  Request for an NFS Share (NFS=Network File System) 

Please follow the instructions at the following link on how to order a Fileshare with NFS:

https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/UrlzU

!! Please make sure that the following fields are filled out correctly, as shown below:


As “File Share Name” and “DFS Folder Name”: enter your project name (e.g. “lsp_data”).
Please do not use any blanks or special characters apart from ‘_’ or ‘-‘.


"Transport Encryption" is always checked by default when the prompt for "security class"  is C-SC2.
Please note: Do not select the checkbox "2-Factor Authentication" as NFS file shares do not support 2FA


"NFSv4 with Kerberos (krb5p) authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" has to be selected.

(If  the option"NFSv3 with sys authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" or "NFSv4 with sys authentication (Access with Linux/Unix)" is selected, then the additional section Exports with the field ‘Add Export’ is displayed and you have to add @dxmserver to the “Exports. See also here, section 5.1 
Explanation: "@dxmserver" ist a so called netgroup and contains the productive OpenDXM servers that require access to your share. The current server referenced via "@dxmserver" are: fe-138szzc146.de.bosch.com, si-138szzc146.de.bosch.com, fe-610lc330.de.bosch.com, si-610lc330.de.bosch.com)



For “Members and visitors”, select your own users/groups who should be able to access this share.

 Add OpenDXM with the user name “de\dxm” as a “Member” of your share (see screenshot below):


Select “location”: Fe or Si (for better performance)

Finally, submit the request. As a next step, the MoR (Master of Role, usually your manager) has to approve this request.

Some Business units might have their own requesting processes:

e.g. ED, AE, CP,.. use "easy2order": https://rb-easy2order.bosch.com/

Please note: In the case, you request for an NFS share via other services, you have to ensure that the service user “de\dxm” gets change permissions (read, write, create, delete) on this share.”


Background information: Why do you need an NFS share? 

NFS share is a multiprotocol share, that means two different operating systems (UNIX and Windows) can have access to the share.

This is required due to the following reasons:

  • The OpenDXM service runs under the operating system UNIX

  • The customer's operating system is mainly Windows based.


If you want to use an existing multiprotocol share, please notify us of the share name.


Instructions on how to verify that your share is an NFS share:

  • Click with the right mouse button on your share.


  • Select "CI File Service" and then "Share Management"


  • Select "File Share Info":


  • If the tab "Unix" exists, it means that your share is an NFS share:

In the tab "Unix", you can find further information on your NFS share (version, automounter path...).



Another method to check your file share is this tool: https://www.intranet.bosch.com/app/fileservice/cihotlinehelper/#/Access-Rights-Checker



Step 2:  Request for OpenDXM Batch User (your automated data exchange user)

Please use this E-Mail Template to send your registration request to the OpenDXM team.

Based on your request, the OpenDXM team will initiate an approval workflow via Work-On.

How to create a distribution list

If several colleagues should be notified of incoming (received) data, please create an email distribution list.

To do this, please contact IT Service Desk at +49(711)811-3311.

This distribution list can be used by OpenDXM as a recipient email address.

Step 3: Configuration of the NFS share

After your NFS share has been created and the service user “de\dxm”  has "change permission" on this share:


Step 1: You have to create the folders in (for incoming data) and out (for outgoing data) in your share. (see pics below)


Step 2: In the folder "out", you have to create subfolders:

  1. Option:  Create subfolders with the same name as the email addresses of the business partners to whom your files will be sent automatically. (see example below)
  2. Option:  If you have different projects or departments  that use the automated file transfer via this share, you can create folders for each project or department.
    Finally in each folder, you can create subfolders with the same name as the email addresses of the business partners to whom your files will be sent automatically. (see example below)

    Please note: Your business partners have no access to your share!


Testing the automated transfer

You can use the following test users to test the automated transfer:

dxm.test-receiver@bosch.com

dxm.test-receiver2@bosch.com


In the folder "in", you will be receiving the files automatically from any business partner, sending data to your batch user.

You don't need to create any subfolders in the folder in.

Subfolders will be created automatically, when receiving data from you business partners.


Please note that the automated transfer does not support subdirectories. (e.g. out/regine.regenschirm@firma.com/folder1 → NOT supported)
Solution: You could zip the contents of the directory  (e.g. out/regine.regenschirm@firma.com/folder1.zip → supported)


Step 4: How the Automated Transfer works

  1. Make sure you have created an output-folder "out" in your NFS share (see here for further details)

  2. First you have to copy your files (e.g. test1.zip, test2.xls ) to appropriate subfolders of the folder "out" either manually or automated. 

    Please note:

    • Folders and subfolders cannot be processed and an error occurs! If you need to send a folder with multiple files or with subfolders, you have to compress the folder into a ZIP file (using e.g. 7-Zip).
    • If you need to send multiple files, we recommend that you compress the files into a zipped file for easier sending.
    • Single file sizes up to 20GB are supported.
    • We do not support sending more than hundreds of single files within a day 
      In this case, you have to zip your files before copying them to the file share for transfer.
    • If you are not able to compress your files into a ZIP file, ask the OpenDXM Team to configure an automatic zip file creation for your copied files.
      In this case, an OpenDXM process compresses your files into a ZIP file before transfer.

  3. It has to be ensured, that the files are processed by OpenDXM only, if they are fully copied to the file share (otherwise, specially in case of bigger files, this would lead to corrupt files.)


    For this, one of the following two options has to be implemented by you: (Please consult the OpenDXM team regarding this.)
    a. (Preferred solution) OpenDXM checks again and again if the file size and time stamp changes. X seconds (X is configurable) after the file size and time stamp stops changing, the files are sent to the intended recipient.
    In this case, no action is required by the user.

    b. For each file, you have to create a trigger file (zero byte file, add .rdy to the end of the filename) of the same name (e.g. "test1.zip.rdy", test2.xls.rdy ), which indicates the end of the copying process. (see pic below)
    This sequence is important, otherwise OpenDXM won't process the file(s).



  4. OpenDXM automatically sends the files to your business partner(s) whose email address is the name of the subfolders in "out" (e.g. to "test.partner@receiver.com", in case you have copied files to "out/test.partner@receiver.com/").

  5. If OpenDXM is able to successfully process your files, the files will be deleted on the share by OpenDXM automatically.
    Otherwise (in case of errors):
    • OpenDXM does not delete files it could not process.
    • Additionally, OpenDXM creates an "error-file" for each affected file.
      As an example:
      • File "test.zip" could not be processed by OpenDXM. OpenDXM create an error-file "test.zip.error".
      • As long as the file "test.zip.error" exists, "test.zip" won't be processed by OpenDXM any more.
      • You have to check, why OpenDXM could not process affected files. The most common reason is that the business partner is not registered in OpenDXM (yet). In order to register the external business partner in OpenDXM, refer to the docupedia page here.
      • As soon as the issue is ressolved, delete the error-files, to trigger OpenDXM to process the file(s) again.
          
  6. Your business partner(s) are automatically notified by email that data is available to be downloaded via their OpenDXM account.

  7. Finally, your business partner(s) download the files via their OpenDXM account.

    Please note: Your business partners have no access to your share!


File name conventions


  1. Do not use any special characters and german umlauts.

  2. Do not use any whitespaces.

  3. Do not use any file names within a subfolder that differ only in upper and lower case.

Explanation:
OpenDXM runs on a UNIX based operating system which is case sensitive.
E.g.  The following file names are 3 different files under UNIX:
Test.txt
test.txt
TEST.txt


Windows does not distinguish between upper and lower case.

In automated transfer, we have a common file share that OpenDXM accesses from UNIX and the user accesses from Windows.

If UNIX creates two files that differ only in upper and lower case, in Windows we will see a file with a tilde in the file name.
E.g. Solaris creates:
Test.txt
TEST.txt

In Windows, you will see:
Test.txt
TEST~1 (max. 6 characters + tilde + number)

  1. Make sure you have created the folder in in your NFS share (see here for further details)

  2. Your business partner(s) send files to your (batch) user via their OpenDXM account

  3. The received files will be stored automatically on your NFS share, in the folder "in", where subfolders will be created automatically.
    The name of these subfolders is the sender's email address.

    If the received files are very large, the copying process may take longer.
    To prevent the files from being further processed while they are still being copied on the folder, OpenDXM creates "trigger" files (file ending: .rdy) for each file once the copy process is completed. This indicates the end of the file copy.
    Trigger files have the same names as the source files, but in additional .rdy as file ending (e.g. source file: test.txt ; Trigger file: test.txt.rdy)
    Please make sure to process the received files only after the corresponding rdy file has been created.

  4. The files are now available on you NFS share for further processing

    a. Please make sure that the file names of the received files are unique. Otherwise you run the risk that a later file will overwrite an earlier one with the same filename.
    To do this,  we recommend that your business partner (sender) create unique file names using a date/time stamp as part of the filename (YYYYmmddHHMMSS).  

    b. We do not delete any files on your share - you are the master of the data and thus it is your own responsibility to delete files when you no longer need them.

page_name: Power BI - SAP BW driver instructions
html_content:
Power BI - SAP BW driver instructions

All information is to best knowledge. If you find any errors or better ways to use the driver, feel free to let me know!

Thank you for your feedback


Also, be aware that a connection to SAP BW is only possible on your local computer - reports containing connections to SAP BW can NOT be published and made available on the Power BI Report Server.


Access to SAP BW via Power BI is NOT supported by CI - for supported connectivity to BW use the preferred tools by SAP. All usage of the Power BI SAP BW connector on your own risk.


General Information

Please contact/inform the Product-Owner ("Herr der Daten") and the CI Capability Consultant in case you would like to use BW data from the specific BW system and BW application via MS Power BI


Prerequisites

To connect from Power BI Desktop to SAP BW, the following prerequisites have to be fulfilled:

  • Installation of latest Power BI Desktop software (>= August 2018 version) from SCCM
  • Installation of Power BI SAP BW driver package from SCCM
  • Access rights to SAP BW system you want to connect to
  • BEx-query is configured for external access (see "Configuring BEx query for external access" )

Support for SAP BW features

The following table lists all SAP BW features that are not fully supported, or will behave differently when using Power BI.

Read the following list thoroughly - the interface provided by SAP comes with these limitations. There is no possibility for external tools like Power BI to overcome these limitations.

FeatureDescription
Local calculationsLocal calculations defined in a BEx Query will change the numbers as displayed through tools like BEx Analyzer. However, they are not reflected in the numbers returned from SAP, through the public MDX interface.
As such, the numbers seen in a Power BI visual will not necessarily match those for a corresponding visual in an SAP tool.
  For example, when connecting to a query cube from a BEx query that sets the aggregation to be Cumulated (i.e. running sum), Power BI would get back the base numbers, ignoring that setting.  An analyst could certainly then apply a running sum calculation locally in Power BI, but would need to exercise caution in how the numbers are interpreted if this is not done.
AggregationsIn some cases (particularly when dealing with multiple currencies), the aggregate numbers returned by the SAP public interface do not match those shown by SAP tools.
As such, the numbers seen in a Power BI visual will not necessarily match those for a corresponding visual in an SAP tool.
For example, totals over different currencies would show as  "*" in BEx Analyzer, but the total would get returned by the SAP public interface, without any information that such an aggregate number is meaningless. Thus the number (aggregating, say, $, EUR, and AUD) would get displayed by Power BI.
Currency formattingAny currency formatting (for example, $2,300 or 4000 AUD) is not reflected in Power BI.
Units of measureUnits of measure (for example, 230 KG) are not reflected in Power BI.
Key versus text (short, medium, long)For an SAP BW characteristic like CostCenter, the field list will show a single column Cost Center.  Using that column will display the default text.  By showing hidden fields, it will also be possible to see the unique name column (that returns the unique name assigned by SAP BW, and is the basis of uniqueness).
  The key and other text fields are not available.
Multiple hierarchies of a characteristicIn SAP, a characteristic can have multiple hierarchies. Then in tools like BEx Analyzer, when a characteristic is included in a query, the user can select the hierarchy to use.
In Power BI, the various hierarchies can be seen in the field list as different hierarchies on the same dimension.  However, selecting multiple levels from two different hierarchies on the same dimension will result in empty data being returned by SAP.
Treatment of ragged hierarchies
Scaling factor/reverse signIn SAP, a key figure can have a scaling factor (for example, 1000) defined as a formatting option, meaning that all display will be scaled by that factor.
It can similarly have a property set that reverses the sign. Use of such a key figure in Power BI (in a visual, or as part of a calculation) will result in the unscaled number being used (and the sign is not reversed). The underlying scaling factor is not available. In Power BI visuals, the scale units shown on the axis (K,M,B) can be controlled as part of the visual formatting.
Hierarchies where levels appear/disappear dynamicallyInitially when connecting to SAP BW, the information on the levels of a hierarchy will be retrieved, resulting in a set of fields in the field list. This is cached, and if the set of levels changes, then the set of fields do not change until Refresh is invoked.
This is only possible in Power BI Desktop. Such Refresh to reflect changes to the levels cannot be invoked in the Power BI service after Publish.
Default filterA BEx query can include Default Filters, which will be applied automatically by SAP BEx Analyzer. These are not exposed, and hence the equivalent usage in Power BI will not apply the same filters by default.
Hidden Key figuresA BEx query can control visibility of Key Figures, and those that are hidden will not appear in SAP BEx Analyzer. This is not reflected through the public API, and hence such hidden key figures will still appear in the field list. However, they can then be hidden within Power BI.
Numeric formattingAny numeric formatting (number of decimal positions, decimal point, etc.) will not automatically be reflected in Power BI. However, it is possible to then control such formatting within Power BI.
Hierarchy versioningSAP BW allows different versions of a hierarchy to be maintained, for example, the cost center hierarchy in 2007 versus 2008. Only the latest version will be available in Power BI, as information on versions is not exposed by the public API.
Time dependent hierarchiesWhen using Power BI, time dependent hierarchies are evaluated at the current date.
Currency conversionSAP BW supports currency conversion, based on rates held in the cube. Such capabilities are not exposed by the public API, and are therefore not available in Power BI.
Sort OrderThe sort order (by Text, or by Key) for a characteristic can be defined in SAP. This sort order is not reflected in Power BI. For example, months might appear as “April”, “Aug”, and so on.
It is not possible to change this sort order in Power BI.
Technical namesIn Get Data, the characteristic/measure names (descriptions) and technical names can both be seen. The field list will contain just the characteristic/measure names (descriptions).
AttributesIt is not possible to access the attributes of a characteristic within Power BI.
End user language settingThe locale used to connect to SAP BW is set as part of the connection details, and does not reflect the locale of the final report consumer.
Text VariablesSAP BW allows field names to contain placeholders for variables (for example, "$YEAR$ Actuals") that would then get replaced by the selected value. For example, the field appears as "2016 Actuals" in BEx tools, if the year 2016 were selected for the variable.
The column name in Power BI will not be changed depending on the variable value, and therefore would appear as "$YEAR$ Actuals".  However, the column name can then be changed in Power BI.
Customer Exit VariablesCustomer Exit variables are not exposed by the public API, and are therefore not supported by Power BI.
Characteristic StructuresAny Characteristic structures in the underlying SAP BW source will result in an ‘explosion’ of measures being exposed in Power BI. Deletion concept

As we want to keep the platform up to date and not as an archive for any kind of media, the following deletion concept was introduced:

Not published content (status: "Private"):

  • the owner will be informed via E-mail about content, which has not been published for 90 days
  • an additional E-mail to remind the owner will be sent another 30 days later
  • 5 days later the content will be deleted

Published content (status: "Published" or "Unlisted):

  • the Owner will be informed via E-mail about content, which has not been viewed for 360 days
  • an additional E-mail to remind the owner will be sent another 30 days later
  • 5 days later the content will be deleted

Avoid deletion of entries

To avoid the deletion of the entries listed in the E-Mail (subject: Inactivity of [private | published or unlisted] media content), please open the entries one by one and play them once. There is no need to play back the whole video, ~30 sec. are enough.
This play action will reset the deletion counter for another year (published/unlisted) or 90 days (private).

The process prescribes that a video/channel owner must transfer the entries to another employee before changing or leaving the company!

The most common use case is when interns or working students with a temporary employment contract generate video(s) or channel(s) on Bosch Tube and do not transfer them to permanent employees beforehand.
Before changing departments or leaving the company, the video/channel owner must therefore transfer their video(s) or channel(s) to another employee in the video/channel settings if they should remain on Bosch Tube.

  • For channels, it is advisable to enter several channel managers at the same time, as one of the channel managers still available with the corresponding authorisation can remove the user as a channel manager in Bosch Tube who is no longer available in the Active Directory.
  • For videos please create a ticket following the default support process via IT Service Desk if you have more than 10 entries that needs to be changed.
    We must check whether the video(s) are from the same team or department and can only make the desired changes in the back end if the videos are associated with the requester and we are not allowed to make exceptions!

Since only the video owner has the ownership rights for his/her video(s), we are obliged to irrevocably delete the video(s) without owner from the Bosch Tube video platform after a certain period of time due to General Data Protection Regulations!
