Important folder backup (Desktop, Documents, Pictures)

When introducing OneDrive at Bosch it was possible to configure your important folders (Desktop, Documents, Pictures) for synchronization with OneDrive (see screenshot).
The pop-up below was a standard message from Microsoft, not from CI! It gave misleading information especially when strictly confidential data was involved.

API Overview




What is Planner?

Planner is a lightweight task management tool that makes it easier for teams to schedule tasks, and see visibility of where tasks are. Some possibilities with Planner:

  • Create buckets for your tasks to organize them better

  • Label the tasks with custom labels

  • Assign tasks to anyone you've added to a Plan

  • Attach files to a task

  • View out-of-the-box charts on different KPIs for your Plan


When should I use Planner?

Below is a quick picture view of Microsoft task management products. If you are wanting to provide some basic task management for your team, then Planner is the right option. If the scope of who you want to provide task management for grows, then Project Online would be the best tool. For individual task management, ToDo offers the best option here.


How do I create a new plan?

Once you have a team created, you can add a Planner plan to your team. There are two ways you can do this:

  1. In your Teams client application, open your Team and click the "+" icon for your teams tabs. In the list of available apps to add, choose "Planner". From here, you can choose to add an already existing plan as tab, or you can create a new plan.



  2. The other option for creating a plan is to navigate to the Planner Web Application. From here, you can click on "New plan". Give the plan a name, then choose what team to add the plan to.

API Overview



Where can I find the Planner Web App?

 https://tasks.office.com


Can a plan be created in a private channel?

It is not currently possible to create a new plan within a private channel inside of Teams. This is due to how the private channels are set up when they are created, and that they have unique permissions behind that are not tied to the group permissions.


Why do I get the error message "Plan failed to create" when creating a new plan?

When you first had a new team created for Teams, it is possible that your user was not placed into both the Members and Owners group. In order to create plans, you must be a part of both groups. To fix the issue, follow these steps:

  1. Have a second owner of the team completely remove you as an Owner in the team. 
  2. Have the second owner add you back into the team as owner.
  3. You should be able to create a new plan inside of Teams now.


How can I copy a plan?

You can copy a plan in Planner by navigating to the web app for the plan you want to copy. From here you can open the "..." to find additional options of the plan, then you can select "Copy plan".

Once you select "Copy plan", you will be shown a popup to choose a name for the new plan, where the plan should be copied, and what you want to copy.

Copying a plan in Microsoft Teams

You must be in the web version of Planner in order to copy a plan. If you add a new Planner tab to your Teams channel, and choose "Use an existing plan from this team", this DOES NOT create a copy of the plan you choose.


How can I rename a plan?

To rename a plan, you will need to navigate to the web application version of Planner. Once you open your plan in the web application, you can click the ". . ." for the additional options for your plan. Then you can click "Plan settings, and update the name of the plan.

Renaming a plan in Microsoft Teams

You must be in the web version of Planner in order to rename a plan. If you try to rename the plan through Microsoft Teams by using the method pictured below, this will ONLY rename the tab in Microsoft Teams and does not affect the plan at all.



Why can't I create a plan for my personal tasks?

You may run into an issue when trying to create a new plan that is not tied to an existing team:

In this case, the plan was not actually created. This error occurs because O365 group creation is turned off for the Bosch tenant, and the message Microsoft displays is that "you no longer have access". Plans must be created with an already existing group behind it. To create a new group, you need to create a new team, which can be ordered through the IT Service Portal.


I accidentally left a plan and cannot create any new plans. How do I solve this?

When you leave a plan, this is the same thing as leaving the Members group of your team. If you were previously an owner in the team, you'll need to fix the issue by:

  1. Have a second owner of the team completely remove you as an Owner in the team. 
  2. Have the second owner add you back into the team as owner.
  3. You should be able to create a new plan inside of Teams now.

If you were previously a member of the team, you will need to contact the Owner of the team and have them add you back in as a member to the team.


What are the different ways I can access Planner?

Planner is accessible in the following ways:

  1. A Teams plugin
  2. A web application, which can be found here
  3. An iOS application, which can be downloaded from the company portal on your Bosch managed device 


How do I copy a link to a Planner task?

There is currently a known issue with a copying a link to a task when trying to perform this action within the Planner app inside of Teams. You'll need to navigate to the Planner web application in order to copy a link to task. See the below image to find where in the


Why can I not see my Outlook tasks in Planner?

Planner does not roll up all of your Microsoft 365 tasks into one view. If you want to see all your tasks across Microsoft 365 in one place, then you will need to use the Microsoft Todo application. Microsoft Todo will show you all of your Planner tasks, your Outlook tasks, your Microsoft Todo tasks, and any emails that you flagged as to-dos.


Why does the Planner application in Teams disappear when I navigate somewhere else in Teams?

If the Planner app is disappearing from your left hand navigation in Microsoft Teams, that means you haven't yet pinned it as an app there. To do so, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Planner app in Teams
  2. Right click the Planner app icon in the left hand navigation
  3. Choose "Pin".

Now the Planner app will not disappear when you go navigate away from it.


Can additional fields be created for a plan?

It is not currently possible to add more fields to a plan. 


What are the additional options in Planner web application?

When you view one of your plans in the Planner web application, you have some additional links when compared to the mobile or Teams add-in. You can access these additional links by clicking the "..." after opening a plan.

Conversation - This will take you to the Exchange mailbox where the task comments have been stored.

Members - This will take you to the group settings.

Files - This takes you directly to the SharePoint document library that stores all the attached files for tasks

Notebook - This takes you to the OneNote Notebook for your group.

Sites - This takes you directly to the SharePoint sites home page for you group.

Add to favorites - Add this plan to your favorites. Favorited plans show up first in the Planner Hub

Copy plan - Create a new plan from an existing one. Take notice of will/won't be copied by going here

Export plan to Excel - Export the tasks in your plan into an excel file.

Copy link to plan - Get a direct link to the plan

Plan settings - Owners of the plan have the ability to change some settings with the plan such as the plan title and the group notifications.


How do permissions in Planner work?

There are 3 permission levels in Planner: Owners, Members, and Guests. Owners and members are the same owners and members from the team in Teams that the plan was created from. There are a few differences in what owners and members can do. For a list of the different permissions, you can navigate to Owners vs. Members vs. Guests.


What kinds of notifications are available for Planner?

Planner has multiple types of notifications. Some can be switched off, but some are always there. More details can be found on Microsoft's Planner Notification Page.

To change your personal notifications, open up Planner and click the gear icon in the top right, then click "Notifications".

A popup will appear for you to change your personal notifications. The available notification settings are shown in the following picture:

You can also change notification options for a whole plan if you are an owner of the plan. To do so, open the plan, click the additional options "...", then select "Plan Settings".

A popup will appear, and here's where you can choose to send notifications to the group or not.

There is no way to turn off comment notifications at this time.



How can I move/copy a plan to another plan?

When you open your plan, you can click the "additional options" next to the task. From there you can choose to copy the task, or to move the task.

Move = remove the original task and move it to the other plan

Copy = Keeps the original task and also moves it to the other plan


What is the grid view in Planner Web Portal?

On the Planner Web Portal - https://tasks.office.com, through the new Grid view, the users can view more tasks on the screen and more easily to compare task metadata.

It has little difference comparing to the List view on the Planner in Teams. The List has "All Active" and "Completed" views, but Grid lists all Tasks.

You can select multiple tasks (Planner in Teams) in List and change the assignment, bucket, dates, and other settings. For Grid, you can only mark selected tasks for completing / reactivating in the Planner web portal.

Grid ViewList View


What are the Roster Plan (Planner without M365 group) authorization updates?

If you have a OneDrive or SharePoint Online file linked to your Roster Plan, the user with access to the file will automatically get access to the Roster Plan without adding the user to the Roster container.

Recording


🔎 TIP: Use Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site..


The most important points first


  • Legal constraints: Please be aware that Corporate Directive CD 05614 applies and must be respected whenever you record pictures or videos, no matter which tool you use. Please make sure you have understood and implemented the Central Directive CD 05614: Image rights: copyrights and personality rights for your use case. You may want to use the templates (EN / DE) provided in the appendix of CD 05614. Please note that it is in your responsibility to handle recordings according to CD 05614.

NOTE When using Teams the consent will be collected within the feature described in the section "How to start recording" here.

  • Workers council: Alongside workers council agreement KBV 10.14 (for Germany), a protocol notice got published specifically on the subject of recording online meetings. In this notice, you can find more details about the circumstances under which it is allowed to use recording.
    • The German version can be found here.
    • A translation to English can be found here.
  • Storage: Recorded videos must not be stored locally on the PC, on file shares or SharePoint shares or in MS Teams (it will be deleted after 2 years). To ensure that the recordings are stored in a GDPR-compliant way and to save bandwidth and storage, always use Bosch Tube to store and distribute the video.




General


NOTE Please go to the old IdM (not oneIDM) to apply for the recording role! This role is not yet available in oneIDM.

Question

Answer

General prerequisites

 Please note the general prerequisites:

  • Prerequisite is a special IdM role: With the role SKYPE4B_RECORDING, you can record also with Microsoft Teams.
  • The recording permissions are granted per user, not per meeting. 
  • Even if a user has the SKYPE4B_RECORDING permissions, he/she cannot wildly record any meeting out there, but only record meetings for which the meeting organizer (or co-organizer) has SKYPE4B_RECORDING permissions as well.
  • For the recording, organizer can customize whether to record audio, video, chat or desktop sharing.
  • The recording will be produced after the meeting ended.
    • In Microsoft Teams, the recording is saved in the organizer's OneDrive by default.

NOTE Even if the recording is stored on the organizer's OneDrive, the co-organizer also has permission to edit it (if such a person was indicated in the meeting options by the organizer).

How to order the recording IdM role

To request the role SKYPE4B_RECORDING for the first time, continue below:

  1. Go to the IdM portal >> Click "Stay in IdM"!
  2. Click on User Self Service
  3. Click on Skype / Teams
  4. Click on Find access rights
  5. Insert SKYPE4B_RECORDING
  6. Request the role


Applying for the role will
require manager approval.
Please note that the role
requires annual re-approvals.

Is a consent for recording obligatory?

Yes if you want to fully participate in the meeting. Each participant will see the banner containing consent to recording, which must confirm:

NOTE After confirmation all participants will be muted and their cameras will be disabled, so they have to unmute and turn their cameras on manually.

An organizer will see the following banner:

NOTE Consent policy doesn`t apply to ad hoc calls, but only to scheduled meetings. 

Where is recording stored?

The meeting is recorded and saved in the cloud.

Storage location for standard meeting is the OneDrive of the meeting organizer.

HINT Even if the recording is stored on the organizer's OneDrive, the co-organizer also has permission to edit or download it (if such a person was indicated in the meeting options by the organizer).


Storage location of channel meetings is the SharePoint Online side of the corresponding team room.

Is it allowed to record SC3 meetings?

No, this is not allowed. For further details, please have a look here:

  • Microsoft Teams: Strictly Confidential Meetings




Recording Instructions


Question

Answer

How to record a meeting in Teams
  1. Click on the three dots in the meeting
  2. Click on Start recording
  3. A pop up regarding the agreement and a link to Privacy Policy appear.
  4. By pressing “Continue” the meeting recording starts – all participants get muted, with their cameras and content-share off. 

NOTE It might take a couple of seconds until the recording starts.

   5. All users will be automatically informed about the start of the recording with the link to the Privacy Policy. When they decide to unmute, turn on their camera, or share content, they will see another pop up on their screen if they agree to be recorded. If the participants respond “No” to the prompt, they have a view-only meeting experience.

Each participant approval or rejection is recorded in the attendance report of the Microsoft Teams meeting.

NOTE We highly recommend choosing the automatic recording option for the meeting invitation. You can find it in the Meeting options – Record automatically. Note, that the first person who starts the meeting becomes the owner of the recording automatically and this cannot be changed for now.

  1. Click on the three dots in the meeting
  2. Click on Stop recording
  3. Confirm the pop-up window

Storage location

The meeting is recorded and saved in the cloud.

Storage location for standard meeting is the OneDrive of the meeting organizer.
Storage location of channel meetings is the SharePoint Online side of the corresponding team room.


Access the recording

While the recording is being processed you can exit the meeting. When your recording has been processed, you can access it in the meeting chat or meeting`s organizer OneDrive (if you weren`t in this role).
Viewing / accessing the recording of a channel meeting is possible for every member of the corresponding team room.

You can restrict the viewing / access of others by:

  1. Go to your OneDrive
  2. Click on the folder Recordings
  3. Select a recording and click on the three dots > Manage access
  4. Click on Stop sharing

The download of the recording is only possible for the recording person. To do that:

  1. Click on three dots on your recording file →  Open in Stream

   2. In Stream click also on three dots → Download

If you download the file, you can add it to BoschTube: 

  • uploading video to BoschTube
  • publishing video in different channels

 

How to exclude the chat window from the recording

In Teams the chat window is automatically excluded.

Aktualisierung März 2021:

Mit der Version SAC2008, die seit Mitte März verteilt wird, wurde Office 365 Pro Plus umbenannt in Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise.

Grundlagen

Was ist Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise?

Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise ist bei Bosch die Nachfolgerversion von Office 2016.
Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise ist immer noch eine lokal installierte Software (nicht im Web), die die bekannten Office-Anwendungen enthält: Access, Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint, Publisher, Skype for Business und Word.

Was ist der Unterschied zwischen Microsoft 365 und Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise?

Microsoft 365 ist der vollständige Office-Arbeitsplatz von Microsoft mit zahlreichen Anwendungen (z.B. Teams) und Services.
Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise ist ein Teil dieses Arbeitsplatzes.

Was ist der Unterschied zwischen Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise und Office 2016?

Microsoft 365 Apps for EnterpriseOffice 2016

Durch regelmäßige Aktualisierungen (zweimal jährlich) immer aktuell,
deshalb enthält die Bezeichnung auch keine Jahreszahl.

Hat seit der Veröffentlichung keine zusätzlichen Funktionen erhalten

Lizenz muss im Internet aktiviert werden

Lizenz wird innerhalb Bosch aktiviert

64-Bit32-Bit

Kann ich Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise und Office 2016 auf demselben PC installieren?

Nein. Die beiden Office-Versionen verwenden sowohl unterschiedliche Installationstechniken ("msi" vs. "click to run (c2r)"), als auch unterschiedliche Architekturen (64-Bit vs. 32-Bit), die nicht zusammen auf denselben PC passen. Wenn Sie von Office 2016 auf Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise aktualisieren, wird zunächst Office 2016 deinstalliert und dann Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise installiert.

Wie geht es mit Office 2016 weiter?

Allgemeine Informationen zu OneNote-Notizbüchern

OneNote ist ein elektronisches Notizbuch und soll Sie in dieser Eigenschaft, z.B. beim Vorbereiten von Besprechungen, bei der Informationsrecherche oder beim Sammeln von Ideen unterstützen. Bitte beachten Sie, dass OneNote kein Massenspeicher und kein geeigneter Speicherplatz für geschäftsrelevante Daten ist.

Aufbau von OneNote

OneNote besteht aus Notizbüchern. Diese Notizbücher bestehen aus Abschnitten und innerhalb der Abschnitte  speichern die verschiedenen Seiten die Informationen.

Diese Struktur ist wichtig , da es Eigenschaften gibt, die mit bestimmten Teilen des Notizbuchs verknüpft sind. Beispielsweise ist es möglich, nur eine Seite eines Notizbuchs zu erstellen. Sie können dann Inhalte in diese Seite einfügen - sie enthält jedoch keinen Papierkorb oder Versionen der Seite.

Der Papierkorb gehört jeweils zu einem Notizbuch.

OneNote Beschränkungen

Bei der Nutzung von OneNote Notizbüchern auf dem Windows-PC und iOS-Endgerät sind maximale Werte zu beachten:
Microsoft empfiehlt eine maximale Größe eines Notizbuchs von 2 GB, ein Abschnitt sollte eine Größe von 300 MB nicht überschreiten.

Wenn ein Abschnitt die Größe von 200 MB übersteigt, sollte der Benutzer den Inhalt des Abschnitts in mehrere andere (kleinere und neu erstellte) Abschnitte aufteilen und alle nicht benötigten Daten entfernen

Wir empfehlen dringend, keine großen Dateien in einen Abschnitt zu kopieren, da die Inhalte an den Server gesendet werden müssen und beim Synchronisieren Proleme auftreten können.
Vom Einfügen von e-Mails in Notizbücher raten wir ab.

Unsere OneNote Best Practices und Empfehlungen:

  • Vermeiden Sie es, große Inhalte im selben Abschnitt zu führen, einschließlich Dateiausdrucke, Bilder und angehängte Dateien. Große Inhalte machen die Synchronisierung langsamer, da die Inhalte über das Internet gesendet und empfangen werden müssen. Nachfolgend finden Sie die Optionen zur Reduzierung großer Inhalte in einem Abschnitt:
    1. Anstatt Dateien einzuhängen, laden Sie sie an einen gemeinsamen Speicherort hoch (z. B. OneDrive oder OneDrive for Business) und fügen Sie einen Link zu ihnen hinzu
    2. Löschen Sie unnötige/veraltete Seiten mit großen Inhalten.
    3. Versuchen Sie, große Inhalte in mehrere Abschnitte aufzuteilen, anstatt sie in einen einzigen Abschnitt zu packen.
    4. Versuchen Sie, Inhalte auf verschiedene Notizbücher aufzuteilen. Legen Sie archivierte Notizen in verschiedenen Notizbüchern ab, auf die Sie nicht täglich zugreifen müssen. Halten Sie archivierte Notizbücher geschlossen. Sie können diese Notizbücher bei Bedarf jederzeit über die Option „Weitere Notizbücher“ wieder öffnen.
    5. Wenn es Inhalte gibt, auf die Sie weiterhin täglich zugreifen möchten, teilen Sie diese in verschiedene Abschnitte innerhalb desselben Notizbuchs auf.
  • Wenn das Notizbuch auf OneDrive gespeichert ist, von mehreren Nutzern an verschiedenen Standorten auf der ganzen Welt verwendet wird und die Seiten in der Regel gleichzeitig bearbeitet werden, kann es zu Konflikten kommen.
    Falls es einen Konflikt mit Änderungen gibt, die Sie gleichzeitig mit einem anderen Benutzer vornehmen, sollten Sie eine Nachricht erhalten, in der Sie die Version auswählen können, die Sie für die Cloud zusammenführen möchten. Wähle Sie in diesem Falls aus, welche endgültige Version der Seite aktualisiert werden soll.
  • Vergewissern Sie sich, dass das Notizbuch die Größe von 2 GB pro Datei nicht überschreitet, was die Grenze für die Synchronisierung von OneDrive/SharePoint-Dateien ist: Restrictions and limitations in OneDrive and SharePoint (microsoft.com)

  • Vermeiden Sie, dass die Abschnitte des Notizbuchs einen Inhalt von mehr als 300 MB haben; falls sie sich dieser Größe nähern, sollten Sie einen neuen Abschnitt erstellen.

  • Wenn die Notizbücher nach OneNote/SharePoint verschoben wurden, muss sichergestellt werden, dass diese Dateien ordnungsgemäß über die App verschoben werden, damit die korrekte Struktur der OneNote-Datei (Notizbuch) erhalten bleibt: OneNote syncing best practices (microsoft.com)
  • Falls ein Synchronisierungsproblem auftritt und Sie glauben, dass es eine Differenz zwischen Ihrer lokalen Kopie und der Cloud-Datei gibt, können Sie das Notizbuch im Browser öffnen und zwischen der lokalen und der Cloud- Datei vergleichen. Jeder Inhalt, der in der Browserkopie fehlt, fehlt auch allen Nutzern, die das betreffende Notizbuch mit dem OneNote-Client geöffnet haben. Um ein Notizbuch im Browser zu öffnen, klicken Sie einfach mit der rechten Maustaste auf das Notizbuch im Client -> klicken Sie auf "Link zum Notizbuch kopieren" -> fügen Sie den Link in den Notizblock ein und kopieren Sie die erste Zeile -> fügen Sie den Link in die Adressleiste des Browsers ein und drücken Sie die Eingabetaste. Falls dieser Link Sie nicht zum Notizbuch führt, könnte dies darauf hindeuten, dass das Notizbuch verschoben oder gelöscht wurde oder Sie nicht darauf zugreifen können (mögliche Kommunikations-, Authentifizierungs- oder Berechtigungsprobleme usw.).
    Durch erneutes Öffnen des Notizbuchs am Speicherort des Notizbuchs können Sie sicherstellen, dass Sie das aktuelle Notizbuch bearbeiten.  Dies kann mehrfache Synchronisierungsprobleme und andere Konflikte verhindern.  Vergleichen Sie den Inhalt in OneNote in der Desktop App mit der Online-Datei, indem Sie das Notizbuch im Browser öffnen und nach Unterschieden suchen.


Wichtige Hinweise zur Verwendung von OneNote

OneNote ist als Werkzeug zum schnellen Sammeln und Strukturieren von Informationen gedacht. Ein OneNote Notizbuch eignet sich weder als Ablagesystem noch als Dokumentationssystem. 

Geschäftskritische Daten dürfen nicht in einem OneNote Notizbuch gespeichert werden.

 Die meisten Synchronisationsprobleme resultieren aus dem falschen Einsatz von OneNote:

  • OneNote Notizbücher werden missbraucht und als Datei Ablage verwendet, d.h. es werden ganze Dateien in einem Notizbuch gespeichert

    Wir raten dringend davon ab, Dateien in einem Notizbuch zu speichern. Dies führt zu einer deutlichen Vergrößerung des Notebooks und kann dazu führen, 
    o    dass verschiedene Dateiversionen im Umlauf sind. 
    o    Das Notizbuch nicht fehlerfrei synchronisiert werden kann

    Wir empfehlen daher, Dateien in SharePoint zu speichern und in OneNote auf diese Dateien zu verlinken. Diese Dateien können über diesen Link schnell geöffnet und bearbeitet werden.

  • OneNote-Notizbücher werden auf Netzlaufwerken und nicht in einer SharePoint-Bibliothek abgelegt.
    OneNote-Notizbücher, die in einer SharePoint-Bibliothek gespeichert sind, sind weniger fehleranfällig, da OneNote für die Verwendung mit SharePoint optimiert wurde. 
    Für Änderungen muss z. B. jeweils nur der geänderte Teil des Notizbuchs synchronisiert werden. Das entlastet das Netzwerk und minimiert die Fehleranfälligkeit. 
    Es ist auch möglich, Synchronisationskonflikte aufzulösen. Ein weiterer Vorteil ist, dass Sie direkt in OneNote sehen können, wer für das Notizbuch berechtigt ist.

    Ein Anleitung zu Verschieben eine Notizbuchs finden Sie unter Notizbuch umziehen in der Office docupedia 


Häufig gestellte Fragen (FAQ)

Warum wird Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise nicht zur Installation angeboten?

Auch wenn das Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise-Paket bereits zugewiesen ist, kann es vorkommen, dass es auch nach einem oder mehreren Tagen nicht im Software Center des IT Workplace Toolkits zur Installation angeboten wird. Um dieses Problem zu umgehen, versuchen Sie bitte Folgendes:

  • Öffnen Sie das IT Workplace Toolkit über die Taskleiste
  • Wählen Sie "Softwareverteilung deaktivieren"

    und warten Sie die Bestätigung im Action Center ab
  • Danach aktivieren Sie die Softwareverteilung wieder
  • Das fehlende Software-Paket sollte nach einigen Minuten im Software Center zur Installation angeboten werden

Wie installiere ich Visio und Project?

Visio und Project 365 sind separat im IT Service Portal verfügbar (Auftrag "Request for Cloud Software License (except M365)"):

Wichtig

Wenn Sie von Office 2016 auf Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise aktualisieren, werden auch Visio 2016 und Project 2016 deinstalliert.

Neu: Wenn Sie Visio oder Project weiterhin benötigen, müssen Sie die entsprechende Lizenz beantragen.
Bei dem Antrag kann das dazugehörige Paket gleich mit zugewiesen und installiert werden.
Nachdem Ihr Antrag bearbeitet wurde und Sie Visio oder Project zum ersten Mal starten, kann es vorkommen, dass das Produkt scheinbar nicht aktiviert ist. Grund dafür ist, dass die eigentliche Lizenzvergabe bis zu 48 Stunden dauert.
Das ist aber kein Problem, denn Sie können 5 Tage lang ohne Einschränkung mit der Anwendung arbeiten ("Grace-Period"), bis die Lizenzaktivierung automatisch im Hintergrund erfolgt ist.

Sollte die Lizenz nicht innerhalb von 48 Stunden nach dem ersten Start der Visio- oder Project-Anwendung aktiviert worden sein, wenden Sie sich bitte an IT Service Desk.

Es gibt keine Unterscheidung mehr zwischen Standard- und Professional-Version – Es gibt pro Produkt eine Version.

Was tun, wenn meine Project/Visio-Lizenz verloren gegangen ist?

Ein Grund könnte sein, dass Sie Project/Visio zum ersten Mal installiert haben. Lesen Sie dazu bitte das obige Kapitel.

Der andere Grund könnte sein, dass Sie die Software seit über 90 Tagen nicht mehr benutzt haben. Dies ist Teil des Ratio-Prozesses, der die Lizenz frei gibt, um Kosten zu sparen.
Ihr Versuch, die Software erneut zu starten, löst die Neuvergabe Ihrer Lizenz aus. Dies geschieht normalerweise innerhalb von 48 Stunden. Das ist aber kein Problem, denn Sie können 5 Tage lang ohne Einschränkung mit der Anwendung arbeiten ("Grace-Period"), bis die Lizenzaktivierung automatisch im Hintergrund erfolgt ist.

Wenn Sie Probleme mit dem Testmodus haben, können Sie die Lizenz fast sofort aktivieren, indem Sie sie erneut über das ITSP-Bestellformular bestellen. Wenn der Auftrag bereits genehmigt wurde, ist keine neue Genehmigung erforderlich.

Sollte die Lizenz nicht innerhalb von 48 Stunden nach dem ersten Start der Visio- oder Project-Anwendung aktiviert worden sein, wenden Sie sich bitte an IT Service Desk.

Ich benutze Dateien, die Makros/VBA-Code enthalten. Kann es zu Problemen mit Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise kommen?

Ja und nein, es kommt darauf an.

Da wir nicht nur die Office-Version umstellen, sondern dabei von 32-Bit Office 2016 auf 64-Bit Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise umstellen, sollten Sie Ihre Dateien mit Makros/VBA-Code darin testen.
In einigen Fällen können Anpassungen der Makro/VBA-Programmierung notwendig sein, um auch in einer 64-Bit-Umgebung zu funktionieren.
Während die meisten Makros auch mit 64-Bit funktionieren sollten, gibt es einige Unterschiede, die Microsoft im folgenden Artikel beschreibt (Internetzugang erforderlich). Sie können z. B. das neue PtrSafe-Attribut mit einer Declare-Anweisung kombinieren und den LongPtr-Datentyp statt nur den Long-Datentyp verwenden.

Wie kann ich Unterstützung bei der Anpassung/Konvertierung von Makros erhalten?

Wenn Sie verantwortlich für ein Makro oder Add-In sind und Unterstützung für die Anpassungen/Konvertierung benötigen,
dann können Sie sich an Bosch Kollegen von SX/BSA wenden, die einen (kostenpflichtig) Komplettservice anbieten, der auch Codeänderungen/Programmierung enthält.
Einzelheiten zu den Ansprechpartnern und zur Vorgehensweise finden Sie hier.

Welche Office Add-Ins sind mit Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise verfügbar?

Derzeit sind nicht alle Office-Add-Ins in der 64-Bit-Version verfügbar, die die Kompatibilität mit Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise gewährleistet.
Bitte sehen Sie in der verlinkten Liste nach, um den Status Ihres Add-Ins zu überprüfen.

Wo wird sich mein Postfach unter Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise befinden?

Mit dem Release der Microsoft 365-Produkte erhalten Sie das gesamte Microsoft 365-Portfolio, das auch ein Exchange-Online-Postfach in der Cloud beinhaltet.

Wann werden neue Funktionen verfügbar sein?

Da es verschiedene Update-Kanäle gibt, werden neue Funktionen zuerst in frühen Update-Kanälen wie z. B. dem "Current Channel" veröffentlicht.
Wir bei Bosch verwenden den "Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel" als Update-Kanal. Dieser Update-Kanal erhält zweimal im Jahr Funktionsupdates in Q1 und Q3.
Wenn Sie also eine Funktion vermissen, die bereits in einem früheren Update-Kanal veröffentlicht wurde, erhalten wir sie in unserem "Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel" in Q1 oder Q3.

Beispiel: Wenn eine neue Funktion erstmals im Mai 2022 (Version 2205) im "Current Channel" eingeführt wurde, erhalten wir sie nicht direkt in Q3/2022, wenn die Version 2202 des "Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel" veröffentlicht wird, sondern wahrscheinlich in der Version 2208, die im ersten Quartal 2023 für den "Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel" veröffentlicht wird.

General Information

Scheduling Poll (formerly FindTime) is a feature integrated in Outlook, that makes it easier to schedule a meeting with external parties.

The use is useful if external recipients (from other companies) are involved, because you usually can not see the free / busy times in their calendars.
Please continue to create Bosch-internal meeting requests with the standard meeting requests in OWA or the Outlook Client, as the free / busy times are visible here.

Scheduling Poll is the built-in replacement for FindTime in Outlook. Scheduling Poll is available from Outlook version 2308 in the Outlook Client and in the Outlook Web App browser.

Why File Share documents can't be opened?

The app <Microsoft To Do> has no connection to any resources (File/Network Shares) within or outside the BOSCH network.

For this reason, a link to a file with a UNC path cannot be opened.


This applies to all <Microsoft To Do> - apps

  • which are opened in a browser inside the <Outlook on the Web> - App (OWA)
  • Windows Computers
  • MacBook
  • iOS iPhone
  • iOS iPad
  • Android devices


The <Microsoft To Do> app has a connection to the Outlook (Cloud Mailbox) via the logged-in user (e.g. UPN = usr1fe@bosch.com).

In the background, a link is established between <Microsoft To Do> and the task folder of the associated Outlook (Cloud Mailbox).

This connection synchronizes the tasks between Outlook and <Microsoft To Do>


Why does opening the links to documents on File/Network Shares only work on Windows Outlook installations?

  • Office and other programs for opening files are installed locally on the computer
  • Programs for the respective file extension are stored in the registry
  • The Windows computer is registered in the BOSCH network
  • The File/Network Share is connected to the computer or can be connected to the computer

Warum werden keine File Share Dateien geöffnet?

Die App <Microsoft To Do> hat keinerlei Verbindung zu Ressourcen (File/Network Shares) innerhalb oder außerhalb des BOSCH Netzwerkes.

Aus diesem Grund kann kein Link zu einer Datei mit einem UNC-Pfad geöffnet werden.

 

Dies gilt für alle <Microsoft To Do> - Apps

  • welche in einem Browser innerhalb der <Outlook on the Web> – App (OWA) geöffnet werden
  • Windows basierten Rechnern
  • MacBook
  • iOS iPhone
  • iOS iPad
  • Android-Geräten

 

Die <Microsoft To Do> - App hat nur eine Verbindung zur Outlook (Cloud Mailbox) und dem angemeldeten User (Bsp.: UPN = usr1fe@bosch.com).

Im Hintergrund wird eine Verbindung von <Microsoft To Do> zum Aufgaben-Ordner des dazu gehörenden Outlook -Postfachs in der Cloud aufgebaut.

Mit dieser Verbindung werden die Aufgaben zwischen Outlook und <Microsoft To Do> synchronisiert.

 

Warum funktioniert ein Aufruf der Links zu Dokumenten auf File/Network Shares nur auf Windows basierten Outlook – Installationen?

  • Office und weitere Programme zum Öffnen von Dateien sind lokal auf dem Rechner installiert
  • In der Registratur (Registry) sind Programme für die jeweilige Datei-Endung hinterlegt
  • Der Windows-basierte Rechner ist im BOSCH Netzwerk registriert
  • Das File/Network Share ist mit dem Rechner verbunden oder kann verbunden werden

Microsoft 365 Search


The Microsoft 365 Search is your key to the data stored in Microsoft 365 collaboration platform - files, people, sites, bookmarks, e-mails, Teams conversations and everything else - the only prerequisite is that you are authorized to see this data.

You can trigger the Microsoft 365 Search from different starting points and it will provide results matching the environment you are in at the moment - for details see our FAQ: What can be found where?

What is more, search results are tailored to you - they will take into account your previous activity in Microsoft 365 and content that’s trending in your organization. Consequently, even if you are using the same search term as your colleague, you will get the result suggestions that are relevant to you especially!


Please note:

The search functionality was previously called 'Office 365 Search'. However, Microsoft decided to rename their product, a path that Bosch has decided to follow in the spirit of the Evergreen approach. All functionalities have remained the same, only the name has changed!

Searching

The search on this page provides access to data stored in the cloud, provided that you have access:

  • Bookmarks
  • Documents

  • User profiles
  • News from SharePoint Online sites

  • People you are in connection with
  • SharePoint sites where you are a member



These are so-called 'zero intent queries' and they offer relevant information right away.  

When you start typing, the suggestions will be matched with what you have entered so far. If the data you are looking for is already contained in the list, you can simply click on it. Otherwise press 'Enter' to execute the search and you will get a list containing documents, folders, SharePoint sites, people, news (items published on the SharePoint Online team site)...

  • the file type of the result you are looking for

Searching for messages, files, users and apps across Microsoft Teams

The search functionality within Teams provides results for documents and messages stored in teams / conversations that the user has access to. Furthermore, you can find acronyms, bookmarks, users and available apps. When you click on the search window, your latest activities, including the search operations, will be provided, so you can simply repeat the action.

While you start typing your search term, there will already be suggestions with

  • People in your organization
  • Apps that are available to you
  • Teams and Channels where you are a member
  • Group chats (manually created or as a result from meetings) where you are a member
  • Commands that can be used in the search slot (you can get a list of available commands simply by typing '/')

You can use the filters below the search bar to directly limit the search to the type of result you are looking for. If the data you are looking for is already contained in the list, you can simply click on it. Otherwise press 'Enter' to execute the search (or click on the blue script at the bottom of the suggestions list).

Search results are presented as a list. There are several tabs:

  • All: Contains a list divided by headers with bookmarks, messages, files and people (sequence depends on where the most relevant search results are) → clicking on 'More ...' at the bottom of each segment will take you to the corresponding tab
  • Messages: Contributions that contain the search term; clicking on the search result will open the respective message in the channel / chat
  • People: A list of users that match the search term; clicking on the search result will allow you to start a new conversation or continue an existing one
  • Files: A list of files stored in your teams which match the search terms; clicking on the search result will open the file in a new browser tab
  • Group Chats: Chats (manually created or as a result from meetings) that have the search term in their title; clicking on the chat will open it in Teams
  • Teams and Channels: Teams and channels that have the search term as part of the name; clicking on the entry will take you to the team / channel

Results contained in the Messages and Files tabs can be filtered according to different criteria by using the filters at the top, e.g.  by limiting the results to a certain file type or team, by specifically choosing your @mentions or by defining how recent the results should be.

Clicking on any of the menu items on the left (e.g. Teams, Chat...) will return you to the standard Teams functionalities.

DOs and DON'Ts


  • Have a look at our training material: Learning Navigation
  • Add a clear description for each channel, team chat and group chat
  • Come up with a good structure of your team room
  • Set your status manually (e.g. available, away, do not disturb,…)
  • Pin / follow the channels important for you so that you are notified of all posts
  • Set Microsoft Teams as your Default Chat Application

  • Chose wisely, whether you need a team room or a group chat
  • Assign a subject to every conversation
  • Use the reply function to answer directly to a conversation
  • Save messages that are of high relevance to find them easier later
  • When adding people to your (serial) appointments, they will automatically be part of your persistent meeting chat. Please be aware, especially in serial appointments, that they will be able to read all further chats - see here.

  • Use the Announcements in a chat.
  • Use the  Important Announcement wisely. If used to often, people will not react to critical topics anymore.

  • Address team members directly with the @ mention
  • Choose wisely, whether you want to @ mention the whole team, channel, or an individual person.
  • Use tags to mention a certain group of people within a team

  • Make use of emoji to give direct feedback
  • Use the shortcuts Win + . to add emojis in a conversation

  • Type / in the upper search bar to get an overview of all /commands, e.g.

/whats new to get an overview of all new features within Teams
/chat to send a quick message to a person
/files to see your recent files
…and many more!

  • Download the Teams Mobile App for your mobile device

  • Don’t use in serious business communications emojis and giphys too often
  • Don’t use the @ mention for the whole team unless you really need to address everyone
  • Don’t participate in too many teams (considering efficiency, we recommend working in only ~5 teams)
  • Don’t use too many different channels (channels are the “tabs” within each team that cluster the Teams group)

  • Have a look at what you're allowed to upload, store and edit in Microsoft Teams.
    → Click here for more information.
  • Don't assume privacy: Newly added members can see prior discussions

  • Don’t copy and edit files on your local drive
    Instead, learn here how to work with Files

  • Don't give up too easily. Changing towards a new tool and working environment can be quite a change for you and your colleagues.
    Hang in there!

What is a channel?

A channel is similar to a folder in SharePoint or on a file share. With the help of different channels, a Team room can be clustered and organized according to topics.


How to create a channel

Click on the three dots next to your team. Then click on Add channel.

If you cannot create a channel, please contact the team room owner. The owner is able to restrict / allow the creation of channels by team members.


How to work with channels
  • Don't create too many channels in the beginning - keep it simple!
  • Only create a channel when you are sure you need it
  • Don't re-name a channel without informing your team members
  • Have one channel for fun-stuff to separate work and social stuff
  • Create one channel for "general" stuff, e.g. announcements, new topics, etc.
  • You can pin a channel - this way it's always visible on top: Click on the three dots next to the channel > click on Pin:

What is a Note tab

When creating new standard channels, you will see a Notes tab button in the top bar, which is powered by OneNote. 

It means that a new OneNote for this channel is created automatically. All members in a team will be able to access the content captured in Notes tab across all standard channels within that team by clicking on the Show navigation  icon on left.


NOTE If you accidentally removed Notes tab or you want to change the name of the OneNote tab in the older channels, follow this instruction:

  1. In Teams, go to the channel you want to add the Notes tab again.
  2. In the tabs bar across the top, select Add a tab  . The Add a tab window will open.
  3. Select the OneNote tile. The OneNote window will open.

Channel types


Channels are places where conversations happen and where the work actually gets done. So far we have been able to use two types of channels:

  • Standard channels - open to all team members in Teams and anything posted is searchable by others.

  • Shared channels - for collaborating with people inside and outside your team or organization*. Note, that this kind of channel is only needed in special collaboration scenarios – check out this use case.

What is a shared channel?

A shared channel can be created within a Team and comes with different pre-configured privacy advantages. You can add every user with Bosch ID (excluding ECI) of your organization to a shared channel and this user does not have to be part of the team the shared channel was created in. That allows you to use the shared channel as a collaboration tool without giving the user access to the whole team.


How does a shared channel work in general?

A user who is not part of the team, but added to shared channel of this team, will only be able to see the name of the team and the shared channel itself. He will not have access or even information of the remaining channels and file stores of the team. The shared channel will also get a dedicated SharePoint-site which also behaves just like the shared channel itself. He can collaborate with every user in this shared channel, but NOTE, that for now, that means only within the Bosch organization!


Working with Externals in shared channels:

Note, that there are two types of users for external collaboration at Bosch:

  1. External Standard Identity (ESI) - associates who have a Bosch address, e.g. max-smith@de.bosch.com (for example colleagues from BSH) and certified Bosch hardware. They are fully licensed and treated like normal Bosch users and can be added to shared channels.
  2. External Collaboration Identity (ECI) – associates from external companies without Bosch address and their own hardware. They cannot be added to shared channels! They can be added only to a private channel. So if you already work with such externals in any channel, just keep it as it is!

Adding external users outside of Bosch (ECI according to the above distinction) to a team or further collaboration scenarios are not supported yet, but such possibility is on the road map.


Why not just use private channel - use case

A shared channel helps to keep the number of created teams and the maintenance of these easier while offering you better way to collaborate across the borders of your core team. To give a better insight let’s look at the following USE CASE:


Bosch Sales Department wants to collaborate on a project with a few members of Bosch Marketing Department but have confidential content to discuss and work on internally with only the members of the Sales Department 1. At some point during the project, it is necessary to add a few members from an External Company to the project, but they shouldn’t have access on everything Sales Department and Marketing Department work on.


NOTE There is currently no way to directly add externals or externals with an ECI account to a shared channel in our environment. Only externals with a full External Standard Identity can be added.



 NOTE External Company has to have a Bosch ID! 

1st use case – working with standard and private channels:

Marketing Department isn`t able to join a Sales Department Team 1, because this team is private and confidential. In this case Sales Department creates Team 2, which doesn`t include their confidential information from Team 1.

If they want to start a collaboration with the External Company, they have to create Sales Department Team 3, because externals shouldn`t have an access to internal information from Team 2, which consists of Bosch Sales Department and Marketing Department. Such new Sales Department Team 3 provide private communication among internal and external members of this team through standard and private channels.


2nd use case – working with shared channels:

In this scenario only one team (Sales Department Team 1) is needed to provide communication between project members. Sales Department creates two shared channels: first for communication with Marketing Department and second for communication with both Marketing Department and External Company. Members of each shared channel can access only information stored in this particular channel.


How to create and work with a shared channel?

1. As an owner of a Team go to your team and add a channel

2. Set name and description and select Shared – People you choose from your org have access as a privacy setting

3. If you want to automatically include every member of the parent Team also select Share this channel with everyone on the team

4. Now chose every additional member you want to add to this channel → they will only have access to the shared channel and not to the team itself!

Changing settings and doing administrative tasks behave just like any other type of channel.


NOTE In theory it is possible to add users from different companies directly to a shared channel if the azure directories are allowed to communicate with each other. That means that you could go ahead and add “user@examplecompany.com” directly to your shared channel without the need of an External Standard Identity. A tenant switch wouldn’t have to be performed anymore. However, the current implementation at Bosch does not allow this feature (Azure B2B connect) due to ongoing security evaluations.


Further information
  • Shared channels can be recovered within 30 days after deletion
  • You can share the channel with another team directly to allow every user of the team access
  • Only direct members of the channel will have access to the files on the SharePoint site
  • For a list of supported apps in shared channels please refer to: Shared channels in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn  
  • For the shared channels members roles please refer to: Shared channel owner and member roles in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Support



Limitations
  • External Collaboration Identity (ECI) cannot be added to shared channel!
  • Bots, connectors and message extensions are not supported.
  • If every member of your team leaves the channel it will become ownerless. As long as users of your organization are left, one will automatically be promoted to be the new owner→ please be careful with external members to not give them ownership of the shared channel since the Bosch Standard External Identity is treated as a regular Bosch user.
  • The tabs Stream, Planner and Forms are not supported.
  • Max 200 shared channels in one team.
  • A shared channel can be shared with a maximum of 50 Teams.
  • Max 5000 members of a shared channel (one team counts as one member).
  • You can only have teams of up to 25 000 users (which would exclude some companies using the org-wide teams above this limit).



Private Channel


What is a private channel?

A private channel is a hidden channel within a team with restricted access. The owner of the private channel can select which team members are allowed to see the channel and its content.

Please note the below limitations first:

Limitations

Please check the Microsoft page.


When should I use a private channel?
  • The major benefit is that instead of creating multiple teams to work on your topics, you can only use one team and select whichever team member can access the content of the private channel. The private channel (like all channels in general) is aimed to be used for long-term communication and collaboration. If you only need to a quick clarification with some colleagues, create a group-chat with the relevant members for short-term communication. To better understand the different use cases, see difference between channel and group chat.
  • Please evaluate carefully, whether a private channel is needed in your case. We want to support the concept of open and transparent communication. Only use a private channel if the content is for dedicated users within the team and for long-term communication and collaboration.
  • There are several limitations to a private channel. Make sure you have read and understood what these mean to your use case.


Creation & Life Cycle
  • By default, only team room owners can create a private channel
  • The creation procedure is the same as creating a channel
  • Whoever creates the private channel is automatically the private channel owner
  • The private channel owner can add new private channel members and make them to private channel owners if needed
  • If a member leaves the team, he automatically leaves the private channel as well
  • You can create tabs and connectors in the private channel
  • A private channel aims at long-term oriented collaboration. See difference between channel and group chat
  • Deleting a private channel will delete the chat conversation and all files in the private channel
  • Restoring of a deleted private channel is possible within 30 days by team owners


Permissions
  • A member of a private channel needs to be a member of the team
  • Private channel owners and members can change the private channel name
  • The chat and the files in the private channel are stored in a dedicated workspace. Whoever is not owner/member of this private channel cannot access the content.

What is the difference between a team and a group chat in Teams?
Team roomGroup chat

A team is a workspace for collaboration and communication:
Everything is in one place:

  • Threaded (you can divide the chat room into conversations)
  • Chat based interaction with your group members. It is often used in departments or for a project with a long-term focus.
  • You can upload and work on files, which are automatically stored and updated in SharePoint online in the background.
  • Shared data will be stored on the SharePoint of the channel.
  • Visible for all members / owners.
  • A team can have up to 25 000 participants.

A group chat is more short-term oriented compared to a team.

  • Flat (only one interface)
  • You don´t need to order a group chat via the ITSP. You can easily create a group chat just with a few clicks in the Microsoft Teams client itself.
  • Short-term focus to discuss quick topics.
  • There is no permission structure in the group chat. Everyone has the same permissions and can leave the chat at anytime. Everyone can add new members or rename the group chat.
  • Shared data will be stored on the OneDrive of the user and automatically be shared with all chat-members. (Note, that if an user leaves the company, other chat members won`t have an access to his OneDrive anymore.)
  • Only visible for the people in the chat.
  • A group chat can have up to 250 participants.

Loop components in a chat


Loop components are for example paragraphs, tables or lists. Everyone in your chat will be able to edit it inline - and see changes instantly. It means meeting participants can also directly from the meeting window create agendas, take notes or assign tasks to colleagues.


How to send a loop component?
  1. Go to the box where you type a chat message. Select Insert loop components right beneath the box. 

 Tip: Make sure the box is empty - with no text in it - when you do this.

       2. Select the type of component you want to insert into your message.

      3. Enter content into the component and select Send . Everyone in the chat will be able to edit the content inline.

 Tip: @Mention people inside the component to show where you’d like them to contribute. They’ll get an activity feed notification that brings them right to the component.


NOTE You can add your loop component to your whiteboard. Check details here.

How to edit a loop component?

Simply click where you want to add or edit content and start typing.


 Tip: When editing, you can type / to insert things like an @mention, date, or even a component. If you want to comment on existing text vs edit it, type //. This will attribute the comment to you. 


View activity and access

If others are editing while you are viewing the component, you will see different colored cursors within the text and you’ll possibly see text being edited as well.

Avatars appear in the upper right corner to let you know who is viewing, editing, or has recently edited the component. Hover your cursor over any avatar for details.

Select See who has access    to understand who can view or edit the component. Avatars of people who have viewed the component at least once appear here, too.


How to share a loop component in another chat?
  1. Go to the upper right corner of the component and select Copy link.
  2. Switch to a different chat.
  3. Go to the box where you type a message and press Ctrl + V to paste your loop component into an empty chat.

Both, people in your original chat and in this additional chat will be able to edit the content. No matter where people are editing, the component will always show the latest updates.

Retentions

Retentions (automatic deletion times) will apply due to GDPR and ILM


What are retentions?

Retentions describe the time how long data is stored until it is (automatically) deleted. In the following, we are talking about chat and conversation retentions in Microsoft Teams. 


Which chats / conversations are affected by retentions?

Structured and unstructured chats will be deleted two years after they were initially created.


#1 Types of chats… 

  • Structured chats are used in team rooms.
  • Unstructured are used in 1:1 chats, calendar meeting chats or ad hoc group chats.


#2 Deleted are… 

  • Deleted are pictures, links, and all text / writing that were created longer than retention time


  • Not deleted are all other parts like files, planner tasks, Whiteboard, etc.
    They are stored on the SharePoint Online     of your team room or your personal OneDrive:


  • Hint: The function  will not save the message for longer than the above-mentioned times. 


Once the message is deleted, you will see the following information from Microsoft:


Why retentions?

Why don’t we keep all conversations forever? Here’s why several stakeholders at Bosch, including our board of management, decided on the retentions:

  1. GDPR: We as Bosch need to be compliant with all GDPR regulations. Amongst others, GDPR states that data must not be stored for longer than necessary.

  2. Legal departments: Our legal departments make sure we as Bosch comply. To be compliant with these requirements from legal departments, a technical measure needs to be in place that allows Bosch to delete chat conversations automatically after a certain time period.

  3. The right storage: No matter which tool you use, neither Microsoft Teams, nor Skype for Business, nor Outlook are storage platforms! Please take a look at the official Bosch storage guide.


How to save / archive important information for longer than two years?
  • In case parts of your conversations need to be archived / saved for longer, please create a ILM-compliant document .
  • Please have a look at the latest Storage Guide.

End-to-end encryption

End-to-end encryption or E2EE means, that when both parties are in a one-to-one call, the communication between those is encrypted from End-to-end. No other party, including Microsoft, has not got access to the encrypted conversation. Encryption in Microsoft 365 protects chat, file sharing, presence, and other content in the call.

NOTE Both people on the call must turn on E2EE for the technology to work.

 Please note, that if you are not using End-to-end encryption, your calls are still encrypted according to general Microsoft encryption rules.


To turn on End-to-end encryption, follow these steps:

  1. On the top right of the Teams window, select the three dots next to your profile picture.
  2. Choose Settings > Privacy.

                3. Turn on End-to-end encrypted calls by toggling the switch.

                4.  You will see the encryption indicator on the Teams call window in the upper left corner

NOTE Turning on end-to-end encryption on one device also turn it on for all your devices.


ATTENTION Using end-to-end encryption the following features will be unavailable:

  • Breakout rooms

  • Copilot for Teams meetings

  • Excel Live

  • Live captions and transcription

  • People dialing in by phone

  • PowerPoint Live

  • Recording

  • Request control of shared content

  • Together mode, companion mode, large gallery

 Please note, that this feature is generally available on the latest version of the Teams desktop client for Windows or Mac. Note also that it`s limited to meetings with up to 50 attendees unless you have Teams additional feature package.

Due to the KBV10.14, point 7: The video usage is generally enabled for everyone at Bosch.

As it is only available in German, you can find an analogous translation of KBV10.14, point 7 below:

7. Use cases and organizational prerequisites of video communication

The video usage of UC systems is generally enabled for everyone at Bosch. Here are some examples of possible use cases:

  • Use as videophone: Communication via video between two or more participants as a supplement to audio-telephony.

  • Transmission of meetings: Transferring video between two or more participants or rooms as a supplement to audio-telephony.

  • Participation in meetings/events: Employees can participate in meetings/events that are streamed via video communication [and see the meeting/event on screen] - without having to turn on their own video camera.

The use of UC systems for video communication requires the following organizational prerequisites:

  • When participating in video conferences (workplace, home office, mobile working, etc.), the employee controls the transmission of his video image by switching the video function on or off. Supervisors and other employees must respect the personal responsibility.

  • In all other respects (e.g. when a video is transmitted from a meeting room in which several employees are participating in a meeting), video communication is treated as a face-to-face event.

  • For transmissions with active camera control, the manual focusing on individual employees should be avoided.

  • The captured camera image to be transmitted must be set in such a way that no uninvolved third parties are captured. This must be ensured by suitable measures, especially in open office environments (e.g. IWC areas), other open spaces (e.g. lounge) or in public spaces (e.g. train, airport).

To avoid capturing uninvolved third parties, we recommend using Background Effects (below). It is not possible to enable a blurred background by default - this is a Microsoft restriction.

Validity: Strictly speaking, the KBV10.14 is only relevant for associates in Germany. However, it is our central decision to apply the same rules worldwide due to three main reasons:

  1. Our largest user population is in Germany

  2. We at RB GmbH who operate the service are bound to KBV 10.14

  3. We cannot use different settings in different countries, for technical reasons and also for efficiency reasons.

What is a Speaker View

This option can be selected from the view switcher within meetings, allowing users to effortlessly track the current active speaker.

 

Speaker View is particularly effective in scenarios with a limited number of key speakers and a large audience, such as town halls, training, or lectures.


The Speaker View offers several enhancements, including:

  • Easy tracking of the active speaker: The view includes a primary area on the stage to focus on key participants in the meeting.

The main area designated for the active speaker is also utilized for shared content, enabling seamless transitions during presentations.

Co-organizer meeting role

Organizers are able to share control by assigning the "Co-organizer" role to people they invite. Meeting organizers can assign the co-organizer meeting role to up to 10 people they are inviting to a meeting. Co-organizers are granted most of the capabilities of the organizer in the meeting, including being able to access and modify the meeting options for the meeting.


What Co-Organizers Can and Can`t

Co-organizers are treated like organizers. It means they are able to:

  • Access and change meeting options
  • Create breakout rooms, but only during a meeting!  They can’t pre-create rooms or assign participants prior to the meeting start.
  • Manage breakout rooms
  • Bypass the lobby
  • Admit people from the lobby during a meeting
  • Lock the meeting
  • Present content
  • Change another participant’s meeting role
  • Change meeting options during a channel meeting → but they must be directly invited in the channel meeting invitation
  • End meeting for all

NOTE Co-organizers won't be able to pre-create Rooms and pre-assign participants ahead of meeting start. Breakout Room Creation/Management will only be possible during live meeting for co-organizers. They also can`t:

  • View and download attendance reports.
  • Edit the meeting invitation.
  • Manage the meeting recording.
  • Remove or change the Organizer role.

 External users can't be made co-organizers!



How to add Co-Organizers?

        3. Select co-organizers from the set of people already invited to the meeting

NOTE You can select max. 10 people

       4. Save changes

NOTE Only tenant accounts can be chosen as co-organizers. This is different to the presenter role, which can be assigned to guest accounts from other Teams tenants. 

       5. Co-organizers are shown as meeting organizers when meetings start. Other people who have been assigned the co-organizer role but have not joined the meeting don’t receive this designation until they join the meeting.

Virtual Green Room

This feature enables organizers and presenters to come together to socialize and prepare in a virtual green room ahead of going live. They also can monitor chat and Q&A with attendees.

To start a green room: 

  1. Go to your Teams calendar and open your meeting or webinar. 
    NOTE If enabling green room for a webinar, set the lobby policy to Everyone for a public webinar or People in my organization for a private webinar.

  2. Select Meeting options.

  3. Specify presenters by selecting Specific people or Only me and co-organizers from the Who can present dropdown menu. 
    NOTE You must specify presenters to enable green room.

  4. Enter presenter names in the Choose presenters field. Presenters must already be invited as a participant to appear in the drop-down list.

  5. Turn on the Enable Green room toggle.

  6. Select Save.

Organizers can turn green room on or off while a meeting is active by going into Meeting options, but the change won’t be reflected unless they end and restart the meeting. If attendees join the meeting while the green room is active, they’ll be greeted by a waiting screen and can chat or use enabled apps until the meeting starts.


The green room is turned on by default for Teams webinars. When a webinar is joined, organizers and presenters will join the webinar in the Green Room and attendees will wait in the Waiting Room until the event starts.


There are some limitations when organizers and presenters join the green room:  

  • CVI presenters who join will wait with attendees for the meeting to start and cannot interact with users in the green room. In this state, any audio shared by the CVI presenter will be audible to other attendees.

  • If a user in the green room is made an attendee, they will be unable to speak or share their video.

  • If an attendee waiting for a meeting to start is made a presenter, then other attendees who are waiting for the meeting to start will be able to hear them. We recommend removing a user if you would like to promote or demote them.

  • Compliance recording will not be available to those who join the green room or attendees who are waiting for the meeting to start; however, compliance recording will start for all specified participants once the meeting has also started. 

  • Green room capacity is limited to 100 presenters at a time. 
  • Organizers and presenters can’t change the meeting layout or turn on recording, or Speaker Coach from the green room. They’ll be able to do so when the meeting starts.

  1. In Teams, select Calendar.
  2. Find the meeting you've scheduled for which you want to add polls and click or tap it.
  3. Select Chat with participants.

       4. Select + Add a tab, search for and select Polls, and then click or tap Add.

       5. Select Save. A new Polls tab will be added to your meeting.

       6. Select +Create New Poll, and then choose one of the following:

  • Multiple Choice Poll - Create your question or statement, and then provide answer options (up to 12) from which your audience can choose.
  • Multiple Choice Quiz - Mark a correct answer for your multiple-choice quiz. You can have a single option as a correct answer, or more than one if you select Multiple answers.
  • Word Cloud Poll - Ask an open-ended question and see responses reflected in a word cloud.
  • Rating Poll - Let your respondents rate a statement. You can customize the ratings scale up to 5 and display those ratings by stars or numbers.

HINT You can also use ready-made suggestions or use your previous Polls.

         7. Add your question options and your answer options.

         8.  As appropriate for your meeting, you can select Record names of respondents, Share results automatically after voting and/or Allow co-presenters to edit your poll while it`s a draft poll

         9. Select Save as draft. This will save your poll as a draft until you're ready to launch it during your meeting. You can also launch it at once.

NOTE You'll see DRAFT marked in green in the midsection. Later you can launch it, edit or delete.

To change the order of the polls, click or tap and hold a poll, and then drag it into the position you want.



Once attendees pick their answer, they'll select Submit and you'll be able to see their responses immediately. Meeting attendees also have the option of not participating in the poll by closing the poll notification that appears in the middle of their meeting screen without picking an answer nor selecting Submit.

NOTE Only meeting owners and presenters can create, manage, and launch polls. Meeting attendees have the ability to respond to polls but can't edit them.


Tips

  • Polls that have been launched and are accepting responses will be marked in red with LIVE in the midsection of the poll.
  • Polls that have been closed and are no longer accepting responses will be marked in dark gray with CLOSED.
  • If you want to reopen the poll, select the drop-down list next to Export results and choose Reopen poll.
  • If you want to close a poll, see the response details, export poll results, or delete a poll, select the drop-down list next to View results and select Close poll, Response details, Export results, or Delete poll, respectively.


B. During a meeting

  1. Click on + Apps and add Polls
  2. Select Polls tab

       3. Click on +New poll or Launch instant poll


HINT You can also use a ready-made suggestions by clicking on the bulb icon:

Or choose from your existing recently used polls:


      4. Choose the poll type

      5. See points 7-9 in the above part

Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI)


Calling and meetings

It is possible to blur and use effects on your background for virtual desktops and Citrix.

The following calling and meeting features are not supported:

  • Enhanced emergency services
  • HID buttons and LED controls between the Teams app and devices
  • Broadcast and live event producer and presenter roles
  • Location-Based Routing (LBR)
  • Call park
  • Call queue
  • Shared system audio/computer sound
  • Media bypass for Direct Routing


The following are known issues and limitations for calling and meetings:
  • Interoperability with Skype for Business is limited to audio calls; there is no video modality.
  • Only a single incoming video stream is supported in meetings or group calls. When multiple people send video, only the dominant speaker's video is shown at any given time.
  • Incoming and outgoing video stream resolution is limited to 720p resolution. This is a WebRTC limitation.
  • Only one video stream from an incoming camera or screen share stream is supported. When there's an incoming screen share, that screen share is shown, instead of the video of the dominant speaker.
  • Outgoing screen sharing: Application sharing is not supported.
  • Give control and take control: Not supported during a screen sharing or application sharing session. Supported during a PowerPoint sharing session.
  • Dual Tone Multi Frequency (DTMF) interaction with telephony systems is currently not supported.
  • When screen sharing in a multi-monitor setup, only the main monitor is shared.
  • High DPI scaling on CWA is not supported.


Microsoft Teams on Chrome browser vs. desktop app for VDI

Microsoft Teams on Chrome browser doesn't provide a replacement for the Teams desktop app for VDI with AV optimization. The chat and collaboration experience works as expected. When media is needed, there are some experiences that might not meet user expectations on the Chrome browser:

  • The audio and video streaming experience might not be optimal. Users might experiences delays or reduced quality.
  • Device settings aren't available in browser settings.
  • Device management is handled through the browser and requires multiple settings in browser site settings.

Data in Microsoft 365: Which documents am I allowed to upload, store and edit?

Other languages | weitere Sprachen


This applies to all Microsoft 365 applications.

All chats and documents published and uploaded to Microsoft 365 applications are being stored in the Microsoft Cloud.


C-SC0, C-SC1, C-SC2 data can be uploaded, stored and edited in Microsoft 365 applications without any further user activities.


For strictly confidential data (C-SC3) the following regulations apply:

  • Telephony & Meetings: These requirements are obligatory for C-SC3 meetings in Microsoft Teams.
  • E-mails: SC3 e-mails have to be encrypted via S/MIME for emails (as usual)
  • Files: Upload, store and edit SC3 data on SharePoint on premises (as usual)
    or encrypt your data before the upload to Microsoft 365 (SharePoint Online) by using Entrust for files


Business Records: It is not yet possible to store business records in order to archive them in Microsoft 365 applications.
Product liability requires ILM (Information Lifecycle Management) for revisions and baselines (e.g. development documentation). The requirements for document management (CD02981, for BSH: HQ_R_367) and other standards (e.g. ASPICE; ISO 9001,...) are not given in Microsoft 365.

  • Share files in Microsoft 365 by using working documents or file copies
  • Use ILM suitable storage places, e.g. SharePoint on premises for final versions (compliant CD02981, for BSH: HQ_R_367)
  • Add a SharePoint on premises Site as a tab in your Teams room


In individual cases, there are contractual restrictions from customers that do not yet allow to store data outside Bosch (mostly very old contracts). In these cases, contracts must be reviewed and if necessary adapted.


For Microsoft Teams, please keep in mind that whenever you send a chat messages / share a document / or any other data via Microsoft Teams chat or channel, it is uploaded to the Microsoft Cloud:

  • Screen sharing: ad-hoc sharing of your own desktop and subsequent display of C-SC3 data are allowed while observing general safety rules
  • Chats: 
    • Chatting about technical aspects of the meeting is not forbidden, but the content of the chat is no allowed to be C-SC3
    • All chat conversations in Microsoft Teams will be deleted two years after they were initially created. For more details: Chat & Activities Retentions
  • Live Caption as well as PowerPoint Live functions are not allowed with C-SC3 data 
  • Direct phone calls (without team app) are forbidden with C-SC3 data, but please consider end-to-end encryption feature.

Check also Strictly Confidential Meetings
