Power BI Platform Overview


TIP: Use Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site.

Didn't find what you were looking for? Click here for our support channels.

1.1. What is Power BI?

Imagine you have a mess of data coming from different places, such as Excel files, databases in the cloud or on your computer. Power BI is like a super-organizer for this mess! 

It has a lot of tools and applications that work together to turn all that messy data into things that are easy to understand, beautiful to look at and even interactive. This means you can see cool graphs, charts and maps that show what your data is saying. 


Check out the video below to learn more

1.1.1. Benefits of using Power BI 

Power BI offers a number of advantages that make it a popular choice for data analysis and report generation. Here are some of the main reasons: 

  1. Extensive connectivity: Power BI can connect to a wide variety of data sources, including local databases, cloud services, Excel files and many others. This allows users to aggregate data from different sources in one place for analysis.
  2. Ease of use: With an intuitive interface and drag-and-drop features, Power BI is relatively easy to learn and use, even for users without advanced technical experience in data analysis. 
  3. Interactive visualizations: Power BI offers a variety of visualization options, such as graphs, tables, maps and more. These visualizations can be easily customized and made interactive, allowing users to explore the data in a dynamic way. 
  4. Advanced analysis features: In addition to basic visualizations, Power BI offers advanced analysis features, such as predictive analysis and machine learning capabilities, which allow users to discover deeper insights in the data. 
  5. Integration with the Microsoft ecosystem: As part of the Microsoft ecosystem, Power BI integrates seamlessly with other tools and services, such as Excel, Azure and SharePoint. This facilitates collaboration and data sharing within an organization. 
  6. Regular updates and support: Microsoft continues to invest in the development and improvement of Power BI, regularly releasing new features and updates. It also offers users comprehensive technical support. 
  7. Flexible deployment options: Power BI is available as a cloud service (Power BI Service), as well as in desktop (Power BI Desktop) and mobile (Power BI Mobile App) versions, providing flexibility in deployment and data access. 

These are just some of the advantages of Power BI, which make it a powerful choice for data analysis and insight generation in a variety of organizations and sectors.


1.2. Power BI Options

The tool portfolio offered by BD at Bosch consists of three components. Find out more about the individual tools in the following sections of this page.


1.2.1. Power BI Desktop

Power BI Desktop is a local design and development tool used to create reports and data models before publishing them in Power BI Cloud or On-Premises. 

At Bosch we currently offer the following download options and you must request installation via ITSP  help Request installation

Here are some highlights:

Local Development Tool: It is installed locally on users' computers and used to create reports, data modeling and advanced analysis. 

Connection to Different Data Sources: Offers support for connecting to a wide variety of data sources, including local databases, cloud services, CSV files and more. 

Data Modeling: Allows users to create complex data models, define relationships between tables and create calculated measures using the DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) language. 

Custom Visualizations: Offers a variety of custom views and formatting options to create visually appealing and informative reports. 

Free to Use: Power BI Desktop is free to download and use, making it accessible to individuals and organizations of all sizes.


1.2.2. Power BI Service Cloud

Power BI Cloud is the hosted version of Power BI, provided as a cloud service by Microsoft.

view Power BI Cloud documentation


Here are some key points: 

Cloud Hosting: All data and reports are hosted on Microsoft servers in the cloud, providing access from anywhere and on any device with an internet connection. 

Web Services: Offers a full range of web services for creating, sharing, collaborating and viewing reports and dashboards. 

Automatic Updates: Updates and new features are applied automatically by Microsoft, ensuring that users have access to the latest functionality without the need for manual updates. 

Real-Time Collaboration: Allows teams to collaborate on reports and dashboards in real time, facilitating data-based decision-making. 

Integration with Other Services: Integrates easily with other Microsoft services, such as SharePoint, Teams, Azure and more.


1.2.3. Power BI On-Premises > publishPowerBI

Power BI On-Premises is a version of Power BI that allows organizations to host their own servers and maintain full control over their data. At Bosch, the Power BI Platform team offers the service on its own server called publishPowerBI.

view publishPowerBI documentation


Here are the main aspects:

Local Deployment: Power BI servers and data are deployed and maintained on the organization's premises, providing greater control and security over the data. 

Increased Security: Organizations can implement additional security measures according to their specific policies and requirements. 

Controlled Updates: Updates and new versions of Power BI can be installed and managed locally by the IT team, allowing for more granular control over software updates. 

Connectivity to Local Sources: Provides support for connecting to local data sources and legacy systems that cannot be accessed through the cloud. 

Integration with Existing Infrastructure: Allows you to easily integrate with the organization's existing infrastructure, such as active directories and security policies.


1.2.4. Difference between Power BI Cloud and On-Premise

Power BI Product Team provides 2 kinds of hosts, one is publishPowerBI (known as On-Premise Report Server) hosted in Enterprise Network BCN, another one is Power BI Cloud (on market, it is so called Power BI Service) hosted in Microsoft Cloud. 

We will introduce the difference in details below. 

Security Level

Both Power BI Cloud and Report Server maintain the same level of security (SC2), with terms and conditions regarding confidential and personal data equally applied. 

To access Power BI Cloud, Bosch-managed devices and the Bosch Network (or Bosch VPN) are required, along with login credentials.  

If there are company or BU restrictions or processes for cloud integration, these can be followed accordingly.

Desktop software

Be noticed that Power BI Report Server (On-premise) and Power BI Cloud they have 2 different desktop type. You must use right desktop software to deploy report to corresponding host (On-Premise Report Server or Cloud).

You could get both of this 2 desktop types from ITSP.


Maybe somebody doesn't remember what type installed already. Let's look at what's the desktop type installed on your computer.

This is desktop for Report Server, so you could see the "RS" flag in the icon. By using this desktop software, you should deploy your report to Power BI Report Server (https://powerbi.bosch.com)

This is desktop for Cloud, by using this, you should deploy your report to Power BI Cloud (https://app.powerbi.com).

Performance

There are lots of aspects impacting Performance. Network Latency, Model Quality, Data Source(size, type…), Formula(DAX, M Language) Quality, Infrastructure, Hardware resources, etc.

Both hosts we apply Share Model across Bosch in order to make cost effective, thus resources are limited and performance is easy to reach critical point.

Regarding report server, due to complex infrastructure it can't scale easily.

But with Power BI Cloud, as it's kind of Microsoft cloud service, it's easy to scale up or scale out to guarantee general performance.

Embed

If host on cloud, Power BI Reports could embed into Teams, PowerPoint as interactive report.

Furthermore, compared with reports on Report Server, if host on cloud, reports can embed individual Tile instead of whole report if people are familiar with web development by using JavaScript. It brings much more flexibility to generate rich style reports

Access https://playground.powerbi.com/en-us/showcases-gallery/quick-visual-creator to get sample from "Microsoft Power BI Embeded Analytics Playground"

Collaboration

Communication

Compared with hosting on On-Premise Report Server, people is able to leave comments to reports for collaboration.

Development

Have you ever wondered that you have shaped data within Power BI and want to share with self or others with next report generation by using same data?

In Cloud, once you upload your pbix file(import mode), thus dataset is uploaded as well, and you could share this dataset  for report generation next time when you select "Power BI Dataset" as data source.

Data Refresh

Regarding import mode, as you know that regarding publishPowerBI, we restrict that maximum 3 times per day to refresh data, but regarding Power BI Cloud, the frequency is much higher - every half an hour. But of course, don't set so high frequent scheduled job, as it would consume too much resource and if we detect your job impacting Premium Capacity's performance too much, we will stop your job.

Real-time streaming is supported by Cloud and the report could be refreshed automatically, currently our setting is every 5 minutes in order to not consume resources too much. If you have Real-time streaming data need to be refreshed every several seconds, could let us know.

Dashboard

Sometime when people develop a report, he may say he did a dashboard. Actually Power BI Cloud brings a different meaning to "dashboard" . If there are existing Report A, B, C and if people want to create a new report with visuals from these existing reports, he can actually just pin tiles(visuals) from Report A,B,C and then generate a dashboard. No new reports to be developed!

Email Subscription

If you don't want to always check report to capture changes, you could use this feature.

Alerts - Threshold

Helps in keep a track when a Card, KPI or Gauge Chart goes above or below a threshold

Subscription - Data updated

Email whenever the underlying data in a report is updated

Python

Python is supported by Cloud in 2 scenario.

  • Python as data source
    • People can use Python to shape data
    • Then Power BI get data from Python
    • Be noticed that if you want to keep the data refreshed, because Personal Gateway is forbidden in Bosch, you must release your python script as web resource(e.g. http://xxxx.py). Then use Web connector to load Python.
  • Python as visual
    • You could use Python Visual to enrich your Power BI Visual Library.

Below is the pure Python visual and could display in Power BI

Below is the comparison provided by Microsoft

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/report-server/compare-report-server-service

page_name: Get Access to Power BI Cloud
html_content:
Get Access to Power BI Cloud


TIP: Use Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site.

Didn't find what you were looking for? Click here for our support channels.

Here you will find all information necessary in case you just want to access Power BI Cloud content or actually publish and share content with other users


Make sure to check out the Power BI in General section of our documentation to understand the different options you have.

I want to access content that somebody shared with me

Good news - you already are a Power BI Free user which means you can already access Power BI Cloud and content that has been shared with you!

Just follow this link, bookmark it and start using Power BI right away!

Another easy way to access Power BI is to use the integrated Power BI app in Teams by clicking this link and installing the app! (make sure to pin the app by right clicking on Power BI to the left in the bar so that you always access it easily when in Teams)


Inside Power BI you can then click on "Apps" and filter for "Organizational Apps" to see all the Power BI content that you already have access to.


If you see anything that you like click on "Get it now" to access it and have it added to your personal "Apps" section. 

You can also take a look at the "Shared with me" section to see all content that has been shared with you


If you receive a message that you need a Pro license to access this content it means that the content provider has not assigned the content to one of our Premium capacities.
In this case you need to contact the publisher directly to ask them to move their content to Premium or - if they do not choose to do so - get a Pro license to access this content.


I want to publish and share Power BI content with other users at Bosch

Sharing content with your colleagues has never been easier! Just follow our simple steps to get started!



1. Step 1: Get Power BI Desktop

Just like any other software on your computer you can have Power BI Desktop assigned to your client via the IT Service Portal.

Make sure to get Power BI Desktop - Cloud!

If you want detailed instructions, expand the "How to install Power BI Desktop to your computer" section below.

  1. Visit the IT Service Portal
  2. Search for Add/remove software in the search bar


  3. Click on “Order”



  4. Search for “Power BI” under Search Software and Configurations
  5. Select "EAN - Microsoft Power BI Desktop - Cloud (install)"
  6. Check Power BI Desktop – Cloud (install) button and submit the request (Reason for Request is an optional field to fill it.). Once the request is submitted, software will be pushed to your computer after the approval and be installed. 
  7. After Installation, you can find the software from your computer’s Start Menu->Power BI Desktop.



If you have never used Power BI Desktop before make sure to take a look at this free beginners course Get data with Power BI Desktop - Learn | Microsoft Docs from Microsoft!

It will only take about an hour of your time 

2. Step 2: Get your Power BI Pro License

If you want to share content with other users you need your Power BI Pro license (see Power BI in general)

Getting a license is easy!

Open Service portal link and go to "Pro license assignment"

1.The "License Available" on the top shows the number of license available in the stock, if the number is 0, then you will not able to apply new license. (we will order the new license as soon as we can)

2.Click this button to remove your current license

3.Click this button to order a new license, but if already have one, then you will not able to order second one license.

4.It will trigger a workon approving workflow for any new license request, after you apply for a new license, it will create a workon item and send to your line-manager for approval. After manager approves, the license will be finally assigned to your account.

5.Click it to view all the change history of Pro-license assignment / un-assignment of your account.

2.1. To remove Pro-license. Click on Unassign License button

Click Apply, and then click Confirm.

2.2. To apply for a new license. Click on Request New Licenses button.

Click Apply and Confirm.

It will initiate an workon workflow, after approved by the line manager, the license will then be assigned to your account.


After your manager approves, please click “Workflow status” in pic 1 and click the “sync” button in below pic2 to synchronize the workon status. The application will also syncchronize the status automatically every 30 minutes, but you can get the status updated by clicking the button manually  in pic2.


Only internal users can apply from this portal, BSH & externals have to use ITSP for Pro License request 

3. Step 3: Create the workspaces that you need for your reporting

Once you have your Power BI Pro license assigned to your user you can create as many worspaces as you need for your reporting purposes.

You can create one Power BI App per workspace - therefore it makes sense to bundle reports in workspaces according to your target audience.

Any newly created workspace is a Pro workspace - this means, only users with a Pro-License can access this workspace. 


Expand the next section to see how you can create workspaces!


To create a workspace, click on "Workspaces" in the left navigation bar and then on "Create a workspace". One Pro-Licensed users can create workspaces!



Workspace names need to be unique at Bosch, if your name is already taken you will see a warning message and need to find another name. In the Description field you can describe the purpose of this workspace, this information is visible to any user that has access to this workspace.

If you want to, feel free to upload a little image - it looks always nice to have an icon for workspaces and Power BI apps, but this is only optional.


If other colleagues have granted access to their workspaces to you you will see those workspaces showing up in the list of workspaces. 


Congratulations! You have created your first workspace and can now publish content into this workspace!



Pro-Tipp: The Workspace is your "kitchen" - only let other cooks have access to the kitchen. If you want to share content with your colleagues, always use Power BI Apps ("dining room"). 

4. Step 4: Have your workspace assigned to Premium

PROCESS of Tier 0

With your Power BI Pro license comes Power BI Premium (Tier 0) for free!  This will allow you to share your Power BI content with an unlimited number of unlicensed users as long as your datasets are less than 50 MB in size.

  • New workspaces created with default settings are automatically assigned to Tier 0,
  • Those old workspaces if you are Pro user and admin of those workspaces, you could assign Tier 0 by yourself. 

for more details see Power BI - Assign workspace to Premium capacity - Next Generation Workplace - Docupedia (bosch.com)

Known Issue of Capacity 0: Because all of Pro users are able to utilize Capacity 0 for free, but the cloud resources are limited, so the performance and stability of Capacity 0 maybe not satisfying. If your reports are performance and stability sensitive, please consider ordering a Premium Subscription - Capacity 1, Capacity X or Customer Owned Capacity.

PROCESS of Tier 1 and Tier X

If your datasets are larger or need high performance and stability, please consider Capacity 1 or Capacity X

To assign your workspace to such higher Premium capacity, use the Power BI service portal - "Subscription management".

Entrance: https://power-bi-service-portal.bosch.tech

PROCESS of CoC(Customer Owned Capacity)

If you'd like to order a Customer Owned Capacity, please contact YU McCarthy (BD/DPA-GOI3 BD/DPA-DAP-Sq3) to request. 

4.1. Premium Subscription Creation and Modification

Expand the following section for detailed instructions on how to request and manage your Premium Subscription regarding  Power BI Premium Tier 1 or Tier X.

4.1.1. How to request a new subscription

How to request a New Subscription

The application will firstly search the database and check the current user if has a subscription already, even when no subscription ID under current user, the new button on the left is clickable. (One user can only have one subscription ID).


Click the +New button to create new subscription, it will pop up a dialog regarding the terms and conditions which user need to check and agree to process to next

Input all the fields required to request new subscription

After clicking Agree, it will pop up a form on the left side as below, most of the data field is auto-generated

  • 1. Subscription ID, is auto generated based on the "last" subscription ID in the database and plus 1(auto incremented by 1)
  • 2.Subscription Owner, is the current user (user data comes from SSO)
  • 3.Owner Department,  is the department of the current user (fetch data from COMPAS API)
  • 4.Owner CostCenter, is the cost center of the current user (fetch data from COMPAS API), cost center value can be changed, the default value is the cost center from employee data, but if it's need to charge to a different cost center, just enter the cost center directly. the cost center manager field will updated based on it.

          Also, user can switch the cost center to solution ID, by clicking the pencil icon on the top right of the input box, currently no API to fetch the Solution manager based on it, so after switch to solution ID, user needs to manually select a solution manager.( When selecting approving manager, please type either the full Bosch NT or the full mail address)                                

  • 5.Tier Type, a dropdown box to select which subscription type you need, currently Tier-1 and Tier-X are the two options available to select
  • 6., the number of the unit, for Tier-1, the units is 1 by default, and cannot be changed, for Tier-X, then the minimum number for units is 2, and you can increase the number if you need more units. we will charge you based on the units you selected.
  • 7.Cost, it auto generated based on Tier Type and Units you selected, the unit cost for current subscription is 203.33 EUR/month, two units will double the cost equals 406.66EUR/month, and so on.
  • 8.Disciplinary manager, is the manager of current user (fetch data from COMPAS API)
  • 9.Cost Center manager, the cost center owner (call Cost Center API), or the solution manager (if user switch the cost center to solution ID, and user needs to select the solution manager manually),
  • 10.Click Submit to send the request.


New subscription request triggers a workon approval workflow.

After submit the request, application will trigger the workon approval workflow, default status is "pending for Approval"



User can click the button (yellow button as above under Workflow status column) , it will show up the below window, which user can check the Workon ID and workon status.

By click the "sync" icon as below 2, it will trigger a API to call for "search for workon item detail" in the background and check if the Workon status has updates, and update the workflow status accordingly.


Workon status Sync

Besides the user manually click button to sync the status, the application also has a schedule job to call the workon API to sync the status automatically every 30 minutes.



If the workon status has changed, it will sync the status as below shown, also along with finally active the subscription ID, and send out notification mails to users.


After your workon item has been approved, the Workflow status will changed to Approved, and then you can process the workspace assignment (you will also received a notification mail regarding the New Subscription request succeed)



4.1.2. How to modify an existing Premium Subscription

Info

As each user can have only one subscription ID, and which Capacity (Capacity X or Capacity 1) your workspace is in is strongly linked to which premium option your subscription is in (Tier-X or Tier-1). which means no matter you want to downgrade or upgrade your workspaces (from Capacity X to Capacity 1 or the opposite way), you need to firstly upgrade or downgrade your subscription. After the subscription ID is in the certain premium option, your linked workspaces can be upgraded or downgraded to the correspondingly Capacity.


There are three icons for each line of subscription records as below.

          1.Edit the subscription

          2.View the change history of the subscription

          3.View the workspaces currently linked to this subscription


How to edit the subscription

                   1. User can Inactive(remove the subscription), but please be noted, to remove subscription, all the workspaces linked to this subscription will be firstly moved to Capacity 0 as prerequisite.

                   2. User can also change the subscription owner

                   3. or change the cost center,(change cost center or switch to solution ID by clicking the pencil icon on top right of the input box)

                   4,5. User can also change the Tier type and units. please note that if choose to downgrade subscription (from Tier-X to Tier-1), all workspaces linked to this subscription will be moved to Capacity 1, if you choose to upgrade your subscription, all workspace linked to this subscription will also automatically upgrade to Capacity X (after workflow gets approved).

                   After you make these changes, it will trigger workon API to send the approval workflow to the relevant managers, once the managers approved, the new subscription will replace the old one. Before managers approved such request, the old subscription will still be the valid one.

                  

Edit subscription form


View the change history of the subscription


Click icon 2 as below can view the change history of the subscription.


View all workspace linked to this subscription or workspaces you have admin access.


by clicking icon 3 as below can view the relevant workspaces assigned to the current subscription.

By default, it shows all the workspaces linked to the subscription, but if user want to view all workspaces you have admin access to, can click the button as below-click here.

4.2. Workspace assignment

4.2.1. How to assign workspace to subscription

Go to the workspace assignment page, clicking the button on the left to open the assign workspace dialog


Type the workspace name in the box, and it will search for all the workspaces you have admin access, and generate a drop down box for you to select


You can also input multiple workspaces.



Workspace assignment does not invoke workflow, that means it will take effect immediately after you click submit, you can open the Power BI service (https://app.powerbi.com) and check your workspace premium options, it should changed to the new subscription based on what you requested in service portal.

4.2.2. View workspace users and change history

For each workspace record, it has two icons on the right as below,

  1. View the users for the workspaces, including all types of users, and user department information (only personal user, group user only show groupID)
  2. View the change history of the workspace assignment.

5. Step 5: Optional: Have your on-premise data sources connected to the cloud

See our Data Source Connection - Next Generation Workplace - Docupedia (bosch.com) section for details.

This is only necessary if your Power BI reports contain data from on-premise data sources and you need them to refresh automatically inside the cloud.

Pro-Tipp: Use SharePoint Online (Teams Rooms) for your Excel files instead of file shares or on-premise SharePoint. This way you don't need to worry about setting up a data source in the Power BI Gateway



SELF SERVICE DATA GATEWAY PILOT

Self-Service On-Premises Data Gateway - Next Generation Workplace - Docupedia (bosch.com)

Participate in our pilot for the easiest and fastest way to connect to your on-premise data!



6. Step 6: Create a Power BI App

The Power BI App is the best way to share content with your colleagues at Bosch. 

Granting access to your workspace will still require users to have a Pro license, even if your workspace is Premium. 


You have the option to grant "viewer" access to your workspace (users will not need a Pro license then) but please don't do this. If you add users to your workspace, they will see this workspace in their list of workspaces and all the content on it unfiltered. They will also see all the datasets in this workspace. Only grant access to workspaces if you know what you are doing.

And it gets even worse - they have no option to remove themselves from this workspace. Yikes! Imagine app developers could just install apps to your smartphone without asking you first. No thank you 


With apps, users can decide for themselves if they want to use the Power BI App or not. 


Find out how to setup a Power BI App by expanding the following section

Setting up a Power BI App 

This is one of the new concepts on how to share your reports across the company that once you understood it it's fun and easy and your users will love it too!

A Power BI App is the seperation of the presentation layer that you prepare for your users from the "WORK"-spaces. Coming back to the "Cook" and "Kitchen" example - the Power BI App is the dining room where you present some of the content/food from your kitchen in a nice and tasty way to your customers.

It's also the way to make Power BI content available to your users without the need for a license!

You can actually compare the idea of Power BI Apps like apps you have on your iPhone. There is an AppStore where you browse for apps that are available to you and you pick the ones you like and install it to your phone.

The same thing users at Bosch will do in the Power BI AppStore which is called the AppSource: They see all apps that they have been granted access to and can pick the ones they are interested in and install them to their Power BI.


When using a Power BI Subscription and Power BI Apps, users don't need a Pro-License to use Power BI Reports!


Select content to be part of your Power BI App

But before they can do so, you will need to prepare the Power BI App for them. There can be ONE Power BI App per ONE Workspace. A Power BI App must contain at least one report or dashboard from this workspace, but it is not necessary to make every report or dashboard inside your workspace available to the users!

When you go inside your workspace, you will see all the reports and datasets that you have published and a little switch next to them that says "Include in app". Per default, all reports that you have published into a workspace are marked to be included in the app.

You can have many versions of your report in a workspace, maybe you have continued working on a report and have three or four versions in the workspace. Select the content that you actually want to share with your users by flipping the switch to "Yes".



Create the app

Then in the top right corner click on the button that says "CREATE APP". 



This will lead you to the app creation process that contains of three steps:

  • Setup
  • Navigation
  • Permissions


Setup

In this section you describe your Power BI App that will be visible to the users when browsing the AppSource. 

Name

Description

App nameThe name of your app that will be shown in the AppSource. Choose a name that will easily indicate to the users what the content of this app will be.
Use something catchy that users will use when they refer to that Power BI App.
DescriptionThis text will be shown underneath the App name in the AppSource and further describes the purpose and content of the app. 
Try to use a one-sentence description to describe your app. If the text is too long it will be truncated in the AppSource.
Support SiteIf you prepared some documentation about your Power BI reports, add the URL here. This could be i.e. some docupedia page or connect community. 
The link to the support site is accessible to users when using the Power BI App!
App logoUse a little catchy icon to "brand" your Power BI App and give it a nice look in the App overview of your users. 
If you don't use one, it will just have a default icon from Power BI.
App theme colorWhen using the app this color will be used in the navigation and the surrounding frame of your reports.
Choose a color that comes closest to the colors you are using in the report
Contact informationBy default, your name will be shown as the contact for this app.
If you have a support-email address for this app, a distribution list or another contact enter it here


Once you are done with the initial setup, click on the "Navigation" tab next to Setup



Navigation

In the navigation section, you define how users can browse through the content that you bundled in this Power BI App. 

When using publishPowerBI, users open one report and see all the different report pages as little tabs at the bottom of the report that allows them to navigate through the different report pages.

In a Power BI App, you have different options on how you want users to interact with your content.


To the left, you will see the reports that you have included in the App and can change the order that they will be displayed. Per default, the sorting order is alphabetical, but you can change the order in a way that is more intuitive for the users.

On the right side "Report Details" you can change the name of your reports to a user-friendly non-technical name. Give your reports some nice friendly name, don't use CamelCase or similiar techie stuff. The users of your Power BI App will thank you!

By clicking on "+ New" you can add sections or links to that navigation! In my example, I have two demo-reports and one report that contains information and created two corresponding sections. After adding sections, assign reports to them in the report details section.



And you can even add a link to another application at Bosch! Maybe you want users to have the opportunity to jump to a specific URL !



Once you have prepared the navigation, let's jump to the Permissions section.


Permissions

The permissions part of the Power BI App is vital to understand because mistakes here might exploit your report or data inside your report in a way that you didn't intend. So pay good attention now 

Access

In the access-section enter the users that you want to publish content to. You have access to any WOM-group that is present in the corporate directory and it's easy to find them by just starting to type the name of them.

If I want to share content with my department, I will type CI/DAP4 until I see the exact WOM group I want to share content with. Users who are part of this WOM group will be able to install this App from the AppSource.


You can also use IDM2BCD-Groups or managed Security Groups from the IT Service Portal. See Access Management for more information.

It is possible to add named users here. This is OK for some functional testing, but once you go live with your Power BI App and share it with a larger audience you need to follow the processes described in the Access Management section for compliance at Bosch!


Allow everyone who has app access to

The selections you make here are important in regards to data security and you should read this information carefully


Per default, a Power BI App will allow users that have access to the App access to the underlying datasets. When users have access to the underlying datasets, they will be able to build their own reports on your data model and data.

With this checkbox enabled, users will have full access to ALL data inside all datasets of this Power BI App, even if in your report you are now showing all the data. 

Make sure that this is your intention! If this is not a problem, make sure that your dataset is user-friendly! Have a clean data model with end-user friendly names. 

If you are not sure what you are doing here, disable this functionality until you have evaluated what this means 


Allowing users to share the app and underlying datasets should also be disabled - you don't want users to share your data with other users that you are not aware of!

Unless the data inside your report is not critical and you explicitly want users to reshare your content, you can enable this.


Click on "CREATE APP" to create the app and after successful creation you will see something like this:



Users that have permission for the app will now be able to install the App from the AppSource or - if you want - you can share the link that is shown to you with the users so that they can immediately start using the app.



Congratulations - your Power BI App is now ready to be shared with your users!

Power BI Cloud "On-Premise" Data Source Creation

When should I request a data source connection?

Power BI Cloud is a data analysis tool that connects to many data sources. If the data source for your Power BI report is located on-premise, then a connection must be established from Power BI Cloud to the on-premise data source using an application called Enterprise Gateway.

The Enterprise Gateway is required whenever Power BI Cloud must access data that is not accessible directly over the Internet.


The Power BI Platform team is operating and managing an Enterprise Gateway cluster in the BCN that can be used to connect to your data.


The following on-premise data sources have been successfully tested and can be used from Power BI Cloud:

  • Fileshare folders
  • Microsoft SQL Server databases
  • Oracle databases (if the servername provided is a valid TNS Name from the TNSNAMES.ORA central file)
  • MySQL
  • Microsoft SQL Server Analysis Services (SSAS)
  • Web
  • Impala (when using the built-in Impala connector of Power BI Desktop)
  • Vertica Database
  • InterSystem

The following on-premise data sources can NOT be used with Power BI Cloud

  • SAP BW
  • SAP HANA
  • Any ODBC connection
  • Access DB / Legacy Excel files (.xls)
  • Sharepoint "on-Premise" (i.e. sites.inside-share.bosch.com)


Any data source that is not listed here MIGHT be possible to use, but the Power BI Platform team needs to see on a case-by-case base and there is no obligation on our end to make your data sources available in the Cloud.

Currently using a windows file share or SharePoint?

If you are currently using i.e. Excel files that reside on a windows file share or a Sharepoint ( "sites.inside-share.bosch.com" ) we strongly suggest you use SharePoint Online! If you are using Teams, you are already using SharePoint Online and can start right away!

The on-premise SharePoint ( sites.inside-share.bosch.com , sites.inside-share2.bosch.com, etc.) cannot be used as a data source with Power BI Cloud.

When using SharePoint Online, you don't need to have a gateway connection created by us and can manage your dataset by yourself.

A tutorial on how this can be done can be found here: Power BI Cloud SharePoint Online migration tutorial

This way you can also make use of all the cool new features only available in SharePoint Online like reading files from a SharePoint folder.

For more information about SharePoint Online follow the link.

Please review and perform the following to process your Power BI Cloud data source creation request:


Using your browser, open and download a copy of the DataSource_Creation_Template to your local computer using the following link:


Data Source Creation Template v2

Populate the new DataSource_Creation_Template using the correct sheet for your data source type. Sample values and description is provided in the file.  Additional data population support provided below:



  • All fields in each sheet are mandatory
  • You must enter a data source name (without whitespaces), which will be visible in the IT Service Portal for the Master of Role
    We will use this name for the creation of a security group that will be used for access management. Choose a name that helps you and others easily identify the data source 
  • You will need to determine the Data Security Class of your data. Only data with SC-2 or less will be allowed on Power BI Cloud

  • When providing the server name or file path of your data source make sure it is identical to the name you are using in Power BI Desktop! It has to match the name of your dataset in Power BI Desktop. Otherwise, Power BI Cloud cannot map to it
  • You must choose the authentication method used. For Oracle, this is always Basic. When using your Bosch user, you will choose Windows authentication. If no credentials are provided, then choose Anonymous. Windows users can only be used when a technical user is provided. Please notice, each username can only be used one time
  • Provide the username for authentication. For windows, you need to include the domain name (e.g.DE\ProjectNTechUser )

  • You need to provide a technical user,  not your personal user! For databases you can have the Database Administrator create a database user for you, otherwise you can order a technical user in the ITSP (Manage Resource Accounts) (→ System Account) and have access granted to this user for your data source

    The user EMEA\POWRBI as a technical user is deprecated and can't be used for the creation of data sources in the Power BI Enterprise Gateway

  • You must provide the organization office (WOM) for master of data. The Master of Role must be a position holder of an organizational office (e.g. BD/XYZ1). He/she will also be responsible for granting access to this specific data source for the report publisher

Processing Time

Please be aware that due to the high amount of data source creation request the processing time takes longer than usual.

Processing can currently take up to 5 business days, depending on the quality of the information inside the data source creation template. 

Whenever possible use SharePoint Online as your data source as this will eliminate the need to setup and maintain an enterprise gateway connection!

We are sorry for any inconveniences this may cause.



How do I manage data source access?

Once a Power BI Cloud data source is created, report publishers must be granted access to use the data source in their datasets.  ITSP security groups (email enabled) are used to support Power BI Cloud data source access management.  As part of the data source creation process, a member of the Power BI Cloud team will create the new ITSP security group (on behalf of the requestor) for each data source.

The security group will be configured to use the Organizational Office provided in the DataSource_Creation_Template as the Master of Role.  This allows the position holder of the organizational office to self-administrate access to their Power BI Cloud data sources.  As the default delegate, the organization office position holder will be able to add additional delegates to further assist with data source access management.

When configuring the data source in your Power BI dashboard, please make sure you are using the very same Server Name you provided in the DataSource_Creation_Template, otherwise the dasboard won't "find" its respective gateway after being published in the cloud.

Um zu vermeiden, dass Sie E-Mail- und Kalenderbenachrichtigungen doppelt erhalten, können Sie die Standard Apple iOS-Synchronisierung von Mail und Kalender deaktivieren. Apple Mail und Apple Kalender zeigen dann keine Geschäftsdaten mehr an:

  1. iPhone Einstellungen öffnen
  2. Klicken Sie auf Mail
  3. Klicken Sie auf Accounts
  4. Wählen Sie Bosch (oder "Bosch verschlüsseltes Profil")
  5. Deaktivieren von Mail, Kalender

  1. In der Outlook Mobile App, klicken Sie auf das Mail Icon unten links
  2. Klicken Sie auf Ihr Profilbild / Haus Icon oben links
  3. Klicken Sie auf das Symbol + Mail
  4. Klicken Sie Geteiltes Postfach hinzufügen

Wichtig: Es können nur Shared Mailboxen eingebunden werden, welche ebenfalls in der Cloud (bei Exchange Online) gespeichert sind

Wie kann ich einen Shared Kalender einbinden?

Warum kann ich keine E-Mails im Stellvertreterpostfach löschen?

In der Outlook Mobile App für iOS und Android Geräte gibt es eine technische Beschränkung.

Es ist nicht möglich, mit Standard - Stellvertreterberechtigungen E-Mails zu löschen. Das Löschen von E-Mails im Stellvertreter Postfach mit Standard-Rechten ist nur mit der Outlook Version auf einem Windows-Rechner oder via OWA möglich.

Workaround: Für den Stellvertreter müssen Editor-Rechte auf dem <Posteingang> - und <Gelöschte Objekte> - Ordner im Stellvertreterpostfach gesetzt werden.

Warum erhalte ich Nachrichtenerinnerungen in der Outlook App?

Allgemein:

Microsoft hat eine Nachrichtenerinnerungen als neue Funktion implementiert, die E-Mails, auf ein Anwender möglicherweise antworten möchte, werden oben in Posteingang ablegt.

Es werden oben in ihrem Posteingang Erinnerungen für Nachrichten angezeigt, bei denen Outlook erkennt, dass die E-Mail möglicherweise eine Antwort erfordert, auf die der Benutzer jedoch nach drei Tagen noch nicht geantwortet hat.
Diese Erinnerungen verschwinden, nachdem der Anwender geantwortet hat, oder sie durch "wischen" geschlossen werden.
Sie können diese Funktion auch vollständig in ihren App-Einstellungen deaktivieren.

Benachrichtigung aktivBenachrichtigung deaktiviert

Wenn sie auf eine Erinnerung tippen, wird im Lesebereich ein Hinweis angezeigt, der erklärt, warum die Erinnerung oben im Posteingang angezeigt wird.

What is it?
The Outlook (Cloud Mailbox) means that we migrate the Outlook mailboxes from the Bosch network to the cloud (Microsoft 365). It is a hosted messaging application that provides access to email, calendars, contacts and tasks. You get more storage space for your mailbox and can access it from any Bosch managed device.

What are the preconditions?
Important points in advance:
  • Delegates: The delegated mailboxes need to be moved together (boss + assistant), see below "Delegates (for calendar + e-mails)"

How do I register for the M365 products/services?

The introduction of M365 at BOSCH means that a User Principal Name (UPN) has to be created in the Windows Active Directory for each user.
The User Principal Name (UPN) is a name of a user in an email address format. A UPN (for example: john.doe@domain.com) consists of the username (login name), the separator (the @ symbol), and the domain name (UPN suffix).

This UPN is required to connect to his "Outlook in the Cloud mailbox".
This UPN is also required to enable a login to the new M365 products such as <Microsoft To Do>, MS Whiteboard etc. .

In order to register for the M365 products and services, a UPN and password are required.

What is not working?

 Generally, most features should work as usual!
It is ensured that you will not lose any e-mails when migrating your mailbox to the cloud!

In some specific cases, the following points are not working. Have a look whether one of them is relevant for you:

Distribution Groups cannot be managed using Outlook (when migrated to the cloud) or Outlook Web App anymore:
To make changes to manually managed distribution lists as ExOnline owners you have the following possibilities:

    • For non-ITSP Distribution groups: Do changes via CI-CAT
    • Add a second owner who does not migrate his/her mailbox in the cloud (EXO)
    • Open a SMT ticket, choose "MAIL SERVICE" and assign it to the messaging solution group

You will not be able to check calendar availability of colleagues in BSH, and they will not be able to check yours.

The delegated mailboxes need to be moved together (boss + assistant) to avoid issues with the mailboxes. Click here for more details.

This information only concerns the delegation of calendar + e-mail inbox. It does not include the call-delegation functions in Skype for Business or Microsoft Teams!

  • Calling delegation for Skype for Business: More information can be found here.
  • Calling delegation for Microsoft Teams: This is not possible yet but on the roadmap.

3rd party applications like CRM cannot access your mailbox anymore.

Once your mailbox is moved to the cloud, you can no longer use the SfB contact folder. It won't be visible anymore in Skype for Business.
This is a restriction from Microsoft.

  • Exchange Online is currently not supported on OSD Linux Evolution Mail Client, OSD users should use the web application. By migrating, you will be able to schedule Teams meeting via Exchange Online Mailbox but you will no longer be able to schedule Skype meetings in Outlook Web App.
  • For Mac users, native Mail app, Calendar app and 3rd party apps (for example, Fantastical Calendar app) will not be working with Exchange Online.

After migrating to the cloud mailbox you will not be able to work with PST files anymore (see preconditions). Import of PST files possible before migration (see cloud mailbox migration platform)

Was ist die "Outlook (Cloud Mailbox)"?

Das Outlook-Postfach in der Cloud / Exchange Online bedeutet, dass wir die Outlook-Postfächer aus dem Bosch-Netzwerk in die Cloud (Microsoft 365) migrieren. Exchange Online ist eine gehostete Messaging-Anwendung, die Zugang zu E-Mails, Kalendern, Kontakten und Aufgaben bietet. Sie erhalten mehr Speicherplatz für Ihr Postfach und können von jedem von Bosch verwalteten Gerät darauf zugreifen.

Was sind die Vorteile?
  • Die Größe der Mailbox beträgt 99 GB.
  • Sie können Microsoft To Do verwenden.
  • Sie können FindTime verwenden, um Besprechungen zu planen.
  • Sie können Ihren Kalender in Teams anzeigen.
  • Sie können in ein Profilbild in Microsoft Teams verwenden
  • Sie können den Meeting-join reminder in Microsoft Teams nutzen
  • Sie können die Funktion In Outlook teilen in Microsoft Teams nutzen
  • Sie können die Outlook Mobile App (iOS) nutzen
Was sind die Voraussetzungen?
Wichtige Punkte vorab:
  • Assistenzfunktion: Die delegierten Postfächer müssen gemeinsam migriert werden (Chef + Assistent), um Probleme mit den Postfächern zu vermeiden. Klicken Sie hier für weitere Einzelheiten.
  • PST-Dateien: Dies ist ein optimaler Zeitpunkt, um Ihre PST-Dateien loszuwerden (Die Verwendung von PST-Dateien wird bald verboten werden und Sie werden sie später nicht mehr migrieren können). Der PST-Migrationsdienst unterstützt Sie dabei, Ihre PST-Dateien in Ihre persönliche Mailbox zu importieren.
    Klicken Sie bei der Installation (siehe unten) auf das nebenstehende Feld, wenn Sie noch PST-Dateien haben, die Sie jetzt importieren möchten!
  • Zustimmung zum Datenschutz: Personenbezogene Daten wie Vorname, Nachname und Ihr Profilbild werden mit Ihrem Postfach an Microsoft 365 übertragen und von allen Bosch Microsoft 365 Diensten genutzt. Alle Bosch-Benutzer haben Zugriff auf diese Daten. Aus rechtlichen Gründen dürfen wir Ihr Profilbild nicht automatisch in die Microsoft-Cloud übertragen (im Rahmen des Microsoft 365-Rollouts). Aus diesem Grund wird es gelöscht, bevor Ihre Daten in die Cloud migriert werden. Sie können Ihr Profilbild anschließend wieder hochladen. Wie melde ich mich an den M365 Produkten/Services an?

Durch die Einführung von M365 bei BOSCH ist es nötig, dass für jeden Anwender ein User Principal Name (UPN) im Windows Active Directory erzeugt wurde.
Der User Principal Name (UPN) ist ein Name eines Anwenders in einem E-Mail-Adressformat. Ein UPN (zum Beispiel: john.doe@domain.com) besteht aus dem Benutzernamen (Anmeldename), dem Trennzeichen (das @-Symbol) und dem Domänennamen (UPN-Suffix).

Dieser UPN wird benötigt um sich mit seinem "Outlook in the Cloud Postfach" zu verbinden.
Weiterhin wird dieser UPN benötigt um eine Anmeldung an den neuen M365 Produkten wie <Microsoft To Do>, MS Whiteboard etc. zu ermöglichen.

2.2. Data in Microsoft 365: Which documents am I allowed to upload, store and edit?

Other languages | weitere Sprachen


This applies to all Microsoft 365 applications.

All chats and documents published and uploaded to Microsoft 365 applications are being stored in the Microsoft Cloud.


C-SC0, C-SC1, C-SC2 data can be uploaded, stored and edited in Microsoft 365 applications without any further user activities.


For strictly confidential data (C-SC3) the following regulations apply:

  • Telephony & Meetings: These requirements are obligatory for C-SC3 meetings in Microsoft Teams.
  • E-mails: SC3 e-mails have to be encrypted via S/MIME for emails (as usual)
  • Files: Upload, store and edit SC3 data on SharePoint on premises (as usual)
    or encrypt your data before the upload to Microsoft 365 (SharePoint Online) by using Entrust for files


Business Records: It is not yet possible to store business records in order to archive them in Microsoft 365 applications.
Product liability requires ILM (Information Lifecycle Management) for revisions and baselines (e.g. development documentation). The requirements for document management (CD02981, for BSH: HQ_R_367) and other standards (e.g. ASPICE; ISO 9001,...) are not given in Microsoft 365.

  • Share files in Microsoft 365 by using working documents or file copies
  • Use ILM suitable storage places, e.g. SharePoint on premises for final versions (compliant CD02981, for BSH: HQ_R_367)
  • Add a SharePoint on premises Site as a tab in your Teams room


In individual cases, there are contractual restrictions from customers that do not yet allow to store data outside Bosch (mostly very old contracts). In these cases, contracts must be reviewed and if necessary adapted.


For Microsoft Teams, please keep in mind that whenever you send a chat messages / share a document / or any other data via Microsoft Teams chat or channel, it is uploaded to the Microsoft Cloud:

  • Screen sharing: ad-hoc sharing of your own desktop and subsequent display of C-SC3 data are allowed while observing general safety rules
  • Chats: 
    • Chatting about technical aspects of the meeting is not forbidden, but the content of the chat is no allowed to be C-SC3
    • All chat conversations in Microsoft Teams will be deleted two years after they were initially created. For more details: Chat & Activities Retentions
  • Live Caption as well as PowerPoint Live functions are not allowed with C-SC3 data 
  • Direct phone calls (without team app) are forbidden with C-SC3 data, but please consider end-to-end encryption feature.

Check also Strictly Confidential Meetings 


Further information:

  • Check this little video to get more information about security classes.
  • Microsoft 365 Welcome Page FAQ > "SC3".

OpenDXM Rollen und Rechte

Die Rechte in OpenDXM werden mit Hilfe von Rollen gesteuert, die über IDM zugewiesen werden.

Definition Interne / Externe Anwender:

Interne Anwender

Mitarbeiter der Bosch-Gruppe (auch fixed-term, external), die Bosch-intern auf OpenDXM zugreifen.

Externe Anwender

Geschäftspartner der Bosch-Gruppe, die vom Internet auf OpenDXM zugreifen.

Regeln und Namenskonvention der Rollen:

internal-…            
bosch-…

wird nur an interne Anwender vergeben.

external-…wird nur an externe Anwender vergeben.

Im Folgenden sind die Rollen aufgelistet, die an OpenDXM-Nutzer vergeben werden können:

Rolle

Erläuterung

internal-users

Standard-Rolle für alle internen Anwender. Mit dieser Rolle ist es möglich, Daten an interne und externe Geschäftspartner zu versenden.

external-users

Standard-Rolle für alle externen Anwender. Mit dieser Rolle ist es möglich, Daten an interne Anwender zu versenden.

Mit dieser Rolle ist es nicht möglich, andere externe Anwender als Empfänger auszuwählen und ihnen Daten zu senden.

bosch-proxy-[XYZ]

Mehrere interne Anwender können zu einer „Proxy-Gruppe“ zusammengefasst werden.

Erhält ein Mitglied der Proxy-Gruppe Daten, so werden alle Mitglieder der Proxy-Gruppe informiert.

Alle Mitglieder der Proxy-Gruppe können die Daten sehen und herunterladen.

external-proxy-[XYZ]

Mehrere externe Anwender derselben Firma können zu einer Proxy-Gruppe zusammengefasst werden.
Anwender verschiedener Firmen dürfen nicht in derselben Proxy-Gruppe sein.

Erhält ein Mitglied der Proxy-Gruppe Daten, so werden alle Mitglieder der Proxy-Gruppe informiert.

Alle Mitglieder der Proxy-Gruppe können die Daten sehen und herunterladen.

bosch-download-[XYZ]

Mehrere interne Anwender können zu einer „Download-Gruppe“ zusammengefasst werden.

Alle Mitglieder der Download-Gruppe können die Daten sehen und herunterladen, die an einen bestimmten internen Anwender gesendet wurden.

Im Gegensatz zur Proxy-Gruppe:

  • werden die Mitglieder der Download-Gruppe nicht informiert, wenn neue Daten vorhanden sind.
  • können die Gruppenmitglieder nicht die Daten sehen, die an andere Mitglieder der Download-Gruppe gesendet wurden.

Um die Daten zu sehen, die an eine andere Person gesendet wurde, selektieren Sie "Webspaces" und wählen Sie den entsprechenden Namen.

external-download-[XYZ]

Mehrere externe Anwender können zu einer „Download-Gruppe“ zusammengefasst werden.

Alle Mitglieder der Download-Gruppe können die Daten sehen und herunterladen, die an einen bestimmten externen Anwender gesendet wurden.

Geschäftspartner verschiedener Firmen können Mitglied dieser Gruppe sein.

Im Gegensatz zur Proxy-Gruppe:

  • werden die Mitglieder der Download-Gruppe nicht informiert, wenn neue Daten vorhanden sind.
  • können die Gruppenmitglieder nicht die Daten sehen, die an andere Mitglieder der Download-Gruppe gesendet wurden.

Um die Daten zu sehen, die an eine andere Person gesendet wurde, selektieren Sie "Webspaces" und wählen Sie den entsprechenden Namen.

bosch-upload-[XYZ]

Diese Gruppe wird dazu verwendet, um den Upload an einen bestimmten Empfänger zu beschränken.

Nur Mitglieder dieser Gruppe können Daten an einen bestimmten Empfänger senden.

no_email_notificcation

Mitglieder dieser Gruppe erhalten von OpenDXM keine E-Mails:
Sie werden nicht per E-Mail infromiert, wenn Daten an Sie gesendet werden.
Sei werden auch nicht informiert, wenn sie in einer Proxy-Gruppe sind und Daten an andere Proxy-Gruppen-Mitglieder gesendet werden.

Standardmäßig (ohne diese Rolle) werden Sender und Empfänger informiert, wenn Daten vollständig übertragen (gesendet) oder empfangen wurden.

proxy-no_email_notification

Optionale zusätzliche Rolle (Gruppe) für Proxy-Gruppen Mitglieder.
Mitglieder dieser Gruppe werden nicht per E-Mail-CC infromiert, wenn Daten an andere Proxy-Gruppen-Mitglieder gesendet werden.

Standardmäßig (ohne diese Rolle) wird jedes Proxy-Guppen-Mitglied per E-Mail-CC informiert.

bosch-restapi-users

Diese Rolle ermöglicht, Daten von einem Programm aus (Bosch-intern) automatisch zu versenden.

Ein automatisierter Download von Daten ist aktuell nicht möglich.

Weitere Informationen finden Sie unter OpenDXM REST APIs.

external-restapi-users

Diese Rolle ermöglicht, Daten von einem Programm aus (Internet) automatisch zu versenden.

Ein automatisierter Download von Daten ist aktuell nicht möglich.

Weitere Informationen finden Sie unter OpenDXM REST APIs.

bosch-batch-transfer

Diese Rolle wird nur Batch-Accounts zugewiesen (User-ID batch_...) Sie ermöglicht, Daten automatisiert von einem NFS Laufwerk an registrierte OpenDXM Nutzer zu senden.

Weitere Informationen finden Sie unter Automated file transfers to or from business partners (nur in Englisch verfügbar).

bosch-extended-webspace

Bitte sprechen Sie uns an (siehe unten), wenn Sie diese Lösung benötigen.

Diese Rolle kennzeichnet einen Account mit erweiterten Webspace-Optionen:

  • Im Webspace dieses Accounts können (manuell) weitere Unterordner angelegt werden, um Daten in einer Ordnerstruktur bereitzustellen.
  • Der Webspace dieses Accounts kann von mehreren Bosch-Internen Benutzern verwaltet werden (Unter-Ordner anlegen, ändern, Daten bereitstellen, löschen... - Gruppe bosch-upload-...)
  • Der Webspace kann eine längere Vorhaltezeit für Daten bieten z.B. 1 oder 2 Jahre.

Diese Rolle kann z.B. dazu verwendet werden:

  • Um Daten durch Bosch-interne Anwender strukturiert bereitzustellen (nicht durch externe Anwender, nur durch Bosch interne Anwender)
  • Mehrere externe oder interne Anwender (Gruppe external-download-... bzw. bosch-download-...) können die Daten bei  Bedarf herunterladen

Hinweis:
Eine Verwaltung von Webspaces (Strukturierte Bereitstellung von Daten) durch externe Benutzer ist nicht zulässig.

bosch-extended-routing

Bitte sprechen Sie uns an (siehe unten), wenn Sie diese Lösung benötigen.

Diese Rolle wird einem internen Account zugewiesen, wenn ein spezielles Routing von Dateien (intern / extern) benötigt wird.

Beispiele:

  • Die Daten werden mit der externen Firma über einen Bosch SFTP oder FTPS Server ausgetauscht
  • Die Daten werden auf einen externen SFTP oder FTPS server kopiert
  • Die Daten werden intern über ein CURL-routing zu einer Anwendung oder in die AZURE Cloud kopiert

Für die Einrichtung von Proxy-Gruppen, Download-Gruppen, Upload-Gruppen oder von besonderen Anwendungsfällen, wenden Sie sich bitte an Dataexchange DXM (CI/POI2)

Power BI Cloud - Access Management

Power BI Cloud is a self-service data analysis tool and it is necessary that any user, who has been granted the appropriate license to provide content in Power BI Cloud to their target groups fully understands the importance of access management and the processes necessary to ensure AIM compliance.


1 - Introduction

1.1 Access Management

Access Management describes the compliant management of access rights i.e.

  • the right target groups
  • get the appropriate access rights
  • after approval of the correct organizational office (clear responsibility)
  • exclusively for the period of the requirement.

In the context of Power BI Cloud, there are two relevant areas in which it is the responsibility of the content provider to implement proper access management

  • when configuring a data source connection to be accessible from within Power BI Cloud
  • when granting access to content inside Power BI Cloud to target groups

Power BI Cloud is a self-service data analysis tool and it is necessary that any user, who has been granted the appropriate license to provide content in Power BI Cloud to their target groups fully understands the importance of access management and the processes necessary to ensure AIM compliance.

In this document all the necessary processes to be AIM compliant are described and any user that has been granted a Power BI Pro license has acknowledged to fully understand and implement these measures when using Power BI Cloud.

The responsibility to ensure AIM compliance lies with the Power BI Pro licensed individual.


1.2 Personal related data / GDPR

Besides the responsibility of the user to ensure AIM compliance, the user also needs to ensure to be compliant in the processing and distribution of personal related data in accordance with the KBV 10.13.

For Power BI Cloud, the following questions need to be considered:

Does your report contain any employee data that can be linked to a specific Bosch employee?

No - my report does not contain any personal related data

Yes - my report does contain personal related data but I have the written consent of the responsible workers council 

Not applicable, because there is no worker’s council in my country and my report doesn’t contain personal data of employees that live in a country where there is a worker’s council


It is not allowed to publish reports that do contain personal data or personal relatable data and don't fall into one of these 3 categories.

In general, the user confirms that their reports do not include data that can be used to control employee performance or attendance data.


2 - Access Management

2.1 On-Premise data sources to be used with Power BI Cloud

Power BI Cloud is a SaaS (Software as a Service) offer by Microsoft and when using Power BI Cloud you are connecting to servers outside the BCN (Bosch Corporate Network) where your data can be stored and is made accessible by the target groups.

If your Power BI Report is using data from a on-premise data source and you need this data to be refreshed on a schedule or you need to create a live connection using DirectQuery it is necessary for this connection to be created inside the BD/DAP4 managed Power BI Enterprise Gateway.

The Power BI Enterprise Gateway enables a secure connection between Power BI Cloud and on-premise data sources residing inside the BCN.

To be able to connect to a on-premise data source from within Power BI Cloud, the following requirements must be met:

  • the data source has been added to the BD/DAP4 Power BI Enterprise Gateway by the Power BI Cloud Team (Gatekeeper)
  • the Power BI Report Admin that wants to use this data source has been granted the access rights to this specific data source


Only when both of these requirements have been met, the data source can be utilized and data inside the Power BI Report in Power BI Cloud can be kept up-to-date.

No other users are able to use these data sources in their Power BI Reports.


2.1.1 Adding a data source to the Enterprise Gateway

The process of adding an on-premise data source to the Enterprise Gateway is as follows:

  1. The Data Source Requestor fills out the Order Form (Data Source Creation Template) and provides all relevant information, i.e.
    1. Information about the data source requestor
    2. All necessary technical information of the data source (i.e. server name, database name, file path, etc.)
    3. Information about the data security classification of the data contained in the data source (only data up to SC-2 is allowed to be used with Power BI Cloud)
    4. Information about personal related data in the data source and if the proper approval has been granted by a workers council if applicable
    5. The Master of Data which will be the Master of Role and must be an organizational office position holder
    6. Data source name that will be used for access management and publicly visible

  2. The Data Source Requestor provides the necessary credentials for this data source via encrypted e-mail
    1. Only technical users can be used when setting up a enterprise gateway data source

  3. The Power BI Cloud Team will perform the following steps
    1. Creation of a Security Group inside the BCD following our internal naming convention and the provided MoR as the owner
    2. Creation of the data source in the BD/DAP4 Power BI Enterprise Gateway using the provided information
    3. Granting access to this data source to the security group that has been created in this process
    4. Informing the user of the created data source and the name of the Security Group


2.1.2 Requesting access to a data source in the Enterprise Gateway

Once the data source has been added to the Power BI Enterprise Gateway by the Power BI Cloud team, a user needs to request access to this data source by following these steps:

  1. The requesting user needs to request access to the Security Group that has been created which will involve the provided MoD/MoR 
  2. Once the user has been granted access to the data source, they are then able to map their data source inside their Power BI Report with this data source

Once the MoD revokes access to the user inside the security group, the user will not be able to utilize this data source for their Power BI Report anymore


2.2 Access to Power BI content in the Power BI Cloud

For each target group, the user utilizes Power BI Workspaces which are logical containers that can contain Power BI Reports, Power BI Dashboards and Power BI Datasets .

From these workspaces, Power BI Report Admins (licensed Power BI Pro users) are able to create "Power BI Apps" which are a subset of the content inside the Power BI Workspace.


2.2.1 Preparing Power BI Content for access by the target groups

To ensure AIM compliance, the user will need to follow these steps to make content available to end users:

  1. Creation of an AIM-compliant security group that will be used for access management for each target group (see Security Groups / Distribution Lists in ITSP)
  2. Creation of the Power BI Apps for the target groups
  3. Granting access to the Power BI App to the target groups by using the AIM-compliant security groups that have previously been created


2.2.2 Requesting access to Power BI content from the target groups

  1. The Power BI Report Admin informs the user of the target group about the Security Group that they need to request access to
  2. The user requests access to this Security Group in the IT Service Portal (see Security Groups / Distribution Lists in ITSP)
  3. The MoR or their configured delegate grants the user access to the security group
  4. The Power BI App will now be visible inside the Power BI App Store inside Power BI Cloud and access is possible

Fair Play Guidelines / Terms and Conditions



TIP: Use Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site.

Didn't find what you were looking for? Click here for our support channels.



By using the Power BI Cloud service offered by BD/DPA-DAP you agree to the following terms and conditions which are subject to change:

1. General

  1. By using the Power BI Cloud offering you are ensuring that your actions are in accordance to the Information Security (CD 02900) and IT Security (CD 07900) central directives
  2. Power BI Cloud is on-boarded to support data up to SC-2, it is not allowed to publish reports that contain SC-3 data to the Power BI Cloud
  3. Reports and datasets published to the Power BI Cloud cannot contain any employee data that can be linked to a specific Bosch employee unless
    1. you have the written consent of the workers council (see KBV 10.13)
    2. there is no workers council in your country and your data does not contain personal data of employees that live in a country where a workers' council is present
  4. Reports and datasets published to the Power BI Cloud cannot contain data that can be used for employee performance and attendance data

2. Licensing

  1. Every user at Bosch has been granted a Power BI (Free) license automatically
  2. A Power BI Pro license can only be ordered and assigned to a personal account
  3. It is not allowed to have a Power BI Pro license assigned to a resource account
    1. Account sharing is strictly forbidden
    2. Any user that needs to have access to Pro features needs to get an own license
    3. Power BI Pro licenses can only be assigned to personal accounts
  4. License cost is charged by the full month independently of the actual date a user had a license assigned or unassigned

3. Subscriptions

  1. It is not allowed to share your subscription with other users
    1. you need to be admin of all workspaces that your subscription holds at all times
  2. The subscription holder is responsible for all workspaces assigned to their subscription
  3. Workspace assignments can only be ordered by the subscription owner themselves
  4. Any violation of our terms and conditions in one workspace of a subscription will affect all associated workspaces
    1. i.e. if your subscription shows unusual high CPU or refresh activity, all associated workspaces will be removed from Premium until the issue is resolved
  5. Your subscription will be upgraded to the next level automatically if your resource consumption is unusually high (paid-for subsriptions) or we will temporarily remove your workspaces from shared Premium capacities until the dataset has been optimized

4. Premium Capacities

It is important to understand that with Premium Gen2 we have almost no limitation in the size of your datasets but it all comes down to CPU time. Larger datasets lead to more CPU consumption, bad data models lead to high CPU consumption. Bad DAX formulas lead to high CPU consumption.

To ensure enough CPU power for all users at Bosch, you need to follow our terms of use for Power BI. Failure to do so will lead to removal from Premium. 

  • 4.1. Refresh

    1. The sum of all scheduled refreshes should not take more than 120 minutes in a 24 hour window
    2. Workspaces that run refresh operations that cause high CPU cost and therefore a throttling of Premium capacities will be removed from Premium immediately until the workspace admin has changed the frequency of their scheduled refreshes
    3. you are not allowed to trigger dataset refreshes via api to workaround the timeout limits or maximum number of refreshes
    4. when using PowerAutomate or other tools to trigger a dataset refresh, the maximum number of refreshes must be 48 or less per day
    5. Make use of Incremental Refreshs for your large tables whenever possible. This will reduce refresh time drastically
    6. If your data source is extremely slow blocking our refresh capacities for too long you need to extract the data outside of Power BI by using i.e. Knime or any other ETL technology and access the extracted data

  • 4.2. Dataset size

    1. It is not allowed to split datasets into smaller chunks in order to work-around our dataset limit sizes
      1. i.e. If you have a 100 MB dataset you can not split it into 5 files with 20 MB each to stay in the Tier 0 capacity
    2. Dataset size is the only parameter that we can actually control, but if your dataset is causing a high CPU consumption we will upgrade your subscription to the next level (paid-for subscriptions) or temporarily remove your workspaces from shared Premium capacities until the dataset has been optimized
    3. It is your obligation to REMOVE all unused columns from your dataset, regardless of your Tier-Subscription. Any unused columns in your dataset cause unnecessary CPU and Memory consumption which are the cause for bad performance and large size. Columns can be added to datasets when necessary at a later stage
    4. Make use of Cloud features like Aggregations, Composite Datamodels, Incremental Refreshs, Hybrid Tables, etc. to ensure minimum CPU usage

  • 4.3. Overloading

    1. If our monitoring shows unusually high CPU consumption from your workspaces causing Overload of our Premium capacities, we will remove your workspace from Premium until you have improved your data model / user activity
    2. Overloading can not be tolerated as this affects all Power BI users with throttled performance (read more about overloading here: Power BI Premium Gen2 capacity load, overload, and autoscale - Power BI | Microsoft Docs )

  • 4.4. Embedding

    1. you can utilize Power BI Premium to embed content into your applications
    2. It is not allowed to use our shared Premium capacities to embed content for external customers

      1. You need to use Azure Power BI Embedded at your own expense to embed content for external customers


Pro workspaces

You are always free to revert your workspace to Pro and get licenses for all your users - with "Pro" workspaces, the above terms and conditions do not apply but the restrictions on Pro workspaces by Microsoft.

5. Power BI Desktop

  1. If there's a change in computers, or Power BI Desktop won't be used any further, users have to perform the uninstallation through IT Service Portal. 
  2. Power BI Desktop installations are only supported on Bosch managed Windows machines. 
  3. Installation has to be done through IT Service Portal.
    1. Please be aware that a manual installation may lead to increased security risk.
    2. Manual installations of Power BI Desktop are neither supported nor maintained by Power BI Team.

5.1. Forbidden Actions Power BI Desktop

  1. It is not allowed to use data which exceeds the platform limitation of SC2.
  2. Only the official Power BI Desktop version available through IT Service Portal is compliant with Bosch Guidelines.


Power BI Desktop users automatically agree to the Terms of Use and Performance Best Practices when using the product.

6. Automated processing of data outside of Power BI

  1. It is not allowed to schedule automated data exports with outside tools, i.e. Power Automate
    1. automated data exports cause a high resource consumption
    2. Instead of mass-exporting data educate your users to access the Power BI Cloud reports and dashboards directly
  2. Power BI Cloud is not to be seen as an intermediary database to hold data for further processing, use Power BI Cloud for data analysis


We closely monitor our Premium capacities for users and operations that interrupt our service and we reserve the right to remove your workspace from shared Premium capacities at any time without prior notification if there is any suspicious activity that might impact other users
