OpenDXM roles and permissions

The permissions in OpenDXM are managed by using roles that are assigned via the IdM system.


Definition of internal / external users:

Internal user

Employees of the Bosch Group (including those with an email prefix like “fixed-term”, “external”) that access OpenDXM within the Bosch Group.

External user

Business partners of the Bosch Group who access OpenDXM via the internet.

Rules and naming convention of the roles:

internal-…            
bosch-…

is only assigned to internal users.

external-…is only assigned to external users.

Roles that can be assigned to OpenDXM users are listed below:

Role

Explanation

internal-users

Standard role for all internal users. With this role, it is possible to send data to internal and external business partners.

external-users

Standard role for all external users. With this role, it is possible to send data to internal users.

With this role, it is not possible to select other external users as recipients and send data to them.

bosch-proxy-[XYZ]

Several internal users can be put together into a "proxy group".

If a member of the proxy group receives data, all members of the proxy group will be informed.

All members of the proxy group can view and download the data.

external-proxy-[XYZ]

Several external users from the same company can be put together into a proxy group.

Users from different companies may not be in the same proxy group.

If a member of the proxy group receives data, all members of the proxy group will be informed.

All members of the proxy group can view and download the data.

bosch-download-[XYZ]

Several internal users can be put together into a "download group".

All members of the download group can view and download data sent to a specific internal user.

Unlike the proxy group:

  • the members of the download group are not informed when new data is available for download.
  • the group members cannot view the data that has been sent to other members of the download group.

To view the data that has been sent to another person, select "Webspaces" in the navigation bar and click on the corresponding name.

external-download-[XYZ]

Several external users can be put together into a "download group".

All members of the download group can view and download data sent to a specific external user.

Business partners of different companies may be members of this group.

Unlike the proxy group:

  • the members of the download group are not informed when new data is available for download.
  • the group members cannot view the data that has been sent to other members of the download group.

To view the data that has been sent to another person, select "Webspaces" in the navigation bar and click on the corresponding name.

bosch-upload-[XYZ]

This group is being used to restrict the upload to a specific recipient.

Only members of this group can send data to the specific recipient.

no_email_notification

Members of this group do not receive any emails from OpenDXM:
You will not be informed by email when data is sent to you.
You are also not informed if you are in a proxy group and data is sent to other proxy group members.

By default (without this role), the sender and recipient are informed when data has been completely transmitted (sent) or received.

proxy-no_email_notification

Optional additional role (group) for proxy group members.
Members of this group are not informed by e-mail CC when data is sent to other proxy group members.

By default (without this role), each proxy group member is informed via Email-CC.

bosch-restapi-users

With this role, data can be sent automatically from a program within the Bosch Group.

An automated download is currently not possible.

Further information can be found at OpenDXM REST APIs.

external-restapi-users

With this role, data can be sent automatically from a program ouside the Bosch Group.

An automated download is currently not possible.

Further information can be found at OpenDXM REST APIs.

bosch-batch-transfer

This role is only assigned to batch accounts (User-ID batch_...). It enables to send data from  NFS file shares to registered OpenDXM users in an automated way.

For more information, see Automated file transfers to or from business partners.

bosch-extended-webspace

 Please contact us (see below) if you require this solution.

This role indicates an account with extended webspace options:

  • In the webspace of this account, further subfolders can be created (manually) to provide data in a folder structure.
  • The webspace of this account can be managed by several Bosch internal users (create, change, provide data, delete subfolders...). - Group bosch-upload-...)
  • The webspace can have a longer data retention reriod, e.g. 1 or 2 years.

This role can be used, for example:

  • To provide data by Bosch internal users in a structured way (not by external users, only by Bosch internal users)
  • Multiple external or internal users (group:  external-download-... or bosch-download-... ) can download the data if required

Note:
Webspace management (Structured provisioning of data) by external users is not allowed.

bosch-extended-routing

Please contact us (see below) if you require this solution.

This role is assigned to an internal account when special routing of files (internal / external) is required.

Examples:

  • The data is exchanged with the external company via a Bosch SFTP or FTPS server.
  • The data is copied to an external SFTP or FTPS server.
  • The data is copied internally via CURL routing to an application or to the AZURE Cloud.


To assign an OpenDXM role to your OpenDXM account, follow the instructions here.

To request the creation of proxy groups, download groups, upload groups or special use cases, contact us on Dataexchange DXM (CI/POI2)

Enterprise Gateway - Data Source Management

Once you went through the process of having your on-premise data source created in the Power BI Enterprise Gateway, please follow this guideline on how to use it in Power BI Cloud.

Mapping your data source to your data set

If you have been granted access to an Enterprise Data Gateway connection, you are able to map a connection in your dataset with this data source.

After you have published your Power BI Report into your workspace in the cloud, go into the settings of your dataset by clicking on the three dots and choosing "Settings"

You should be seeing a list of the connections used in your dataset and can choose from the drop down menu the correct gateway connection to map this connection to.

If you don't see anything here, you either haven't been granted access to this gateway connection by the Master of Role or your connection string doesn't match the connection string from the Gateway. It must be identical to be able to map a connection!

Once you have mapped the data source from your dataset with a gateway connection, don't forget to click on Apply!


Getting access to a gateway connection

If one of your colleagues has already created a gateway connection in the Enterprise Gateway, they can provide you with the name of the Security Group used for access management of this data source.

Go to IT Service Portal / Security Groups Order Form and search for the name of the security group that you have been provided in the search box

After you found the security group, fill out all mandatory information to request access to this data source. The WOM-office holder that has been provided as the Master of Data for this data source or one of the delegates they might have configured will be able to process your request and grant access to the data source.

If you get granted access to the security group, you will be able to map your data sources to this data set


Why do I not see any gateways in the "Manage Gateways" section of Power BI?

The manage gateway section will generelly only show gateways that you are the administrator of. When requesting a data source to be added to the Bosch enterprise gateway, you will not be granted administrative rights to the gateway.

To be able to use the data source that we created for you in the gateway it is not necessary.

If your dataset contains any data source that has not been added to the gateway yet or you do not have access to the already created gateway this message will also show! 

FAQs

  • I don't see the gateway connections in my dataset settings
    • You either haven't been granted access to the gateway connection
    • or your connection string doesn't match the connection string from the gateway connection
    • or there are other on-premise data sources not have gateway connection yet.
  • My dataset can refresh successfully in the past, but now it isn't able to refresh
    • First, please self-check the error message by yourself. Take below screenshot for example, you could understand what's wrong by yourself.

    • There are lots of reason causing dataset refresh failure.
      • Password of connection user id expired
      • Permission of connection user id removed/expired
      • Data source did some changes, e.g. column/field type change
      • Refresh timeout
      • Too many dataset running at same time
      • Gateway server isn't stable
    • You could provide your connection id in SMT ticket for "Power BI Cloud" service.

  • Do all data sources need a gateway connection?
    • No - only on premise data sources. If you are using flat files on a file share or a Bosch Sharepoint, we strongly recommend you migrate these files to Sharepoint Online which will allow you to use these data sources without the need for a gateway connection

ECU Migration - User cleanup

OpenDXM needs to be compliant with the Bosch CD 2900 A.9.4.2 (4) and has to enable MFA (Multi Factor Authentication) for external business partners.

At Bosch there'a standard user type available that supports MFA, it's called ECU (External Colaboration User).

Currently OpenDXM uses IDM/WAM users without MFA support. These users need to be migrated to ECU.

To be able to migrate the users it's essential to have the correct department and the correct cost center of a user, but this data is quite old and most of this data hasn't been maintained in the last years.


On 2024-04-16 the OpenDXM team started to inform the Bosch internal data exchange contacts to check the department and cost center of their external business partners.

If there are any questions concerning the migration, this page tries to answer them.


Sent email:

User_cleanup_template.html

1. Questions and Answers

1.1. What exactly needs to be done (in short)?

  1. Please check with the other recipients to which department the user should belong.
  2. check department and cost center.
    1. If both are correct, no further actions are required.
    2. if department or cost center needs to be updated, please forward the email to "IT Service Desk" and ask to adjust the departmentn and / or cost center of the User-ID in IdM.

1.2. It seems the user data is wrong

There was a problem with some accounts getting / showing the correct personal data - this has been fixed and new emails have been sent for these accounts.
Affected users can be found in the attached list:

user_check_to_be_resent.txt

1.3. All recipients are shown twice

It was necessary to address the email to "userid@bosch.com" and to the registered Bosch email.
Reason: To reach all recicpients, we have to use both addresses:

  • Not all user-ids have an AD account. In this case we have to use the registered email address..
  • Not all email addresses are valid. In this case we have to use userid@bosch.com.

1.4. Does the user cleanup affect Bosch accounts or internal accounts of external business partners?

No, the user migration and cleanup only affects external business partner who access OpenDXM from the internet.
Bosch Internal users will not notice any change using OpenDXM.

1.5. UAES associates are listed to be checked

UAES associates are treated as external business partners, but they login in from Bosch with internal accounts. These accounts are up to date. There's no need to check or adjust these accounts.

The Product and Service Manager for the Office Store is Prommersberger Karin (BD/WPA-WCS4)
Proxy: Mitschelen Tanja-Iris (BD/WPA-WCS4)  


The Office Store is your "Add-In" store for Microsoft 365 Office products.

Add-Ins are mini applications that extend what you can do (for example: eForms NG in PowerPoint) with the following tools:

Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Sharepoint, Teams, MS Project and PowerBI


QuestionAnswer
Is the "Office Store" automatically available on my computer?
Yes, it is included in the above mentioned tools.
How do I get an Add-in?
Office applications - Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook

Via the integrated "Office Store". You are able to find this in all the above mentioned tools by clicking on the Add-in tile in the 'Home' tab, here for example in Excel:

In the overlay you will see all approved Add-Ins for Bosch that are available for you. To install one, select it and click on 'Add' (sometimes additional entries need to be made).


Please note:

If you are using the web clients, the menu tile for choosing Add-ins is also located in the Home ribbon:

Microsoft Teams

Click on the Apps tile on the left to open the catalog.

Available Add-ins can be added directly to your chat or channel, those marked with a padlock are not available (please see here for more information how to request an Add-in for Teams).

How do I Sign in to the Office Store?

To Sign in and enable the Office Store, you need to Sign in to at least one Office application.

You can find the Sign in in each Office application under 'File' → 'Account' (1). Click on 'Sign in' (2), enter your Username in the form NT-ID@bosch.com (e.g. abc1fe@bosch.com) (3) and select 'Next' (4)

Here for example in PowerPoint:

How can I request for a new/missing Add-in to make it available in the Office Store?

Follow the steps as described here: How to get a new Office Store Add-in (incl. Teams)

The Add-In is not available even though I am authorized to use it - what went wrong?
  1. Please be aware that it can take up to 48 hours for an Add-in to be visible after you have been added to the list of authorized users. Please make sure enough time has elapsed.
  2. Make sure your mailbox is no longer on-premise but already migrated to the cloud (Exchange Online).
How can I tell which Add-ins are already available in MS Teams?

When you open the App overview in MS Teams, you can search for Add-ins. The overview will show both those Add-ins that are available for you as well as those that could be made available by completing the onboarding process. The latter can be identified through the small lock symbol in the bottom left corner of the icon.

If you click on one of the locked Add-ins, you will see a button to request the onboarding for this Add-in.

Please note:

Just clicking on the request button will just take you to the description of the onboarding process which, of course, you can initiate: https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/CYKhag

There will, however, be no automatic start of the onboarding process!

Why does it say the Add-in store is disabled?

When opening the Office Store in Word, Excel... you will get a notification that the Add-in store has been disabled.

This just means that you will see only the Add-ins that have been made available to you by the admins (e.g. SAP Analytics in the screenshot), but cannot 'shop' for Add-ins that have not been onboarded yet. 

Please note:
In Teams you can see all Add-ins that are potentially available. However, you can only use those that do not have a small padlock sign in their icon (cf. this FAQ entry).
How can I get support for issues with an Add-In?
The Overview of available Add-Ins contains a column 'Support' where you can find out who to contact.
What is the difference between an App and an Add-In?

An App is the Office or Microsoft 365 product on its own like "Teams", "PowerPoint", "Whiteboard", etc.

An Add-In is a mini application within the product that can extend what you can do with it, or even give better support like for example 'eForms NG' in PowerPoint.

The Add-in overview in Power Point does not load - what can I do?

Depending on different factors, there is a possibility that the Add-in overview does not complete loading on your secondary monitor - this will look like this:

You are asked to wait but the window will not complete loading (normally you should be able to see the available Add-ins within 2-3 seconds).

In order to fix this, go to File > Options. In the General tab select 'Optimize for compatibility' (section User Interface options). You will have to close and re-open PowerPoint for this to take effect.

Migration Guide

Draft

This content is not up-to-date anymore. You can still read it for basic knowledge and valuable information about migrating existing Reports to the Cloud




If you have been using Power BI at Bosch before the Power BI Cloud EAN you might already have created Power BI Reports and shared those with other users at Bosch, either with publishPowerBI or on another Power BI Report Server.

This means, you are already familiar with Power BI and are now curious on how you can add all these new cool features from Power BI Cloud to your existing solution!


The way you work with Power BI Report Server (publishPowerBI) and Power BI Cloud is similar in many ways and completely different in some and that's why there might be a lot of confusion on your end at first.

But don't worry - we got you covered! This migration guide will help you to get your current reports to the cloud and understand the processes that are new and different.


This guideline's target audience is the users, that create and share content with other users at Bosch.

In the first part of this guide, we will talk about the initial things that you need to do to be "Power BI Cloud Enabled". In the second part you will learn how to work with Power BI Cloud and share content with others.


1. Initial Setup

To get started with Power BI Cloud, you will need to perform the following steps:

  • Assign Microsoft Power BI Desktop (Cloud) to your computer
  • Order a Power BI Pro License in the IT Service Portal
  • Order a Power BI Subscription


1.1. Power BI Desktop

As you have previously already been using Power BI Desktop at Bosch, you will have a version of Power BI Desktop on your computer that is a special version for the Power BI Report Server. 

The Power BI Report Server only supports a subset of the functionality of Power BI Cloud and therefore the Power BI Desktop must match the features available on the on-premise Report Server.

You can identify this Power BI Desktop Version by the color of the icon which is black:


For the cloud, you will need to install an additional Power BI Desktop client to your computer, specific for Power BI Cloud. To do so, go to the IT Service Portal and assign the Power BI Desktop Cloud package to your computer.

Detailed instuctions for this are available in the "Get Access to Power BI" documentation "Installation & Download" Option 2. 


Once the installation has been successful on your computer, you will find a second Power BI Desktop installed on your computer with a yellow icon:


This will be the software to use when you want to prepare and publish content to the cloud. 

Important

You can use Power BI Desktop Cloud to open and edit files that you have previously created with Power BI Desktop (May 2020).

It is NOT possible, to use a Power BI File that has been opened or created with Power BI Desktop (Cloud) ! If you want to be able to continue using a report for Power BI Report Server, be sure to make a copy of the file before you open it with Power BI Desktop Cloud!

There is a warning when you open a file with Power BI Desktop Cloud that has been created with Power BI Desktop (May 2020)

When you see this warning, you can still close the file without saving it. If you save the file it will not be possible to use it with Power BI Report Server anymore!


When using Power BI Desktop Cloud, always sign-in using your NT-User@bosch.com


1.2. Power BI Pro License

To make content available to other users it is necessary to have a Pro license. The Pro license will allow you to do the following:

  • Create workspaces
  • Access workspaces
  • Create Power BI Apps
  • Publish reports into workspaces


I will go into detail about a workspace in the following chapters, but as a first step please follow the instructions in the Get Access to Power BI Cloud Option #2 to initiate the process of the Pro-License order.

Once you order the Pro license, the following processes take place in the background:

  • An order is placed in the IT Service portal
  • Your line manager has to approve the Power BI Pro license order
  • Once the manager has approved the order, our team will assign your user to the group of users that will be assigned a Pro license
  • After successful sync between the Bosch Corporate Directory and the Azure Active Directory you're ready to go!
    • this might take up to 4 hours after you receive an email from us about the order fulfilment


Until you have a Power BI Pro license assigned to your account or if you just want to use Power BI Cloud without sharing to other users, you can make use of the "My Workspace" area in Power BI to get to know Power BI already!


1.3. Power BI Subscription

The Power BI Subscription is the core element of our Power BI Cloud EAN offering and also the most difficult element to understand for most of the users of Power BI.

1.3.1. Workspaces

Workspaces are one of the key elements of Power BI Cloud and necessary for collaboration.

A workspace in Power BI is a logical container that contains your datasets, reports and dashboards. The concept of datasets and dashboards is a key feature of Power BI Cloud and doesn't exist in the Power BI Report Server, I will explain these in one of the following chapters in detail.

In the Microsoft 365 eco-system, any Microsoft 365 Group is also a Power BI Workspace. Microsoft 365 Groups are a concept used all over the place at Bosch, initially with Teams (1 Team in Teams = 1 M365 Group), and since November additionally with SharePoint Online (1 M365 Group = 1 SharePoint Online).

Therefore, you will already see all the Teams and SharePoint Onlines that you have access to in the list of Workspaces in Power BI. These Workspaces can also be used for Power BI! 

Power BI itself has introduced an own concept of workspaces that is not connected to M365 Groups anymore. So whenever you create a new workspace in Power BI itself, this is not a M365 group anymore. 

M365 groups and Power BI Workspaces behave a little differently in Power BI and as a best practice you should not use your Teams M365 Groups in Power BI unless you convert them to a Power BI Workspace (How to do this will be explained another time, just stick with the new workspaces for now)


To understand workspaces in Power BI I like to use the analogy of the "Kitchen". The workspace is the kitchen and only the "Cooks" - that are the admins/key users that prepare the "food" (Power BI content to share) - should be granted access there. 

As a best practice - don't add the target users of your reports to the workspace. Use Power BI Apps instead. 


1.3.2. Initial Concept of Microsoft using Pro-Licenses

The initial concept by Microsoft for Power BI Cloud was the following:

  • Anybody can use Power BI and publish content into their personal "My Workspace" 
  • If you want to use collaboration features of Power BI, you need to create a workspace and grant access to this workspace to other users
  • To access workspaces, you need a Pro license
    • Every user that you want to share reports with therefore will also need a Pro license
  • The content is stored on shared capacities within the MIcrosoft data centers
  • infrastructure cost that comes with more users is covered by the Pro license fee → more users, more licenses, more budget for Microsoft to increase the Hardware behind Power BI


This setup is feasible for a small company with a limited amount of users to share reports with. At Bosch, we might want to share content with all users at Bosch - this would mean, we need a license for every user at Bosch!

Luckily, Microsoft introduced the so called "Power BI Premium" and changed the possibility to share content with your users and added some more features on top of that.

1.3.3. Power BI Premium

Power BI Premium capacities are dedicated resources that belong to the customer and start with something called "P1". For those who are interested - A P1 capacity consists of 25 GB Cache and 8 CPUs. Since Power BI is an in-memory technology, all data that is made available in a report will be loaded into memory and you need CPU power to query and access the content and for processing the source data to prepare it for the reporting with Power BI.

You can have a workspace and all its content inside assigned to a Power BI Premium capacity. Since Bosch is already paying for these resources, there is no additional charging for accessing the content that resides on these capacities. This changes the cost structure from "per user" to "limited resources".


The analysis of over 6.000 reports published with publishPowerBI on premise has shown that 80% of the reports users uploaded are < 10 MB in size and 90% of the reports users uploaded are < 20 MB in size.  These reports have been shared with ~ 60.000 users across Bosch! This shows that 90% of the users that use Power BI at Bosch today have very small demands in resources but a high demand in the number of users they want to share their reports with.


1.3.4. Tier 0 and Tier 1 Subscription

To use Power BI Premium and assign workspaces there you will need to get a Power BI Subscription from our initial offering with either Tier 0 or Tier 1. Details about the Tier-Levels and the differences can be found in the Power BI Platform Overview and Get Access to Power BI Cloud sections of the NGW article of Power BI.

Since Tier 0 is free of charge, go ahead and order yourself a Tier 0 subscription as described in Option #3 in the Get Access to Power BI Cloud documentation. After your manager has approved your request to a Power BI subscription and our team has processed your request you will receive a Power BI Subscription ID.

Please keep the e-mail with this Subscription ID as you will need it to actually assign workspaces to Power BI Premium and unleash the features of Premium like sharing with anybody at Bosch!

1.4. Prepare your reports for the cloud

While you are waiting for the Pro-License and Power BI Subscription order to be processed, you can use this time to prepare your reports for the cloud. If your report is using static data and doesn't need to be refreshed, you are good to go and can skip this step. 

If you want the data inside your report to be refreshed on a schedule or you are using a live-connection to an on-premise data source, there are some preparations to be done. 

Power BI Cloud is located OUTSIDE the BCN (Bosch Corporate Network) and if your report is using an on-premise data source like for example:

  • Flat-Files (Excel, CSV, Json, etc.) located on either the Bosch-Sharepoint on-premise or a windows-fileshare or
  • a connection to a relational database like Oracle (REDlake), SQL Server, or MySQL located in the BCN or
  • connecting to a Web API like Track&Release


the report will not be able to access these data sources as access to these data sources from outside the BCN is not possible. 

Does this mean you are not able to use these data sources with Power BI Cloud???

No  There are solutions to these use-cases, some are quite easy and some require some one-time preperation but let's start with the easy one!

1.4.1. Use SharePoint Online

If you are using Flat-Files like Excel that are located in SharePoint you will need to start using SharePoint Online. SharePoint Online is already available to you when you are using Teams or you can just order a SharePoint Online following the instructions here: SharePoint Online

We have prepared detailed instructions on how to migrate your On-Premise data sources easily to SharePoint Online. If you use SharePoint Online it is the easiest and most convenient way to use Power BI Cloud right away!

Click here Power BI Cloud SharePoint Online Migration

This is a one-time activity for your existing reports and for new reports you will see it's so simple to use SharePoint Online, you will never want to use anything else again  

We understand that not all use-cases can be migrated, if this is the case see the next chapter on what you need to do


1.4.2. Enabling access to on-premise data sources

From our experiences with the pilots before we started the Power BI Cloud EAN and also from the first weeks into the EAN this seems to be the most difficult topic for users to understand since this is a new concept on how to make data available to be used with the cloud.

If you have the chance to use SharePoint Online - please do so, it will make your transition into the cloud very easy!

But some data just needs to stay in the BCN and we got you covered!


To allow Power BI Cloud EAN to access data in the BCN, there is a software called "POWER BI ENTERPRISE GATEWAY" which can send data to Power BI Cloud EAN for data sources that have been configured by our team.

In simple words, it works like this:

  • The Enterprise Gateway is located inside the BCN and has network access to all data sources located within the BCN as you have when using Power BI Desktop on your laptop
  • The Enterprise Gateway has access to Power BI Cloud EAN via an encrypted secure connection (SSL) 
  • In the Enterprise Gateway, our team is able to add a data source and therefore securely grant access to the data inside that data source
  • Once a data source has been configured inside the enterprise gateway by our team, access to this particular gateway connection is granted to the Power BI user that requested the data source to be added to the gateway following this process
  • The Power BI user that has access to this configured data source is able to map his Power BI Dataset with this gateway connection
  • Whenever the dataset in Power BI Cloud is being refreshed, the Enterprise gateway will collect the data from the on-premise dataset and send it to the cloud where it is being processed
  • After successful refresh of the dataset, the report contains the latest data

This is a ONE-TIME process for each data source you want to use in Power BI Cloud. Once it has been setup, you can re-use this connection for all reports that use this data source!


Setting up a gateway connection to an on-premise data source can ONLY be done by the Power BI Cloud Team!

When previously publishing a report with publishPowerBI and configuring a data source in publishPowerBI - THIS is the part that needs to be done for you by our team now. This is a main difference in using Power BI Cloud with on-premise data sources.

Remember - it's a one-time process for each data source. 



1.4.2.1. Oracle data source

Let's take a very common data source with Power BI at Bosch - Oracle. 

Your report is connecting to one or more tables inside an Oracle database. When you built that report using Power BI Desktop at some point you were asked to configure that connection to the Oracle DB by providing

  • the server name - usually this is something like abctest123.world
  • and your credentials to the database - these are NOT your windows-credentials 
    • a username
    • a password

For our team to configure this data source in the enterprise gateway, it looks something like this:


Therefore, to connect to the Oracle DB, all you need to provide is the Servername (this must be a TNS-Name like abctest123.world), the username and the password.

Please don't provide your PERSONAL username and password that you have been provided, but request a TECHNICAL user that has read-only access to your Oracle database with a password that doesn't automatically expire!


1.4.2.2. Microsoft SQL Server

Almost the same as with the Oracle data source, except for the following differences:

  • in addition to the servername, you will also need to provide the database name
  • for authentication, you can either use a username and password OR a technical user from the BCD with a username and password


For our team, the configuration looks something like this in the Enterprise Gateway:


1.4.2.3. Windows File-Share

If you are not able to use SharePoint Online, for example because your data source is automatically putting files into a fileshare every night, we will need the following information from you:

  • The fully qualified data source path of your source files
    • pick the folder that includes ALL files if possible (it will also include the subfolders and all files within the subfolders)
  • The credentials of a technical user that has access to this folder


For our team it will look something like this to configure:




Once you have followed the process and we have added your data source to the Enterprise Gateway you are ready to go for the cloud! But don't worry, while you are waiting for your data source to be setup in the cloud, you can already prepare things in the cloud!

2. Setting up things in Power BI Cloud

2.1. Create a workspace

If you have ordered a Pro license and it has been assigned to you, you are now able to create a workspace. To create a workspace, simply click on "Workspaces" in the left navigation pane of Power BI Cloud and then the "Create Workspace" button

In the following screen, you are asked to name your new workspace and have the option to use a logo for it. When naming a workspace, use a name that easily describes the content and purpose of that workspace. Remember, you can create ONE Power BI App from a workspace that can include many reports, so the scope of that workspace must be matching the target audience of your Power BI App. It's also fine to have a workspace containing only one report. Not all content inside a workspace must be used for the Power BI App!

The name you are using for your workspace will only be visible to whoever has been granted access to the workspace - the Power BI App can have a completely different name.

Granting access to your workspace

Consider the workspace as the "kitchen" where you are the "chef" and prepare the "food" (reports) for your customers (users). It is not necessary and might even be confusing for the end-users of your report if you grant access to the workspace to them. 

  • they will see the workspace in their list of workspaces, but won't be able to access it without having a Pro-License
  • Inside the workspace, you might be using technical names for your reports
  • Users that have access to your workspace might be able to add, delete or modify content or your Power BI App and even download your raw Power BI files which might give them access to data inside your file that you didn't intend


As a rule of thumb - you should only grant access to your workspace to your delegates that should be able to update, support and maintain your Power BI App during your absence. Compared to publishPowerBI, this is comparable with the Report Admins.


Now that you have created the workspace, you will also be able to publish content directly to this workspace from within Power BI Desktop!


2.2. Publishing your report into your workspace

You are not ready to publish your report into that workspace that you just created. To do this, there are two options:

  • Use the web-browser to upload the file
  • Publish the file directly from Power BI Desktop Cloud

It is recommended to publish directly from Power BI Desktop Cloud into your workspaces. When using the web-browser, Power BI will add an unnecessary "Dashboard" into your workspace that you will need to delete. 

Publishing a report into your workspace is easy - Open your PBIX file with Power BI Desktop Cloud (yellow icon) and click on the "Publish" button in the top home ribbon:

If you are currently not signed-in with your Bosch Microsoft Account, please do so as described before.

You will be presented all the workspaces that you have write-access to. Select the workspace you just created and click on "Select"

Depending on your report size and internet connection this might take some time.

If you already have a report with the same name deployed to this workspace, you will be asked if you want to overwrite this file.

After the upload is complete, you will see a message and are able to follow the link to this report in Power BI Cloud



Congratulations! You successfully published your report into your workspace. Now it's time to configure your dataset to allow a scheduled-refresh of your data.

2.3. Setting up a Power BI App 

This is one of the new concepts on how to share your reports across the company that once you understood it it's fun and easy and your users will love it too!

A Power BI App is the seperation of the presentation layer that you prepare for your users from the "WORK"-spaces. Coming back to the "Cook" and "Kitchen" example - the Power BI App is the dining room where you present some of the content/food from your kitchen in a nice and tasty way to your customers.

It's also the way to make Power BI content available to your users without the need for a license!

You can actually compare the idea of Power BI Apps like apps you have on your iPhone. There is an AppStore where you browse for apps that are available to you and you pick the ones you like and install it to your phone.

The same thing users at Bosch will do in the Power BI AppStore which is called the AppSource: They see all apps that they have been granted access to and can pick the ones they are interested in and install them to their Power BI.


When using a Power BI Subscription and Power BI Apps, users don't need a Pro-License to use Power BI Reports!


2.3.1. Select content to be part of your Power BI App

But before they can do so, you will need to prepare the Power BI App for them. There can be ONE Power BI App per ONE Workspace. A Power BI App must contain at least one report or dashboard from this workspace, but it is not necessary to make every report or dashboard inside your workspace available to the users!

When you go inside your workspace, you will see all the reports and datasets that you have published and a little switch next to them that says "Include in app". Per default, all reports that you have published into a workspace are marked to be included in the app.

You can have many versions of your report in a workspace, maybe you have continued working on a report and have three or four versions in the workspace. Select the content that you actually want to share with your users by flipping the switch to "Yes".



2.3.2. Create the app

Then in the top right corner click on the button that says "CREATE APP". 



This will lead you to the app creation process that contains of three steps:

  • Setup
  • Navigation
  • Permissions


2.3.2.1. Setup

In this section you describe your Power BI App that will be visible to the users when browsing the AppSource. 

NameDescription
App nameThe name of your app that will be shown in the AppSource. Choose a name that will easily indicate to the users what the content of this app will be.
Use something catchy that users will use when they refer to that Power BI App.
DescriptionThis text will be shown underneath the App name in the AppSource and further describes the purpose and content of the app. 
Try to use a one-sentence description to describe your app. If the text is too long it will be truncated in the AppSource.
Support SiteIf you prepared some documentation about your Power BI reports, add the URL here. This could be i.e. some docupedia page or connect community. 
The link to the support site is accessible to users when using the Power BI App!
App logoUse a little catchy icon to "brand" your Power BI App and give it a nice look in the App overview of your users. 
If you don't use one, it will just have a default icon from Power BI.
App theme colorWhen using the app this color will be used in the navigation and the surrounding frame of your reports.
Choose a color that comes closest to the colors you are using in the report
Contact informationBy default, your name will be shown as the contact for this app.
If you have a support-email address for this app, a distribution list or another contact enter it here


Once you are done with the initial setup, click on the "Navigation" tab next to Setup



2.3.2.2. Navigation

In the navigation section, you define how users can browse through the content that you bundled in this Power BI App. 

When using publishPowerBI, users open one report and see all the different report pages as little tabs at the bottom of the report that allows them to navigate through the different report pages.

In a Power BI App, you have different options on how you want users to interact with your content.


To the left, you will see the reports that you have included in the App and can change the order that they will be displayed. Per default, the sorting order is alphabetical, but you can change the order in a way that is more intuitive for the users.

On the right side "Report Details" you can change the name of your reports to a user-friendly non-technical name. Give your reports some nice friendly name, don't use CamelCase or similiar techie stuff. The users of your Power BI App will thank you!

By clicking on "+ New" you can add sections or links to that navigation! In my example, I have two demo-reports and one report that contains information and created two corresponding sections. After adding sections, assign reports to them in the report details section.



And you can even add a link to another application at Bosch! Maybe you want users to have the opportunity to jump to a specific URL !



Once you have prepared the navigation, let's jump to the Permissions section.


2.3.2.3. Permissions

The permissions part of the Power BI App is vital to understand because mistakes here might exploit your report or data inside your report in a way that you didn't intend. So pay good attention now 


2.3.2.3.1. Access

In the access-section enter the users that you want to publish content to. You have access to any WOM-group that is present in the corporate directory and it's easy to find them by just starting to type the name of them.

If I want to share content with my department, I will type CI/DAP4 until I see the exact WOM group I want to share content with. Users who are part of this WOM group will be able to install this App from the AppSource.


You can also use IDM2BCD-Groups or managed Security Groups from the IT Service Portal. See Access Management for more information.

It is possible to add named users here. This is OK for some functional testing, but once you go live with your Power BI App and share it with a larger audience you need to follow the processes described in the Access Management section for compliance at Bosch!


2.3.2.3.2. Allow everyone who has app access to

The selections you make here are important in regards to data security and you should read this information carefully


Per default, a Power BI App will allow users that have access to the App access to the underlying datasets. When users have access to the underlying datasets, they will be able to build their own reports on your data model and data.

With this checkbox enabled, users will have full access to ALL data inside all datasets of this Power BI App, even if in your report you are now showing all the data. 

Make sure that this is your intention! If this is not a problem, make sure that your dataset is user-friendly! Have a clean data model with end-user friendly names. 

If you are not sure what you are doing here, disable this functionality until you have evaluated what this means 


Allowing users to share the app and underlying datasets should also be disabled - you don't want users to share your data with other users that you are not aware of!

Unless the data inside your report is not critical and you explicitly want users to reshare your content, you can enable this.


Click on "CREATE APP" to create the app and after successful creation you will see something like this:



Users that have permission for the app will now be able to install the App from the AppSource or - if you want - you can share the link that is shown to you with the users so that they can immediately start using the app.



Congratulations - your Power BI App is now ready to be shared with your users!


2.3.3. Sharing the app with your users

There are many ways to share content with your users, but let's name a few:


  • Share the link that you just created by e-Mail or Chat
  • Use TEAMS to add a tab inside a Teams Channel and include the Power BI App Content that you want to share
  • Have the user find the app in the AppSource and install it by themselves


2.4. Configuring the dataset to allow a scheduled-refresh of your data

Your app has been published, users can access the app but there is one more thing that you need to take care of... The question is - how can you refresh the data inside your report?

This is one of the hardest to understand parts of Power BI Cloud since it is completely different from how you have done it before using publishPowerBI.

With publishPowerBI you would just go into the Data Source settings and provide all the credentials necessary so that the Power BI Report Server would be able to connect to your data sources and refresh the data at a defined schedule.

Unfortunately, Power BI Cloud is not hosted inside the Bosch Corporate Network and Power BI Cloud is not able to just access your on-premise data sources. The BCN is like Fort Knox and nobody - not even Power BI Cloud - can get into it from the Internet.


If you have followed my instructions and moved your data sources to SharePoint Online - good for you! Power BI can just directly communicate with your data source since they are all in the Microsoft world.


2.4.1. Configuring SharePoint Online data sources

The following steps don't work with Firefox! We don't know why but we are working on it. So before you continue, please use any other browser.


For your dataset, go into the settings



Inside the settings of your dataset, you will be able to configure all data sources included in this dataset.


For SharePoint Online, go into the Data Source credentials section and click on "Edit Credentials". Use the same user that you are using with Power BI (that should have access to your SP Online data source) and thats it. Mission accomplished!


Go back to your workspace and click on the refresh button next to your dataset. After a few moments your dataset should be refreshed and you're good to go.


2.4.2. Configuring On-Premise Data Sources

Configuring the on-premise data sources you are using in your report is actually easy. Prerequisite: You have already created the gateway connection as described in the "Initial Setup" section. 

If you have received an e-mail from our team that your on-prem data source has been added to the Enterprise Gateway, you can go ahead and map your data source to the gateway connection.

To do so, go into the dataset settings:


For each data source used in your Power BI data set, you will see an entry and will be able to map this entry to the gateway connections that you have access to. 


If you DON'T see anything here, this could have the following reasons:

  • You have not been granted access to this data source by the Master of Data provided when creating the data source (if you requested the data source to be added to the gateway, you have automatically been granted access)
  • Your connection string is different from how the data source has been created. Examples:
    • In Oracle you didn't use the TNSNAMES entry like redlake_dwhp.world but instead the full connection string
    • You didn't use the FQDL , SI0VSQL123 instead of SI0VSQL123.de.bosch.com
  • Power BI neeeds to be able to map your data source to a gateway connection, it must be identical !


Once you picked the correct gateway connection to map don't forget to click on the APPLY button!


Congratulations !  Your dataset is ready to be refreshed.


2.4.3. Setting up a schedule

You were able to manually refresh your dataset, but usually you want this to happen on a daily base without the need to click on a button.

In the dataset settings go into the Scheduled Refresh section and configure your schedule:

You are able to configure up to 48 scheduled refreshes. Only set up schedules that match your business need. We actively monitor the refresh operations on our Premium capacities and if we see users allocating a lot of resources by permanently refreshing their data set we will step in contact with the user and support them in finding the right solution for their business case.

If your demands are higher than we might have to upgrade your Tier-Subscription to a higher level.

Microsoft 365 Life Cycle - on hold

Automatic cleanup of unused resources (information mainly for Teams room owners)


Summary

With every room, site or mailbox, the number of resources and account settings are growing in the context of Microsoft 365.
With the help of the Microsoft 365 Life Cycle and its policy, unused resources are cleaned up automatically.

This will be activated at Bosch at a later point in time as we are still clarifying organizational and legal topics. Once activated, we will inform you here in this blogpost.


What is a Microsoft 365 Group?

A Microsoft 365 Group is an object in the Microsoft identity and access management solution “Azure Active Directory” with a list of members and a coupling to dedicated Microsoft 365 services. It is used to manage access to a collection of shared resources and for communication and collaboration.

When you order a Microsoft Teams room, a Microsoft 365 Group is automatically created by Microsoft including:

  • a Microsoft Teams room – a dedicated space for communication and collaboration
  • a SharePoint Online Site – all documents that you upload in the respective Teams room are stored here
  • a shared Outlook Cloud Mailbox – basically the e-mail address of your Teams room, hosted in the Microsoft cloud (Exchange Online)

Together, the above three components are called Microsoft 365 Group.

With a Microsoft 365 Group, you don't have to manually assign permissions to each of these resources. Adding people to the group automatically gives them the permissions they need.



Life Cycle

As many Teams rooms are created every day, the respective number of Microsoft 365 Groups is growing. With the help of a policy unused resources are cleaned up automatically.


How does it work in detail?

When all three parts of a Microsoft 365 Group are inactive for more than 180 days each, an automatic process is triggered to deactivate the whole group as a first step. This means, all parts are not accessible anymore.

As a second step, all components (Microsoft Teams room, SharePoint Online Site and shared Outlook Cloud Mailbox) will be deleted 30 days later.

Inactivity means, e.g., no chatting in a team room, no editing of files, no uploads, etc. Just opening the team room/SharePoint Online Site does not count as an activity, whereas opening a file and downloading count as activities.

E-mail notification

All owners will receive an automatic e-mail notification once the whole group is inactive for 180 days. This notification is sent to the defined Microsoft 365 Group owner(s) in total three times: 30 days, 15 days and 1 day prior to the deletion date.

The e-mail contains a button to directly renew the counter, i.e. set back to 180 days.

How can I restore a deactivated group?

When the group has been deactivated you can restore it within the next 30 days. To do so, please contact the IT Service Desk (3311).

Note: After the deletion date, a group with all its components cannot be restored and is gone forever.


Special case: shared Outlook Cloud Mailbox

As stated above, the shared mailbox is part of a Microsoft 365 Group and created automatically. Currently, it is not in use at Bosch. We are clarifying the usage and the maintenance of this mailbox.


How to delete a Microsoft 365 Group?

To delete a Microsoft 365 Group with all its components, you have to be a team owner. Then, open the settings of your team in Microsoft Teams to delete it. Detailed information about how to close a team can be found in this description.

Production


Tips & Tricks for Recording

TIP 1: FRAMING

  • Shoot in landscape mode. Wide, horizontal film formats correspond to the natural human field of view. Landscape format is ideal for presenting rooms, providing overviews and introducing (multiple) people in the frame. In addition, black bars to the left and right of the image after upload can be avoided.

  • Note the golden section. Try to frame your subject on left or right side of your image. The golden section is a proportion ratio and a tool that supports you in the optimal image composition. Many smartphones and cameras already offer an optional switchable template via the menu function, so that you can already consider the image splitting during shooting. See the manual of your smartphone or camera for more information.



  • Keep the Camera on eye level of your interview partner. Try to avoid low or high camera angles as this have an impact on meta level and may characterize your protagonist in a wrong way. Comparing the following shots it's noticeable that the appearance and attitude of the shown persons is totally different.


    High Camera angle: people seem small and powerless – Low camera angle: this person seems to have the upper hand, the lower angle empowers him



TIP 2: KEEP IT STEADY

  • Bring the smartphone or camera closer to your body. The further away it is, the naturally harder it will be to keep it steady.

  • Always use both hands when filming. One hand starts to tremble faster.

  • Always try to use three points of contact. Similar to a three axis gimbal, having three points of contact will help get your footage more stable.
    1 - one hand on the camera
    2 - the other hand on the lens
    3 - camera strap with tension around your neck
    Read more details here:     Shaky Footage? How to get SMOOTH HANDHELD shots like a beast!



  • Shoot with a wide angle. On a closer, macro shot every little movement of your hands will be visible, the image shakes a lot. A wide-angle image compensates for this.
     
  • Use a tripod if possible especially when shooting longer sequences like e.g. interviews. If you don't have access to a tripod and still don't want any movement, you can also place the camera or smartphone e.g. on a table to get a still image.
     
  • Optional: Use a mobile gimbal. With a gimbal you achieve an ideal stabilization of your image. When you work with movement, the image looks very smooth and natural.


TIP 3: LIGHTING

  • Right position of your protagonist. The subject or protagonist should always in focus of your shot, except when you plan to use the blur for design means. Keep distance between your protagonist and the background for at least 1 m to avoid hard shadows.
     
  • Create a contrast between your subject and the surroundings.  Use a darker background than your subject. This will put your subject in the foreground of your image.
     
  • Use natural light. Use the surroundings of your shooting place to their advantage and use the natural light from outside as your main light source (also called "key light"). But note the timing of your shoot! The daylight can change very quick, this will affect the light of your shoot and therefore the look and mood of your image.
     
  • Avoid shoting against light. Make sure that the light source is not directly behind your subject, this will result in a high contrast where the protagonist will only be seen as a silhouette.

  • Position of (further) light sources. A common way of professional lighting on film sets is the Three Point Lighting. By following some small tipps your video will look much more high-quality.

    1 - Key Light: main light for your scene that is positioned either on the right or left side of your protagonist to light up the face first.
    2 - Fill light: always positioned on the opposite of the key light to brighten up dark shadows (but not as bright as the key light.
    3 - Back Light: standing behind the subject it creates separation between the subject and the background
     

Read more details here - Three Point Lighting Setup

  • Camera Settings for better light
    • Use the largest aperture: If the video camera has an F-stop or aperture setting, change that setting to the lowest number possible. By decreasing the f-stop number on the camera, you can get a larger aperture. Creating a larger aperture lets more light into the camera, creating a brighter image.
  • Reduce the frame rate: Typically, all cameras default to 30 frames per second, although 24 frames per second will capture sharper video in low-light conditions. The slower frame rate brings more light into the camera, brightening the video footage.
  • Reduce the exposure time: Normally, slowing down the exposure time will automatically brighten your footage. If you decrease the exposure time, the camera aperture will open longer and the camera will get more light.


TIP 4: AUDIO

  • Always choose a quiet location. Find a quiet place for your shoot where there is only a little or no ambient noise. If you are filming in a room, ideally close windows and inform colleagues to avoid ambient noise.
     
  • Do the "clap test" when you enter a room to see if the room is suitable. If there is a strong echo or reverberation, you should find another room for your shoot.
     
  • Use external microphones. For a high-quality voice recording, you should use an external microphone. Avoid shooting with the integrated microphones of your smartphone or camera. Often the distance between your camera and protagonist is too far, to get a clear audio. Especially if ambient noise is unavoidable during your shoot this will automatically affect the quality of your video (and once you shoot in bad quality, it will not be fixed in postproduction - technically impossible).

    Tipp: If you have no external microphone, you can use another smartphone to record the audio. Be aware to keep then the smartphone (as audio recorder) as close as possible to the protagonist and the quality will be better.

OBS - Open Broadcast Software

Quick Start Guide for Live Streaming


Installation
  1. Request the software via IT Service Portal (ITSD)
  2. In the ITSD, search for Add/Remove Software and click on order
  3. Search for OBS-Studio and install it

Settings
  1. Open OBS
  2. Click on Settings

  3. In General disable automatic updates, if they are enabled

  4. In Stream, select Custom... and click on Show.
    Then, copy the Primary RTMPS URL from Bosch Tube webcast edit page (not from Bosch Tube Kaltura Webcast Studio as RTMP without encryption is not supported!) and past it in the Server URL-Box.
    Copy the Stream Name from Bosch Tube webcast edit page and paste it in the Stream Key box and click on the Apply button.

    Please note that the Stream Key / Stream Name is always numeric "1" and will not change for each webcast. You only need to exchange the Primary RTMPS URL for recurring events.
    “RTMPS Secondary URL” is a new feature and can be used optionally as fallback. For that you need a second streaming laptop with OBS running on it.
    Please note there is no recording available for the backup stream and it works as designed.

  5. In Output, select Streaming. Then perform the following changes:
    1. Output mode > Advanced
    2. Encoder x264
    3. Check the box Enable rescale output with a resolution of 1920 x 1080
    4. Set Rate Control to CBR
    5. Enter Bitrate to 3000
    6. Set Key frame interval to 2
    7. Set CPU settings to very fast
    8. Choose Profile as Main
    9. Set Tune as none

  6. In Output > Recording no changes are necessary
  7. In Output > Audio set all audio tracks with an Audio Bitrate of 128

    Names are not mandatory
  8. In Video perform the following changes:
    1. Base Canvas (Work Area) resolution to 1920 x 1080
    2. Output (scaled) to 1920 x 1080
    3. Downscale Filter as Bicubic (if selectable)
      If your streaming device (e.g. laptop) is having trouble while Bicubic is selected then please select the option Bilinear.
    4. Integer FPS Value to 30

  9. Then, click on Ok


How to set up your video source
  1. Click on + and select Video Capture Device

  2. Create new and name it e.g. video or camera
  3. Make sure to check the box Make source visible
  4. Click on Ok

  5. Choose your camera device
    If you see no video, please make sure it's activated
  6. In Resolution/FPS Type select custom - or leave as "Device Default"
  7. In Resolution set 1920 x 1080 (if possible, otherwise use what is available)
  8. In FPS Value select 30

  9. Click on Ok


How to set up your audio source
  1. Click on + and select Audio Input Capture

  2. Create new and name it e.g. Mic 1
  3. Make sure to check the box Make source visible
  4. Click on OK

  5. Choose your microphone device based on the microphone you are going to use
How to fit the video to your screen
  1. Right-click on the displayed video
  2. Select Transform
  3. Select Fit to screen

  4. Then you're ready to start streaming! To do so, click on Start Streaming in OBS. Now OBS sends the video stream to Bosch Tube.

Don't forget to click on GoLive in Bosch Tube Kaltura Webcast Studio.

Recording

Please make sure all installation steps are done properly.

We recommend to generate a local recording via OBS. In case of any issues with the stream you will be able to restore the webcast with that recording.


Instructions

  1. Press on Settings and navigate to Output.
  2. Select the Recording tab.

  3. Click on Browse if you want to change the file path.

  4. Be sure to record the session in mkv → mkt makes sure your recordings stay usable, even if the power turns off or OBS crashes.
  5. Go to File (upper left corner).
  6. Then, select Remux Recordings, so you can easily convert your recordings to MP4.
  7. Select your file and change the name if you need. Then, click on Remux.

The browser dock is useful for monitoring e.g. Bosch Tube or Mentimeter.

  • You can dock it to any position in OBS

How to use it

  2. Name your dock and enter an URL
  3. With your mouse, drag-and-drop the window and move it around to place it into your OBS UI, wherever desired.

How to add an OBS filter

OBS-Studio allows you to add filters to all your sources, scenes and even audio devices.
You need a performance notebook to use multiple filters.

  1. Right-click on the desired scene, source or device
  2. Select Filters

How to use the OBS filter Noise Gate

The Noise Gate allows you to cut off all background noise while you are not talking.

Select a close threshold above the noise volume and an open threshold slightly below your voice input to get good results.

The following parameters apply:

  • Close treshold: When the mic drops below this volume, the noise gate will turn off the microphone
  • Open treshold: When the mic goes above this volume, the noise gate will turn on the microphone
  • Attack time: How long it takes for the mic to go from off to on, as a fade in
  • Hold time: How long the mic should stay on after the volume has dropped below the close threshold
  • Release time: How long it takes for the mic to go from on to off, as a fade out

How to use it

  1. Right-click on your microphone > select Filters > select Noise Gate


  2. The default settings of attack time, hold time, and release time are usually good

  3. The settings can be tested before closing the filter settings. You can play around with the parameters (mentioned above) by speaking into your microphone.

How to use the OBS filter Gain
  1. Right-click on your microphone > select Filters > select Gain



  2. The filter Gain makes the audio source louder.

    Parameters: Gain (dB): Defines gain of the audio, in decibels.
How to use the OBS filter Noise Suppression

The filter Noise Suppression lowers the noise level of your audio.

  1. Right-click on your microphone > select Filters > select Noise Suppression


  2. Parameters: Suppression Level (dB): Defines the noise reduction level of the audio, in decibels.

    Higher value means more noise hiss removed. Hiss is a broadband noise that spans the entire audible spectrum but with more intensity in the high frequencies.
How to use the OBS filter Video Delay (Async)

The filter Video Delay (Async) delays the video of a source, while audio capturing of the source ignores this filter. Makes video and audio asynchronous. Applies only to sources that contains both tracks (video + audio).
Common usage is video capture device source, which usually imports both tracks into OBS Studio and sometimes can link to alternate audio source or has buffered/filtered audio import that can cause additional undesirable delay.



Parameters: Delay (milliseconds): Defines video delay of the source, in milliseconds.





NDI streaming


What is it?

NDI stands for Network Device Interface and it`s used for catching Audio/Video feeds from Teams-Meetings into OBS (Open Broadcaster Software).

Prerequisite: 

Be sure to already have the SfB-Recording Role. 

  • You can ask for the role over the IDM-Request

  • HERE you can find all necessary information

Attention

  • Please note, that the person, who is performing the livestream (Capturing the NDI sources via OBS) should not be an active part of the MS Teams meeting.
  • This plugin is not available for BSH users yet.



StepInstruction
Activate NDI in your Teams client
  1. Go to Settings in your Teams client

  2. Select App permissions and toggle on NDI

  3. Open the Drop Down Menu over the three dots and select Boradcast over NDI

This setting has to be turned on for every new session!

HINT It`s important to join the meeting and turn on the Broadcast before opening OBS!


ATTENTION The procedure of installing and enabling the NDI output on the new MS Teams client has been changed by Microsoft.

Please follow the following steps to enable the NDI output on the new MS Teams client:

  1. Make sure the new MS Teams client gets installed on your computer and it is ready to login.
  2. Go to the new MS Teams client → Settings → "App permissions" section:



  3. Click the "Download Link" and make sure the binary libraries from NDI gets installed locally on your computer.
    1. You will find the installation file "ndi-win-x64_vs2022-crtdynamic-release.msix" in your "Downloads" folder and can start the file installation without admin rights.
    2. If you have already installed the TxNdi file, it might be that you need to update TxNdi from time to time when a new version will be published. Just click on the "Update" button:



    3. After successfull installation / update, MS Teams TxNdi is ready to use. Please click on the "Close" button:



  4. Start the new MS Teams client. Now you should be able to enable the NDI output feature on your new MS Teams client under "Production tools":



  5. Restart the OBS client & NDI to perform the streaming as usual.

ATTENTION

The message informs about a new feature behavior for NDI in Teams 2.1, requiring manual installation of NDI binaries after each Teams client update.
Users need to validate and possibly update NDI before events. Microsoft is working on solutions to improve the update notification and process by the end of 2024.

Tags:

  • Feature update
  • User impact
  • Admin impact

We would like to bring awareness to the new feature behavior for NDI (Network Device Interface) that’s specific to Teams 2.1. To minimize the size of the Teams client installer for organizations. Microsoft made the decision to let the NDI binaries be manually installed externally by users that desire to use the feature. This installation process would be required by the user at every instance the Teams client proceeds with an automatic update. Note, the update cadence can be viewed in the Teams app versioning page here.

[How this will affect our organization:]

NDI is a critical feature utilized to extract high quality video feeds and help produce highly important events for organizations. Microsoft understands the significance of the feature and is currently prioritizing efforts to address the feedback raised on the user experience.

[What you need to do to prepare:]

Before hosting any meeting or events using NDI, it is currently recommended for users to validate if an update to NDI is required. This would be indicated if “Production tools” under the App permissions page were disabled, prompting the user to redownload the latest NDI binaries.

To reenable “Production tools” and use the NDI feature, the user would need to proceed with the following steps: 

  1. Select “Settings” within the Teams client
  2. Navigate to the “App permissions” page.
  3. Select “Download link” under the “Production tools”. 
  4. Once installed, reenable the “Production tools” feature. 

Microsoft has heard your feedback, and we understand that the current experience makes it difficult for users to use the feature. With a frequent manual update required for the NDI binaries and a lack of notification beforehand, it makes it challenging for a user to host a successful and reliable event. To uphold higher standards to our features, our internal team have prioritized and are immediately working through a short-term and long-term solution for the feedback raised:

Short-Term Solution:

  • Expected delivery: 
    • August 2024
  • Feature behavior: 
    • A user with “Production tools” enabled would automatically be notified once an update to the binaries are required. This would help ensure awareness of these updates prior to hosting any critical events.

Long-Term Solution:

  • Expected delivery:
    • End of 2024
  • Feature behavior:
    • NDI would automatically be updated to the latest binaries with no action required by the end user.

How to Enable Multiple Automatic File Downloads?

By default, the bowsers Chrome and Edge ask for confirmation when a website tries automatically to download multiple files.

When you first try to download your received files in OpenDXM, you will be prompted to confirm that “rb-wam.bosch.com” can download multiple files. 

Please click "Allow":


If you do not allow “rb-wam.bosch.com” to download multiple files (i.e. If you click on "Block"), your files won't be downloaded.

You can see in the address bar (see pic below) that the download is blocked even if you get the message from OpenDXM: "Files are being downloaded" when you attempt to download files again. 


To enable download again, you can proceed as shown in the picture below:


When you allow the website “rb-wam.bosch.com” to download multiple files, it is automatically added to the Allow list under the Automatic downloads.


We recommend that you disable the setting "Ask where to save each file before downloading"

  • In the upper-right corner of the browser, select the menu (three-dot) icon, then choose Settings.
  • Scroll down and click Show advanced settings.
  • Scroll down to Downloads, and turn off the toggle switch "Ask where to save each file before downloading".

→ Now all websites will be able to download multiple files at once.


The default download folder should always be in your local drive C or D.

When is a capacity warning sent?

General:

The Exchange Server (Exchange OnPremise and Exchange Online) provides three kinds of
notifications when a user's mailbox is nearing, or at, capacity.

  • Warning: The user receives an email warning that the mailbox is approaching the maximum
    size limit. This warning is intended to encourage users to delete unwanted mail.
  • Prohibit Send: The user receives a prohibit-send notification email when the mailbox size limit
    is reached. The user can't send new messages until enough email is deleted to bring the mailbox
    below the size limit.
  • Prohibit Send/Receive: Exchange Online rejects any incoming mail when the mailbox size limit
    is reached, and sends a non-delivery report (NDR) to the sender. The sender has the option to
    try resending the mail later. To receive messages again, the user must delete email until the
    mailbox is below the size limit.

Wann wird eine Kapazitäts-Warnung gesendet?

Allgemein:

Der Exchange Server (OnPremise und Exchange Online) besitzt drei Arten von Benachrichtigungen, wenn das Postfach eines Benutzers sich der jeweiligen Kapazitätsgrenze nähert oder sie erreicht:

  • Warnung: Der Benutzer erhält eine E-Mail-Warnung, dass das Postfach sich der maximalen Größenbeschränkung nähert. Mit dieser Warnung sollen Benutzer dazu aufgefordert werden, unerwünschte E-Mails zu löschen.
  • Senden verbieten: Der Benutzer erhält eine Benachrichtigungs-E-Mail, dass das versenden von E-Mails nicht mehr möglich ist, wenn die Größenbeschränkung des Postfachs erreicht ist. Der Benutzer kann neue Nachrichten erst senden, wenn genügend E-Mails gelöscht wurden, um das Postfach unter die Größenbeschränkung zu bringen.
  • Senden/Empfangen verbieten: Der Exchange Server (OnPremise und Exchange Online) lehnt eingehende E-Mails ab, wenn die Postfachgröße erreicht ist, und sendet einen Unzustellbarkeitsbericht an den Absender. Der Absender hat die Möglichkeit, die E-Mail später erneut zu versenden. Um wieder Nachrichten zu erhalten, muss der Benutzer E-Mails löschen, bis die Größe des Postfachs wieder unter dem Grenzwert liegt.

Wird die Empfangsgrenze überschritten, erhalten die Absender von E-Mails an dieses Postfach einen Unzustellbarkeitsbericht mit der Information, dass das Postfach den zulässigen Schwellenwert für die Anzahl zugestellter Nachrichten überschritten hat.
Nach einer Stunde wird die Grenze zurückgesetzt, und das Postfach kann wieder Nachrichten empfangen.
*2Nachdem der Grenzwert für die Empfängerrate erreicht wurde, können Nachrichten erst aus dem Postfach gesendet werden, wenn die Anzahl der Empfänger, die in den letzten 24 Stunden Nachrichten gesendet haben, unter den Grenzwert fällt.
Beispielsweise sendet ein Benutzer um 09:00 Uhr eine E-Mail-Nachricht an 5000 Empfänger, dann um 10:00 Uhr eine weitere Nachricht an 2500 Empfänger und dann um 11:00 Uhr eine weitere Nachricht an 2500 Empfänger und erreicht den Grenzwert von 10.000 Nachrichten.
Der Benutzer kann nachrichten erst um 09:00 Uhr am nächsten Tag erneut senden.
*3Dies ist die maximale Anzahl in Summe von Empfängern, die in den Feldern "An:", "Cc:" und "Bcc:" für eine einzelne E-Mail zulässig sind.
*4Der Grenzwert für die Empfängerproxyadresse ist die maximale Anzahl von Aliasen (E-Mail-Adressen), die ein Empfängerpostfach haben kann.
*5Wenn das ausgehende Nachrichtenvolumina das Nachrichtenratenlimit überschreitet, wird jeder Überschuss bei der Nachrichtenübermittlung gedrosselt und nacheinander auf die folgenden Minuten übertragen.
Dadurch wird das Konto des Absenders normalerweise nicht blockiert.
Exchange Online ist jedoch nicht für Bulk-Mailing-Szenarien geeignet.
*6Die maximale Anzahl innerhalb CI-CAT ist bei Postfächern innerhalb BOSCH wesentlich geringer.
*7Generell gilt das Limit von 3600 Nachrichten pro Stunde.
Zusätzlich wurde in Exchange Online ein weiteres Limit für Sender-Empfänger-Paare (SRP=Sender-Recipient-Pairs) implementiert. Diese Funktion gilt für die Nachrichten, die von einem bestimmten Absender von einem Microsoft Office 365-Postfach empfangen werden. Wenn ein einzelner Absender über 33 % des Schwellenwerts (3.600 pro rollierende Stunde) an einen bestimmten Empfänger sendet, tritt das SRP-Limit in Kraft und das Postfach nimmt keine Nachrichten mehr von diesem Absender an. Die Mailbox nimmt weiterhin Nachrichten von anderen Absendern an.
Das SRP betrifft nicht von intern (innerhalb BOSCH) gesendeten E-Mails.


Welche Grenzwerte bestehen bei Verteilerlisten?

Allgemein: 

  • Die Grenzwerte gelten für Verteilergruppen im freigegebenen Adressbuch (Globales Adressbuch).
  • Maximale Anzahl von Verteilergruppenmitgliedern wird nach der Auflösung/Erweiterung der Verteilergruppe
    vom Server bestimmt.
  • Senden von Nachrichten an große Verteilergruppen werden in Echange Online beschränkt. An den Verteilerlisten wird eine Zustellungsverwaltungs- oder Nachrichtengenehmigungsoption konfiguriert (moderierte Verteilerlisten).
    In der Zustellungsverwaltung kann eine Liste von Absendern angegeben werden, die Nachrichten an die Verteilergruppe senden dürfen. Für die Nachrichtengenehmigung werden ein oder mehrere Moderatoren angegeben, die alle an die Verteilergruppe gesendeten Nachrichten genehmigen müssen.
  • Maximale Nachrichtengröße für große Verteilergruppen:
    Wenn eine Nachricht an 5.000 oder mehr Empfänger gesendet wird, darf die Nachrichtengröße diesen Grenzwert nicht überschreiten. Übersteigt die Nachrichtengröße den Grenzwert, wird die Nachricht nicht zugestellt, und der Absender erhält einen Unzustellbarkeitsbericht (Non-Delivery Report, NDR).

Beispiel: Benutzer A hat eine Postfachregel, die, je nach Absender, Nachrichten an Benutzer B weiterleitet. Benutzer B hat eine Postfachregel, die, je nach Schlüsselwörtern in der Betreffzeile, Nachrichten an Benutzer C weiterleitet. Erfüllt eine Nachricht beide Bedingungen, wird sie nur an Benutzer B gesendet. Sie wird nicht an Benutzer C weitergeleitet, da nur eine Weiterleitung zulässig ist. In diesem Fall wird kein entsprechender Unzustellbarkeitsbericht an Benutzer B gesendet. Benutzer B erfährt nicht, dass die Nachricht nicht an Benutzer C zugestellt wurde. Wir verwenden die Kopfzeile "X-MS-Exchange-Inbox-Rules-Loop", um zu ermitteln, wie oft eine Nachricht umgeleitet wurde. Diese Kopfzeile bleibt auch jenseits der Grenzen einer Exchange-Organisation erhalten.
