page_name: Connection of External Business Partners in OpenDXM
html_content:
Connection of External Business Partners in OpenDXM

There are 2 options to establish a data exchange connection with an external business partner (customer or supplier) in OpenDXM.

  1. OpenDXM web access  (via WAM (Web Access Management))
    Business partners can get direct web-based access to the OpenDXM of Bosch and participate in data exchange via the Internet browser.
    In this case, registration of the external partners in the IdM system is required.


  2. OFTP connection
    Many automotive manufacturers (OEMs) and other large business partners (generally customers such as BMW, Daimler, Mahle, Porsche, John Deere,....) usually have their own electronic data exchange systems connected to the Bosch systems. (see Example Data Exchange with  Daimler)
    In this case, the registration of the external partners in the IdM system is not required. They only have to be added as a contact in OpenDXM.

    OFTP stands for "Odette  File Transfer Protocol".
    It is a protocol for direct electronic data transfers between two communication partners and is used as a standard protocol in the European automotive and supplier industry.
    The list Current OFTP companies contains all companies for which an OFTP connection is set up in OpenDXM. (This list is updated monthly)


 When exchanging data, it does not matter to the OpenDXM user how the external business partner is connected. 


 To request OpenDXM access for an external business partner, you can use the order form "Data Exchange with OpenDXM" on the ITSP  in both cases mentioned above.
The OpenDXM support team decides which user type is required and then creates the user.

Teams mobile app

Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site.

On BoschTube you can find a lot of tutorials how to work with Teams mobile app




Pay attention to Mobile Workplace Lite solution, which  introduces an intermediate tier of business data access for use on personally owned mobile devices.




Advantages

  • The Teams app is part of the Mobile Workplace at Bosch.
  • The app enables the Mobile Workplace user to stay connected with his/her Teams community also on the go
  • The app offers the possibilities of a Teams desktop client also on the mobile device
  • In combination with a desktop client it can help to conduct a Teams meeting (second screen / second device)
  • If you have a hybrid meeting (on- and offsite) you can go into the same Teams meeting with the Teams app and use the camera to show/share a flipchart or experimental setup in the meeting with others


Setup & Initial configuration

 Please note: The included screenshots derive from a specific software version. Due to regular updates it may occur that your current user interface looks partially different.  


QuestionDescription/Answer
What are the prerequisites for the installation of the Teams app?

The prerequisites are:

  • a Bosch iOS device
  • MS Intune enrolled
  • activated mobile data usage (if not connected to any WiFi). To activate mobile data usage, go to iOS Settings → Teams → turn on 'Mobile Data'

Alternatively you can also access Teams mobile app with Mobile Workplace Lite.

How to install Teams app?
  • Option 1:
  1. Open Comp Portal app
  2. Go to Apps and search for Teams
  3. Press Install
  • Option 2 (if issues with Option 1 occur):
  1. Open App Store app
  2. Go to Search and type Microsoft Teams
  3. Tap Get on the respective app
How to log in?
  1. Tap Teams app
  2. Type in your NT user + @bosch.com (e.g. abc1fe@bosch.com)  
  3. Press Sign-in (once asked for your password please provide)
  4. Authenticate MFA
  5. Select OK to restart
  6. Select Allow to send notification
  7. Confirm to access microphone
  8. Signed in
Where to find settings?

You get to your profile settings by tapping your profile pictures or swiping the screen to the right. 

How to set settings?
  1. Tap your profile pictures or swipe the screen to the right. 
  2. Select Settings. First you can find the general settings like:
  • Appearance: When you enable this feature, the colors of the app switch to dark colors. By default, Teams uses lighter colors.
  • Pride theme: When you enable this feature, the colors of the app switch to colorful appearance.
  • Data and storage: Using these settings, you can set the quality (size) of images you upload, clear temporary files and app data, and clear your chat history to help manage the data load on your mobile device.
  • Translation: You can choose the language you want the messages to be translated into.

What kind of additional settings can be found?

Additional settings may be set for each specific team, as shown in the figure following this list:

  • Profile: You can set your profile picture and view your activity, organizational chart, email address, and phone number with this setting.
  • Notifications: You can set the hours you want Teams to be quiet and not send you notifications; set if you want the Teams mobile app to only send notifications when you are not active on the desktop app; configure notifications for incoming calls, missed calls, ongoing calls, chats, likes, and reactions; and set other notification-related settings.
  • Messaging: Use this setting to show channels in your chat list. When you tap the Chat tab at the bottom of your mobile screen, you will then see your channels in addition to your private chats.
  • People: You can see here blocked contacts
  • Calling: Here you can turn on call forwarding, voicemail, block calls, enable encryption, and set noise suppression.
  • About: This setting provides information about the mobile app, such as the version, privacy and cookies, terms of use, and third-party software notices and information.
  • Help & feedback: Click this setting to view help information and provide feedback to Microsoft about the app.
  • Privacy: Information about collecting diagnostic data.
  • Add account: With this setting you can add an additional account to use the app. You can use multiple accounts with my Teams app on your phone.
  • Sign out: Use this setting to sign out of the Teams app. This is useful if you are lending your phone to someone else and don’t want someone else to access the app with your credentials.

Can I remove call/meeting details from iOS device call logs?

Yes. You can enable or disable this option from your calling settings. When this setting is turned OFF, Teams calls/meetings will not be added to your iOS Recents list. All calls/meetings prior to disabling will still be shown in the Recents list.


How to work with Teams mobile app


QuestionDescription / Answer
How the navigation experience looks like?

If you tap the Teams option, you will be presented with all the teams and channels you have. Then you need to tap again to open one of those channels. On a large monitor you can see all the teams and channels at the same time you see the associated messages in the channel. With the mobile app, you need to make another tap in order to get into the channel, and if you want to change channels, you need to tap the back icon and then select a different channel.

How to schedule a meeting in Teams app?

  1. To schedule a meeting, go to Calendar on the bottom of the app, then select Schedule a meeting in the top right 

  2. Go to Add participants and select the people you'd like to invite

  3. If you want have your meeting in a channel, select the appropriate channel by selecting Share to a channel (If not, skip it)

  4. Set start and end times and write a description for the event

  5. Select Done to schedule your meeting

How to join a meeting?

There are many ways to join a meetings on your mobile app:

  • If you've already downloaded the app and signed up, all you need to do is tap Click here to join the meeting in the meeting invite to open the app and join the meeting.

 If you don’t have a Teams account, select Join as a guest and enter your name to join the meeting as a guest. Depending on how the meeting was set up, you may need to sign in to an account that was authorized for the meeting.

  • You can also select Calendar  on the bottom of the app to see your meetings. Find the meeting you want, and then select Join.
  • What is more you can join a meeting by just tapping the notification.

  • If a meeting takes place in a channel, you’ll see an invitation to join, relevant content, and the organizer right in the channel. Just select Join.
  • If the meeting or meeting chat has already begun, it appears in your recent chat list. Select the meeting in your chat list and then select Join at the top of the chat.

  • Some meetings let you join by dialing a phone number if you're unable to use the Teams app. If there's a phone number in the meeting invite, select it to dial the number and the conference ID. Once you're connected, dial 1 to join the meeting. If you see a number in the invite but it's not local to you, select Find a local number to get one that works for you.

How to make a call?
  • To manually dial a phone number, open your Teams app and click Calls(at the bottom), then(top right) and enter the phone number on your dial pad.
  • If you’ve enabled your phone’s settings to allow access to your phone contacts, tap Calls , then Contacts (again, top right) and select the person you want to call.
  • You can also directly call someone from your History by tapping on the number or name of the person in the list.
How can I make a video call?
Prerequisites: 
  • The participants need to be connected to Wi-Fi.
  • Your Teams mobile app needs to have access to your smartphone camera 

How to use background effects?

As you join a meeting from the Teams mobile app, you have the option to set up video and audio before you join.

  1. Turn your video on
  2. Select Background effects in the top left of your video
  3. Choose your background. To do that use the + to use your own image from your mobile
  4. Select Done and start the meeting
How can I find a Bosch colleague in the Global Address Book using the Teams mobile app?
  1. Use the search engine in the chat
  2. Please note, that you have to allow access to your contacts. To do that go to Settings → Teams → Enable Contacts

How can I forward my calls?
  1. Go to Settings by clicking on your profile pictures
  2. Select Calling
  3. Toggle on the Call forwarding

  4. Choose if you want to forward to the Voicemail or to the Contact

How to start a new chat?
  1. Tap the New Chat   button.
  2. Type the name, email address, or phone number of the person with whom you want to chat in the To: field.

 Tip: If you can’t find the person you want to add to the chat, try syncing your contacts on your mobile device. If you still can’t find them, you can invite them to Teams.

  3. Select the person in the list of suggestions or contacts to start a chat.

  4. Type in the Type a new message window and tap Send   to send a message in the chat.

Can I send chat messages to the participant during the conference?

Yes. During a conference:

  1. On the bottom right, tap More .
  2. Tap In call messages .

 Tip: If you share a file via the chat and want participants to edit it, make sure you give participants edit access.

How to manage messages with Teams mobile app?

For chat and channel messages, you can like, copy, share, and mark as unread. You can also edit and delete your own messages.

  • For chats, press and hold in a message to see your options.

  • For channel conversations, tap More options  in the upper right corner of the message. You can also press and hold on the message to see the options.

What is an Intelligent Chat Message Translation?

When you receive a message that is not in your native language, you will see a suggestion under the message to translate it or never translate it:

Once the translation is complete, you can long press on the message and go to Translate options: 

  • See Original will revert the message back to it's original state.
  • Translation Feedback will take you to a screen where feedback of the translation quality is optional to provide.
  • Translation Settings will take you to the translation settings page where translation preferences can be changed.

The second time you translate a message, Teams will show a coach mark to turn on automatic translation.

How to share screen?
  1. Start or join a meeting.
  2. Tap the More options  in the menu.
  3. Tap Share and then tap Share Screen.
  4.  A menu will pop up to indicate where you’ll share your screen. Select Microsoft Teams.

NOTE You won’t be able to multitask or see others if you need to use other apps on your device, but your colleagues will be able to see your mobile screen.


Before you first share your screen on your mobile device, you may have to proceed with the following steps:

  1. Select Settings
  2. Select Control Centre
  3. Select Customize Controls
  4. Select Screen Recording
How to add attachments?
  1. Open the Microsoft Teams app and go to the chat where you want to add an attachment.
  2. Tap the ‘+’ button to the left of the text box.
  3. Click on the paperclip icon.

   4. Select a file/files you want to attach.

NOTE You can also choose file location (This device or OneDrive).

How to scan using phone Smart Camera?

To use the Smart Camera in Microsoft Teams do the following:

  1. Open the chat where you want to post the picture
  2. Tap the picture icon and then tap the option Take photo
  3. Select the type of photo you are taking
  4. Make sure the content is centered inside the guide lines
  5. Take the photo and sent it to the chat:

How to set quiet hours?
  1. Tap your profile pictures or swipe the screen to the right and select Settings
  2. Select Notifications --> Block notifications --> During quiet time
  3. Toggle Quiet hours to ON and and choose the duration
  4. Tap Quiet days and toggle to ON
  5. Select days you want to be quiet one

            6. Back to main menu using an arrow on the top left

How to turn on / off notification?
  1. Tap your profile pictures or swipe the screen to the right and select Settings
  2. Select Notifications. Here you can find a lot of options connected with this feature:

How do I enable End-to-end encryption from mobile phone?

End-to-end encryption can be activated from your mobile phone:

1. In Teams mobile app go to Settings > Calling.
2. Under Encryption, turn on End-to-end encrypted calls.

NOTE If you don`t activate End-to-end encryption your calls are still encrypted between you and the Microsoft service.

How to turn off meeting chat bubbles?
  • You can turn message chat bubbles off temporarily in the current meeting by tapping on the snooze icon.
  • To turn them off permanently you have to tap on "Don't show chat bubbles" in the overflow (...) menu.

OneNote viewer feature
You are able to open and view OneNote notebooks right within your Teams mobile app. To edit the content you will be directed to the standalone OneNote mobile app. The experience is available as part of the Teams mobile apps on Android and iOS (including iPads) starting with English language users, followed by international languages.
Note, that in some location possibility of using OneNote is impossible due to some local limitations.
What is a Quickly Capture Content feature?

This feature enables users to take screenshots and annotate/add text to content, to be saved/shared with Teams or outside of Teams, using sensitivity labels to ensure only content that is allowed to be saved/shared is done so.

  1. Go to More options (...)

   2.  Click on Quick Capture

   3. Select Share button

Teams mobile app with Public Telephony

QuestionDescription / Answer
Can I also make external calls with the Teams mobile app? 
Yes, this is possible if you have Teams Public Telephony (the possibility to make external calls). As soon as Teams Public Telephony is rolled out at your location, you see a dial-pad in the upper right corner.
Can I share files with externals?
Yes, this is possible if you have Teams Public Telephony (the possibility to make external calls). As soon as Teams Public Telephony is rolled out at your location, you see a dial-pad in the upper right corner.

Joining Microsoft Teams meeting with Apple CarPlay

NOTE Keep these things in mind while using CarPlay:

  • You can join your next scheduled meeting as early as 15 minutes before and as late as 5 minutes after the meeting starts.
  • If you have conflicting meeting times, Teams joins the meeting that starts first. If meetings start at the exact same time, Teams joins the one based on which meeting title comes first in alphabetical order.
  • Teams calendar doesn't update unless you have the app open. It's possible a recent meeting invite won't be reflected in your calendar.
  • You can only use Teams audio.
  • When you join a meeting, your mic is muted.


Joining a Teams meeting
  1. Connect your iPhone to your vehicle using Bluetooth or a USB cable. Your device's screen appears on your car's display.
  2. Select the Teams icon to prompt Siri.

      3. Use Siri voice commands to join your meeting. Say something like, "Call next meeting using Teams".

      4. Use the Teams call controls on your car's display. For example, tap to unmute yourself if you need to say something.



Making calls to speed dial contacts and get back to recent calls on Teams
  1. After tapping the Teams icon and navigating to the Calls tab (which is next to Meetings tab), you can either choose to access speed dial contacts or call history.

     2. Select a contact.

     3. Make a call.

Einsatz von OpenDXM in Embargo-Ländern

Für OpenDXM gibt es keine Einschränkungen von C/TXF-Foreign Trade Governance and Export Control. 

Sie können OpenDXM weltweit nutzen.


  • Der Absender ist für die übertragenen Dateien verantwortlich und muss ggf. Ausfuhrbeschränkungen beachten.
  • Der Empfänger muss sicherstellen, dass er auf ausfuhrbeschränkte Dateien in Embargo-Ländern nicht zugreift.

page_name: Use of OpenDXM in embargoed countries
html_content:
Use of OpenDXM in embargoed countries

For OpenDXM there are no restrictions by C/TXF-Foreign Trade Governance and Export Control. 

You can use OpenDXM worldwide.


  • The sender is responsible for the files transferred and may have to comply with export restrictions.
  • The recipients must ensure that they do not access export restricted files in embargoed countries.

General information: Bosch Connect

What's Bosch Connect?


Bosch Connect is a social enterprise network as well as a collaboration space that was introduced in 2013 and connects Bosch employees all around the world. Our main goal is to support transparent communication. We are the recommended tool for cross-functional, cross-regional and cross-hierarchical collaboration, as well networking, blogging and forum discussions. Bosch Connect comprises i.a. following components: profiles, communities, blogs, forums and wikis offering also its own Desktop application.

New version, new key visual - Experience City News Blog - Experience City (bosch.com)

On this page you can find the information about:


User Guide & Training

The pages on digital workplace Docupedia Space present the User Guide for Bosch Connect (we cannot guarantee the up to date content in other sources referring to Bosch Connect). You can find the latest news about Bosch Connect on our Experience City blog.

BD Training Academy offers a lot of training and materials in Bosch Connect. 


Software and access

Bosch Connect is a customized platform based on HCL Connections software.

If you are an internal/fixed-term associate, please go to the following link and read all the details regarding your access to Bosch Connect: Access for internal/fixed-term associates

For external associates please check the following regulations:  Access for external associates.


What to do if a user profile in Bosch Connect is still active after the user has left Bosch? Please, read more here.


Compliance and Governance

Support

Please visit this section to get more information.


Responsible Team

The product is developed and managed by Bosch Connect Product Portfolio team in BD/WPA-WPS4 department. The responsible Product Manager is is Stefanie Krauss and Service Manager of Bosch Connect is Annette Wittke.

Support: Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

Contact

If you don't have access to Bosch Connect or the Support Forums are not available or Bosch Connect is completely out of service, please call IT Service Desk: 33 11 (+49 711 811-33 11) or IT Service Desk telephone numbers worldwide.

In all other cases please use our Support Forums and search first the question you want to ask. It's very possible that your question has been already answered. If not, just add a new post.

Support Forums

  • ASK! Bosch Support Forum  - Forum to support issues around ASK! Bosch (based on IBM Social Q&A).
  • Bosch Connect Administration Requests  - Please place your Bosch Connect requests like change community members, copy blog, forum, wiki, activities, etc. in this forum.
  • Bosch Connect Product Portfolio Bug Forum  - Here you can report bugs or error messages you might see in the applications of the Bosch Connect Product Portfolio.
  • Bosch Connect Support Forum  - Do you need support with Bosch Connect? Please ask your question here!
  • Bosch Overflow - Feedback, Support and Bug reporting  - This Forum is used for supporting with Bosch Overflow. You can either report bugs, give us feedback or ask for support using the platform. 
  • Community Governance Robot CGR - Support Forum  - Forum to support issues around the Community Governance Robot 
  • Mobile Issues with Bosch Connect app  - This forum is intended to discuss/solve any issues around mobile access to Bosch Connect.
  • Support forum TinyMCE editor in EAN  - This forum is used to provide support for the TinyMCE editor EAN in Bosch Connect. Please post your questions, issues, concerns regarding this editor EAN into this forum.
  • Self-help group for Bosch Connect HTML & CSS specials  - In this forum you may post your questions, and issues you have concerning HTML and CSS for Bosch Connect (all content) - or you can find solutions that are already described! HTML and CSS is out of the usual Bosch Connect support. Therefore please be aware that solutions are crowd based and given on voluntary basis. There is no official tracking and maintaining of questions.

Deleting cookies and cached files

Before posting a support question try to delete your browser cookies (stored information about websites and other browser data) and cache (temporary files stored in order to speed up loading of pages). Here the instructions for various browsers:

  • Microsoft Edge 
  • Mozilla Firefox
  • Google Chrome 

We do not support Internet Explorer.

Blogs in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

What's a blog?

Blogs are a very important and probably the most viewed section (community app) in Bosch Connect. On blogs you can find articles published chronologically and add your comment to each article.

Go to More → Blogs→ Public Blogs to see blog entries from the whole organization.

Try also our searching features to find topics interesting to you.

Blog types

Bloggers may be individuals or organized teams of authors. Basically, there are two different types of blogs available:

  • Community blogs accessible via community, used as the blog component within a community (what we highly recommend);

  • Stand-alone (Private) blogs accessible via your profile, not tied to a community.

A special type of a community blog is an ideation blog component used to generate ideas and gather feedback (votes, comments) on ideas within a community. 

 

                                  

Start a new blog  

Please read first about blog types mentioned above to choose the best blog type for you.

Community blog: Use Blog community app by adding the blog component to your community.  

Stand-alone blog: 

  1. Click on More from the left navigation of the screen. Choose Blogs and click on Start a Blog.

  2. Define a Name and Blog Address, provide tags for your blog using key words and provide a brief description.

  3. When all the required information has been entered, click on Save. 

  4. Your blog is now available on your My Blogs page. To make it visible to others, add an entry to your blog. 


               

Create a new blog entry (blog post) 

After creating a new blog you can write a new blog entry (= blog post):

Community blog: 

  1. Go to a community and create a new entry in an already existing community blog. You can contribute to any blog for which you have an owner, author, or draft permission.
  2. Go to the community blog and click on New Entry. 
  3. Give your new entry a meaningful title. Provide appropriate tags for your entry so that it can be found more easily. Write your content (text, pictures, links, tables etc.).
  4. By clicking on Preview you can review your entry before you post it.
  5. Click Post to publish your entry to the blog. Please note, that if the blog is moderated, your content must be reviewed and approved before it is published and you will have only two options available: Submit for Review and Save as Draft. Your post will be visible, when a moderator will approve it. 

Stand-alone blog:

  1. Click on More from the left navigation of the screen and choose Blogs.
  2. Your stand-alone blog that you have created before will be displayed in the My Blogs List.
  3. Click on New Entry underneath your stand-alone blog.

  5. By clicking on Preview you can review your entry before you post it. Click Post to publish your entry to the blog. Alternatively, you can save the new entry as draft.

Tips for writing a blog post

Topic

  • Take time to research the topic 
  • Form your own views on texts written by others
  • Enhance articles with additional information 

Introduction

  • Make the introduction as brief and concise as possible 
  • It should make the reader want to keep reading 
  • The quality of the introduction will often determine whether or not a reader reads the full article 

Use short and concise sentences

  • Blogs usually consist of short and concise statements
  • Maximum of 1,000 words per article
  • Avoid using long, complex sentences 

Article headings

  • Give the article a meaningful heading 
  • The heading should reflect the article content and make readers want to read the article 
  • Create subheadings that describe the article’s themes concisely 

Structure and paragraphs

  • Structure of the text content 
  • Create paragraphs 
  • End with a summary 

Pictures and videos

  • Add relevant pictures or videos, if available 
  • In many cases, a text is not properly understood until it is associated with a picture
  • Remember: a picture will often say more than a thousand words

Related links

  • If necessary, provide links to more in-depth articles and additional information
  • Not too many links – two to three external links at most 

Examples

  • Clarify a point using examples and make the article more comprehensible 
  • Provide evidence of your expert status by citing examples 

Conclusion

  • End an article with a conclusion or a summary 
  • Readers are then able to review what they have read

Ideation blog

Do you have bright ideas or tips and tricks that you would like to share? An Ideation Blog in Bosch Connect is a great place to store your ideas and let other community members vote for your ideas. An Ideation Blog is a type of blog that is designed to generate ideas on a particular topic, gather feedback on ideas within a community, and reach a consensus on the best ideas. A community can contain multiple Ideation Blogs. An Ideation Blog can only exist within a community and membership is limited to the community (but you can manage the settings for an Ideation Blog from your My Blogs page). 


Voting and giving feedback to existing ideas:

  1. Click Vote to vote for an idea you support. If you change your mind, click Voted to cancel your vote.
  2. Click Add a Comment to comment on an idea.

Please note that only community members participate in an ideation blog. Every member can create a new ideation blog in Ideation Blog App and raise ideas in any ideation blog of the community.


Raising up new ideas and gathering feedback:

  1. After adding community app "Ideation blog" click Create Your First Idea to add an idea to the blog.
  2. To manage settings for the Ideation Blog, click Ideation Blog Actions → Manage Ideation Blog. In addition to managing the settings that are common for all blogs, you can also control voting:
    • Choose Unlimited voting to allow members to vote as many times as they like.
    • Choose Set a voting limit to restrict the number of votes each member can cast to the number you specify.
  3. Click More Actions → Notify Other People to send a link to the idea to people you specify.
  4. Click Graduate when you decide that an idea has enough support from the community. This will freeze all voting and commenting on the idea. If you change your mind about a graduated idea, open the idea and select Cancel Graduation.

To review activity in the Ideation Blog, choose one of the following views from the navigation pane:

  • All Ideas shows all ideas that were contributed to the Ideation Blog, including graduated ideas.
  • Open Ideas shows just the ideas still available for an action, such as voting, commenting, or graduating.
  • Graduated Ideas shows ideas that you graduated.
  • My Votes shows the ideas that you voted for.

You can also freeze the creation of new ideas for the Ideation Blog, click Ideation Blog Actions → Stop Idea Creation. Users can no longer contribute ideas but they can still vote for and comment on existing ideas in the blog. To completely freeze the Ideation Blog, click Ideation Blog Actions →  Freeze Ideation Blog. Users cannot contribute new ideas or vote for or comment on existing ideas.

To mark an idea as a duplicate. Select More Actions → Mark as Duplicate. You must search for the duplicate idea so the votes can be merged. The duplicate idea is marked as a duplicate and no further votes are allowed.

You can also export the ideas from an Ideation Blog to a file. Click Ideation Blog Actions → Export Ideas. The following fields from each idea are saved to a CSV file: Title, Creator, Create time, Last updater, Last updated time, Content, Tags, Vote Count, Comment Count, Status (graduated or not), and Activity link.

To remove an idea from an Ideation blog, select More Actions → Delete Idea for the idea and confirm that you want to remove it.

Frequently asked questions

Why is there a formal procedure to get the community restricted?
Bosch Connect as an open and transparent platform needs to be justified. Hence the goal is to have as few as possible communities (less then 20%) of all communities as restricted.
Can you have a restricted sub-community within a public/ moderated parent community?
Yes, this is possible. Please follow the same procedure as creating a restricted parent community.
Can you create a restricted sub-community within the restricted parent community?
Yes, this is possible. Please follow the same procedure as creating a restricted parent community.
Are the members in the parent community also added by default to the sub-community?
No, only the owners of the parent community are added by default as the owners of the sub-community during the creation of the sub-community. The members can be then added or invited to the sub-community. However the members also need to be part of the main community.
Can you request for a restricted community for setting up your community before the launch?
Yes, there are many instances wherein we have got such requests. Normally, the users like to set up their communities, make sure everything is in place and working fine before it is set open to the members. So you could have restricted access initially and then set it to public or moderated once you are ready.
Do you need to request for opening or changing the community access to public or moderated?
No, this can be done by you as community owners. Please note that after doing this it is not possible for you any more to switch back to a restricted community. Please follow the same procedure as creating a restricted parent community if the community needs to be restricted again.
Can non-members of the restricted community view your community?
Yes, the community can be searched by name if the community owner has enabled this for his community. However no content in the community will be viewable by non-members of a restricted community. To make it searchable: 
  1. Go to “Edit Community” (can be found on top right corner of your community)
  2. Tick the box "Let anyone in my organization see this community’s title, description, tags and owners".

Administrative requests: copying and merging content, transferring members 

Currently, on the Administration Requests forum you can request following tasks: 

  • Convert a community into a subcommunity — This can be done by each community owner now on their own
  • Convert a subcommunity into a community — This can be done by each community owner now on their own
  • Add an owner to a community
  • Merge two blogs
  • Merge two ideation blogs
  • Copy a stand-alone blog into a community
  • Merge two wikis
  • Copy a stand-alone wiki into a community  (valid for older wikis; there is no possibility to set up a stand-alone wiki anymore)
  • Merge two forums
  • Copy a forum into another community as a new forum
  • Merge Activities
  • Remove all members of a community
  • Remove all inactive members of a community
  • Activate inactive members within a community

However, there are some technical limitations by doing these changes:

RequestFirst — please note the following before doing so:

I'd like to copy the contents of a wiki into another wiki

  • It is not possible to copy single wiki pages as only the whole wiki can be copied
  • The contents of the source wiki will be added to the target wiki depending on the hierarchy in the source wiki. You can clean up and rearrange the pages according to your needs afterwards.
  • The author of the wiki pages will be replaced by our administrative user account, but it is possible to automatically add a line below each wiki page indicating who added this wiki page originally ("originally posted by ..."). Also, if you edit the copied wiki page again, the administrative user will be replaced by your name again.
  • Wiki page comments can be copied with the author's name, but the time stamp will be changed to date and time of the copy job
  • The timestamp of the last update of the wiki page will be changed to date and time of the copy job
  • All former versions of the copied wiki page will be lost as only the current version will be copied
  • All likes of a wiki page will be lost
  • Links to your wiki pages will change as the new wiki will have another ID that is encoded in the URL of each wiki page
  • We cannot guarantee that the copy job will work 100%. Sometimes single attachments cannot be copied. The copy job cannot be undone and missing data needs to be copied manually by the user who requested it.

I'd like to copy the contents of a forum into another forum

  • It is not possible to copy single forum topics as only the whole forum can be copied
  • You are free to choose, if the forum topics should be copied into an existing forum or if you want to have everything copied into a new blank forum
  • The authors of the forum topic and replies will be kept
  • Timestamps of the forum topics and replies will be lost, but it is possible to automatically add a line below each forum topic and reply indicating who posted it originally and when ("originally posted by ...").
  • All likes on a forum topic and like of the replies will be lost
  • Links to your forum topics will change as all data is only copied and therefore cannot exist twice under the same URL
  • We cannot guarantee that the copy job will work 100%. Sometimes single replies or attachments cannot be copied. The copy job cannot be undone and missing data needs to be copied manually by the user who requested it.

I'd like to copy the contents of an (ideation) blog into another (ideation) blog

  • It is not possible to copy single blog posts or ideas as only the whole (Ideation) blog can be copied
  • All blog posts of a copied blog will be added into an existing or blank community or stand-alone blog
  • For Ideation Blogs you are free to choose, if the ideas should be copied into an existing Ideation Blog or into a new blank Ideation Blog within your community
  • The authors of the blog posts/ideas and blog comments will be kept
  • Likes of blog posts will be kept. In addition a list of all people who liked the blog post/idea will be added below each copied blog post/idea. (We have requested at the vendor to stop adding this to copied blog posts/ideas.)
  • Likes of blog post comments will be lost
  • Votes of ideas will be kept
  • Blog post drafts will be lost
  • Blog post views/visits will be lost
  • Timestamps of the blog posts/ideas will be kept
  • Timestamps of the blog post comments/idea comment will be lost
  • It is possible to automatically add a line below each blog post indicating who added this blog post originally in which blog ("originally posted by ... in blog ...")
  • You need to check and take care that commenting on each blog post that should be migrated is allowed (and not expired). Otherwise the blog post comments will not be migrated!
  • Links to your Blog posts and ideas will change as all data is only copied and therefore cannot exist twice under the same URL
  • We cannot guarantee that the copy job will work 100%. Sometimes single comments cannot be copied. The copy job cannot be undone and missing data needs to be copied manually by the user who requested it.
  • If the comments include person tags (@mentions) it could be possible that after the copy process the mentions generate another notification email.

I'd like to copy the contents of an Activity into another Activity

Not possible now. 


Please add your request into the Administration Requests forum and list:

  • Correct name and URL/link to each source community, blog, forum, etc. (also, if the community is restricted)
  • Correct name and URL/link to each destination community, blog, forum, etc. (also, if the community is restricted)
  • What should be copied or converted
  • Do you want to have the "originally posted by ..." line below each blog post, forum reply, etc.?
  • Confirmation that you have read and accepted the technical limitations (see table above)
  • For restricted communities: please add the support colleague that is working on your request as an owner to your community. Thanks!

Deleting communities

If a community no longer has a purpose or is inactive, you might want to delete it. Ensure that the community is not in use. Any subcommunities that are part of the community are also deleted.

When you delete a community, all data that is associated with it is moved to a trash area. Provided it is not purged from trash later.

You can restore the community for no more than 30 days. 

To delete a community you, first of all need to be the Owner of said Community and then take the following steps. Be sure that you enter the correct case of any characters that you enter.

  2. Select Community Actions > Delete Community.
  3. Enter the name of the community in the Confirm community name field.
  4. Enter your name in the Sign with your name field. and click OK.

Access levels and roles

Depending on the access level you have to files, you can view, like or recommend, or edit them. There are three primary levels of access for any file: 

  1. Private;

  2. Shared with specific people or communities with either reader or editor access;

  3. Public (when a file is given public access, anyone can read and download it, even people who are not logged in. After they log in, people can also share the file, add it to a folder, comment on it, and receive notification when someone edits it or comments on it).

File owners can choose to allow other people to share files. When someone shares a file with you, they can give you reader or editor access:

  • Reader access: Readers can read, comment on, download, and recommend a file, be notified of changes to the file, and share the file. They can add a file to one of their folders, or to a folder to which they have Editor access.

  • Editor access: Editors can read, edit, comment on, download, recommend, upload a new version of, and set file properties. They can be notified of changes to the file, and share it. Editors can also add a file to a folder of theirs, or to a folder to which they have Editor access.

To see what access you and others have for a file, open its file page and click Sharing.

Working with files

Before starting work on files in Bosch Connect, please read about general rules and decide, if you need social functions. 

If you don‘t need social functions but rather want to work on the content of a file with others, using SharePoint is recommended because of the better co-editing and sharing functionality. Files on SharePoint Sites can also be integrated in a Bosch Connect Community. 

Uploading a file

  1. In the Files view click New → Upload (to quickly upload a file, you can drag and drop a file anywhere in the browser window)

  2. Click Browse, select one or more files, and click Open.

  3. Upload

You can tag and share files during or after upload. Important: If you want to upload a file that belongs to a community, please use the Files component within the community. Open the community of your choice and then open the files component within this community to upload the file. Please do not use this alternative: More→  Files → New... →  New folder... / Upload... and Share with People as the file is owned by you and only shared with the community, but it would not be owned by the community.

To edit a file that is in My Drive, open it from anywhere, edit the content, and save the changes. 

If you have Desktop Plug-in installed and configured, you can  edit it locally.

To edit file properties open the file page, and then click More over the selected file → More Actions → Edit Properties. Change the file name property, description, or file extension, and then click Save. You must be an owner or have Editor access to edit the properties of someone's file.

To add files to a folder open the file page, and then click Add to Folder. Select a folder, and then click Add to Folder (alternatively, you can open the folder page, click Add Files, and select previously uploaded files).

To move a file or more files you have Owner or Editor access to the file and to the destination location. You can move files in any of the following ways:

  • Drag and drop multiple files from the current location to a location in the navigation tree.

  • Drag and drop multiple files from the current location in the content pane to another location in the content pane.

  • Open the folder that contains the files you want to move, select the files you want to move, and click Move. Select a destination in the Move to... window.

  • Files that are not shared externally cannot be moved to a folder that allows access by external users.
