What's a forum?

Bosch Connect forum is one of the Community Apps and is used as an online discussion board where people can ask questions and discuss topics of mutual interest. By participating in a forum, you can exchange ideas, ask questions, and use the expertise of people in your organization. The recommended business cases are project discussions, organizational discussions and product help and support.

Go to the tab More → Forums→ Public forums to see the list of all forums. 

Forum type

We provide only community forum embedded in a community.

How to discuss?

To create a new topic click on the forum of your choice and then click "Start a topic". Next fill up the fields giving an appropriate title and typing your statement. We recommend to tag your statement as well. Here you can also mark your content as a question. As an author you can edit, delete or move your forum post either to a forum in the same community (community owners and topic authors can edit, move, and delete forum topics).

When moderation is enabled for Forums, any content that users add to forums is not displayed until it is approved by a moderator (= community owner). A moderator for Forums can review and manage forum topics before they are published and review forum topics that are already available.

In addition, you can flag a content as inappropriate. A notification is sent then to the community owner who reviews the content and decides what action to take.


Use "Reply" under the already published forum entry (=forum post) to publish your statement. You can also choose to reply to another reply. This would help visualizing the conversation better. 

Use filtering options in the topic, in the top right bottom of the forum, to sort conversations by date.  

There is a quick solution to link any reply in the forum. With "Response permalink" you can modify the page address in your browser in the way, that the anchor to the chosen forum post will be added direct into the page address. After that you can copy the whole modified page address i.e. into MS Teams messages or another forum, so that someone else can find a specific reply faster. 

Modify Display settings to change the display order. The replies can be displayed by date or by conversations.


Forum vs. Topic; Topic vs. Question 


A forum consists different topics about similar issues and in turn a topic is a discussion (or a question) about one specific subject. An example:  Forum = Support for Bosch Connect; Topic 1 = How to generate a restricted community?, Topic 3 = How to upload my profile? 

A topic will be published on the forum with a document icon, when a question will be shown with a question mark icon. All answered questions are displayed with a tick icon. 

As a result each forum has three categories of topics:   

  • regular discussion topics;
  • questions with an accepted answer;
  • questions that need to be answered.

This makes it possible to get a quick overview when looking on the forum page.


Do's and don’t's while using forums in Bosch Connect 

The following Do's and Don't's are recommended for forums. They are based on lessons learned of many existing communities on Bosch Connect. 

Do's 

Don't's 

  • Categorize the discussion topics by creating separate forums. 
  • Define forum moderators for maintenance, at least one moderator is crucial for success. Moderators need to ensure that discussion topics are in the correct forum category, answer questions and guide experts to open questions or hot topics. 
  • Define a tagging structure for better categorization i.e. FAQ, solved-issue, etc. 
  • When you open a forum, you are responsible for it. This means you have to make sure that the discussion is starting and is going into the right direction.... you are the "talk master" and you also need to moderate in conflicting situations (de-escalation) 
  • Consider to end never-ending discussions or bring user back on track. 
  • Define proper Tags for your Forum and ensure tagging by your users. At the beginning, make sure to assist users in tagging their topics properly, and add tags actively if they miss it. 

 

  • Do not use a Forum without any moderator in place 
  • Do not let people wait too long for an answer 
  • Do not forget to clean up the forum time to time (duplicates, outdated content, etc.) 
  • Do not start a forum outside a community, as it reduces visibility of your forum and you can't move it into a community later. 
  • End discussions that lost focus on their original topic / question 

 

Start a new forum

Use Forum community app by adding the wiki component to your community.  

Click Start a Topic to add topics to your new forum. If you do not want to create topics now, you can access the forum later from the My Forums page.

Pinning forum topics

Highlight or prioritize important topics by pinning them. When you pin a topic, it stays at the beginning of that forum's topic listing to ensure that it receives attention from forum users. To pin a topic in a community forum, you must be a community owner. Pinning a topic makes that the topic easy to find in a large forum. For example, if you are posting a topic that contains details about an important event, then you can pin the topic so that users can find it easily. Pinned topics are marked with a thumbtack icon (pinned topic icon). 

Note: When you pin a topic in a community forum and the community contains multiple forums, the pinned topic is not displayed at the head of the Topics tab on the Forums page. You must open the forum from the Forums tab to see pinned topics at the head of the forum.

To pin a forum topic, complete the following steps:

  1. Open the topic that you want to pin.
  2. Click Pin this Topic under the topic.

Select Unpin this Topic to restore it to its regular place in the sequence of topics.

Locking forums and forum topics

Lock a forum to prevent users from contributing to the forum or updating existing posts. If you do not want to lock an entire forum, you can control access at topic level by locking forum topics. To lock a community forum or community forum topic, you must be a community owner.

  • To lock a forum, select Forum Actions → Lock Forum. The forum is marked as locked to advise users that they cannot contribute to the forum. As the forum owner, you can still edit content in the forum. To unlock a forum, open the forum and select Forum Actions → Unlock Forum
  • To lock a forum topic, click Lock Topic. The topic is marked as locked. Users can still read the topic and responses but cannot add or edit anything in the thread. As the forum owner, you can still edit a locked topic and post replies to it even though the topic remains locked for everyone else. For example, if a topic contains inappropriate content, you can lock the topic and then delete or edit replies without having to reopen the topic.

Adding and removing forum owners

If you are a forum owner, you can add more owners to a forum to share the responsibilities of forum ownership. To add more owners to a forum, complete the following steps:

  1. From the Forums tab on the My Forums page, open the forum to which you want to add new owners.
  2. In the Owners area, click Add Owners.
  3. Enter the names of the people who you want to add as owners in the field provided. As you enter names, the type-ahead function predicts the name that you are typing by comparing it to names in your company directory. If it proposes the name that you want, click the name to add it. If the name is not listed, click Person not listed? Use full search to search the company directory.
  4. Click OK to add the new owners.

If you want to remove owners from the forum, clicking the Remove icon near their names in the Owner area.

Renaming forum

As owner of the forum click the "Forum Actions" drop down on the upper right where you find the "Edit Forum" entry to rename your Forum.

Moving forum threads to another forum

As owner you can easily click on "move" in the first thread entry and then select the different target forum. But this works only for internal movement within different forums in one community, so only within one forum application. No movement like this is possible to/from standalone forum or between communities.

Copying and merging content

Please, read more about technical possibilities to transfer your forum content here.

Deleting forums

Delete forums when they are no longer being used. To delete a community forum, you must be a community owner. If you find that a forum is no longer in use, you might decide to delete it. Deleting a forum removes it permanently from the Forums application. When you want to prevent users from updating a forum, but still allow them to view its content, consider locking the forum instead of deleting it. To delete a forum, complete the following steps:

  1. Open the forum that you want to delete.
  2. Select Forum Actions → Delete Forum.
  3. Click Delete to confirm that you want to delete the forum.

Frequently asked questions

No.QuestionAnswer
1.

If I have a multitude of Forums in my Community, is there a possibility to use the search function together in all the forums?

There is a limit of 5 forums for which you can use the search function altogether. The forum limit can't be changed as it could cause several performance issues.

2.Is there a possibility to archive a forum which hasn’t been used in a long time for storage space cleaning?Unfortunately, we don't have an archive function for our forums. You could only delete them or lock them so that nothing else can be posted.
3. How to move / merge my forum?You will find more information here.

page_name: Images and videos in Bosch Connect
html_content:
Images and videos in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

Images sources and corporate design 

You are obligated to follow the common copyrights and not allowed to use any googled image. Here you can find secure image sources with pictures and graphics which you can use in your corporate projects:   

  • PowerPoint Design Kit eForms 
  • Bosch Digital Design System, where you can also find i.a. Corporate Colors data and Icon Library 
  • Bosch Media Service Portal  for overall Bosch specific images 
  • Bosch Media Space for Bosch  mobility / automotive specific images 

Feel free, how you want to set up your pages on Bosch Connect, however we can recommend you to follow Bosch Digital System and use of corporate colors. The Corporate Design Colors with the saturation values 100% and 50% you can find directly in Bosch Connect editor for texts and backgrounds colors.

Using the Editor

In Bosch Connect you post your images and videos using the editor. Please, go to the Editor page to get to know it better, especially the section Posting images and videos.

Embed Images from SharePoint to Bosch Connect

First you will need to make sure you get the correct link to the image from SharePoint following bellow steps:

  1. Go to desired image on your SharePoint page
  2. Open the image in a new tab
  3. Copy link of the image from new tab
  4. Go to the desired Bosch Connect App where you wish to add the image
  5. Click on the insert menu in the editor
  6. Then use the insert/edit image function
  7. Go to Web URL and paste the link

Embed Bosch Tube Media

First you need to upload the file to Bosch Tube, which is our official corporate streaming platform. 

In the editor click on + sign and choose Embed Bosch Tube Media (a new window will pop up, where you can upload your video on Bosch Tube) or choose already uploaded video file. If you are not satisfied with the default embed settings of the integration click on the Settings button and configure the size of the embedded video, start and end time, auto-play and thumbnail features. 

This editor integration is available in Blogs, Wikis, Forum and Rich Content apps. To learn more about Bosch Tube in general, you may visit:  
  • Bosch Tube Docupedia 
  • Which Bosch Tube Training to choose...

Please keep in mind that using the editor integration will not keep the restrictions set up from Bosch Tube, which means that if you have created a Bosch Tube video restricted to a group of people, using the editor integration from Bosch Connect will give access to all the members who have access to the Blogs, Wikis , Forums and Rich Content Apps (which could mean that if they are public, every Bosch Connect user could access the video) and Restricted Communities (which could mean that all community members would see the video, even if the video was restricted to a smaller group of people from Bosch Tube). If you wish to keep the restrictions set in place from Bosch Tube, the only option would be to use the "Embed Code" from Bosch Tube and copy it to the Bosch Connect blogs, wikis or rich content apps.

Bosch Connect Key Visual

Bosch Connect uses HCL Connections key visual. Please find more information about the key visual change here. 

You can find files with our key visual here.

Please, be aware that you are not allowed to modify the key visual - it's a property of HCL Connections and protected by law.

Networking in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

Building your network

Invite someone to join your network. Once they accept, they'll be added to your Network Contacts and you can view each other's status updates. 

  1. Open the person's profile. 
  2. Click Invite to My Network. 
  3. Accept the default message or write a message of your own. 
  4. Enter the keywords that define how you are connected in the Add tags for name field (optional)
  5. If you want updates from this person to display on both your  Home page and in an email summary of updates, click Also Follow.
  6. Click  Send invitation. 

In the tab My profile → My Network → Invitations you will find invitations sent to you. To accept the invitation and join the person's network, click  Accept or click on the person's name and accept the invitation from their profile page.

To ignore someone's invitation and delete it from the Invitations tab, click Ignore  (they won't be notified). 

Follow a person to keep current with their activities and status updates, without having to add them to your network: 

  1. Click on a person's name to open their profile. 
  2. Click Follow. 



Inviting Vs. Following  

Follow and Invite to Network are very similar functionality. Network is for people you want to be connected to, follow is for people you want to listen to. If someone is in my network, everyone else may see this personal connection and benefit from that, e.g. maybe ask one of my network contacts while I'm absent for assistance on a certain topic, or invite that person to his/her own network for better collaboration. Followers can only be seen by you and the person that follows you, but no one else.  

  •  If you have somebody as a network contact without follow-setting, you will not see what this person is posting as a status update or doing within the communities, blogs, forums, activities, files, etc. as long as you are not following the affected communities, blogs, etc. 
  • If you have somebody as a network contact including following, you will see everything this person is posting as a status update and doing in public and moderated communities. (Restricted communities are of course still hidden for non-members.) 
  • If you follow a person, but don't have him/her in your network contacts, you will also see everything (same as above).  


Source: CI Academy Training

Managing contacts 

Go to the tab People → My Network to view your contacts, following profiles (people you follow), followers (people following your profile) and invitations as well contact suggestions in People you may know section.  

You can also add a profile of your colleagues to "Important to me" menu bar.

If you want to remove a single contact:  

  1. Click the person's name to open their profile. 
  2. Click Remove From Network. 

To remove multiple contacts: 

  1. Open the My Network page, and click My Network Contacts. 
  2. Select the check box next to each person that you want to remove, and click Remove from My Network. 

You cannot remove your followers.  

If you remove a person from your network, s:he will not be notified about this.

Notifications in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

My notifications

There are several ways to be informed about what is going on in your network on Bosch Connect:

  • Latest Updates tab is accessed automatically through the Home button of Bosch Connect and shows all the updates for profiles and communities which you follow sorted by date. On the upper left corner, you can choose between four different categories: I'm Following; Mentions; My Notification; Action Required; Saved.
  • Top Updates shows updates for the followed items which have been prioritized automatically by the system for you. On the upper left corner you can choose between three different categories: Top Updates; Mentions; Responses.
  • Important to me bar (at the right side navigation menu) - here you can add people or communities. By clicking on the icon of a profile or community, you can see the updates affecting this person or community. By hovering over the icon, the system gives you the possibility to go to the person's profile.
  • Notification Center (bell icon in the lower left corner of the navigation menu). 
  • Daily/weekly mail newsletters and single notification mails for specific activities. → Email Notifications (bosch.com)

Changing Settings

You can modify the notifications types and frequency. Access your Profile in the lower left corner and then go to Settings.

Trending Topics

Our Trending Topics report shows which blog posts, wiki pages and ideas are trending in Bosch Connect at the moment.

To access it, go to the Burger menu → Trending Topics.

The ranking is calculated daily by a particular algorithm looking on user activity within the last 10, 20 and 30 days. In the navigation, you can filter for more details on the trending blogs posts, wiki pages and ideas. It is also possible to filter for trending topics within all Bosch divisions (according to COMPAS) and to download the report.

BC Wall

BC Wall reads status updates from the general Activity Stream and from communities that are not older than 30 days or have been edited, liked, reposted or commented on during the last 30 days.

To access it, go to the Burger menu → BC Wall. 

You can have a more visual understanding of what BC Wall is and how to use it by completing this Learning Nugget.

You can either show all status updates from Bosch Connect or refine your BC Wall to specific content (e.g. a buzzword like "agile" or the name of your event, e.g. "ibmconnect2016"). BC Wall does not only read tags, but also the complete text of a status update (so all related status updates will be shown, even if no (hash)tag was used by the person who posted it).  

If you want to show status update of a specific community, i.e. NGW Community enter "communityUuid=fc29ba88-808b-49d7-9439-4f1735f3c0f5" (please copy the communityUuid from the URL available in address bar your browser).

You can modify the display settings in burger menu on the upper right corner from BC Wall.  

As community owner, you can also add the BC-Wall to your community. Add Rich Editor community app and use IFRAME (here the tutorial):

<iframe src="https://connect.bosch.com/public/bcwall/#/?q=%23your-special-hashtag1%20OR%20your-special-hashtag2" allowtransparency="true" width="99%" height="400" frameborder="0"></iframe>

If you use one or more search tags, replace the bold marked red text string(s) by your tag(s). If you only use one tag, then skip also the %20OR%20 text string. You also can use the "AND" if you need two or more tags as combination.

The BC Wall can be used on (social) events on a big screen to show participants what other participants of the events are posting on Bosch Connect about the event.

If you need support to BC Wall, please use the thread in our support forum. 

RSS reader

If you want to get notified about blog entries which are tagged with your interests, use the RSS reader.

1. Access Blogs (click More) and choose Public Blogs from top navigation.
2. On the left side, go to the Latest Blog Entries
3. Select the topics which are interesting for you by entering the topic/tag or clicking on the corresponding tag
4. Below the results list you will find the link Feed for Blog Entries. Click on it and choose Subscribe in Your Browser. 

You can also use the RSS icon on other Bosch Connect pages to add content to your RSS reader. 





In the Microsoft Support center you can find out, how to add RSS fields directly to your Outlook.

Information overload

To avoid an information overload:

  • Maintain notification settings and review your network 
  • Do not follow everything. For example follow tags only instead of whole communities. Follow the things only that you are interested in as following a lot of content increases the information flow in your activity stream.
  • Use rules in your e-mail inbox for incoming notifications.

page_name: Profile and Posting in Bosch Connect
html_content:
Profile and Posting in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

Setting up the profile 

Your profile was set up as you as you received Bosch Connect login and filled with your name and the organizational information. 

If your profile information in Bosch Connect is not displayed correctly we kindly ask that you check our blog post on how this information gets to Bosch Connect and create an ITSD ticket if needed. If however, the blog post does not help with your specific issue, we kindly ask that you create a new topic in the Support forum and we will be happy to help you out. However, you can add (edit, delete) your job description displayed next to your name on your own. 

The  first time you access Bosch Connect, a guided tour will automatically start. You will be asked to add more information and a photo. If you close the guided tour, you can always go back to editing your profile.. Just click on the Profile icon in the lower left corner and choose Edit Profile.   

In the profile page you will see your name, location, office, mail and local time, as well some shortcut buttons: Send Mail (opens MS Outlook), Download vCard, Share a File, Invite to my Network, Follow. After a person has been added to network or followed, you can be remove or stop following them from the 3 dots menu.


The profile section comprises four tabs:  

  • Recent updates displays the profile owner's status, messages, comments posted to their profile, and notifications about their actions. Click Filter by and make a selection to control the types of posts displayed in this section. 
  • Contact information displays office location and organizational user data.
  • Background, where you can find user’s summary of their skills, interests, and experiences.
  • BEO Expertise displays expertise areas of a user.

Click Edit Profile button on the Profile page, below your photo, to add, modify or delete information about yourself. You can also add a file with your name pronunciation.

In the My Links section (found on the right side of the page) you can also share with other users links to social media pages, helpful industry websites, and other external resources directly from your profile.

Profile picture 

In the Profile page, go to Edit Profile → Photo to add or remove your photo. You can choose a file from your computer – the photo must be saved in *.jpeg, *.gif or *.png format in recommended size of 155x155 px.  

We recommend you try out Bosch Connect Picture Generator, which automatically sets the recommended size to one of your pictures and let's you add one of the available Bosch corporate statements. Please note, that you have to download the picture from the BC Picture Generator and upload it to your Profile page to see changes on your Profile page. It is also possible to extend the tool with user-uploaded frames without doing any software development. If you are interested to prepare your own frame or you want to contribute to the project as developer, please visit this page BCPPG Development.

Posting messages and updating status 

Directly from the Activity Stream on homepage (site, where you can see all updates) and in the Latest Updates tab, you can share your post by clicking What do you want to share?. You can also add a file to your post. Each post can be shared and commented by others (these comments you can delete), but you can not edit your status update, only delete it or share it again. In all posts you can mention other users by adding @ before the name and tag your content.   

The characters limits for your status update is 1000 characters (incl. spaces). To review all status updates visit our BC Wall. 

If you would like to add a longer text as a blog post, please visit the Blogs page.

Comments, Likes, Trackback

You can comment and like the content on Bosch Connect. The author of the content will be notified about your comment or like. 

Use the trackback feature to turn your comment into a blog post visible on your stand-alone blog or on your community blog.

Searching in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

General Search and logical operators

On the top of all Bosch Connect pages, you can find the Search Bar. When clicking on the search, you will be shown a history of recently visited pages in Bosch Connect. When inserting content in the search bar, you will be shown options that include your search input from All Content, Communities, People and Files respectively. Type the word you want to search for into the search bar and press “Enter”.

In the Bosch Connect search bar you can also use the following marks and operators to leverage your search results:

  • Double quotation marks to search for a phrase: “example phrase”
  • Question mark to replace a single character of the word: te?t will show all the results for text and for test (limitation: you cannot use ? as the first character of the search term)
  • Asterisk to replace zero or more characters in the word: test* will result with test, tests and testers (limitation: you cannot use * as the first character of the search term)
  • OR between two words returns information that contains either the first or the second word: car OR motorcycle
  • AND to search for content where both terms exist anywhere in the text of a single document: cat AND dog
  • + is similar to the AND operator, but it applies only to the word immediately following it: blue+car
  • - operator to exclude a word from your search. Results containing the symbol immediately following the operator are excluded by the search: house –castle (limitation: Using the NOT operator, exclamation point (!), or minus sign (-) with a single term returns no results)
  • You can also group search results. For example, if you want to search for information that contains plane and car or plane and motorcycle, enter the following query: (car OR motorcycle) AND plane


When your search term contains one of these non alphanumeric characters: + - && || ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ * ? : \ you need to escape the character by using a backslash ( \ ) before the character or by enclosing the search term in double quotation marks ("). If you do not perform this escape operation, the search in Bosch Connect interprets the characters as being part of the query instructions. For example, if you want to search for information that contains the text string cat + dog cat + dog and you enter cat + dog as your search term, Search looks for any data that contains both the word cat and the word dog. This result is because the plus sign (+) is a reserved operator with a predefined meaning. To search for information containing the actual text string cat + dog, use one of the following queries: cat \+ dog or "cat + dog".

Search Options

After inserting a keyword into the search bar and pressing enter, you are offered many search options and filters with which you can pinpoint your searches more accurately.

Searching across profiles and users groups

Click on the People → Directory tab and take advantage of Display full search options to find users according to their i.a. tags, job titles, units, countries, cities and much more.

On the user’s profile page in the Contact information tab you can also find another members of groups like legal entities, divisions, organizational units and cost centers. Hover over organizational unit link to choose, whether you want to search for profiles of this organizational unit in Bosch Connect, open the organizational unit’s page in Org Manager or open the BGN page.

Finding (BEO) Experts

To find BEO Experts, we recommend you to use Enterprise Search and filter People & Expertise.

However, you can also search experts directly on Bosch Connect with general searching, directory search (People → Directory) and using advanced filters.   

Searching with Enterprise Search

Bosch Connect is fully integrated within Enterprise Search. It means that your keyword typed into Enterprise Search bar will give the results also from Bosch Connect. On the Enterprise Search page you can also filter the search results very easily and choose only Bosch Connect as the search area or a specific part of Bosch Connect.

Frequently Asked Questions

No. QuestionAnswer
1.

How can you ensure when you search for related words that the correct document is found?

This is actually not possible. The search engine searches after keywords for possible correct documents, but it works the same like the google search. You do not know if the given results are also the correct ones. You just have to go through most of them to see which of them fits best with your search. If you still have difficulties in finding a certain document, please check logical operators and search options.

2. How can I find my own posts better?Search for you name and then set the filter to My own content, right below the name after loading. That should find most of the content you created.

Wiki in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

What's a wiki?

A wiki is a highly collaborative social Media tool. It allows you for example to create new content, collect information, co-create documents and archive your project documentation and much more. Also this Docupedia is an art of wiki.  

Go to the tab More → Wikis→ Public Wikis to see the list of all Wikis.

Why wiki? The Tool has its name by Ward Cunningham, who remembered a Honolulu International Airport counter employee telling him to take the "Wiki Wiki Shuttle" bus. He adopts the duplication “wiki wiki” which means a climax in Hawaiian and called his Tool WikiWikiWeb. 

Wiki type

With Bosch Connect Wiki community app. We provide only community wiki embedded in a community.

Wiki access levels

Access to a community wiki is managed by community owners. Membership roles in the community are replicated in the wiki. Community owners can edit wiki settings, and community members can create and edit pages in the wiki. Users who are not members of the community can read the wiki but cannot edit it.

TermsDefinitions
All users

Everyone can read the wiki, including people who are not logged in.

Wiki members only

Only people whom you specify as members can read the wiki.

All logged in usersAnyone who logs in can edit the wiki
Wiki editors and owners only

Only people to whom you grant editor or owner access.

EditorCan read, edit, comment, create, tag, and like pages
ReaderCan read, comment, and like pages
OwnerCan read, edit, comment, create, tag, like, and delete pages. Owners can tag the wiki and change the wiki description.

Starting a new Community Wiki

Use Wiki community app by adding the wiki component to your community.  

To create a wiki page, complete the following steps:

  1. In the Wiki area of the community's page, click New Page.
  2. Open a page at the same level at which you want to create a page.
  3. Click Page Actions → Create Peer to create a page at the same level as the current page.
  4. Click Page Actions → Create Child to create a page one level below the current page.
  5. Enter a name for the page in the Page Title: field. Choose a name that describes the page content.

  • If you can't add new pages, please read about access levels and contact the community owner.

You can add a variety of content types to the page as follows:

  • Enter your content in the Page Content: field.
  • Use the extensive formatting options, such Paragraph Formatting, Fonts, and Point Sizes to layout and format your content.
  • Use the Insert Image icon to either link-to or attach an image to the page.

If your page has many headings and subheadings, consider adding a table of contents as follows:

  • Place the cursor where you want the table of contents to be displayed.
  • Click the Macros list in the editor toolbar.
  • Select Table of Contents to add a table of contents to the page.

When you have finished click Save and Close.

Starting a stand-alone Wiki

If you want to create a stand-alone Wiki, you can do this now by going to More → Wikis and press the Start a Wiki button. The stand-alone wiki works the same as the community Wiki.

Managing wiki pages

Once you have created some wiki pages, you can work with them in many ways.

  1. Select Wiki on your community's Overview page, and open the page that you want to work with.
  2. There are lots of ways to work with pages, these are the most important:
    1. To create a child page of the page that you are on, select Page Actions → Create Child.
    2. To create a page on the same level as the wiki page that you are on, select Page Actions → Create Peer.
    3. To move the page, select Page Actions → Move Page and select one of the available options (you can also use drag&drop here and move pages with your mouse directly in the menu tree
    4. To delete the page, select Page Actions → Move to Trash... Community members with editor access can only delete pages that they created. Community owners can delete any page in the wiki.
    5. If you change your mind you can restore the deleted page (provided the trash is not emptied):
      • Select Trash from the navigation bar.
      • Select the page you deleted and click Restore.

Wiki owners and editors can check the wiki's size limit and usage by clicking Index. The current size limit is 500 MB for single wiki page and 1,5 GB for the whole wiki.

Please find information about size limits for wiki community app on Size limits page. 

While managing your wiki you can also try out non-standard features through BoschConnectTweak. 

Rolling back wiki pages to previous versions

When you create a page, an initial version is created. Your original work is saved in that first version of the page until you delete the page. Each time a wiki member edits a page, a new version of the page is created. The page displays version information such as the version number, when it was edited, the person who made the edits, and a link to each version. If you own a page, or have Editor or Owner access to it, you can restore an older version as the current version. Owners can also delete versions. To see versions of a page, open the page and click Versions.

Versioning is not possible with blog posts, only with Wiki.

Copying and merging content

Please, read more about technical possibilities to transfer your forum content here. 

Working on layout

Bosch Connect allows you to create and publish content with basic computer skills. However, it's is also possible to work with code.

If you want to prettify your pages using HTML/CSS and more advanced tips&tricks, please visit this page (it's also possible to implement a search engine to your content).

Getting notified about changes on a wiki

Receive updates when a wiki or wiki page changes. Notifications are displayed in your Home page, but you can also receive updates by email (read more about Notifications).

What do you want to do?

Tagging in Bosch Connect


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

What is a tag and why we use them? 

A tag is a keyword that serve as a short description for content in communities, forums, wikis, profiles etc. We use tags to categorize content and make it easier to find in search engines.  


How to add tags? 

You can use tags for nearly every content on Bosch Connect by clicking on “add tag” buttons or filling up “add tag” boxes.  

It’s possible to add tags to your profile by yourself or to add appropriate tags to someone else’s profile. You can also reuse a tag that is already present on the profile to make this tag more visible. Tags that you assign to a profile are listed separately from those that were assigned by others.  

  • Tagging your own profile 
  1. Open your own profile or the profile of the person you want to tag. 
  2. Type a tag name in the tag field. The name must be a single word only; it cannot contain spaces. You can use hyphen (-) to specify multiple word tag names. Separate multiple tags with commas or spaces. 
  3. Click the Add tags to this profile icon to add the tags to the profile. 
  • Tagging a person's profile 
  1. Open the profile page for the person that you want to tag. 
  2. Type the tag name in the Tags field. Type-ahead predicts the tag that you're typing and supplies available tag names. Select an available tag or continue typing to create a new tag. 
  3. Click the + icon to add the tag to the person's profile. 
  4. Enter additional tags as needed. 

The profile tags will be shown whether in form of a list (all tags) or in form of a cloud (the most frequent tags) and you can switch between them very easily while clicking.  

You can remove tags that you or another user added to your profile and remove tags that you added to another person's profile. 


@Mentioning  

Typing @ before user’s name on Bosch Connect creates a link directly to the profile page of the mentioned person. The mentioned user will be notified and can react on your content.  

Please, be aware that mentioning can't be used in the Rich Content App. 

Which tag should I apply? 

  • While sharing information worldwide, use English language for your tags. 
  • While entering tags, use the tag suggestions provided by Bosch Connect instead of creating new tags. 
  • While adding compound words as new tags, always use hyphen ( - ) as a separator.
  • Tags should not contain capital letters (and special characters are problematic as well)
  • Make sure to use the same tags for similar content as it increases findability for you and other people.
  • Keep it simple. Tags should be short, simple, and memorable. 

Where can I find already applied tags? 

You can find already applied profile tags in the tab Profile → My profile and the organization tags in the tab Profile/Directory where is placed a search box allowing you to find all the content assigned with a specific tag. You can also filter tags regarding all updates concerning the chosen tag. From Latest Updates you can set the filter button to Tags. Or you can go to Burger menu (top right)→ BC Wall.


Searching and notifications

Please, read more about monitoring tags in Notifications and Searching sections.

Go into your wiki and look into the left navigation bar. Below all wiki pages you will find Index and the Trash (Papierkorb). There you can delete removed pages by clicking on "Empty Trash" in the top bar.

Each wiki page has versioning. Go into your wiki index that can be found in the wiki on the left side if you look below the list of your wiki pages. Click on "Index" and filter for "size". If you cannot filter for Size you need to adapt your display setting in the upper right corner (to "Summary of all entries"). Pages that have a huge size may also have lots of versions. You can attach files to single wiki pages. Go into your wiki index that can be found in the wiki on the left side if you look below the list of your wiki pages. You can also use the script of @Tuermer Joerg (ST-FIR/ENG4) to identify where you can save some storage within your Wikis.


Check, if Bosch Connect the correct place for your files. Please note that Bosch Connect is not intended to be a Document Management System. Therefore not all files belong to Bosch Connect. We recommend to have a look at: Storage Guide 4.0 – now with Microsoft 365 storage locations.


Extra space 

Bosch Connect is charged to every IT user by default. The cost is included in the mandatory Standard IT User LASL ("Leistungsartenschlüssel"). We do not charge the storage in Bosch Connect separately. Because of that we do not have any mechanism in place to charge you for additional storage and it is also not planned to change this. We do however constantly monitor the needs of our users and act accordingly if necessary. If you would have questions in this matter, please contact us on the support forum.

What does migration mean?


Migration means Microsoft Teams will be your only communication and collaboration tool. 

Question Answer
What will you receive after migration?

You will receive Teams Only;

  • with Public Telephony or
  • without Public Telephony.
Does the migration happen automatically?

Bosch is planned location-based rollout. You will be informed by your location rollout coordinator once it's planned or you can check the rollout status on the Welcome Page (link). And then the migration will take place automatically. You can also join the migration earlier via the order form. 

 Please check first if your location is prepared for Public Telephony. If not, you will lost this feature.

 For BSH users migration from Skype for Business to Teams Only is automatically. 

What is Teams Only with Public Telephony?

It is an optional service for Microsoft Teams. If this service is enabled for you, it will provide you the possibility to reach out telephone numbers like e. g. +49 711 811 3311. In addition this service will provide you a standard landline telephone number to be called from standard telephone devices. Here you can find more details.

For using Teams Public Telephony your user account needs to be migrated to Microsoft Teams only mode!

In which locations is Teams Only Public Telephony available?

Here you can find currently available locations.

What is the rollout plan?

Two options are possible:

  1. Location rollout:

If your location is accessible to Public Telephony, you will have Teams Only with Public Telephony after migration. If it isn`t available yet - you need to wait until it will be. Locations will run one after another:


 Please note, the Teams Public Telephony service is currently in testing (Early Adopter Network). The plan is to provide this service at all locations, where currently the Skype for Business Public Telephony service is offered. You can check available locations here.

   2. Migrate earlier on your own:

To migrate before location based rollout, you can do it on your own using ITSP order form. During ordering process you will see if your location is available for Teams Public Telephony.

  • If not → you will get Teams Only without PT 

 NOTE If you have Bosch manged mobile device, a more economical solution for you would be Teams Only without Public Telephony. If you accept the conditions, you can apply it via the order form before the migration took place at your location.

  • If your location isn`t available for PT and you need to have this feature → wait until location based rollout
Will I keep my Public Telephony feature after migration to Teams Only? 

There are two possible scenarios:

  1. Migration on your own:

During the ordering process via the order form you can see if your location is available for Public Telephony or not:

Teams PT availableTeams PT not available
  2. Locations based rollout:

If you want to wait until location based rollout take place whether or not you get Public Telephony feature depends on your location. There are two types of locations: such, in which PT is available and you will be able to keep your PT and such, in which it isn`t offered. 



 NOTE If you do not need Public Telephony feature, you can apply for the Teams Only without Public Telephony via the order form before the migration  took place at your location.

What will happen after migration to Teams Only with Public Telephony?
  • Your landline number stays the same like in SfB
  • Telephony permissions (local, premium etc. ) stay the same like in SfB

  • All your current telephony configurations like call groups and call forwarding settings will be removed. You need to setup these settings

  • Incoming calls will end up in MS Teams

  • You will lose the SfB federation feature (direct communication to users from other companies) and you need to activate the Federation feature in Teams separately

What will happen after migration to Teams Only without Public Telephony?
  • If you had a Public Telephony feature before, your number will be removed permanently (no reservation)

  • You will not be able to call any external phone numbers with Teams. Note that this also applies for emergency calls, e.g. 112 or 911 and Bosch internal service hotlines, e.g. IT Service Desk (-3311) or HR Service hotline. You will have to use another phone or your mobile phone to reach these numbers. Vice versa, IT Service Desk won’t be able to reach you via a phone call unless you own a mobile device which number is maintained in CI-CAT (personal IT data system)

  • You will lose the SfB Federation feature (direct communication to users from other companies), instead you can apply for the Federation in Teams. It works differently.
  • All your current telephony configurations like call groups and call forwarding settings will be reset to default - you need to setup these settings after migration by your own. 
How can I reach IT Support?
You can reach it via IT Service Portal to initiate instant chat or create a ticket. If you have a business mobile phone you can also use it for this purpose.
Can I still use Skype for Business?
After migrations to Teams Only your Skype for Business functionalities will be reduced to minimum (only for joining meetings).

Pre-information for IT User Request

Your digital workplace at Bosch consists of two main parts: To be able to work efficiently you need a device (hardware) and an IT user. General information

Internal users include all Bosch associates, including subsidiaries. External users are needed when we collaborate with partners, customers, or service providers and want to give them access to Bosch content. With an External User, non-Bosch associates can also access (selected) Bosch content and/or use our shared communication media.

Employees from the production-related environment are referred to as direct workers (also known as "blue collars"). Indirect workers are mostly office employees, for example for administrative activities or software development (also known as "white-collar").

In terms of the hardware used, a distinction is made between whether the device is (mainly) used by one person alone or whether the device is shared with other colleagues. In the production area in particular, there are devices that are used by many colleagues, for example to exchange information on machines or to log on to a kiosk for a short time. For this reason the so called "Shared PC" or "Shared PC extended" is available. A detailed description of the Shared PC is available: SharedPC and Shared PC extended.

In the office area, the devices are mainly assigned to a single employee. Employees here usually work on the devices for several hours a day.

Depending on the user type you need to distinguish between an internet connection provided by Bosch and the necessity of an own private internet connection. Bosch provides an internet connection in the office area as well as for SharedPC in the production environment. A user needs to have a special IdM role to be able to access the internet. If this role is not available, the connection is limited to less available pages, e.g. to access Microsoft 365 applications and documents.

If a user wants to work outside a Bosch office (e.g. working from home) he needs an own private internet connection, which is not offered by Bosch. Anyway, the IdM role to access the internet is needed here as well.

To access the Bosch Associate Portal by using a private device (e.g. a private mobile phone) the employee needs to have a private internet connection as well.

Depending on the assigned license, a User type can use the Microsoft 365 applications in the browsers only (web version, so called F3 license) or additionally installed on his computer (so called E3 license). More information about differences and possible limitations are listed: Microsoft 365. 

There are multiple possibilities to ensure that you have assigned the best user types for each use case within your organization. The correct assignment of user types will reduce license costs and delivers the optimal feature cost balance for you.

  1. Check if you have users where the "Base IT User" profile would be sufficient but the "Standard IT User" profile is assigned. You can use the tables on the subpages to check, if the functionalities provided with the "Basic IT User" are sufficient for your use case.
  2. Check which profiles are assigned to your external users and if the "External Collaboration User (EXU2)" would be sufficient.
  3. Check if you have inactive users / not needed user accounts or users who have never used the features of the Microsoft 365 full license and nevertheless have an assigned "Standard IT User" assigned.

Power BI Cloud - Workspaces Overview

Here you can find all information related to workspaces in Power BI Cloud.

General information

Workspaces are places to collaborate with colleagues on specific content. Workspaces are created by Power BI designers to hold collections of dashboards and reports. The designer can then share the workspace with colleagues. Designers can also bundle a collection of dashboards and reports into an app and distribute it to the entire community, to their organization, or to specific people or groups. 

Everyone using the Power BI Cloud also has a My workspace. My workspace is your personal sandbox where you can create content for yourself.

You can see your workspaces in Power BI by selecting Workspaces from your navigation pane.

Types of workspaces

My Workspace stores all the content that you own and create. Think of it as your personal sandbox or work area for your own content. For many Power BI business users, My workspace remains empty because your job doesn't involve creating new content. Business users, by definition, consume data created by others and use that data to make business decisions. 

Workspaces contain all the content for a specific app. When a designer creates an app, they bundle together all the content that is necessary for that app to be utilized. Content may include dashboards, reports, and datasets. Not every app will contain these three pieces of content. An app may contain only one dashboard, or three of each content type, or even twenty reports. It all depends on what the designer includes in the app. Commonly, app workspaces shared with business users don't include the datasets.

The Bosch Demo Workspace below contains a dashboard, a report, a workbook, and a dataset.

Permissions in the workspaces

Access permissions determine what you can do in a workspace, so teams can collaborate. When granting access to a new workspace, designers add individuals or groups to one of the workspace roles: Viewer, Member, Contributor, or Admin.

As a Power BI business user, you'll typically interact in workspaces using the Viewer role. But a designer could also assign you to the Member or Contributor role. The Viewer role lets you view and interact with content (dashboards, reports, apps) created by others and shared with you. And because the Viewer role can't access the underlying dataset, it's a safe way to interact with content and not have to worry that you'll "hurt" the underlying data.

Licensing, workspaces, and capacity

Licensing also plays a part in determining what you can and can't do in a workspace. Many features require the user to have a Power BI Pro license or for the workspace to be stored in Premium capacity.

Often, business users work with a free license. If the content isn't stored in Premium capacity, the business user won't have access.

If the workspace is stored in Premium capacity, business users will be able to view and interact with the content in that workspace. A diamond icon identifies the workspaces that are stored in Premium capacity.

Roles

Roles let you manage who can do what in the new workspaces, so teams can collaborate. New workspaces allow you to assign roles to individuals, and to user groups: security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, and distribution lists.

To grant access to a new workspace, assign those user groups or individuals to one of the workspace roles: Admin, Member, Contributor, or Viewer. Here's how to Give users access to the new workspaces.

Everyone in a user group gets the role you've assigned. If someone is in several user groups, they get the highest level of permission provided by the roles they're assigned. If you nest user groups, all the contained users have permission. All of these capabilities, except viewing and interacting, require a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User (PPU) license. Read more about licensing in this article.

FAQ - SfB to Teams migration


🔎 TIP: Use Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site.

💬 If you do not find the answers here, see here how to get support.

FAQ

Migration

Please check the basic migration information first.


Question:Answer:
How can I check, if the Teams Public Telephony service is available at my location/for my number?

You can open the ITSP order form "Microsoft Teams - Migrate User". The ITSP service will automatically display you Option1 or Option2:

  • Option 1: You will lose all your Public Telephony capability. For detailed explanation please refer to the ITSP Service.
  • Option 2:  Your number will be migrated to Teams and you can use the Public Telephony Service like you have used it in SfB before.
When will Skype for Business be migrated to Microsoft Teams?

A location-based migration from Skype for Business (SfB) to Microsoft Teams (Teams) has started. It is being introduced simultaneously in all regions depending on the feasibility. A dedicated plan to your location is available at the rollout section on the Microsoft 365 Welcome Page. Please note, a concrete date is only available to the locations which have planned migration in the next 6 weeks. If your location is not mentioned yet, please check again later. There, you can also find the contact details of your local coordinators if you have any questions.

You can also migrate earlier to Teams Only via the order form.

For a more detailed migration plan, please check here.

What will happen when I start the migration to Teams Only Mode, but without the availability of the Teams Public Telephony service?

You will lose the Public Telephony service and the possibility to call internal/external telephone numbers.

The Public Telephony service is not yet available at my location, can I migrate my user now to Teams Only mode and active Teams Public Telephony service as soon as the service is available at my location?

Yes, this is possible, but a reservation of your telephone number is not possible. You will be equipped with the new number.

Are there different pricing tariffs for a call per minute between SfB and Teams?

No, there is no difference.

Can I migrate my user from Teams Only mode back to SfB and Teams in parallel usage?

Yes, via this ITSP order form "Microsoft Teams - Migrate User" 

What are the benefits of being Teams Only mode?
  • You will not have issues with two difference presence status in Skype for Business and Teams anymore. 
  • Headset buttons will be supported in Microsoft Teams.
  • You do not need to run the Skype for Business client anymore all the time. This will be the same as computer performance.
  • Usage of the direct communication to externals (Federation) 
Can I perform an emergency call with Teams Only mode and Public Telephony service?
Yes, but after full rollout. Meanwhile you can use your Bosch managed Smartphone (if applicable) to call those phone numbers.
Can I call the IT Service Desk with Teams Only mode?
No. You can use alternative channels e.g. your Bosch managed Smartphone (if applicable) to call those phone numbers.
Can I call the IT Service Desk with Teams Public Telephony service?
Yes, but you need to wait for the full rollout of the Teams Public Telephony at your location.
Where I can receive support?
For any questions, during the pilot phase, please leave them in the dedicated forum in the EAN community.
Will Skype for Business completely disappear after the migration to Teams Only?

No, Skype for Business stay in the so call "meeting join mode", mean when someone invite you to an Skype for Business meeting you still need your Skype for Business client to join this meeting. 

Hint: Your Skype for Business client does not need to run activity at your computer the whole day. You can just start it for the Skype for Business meeting and close it after the meeting is finished. 

For additional Teams features - can I run order in parallel or should I wait when migration will be done?
You should wait until the migration is complete before ordering the additional features.
If my counterpart has just landline, how can I be contacted?
In case you do not own a mobile, please set up a meeting that e.g. external BP can dial in to the conference. You can yourself join the meeting w/o landline directly.
After migration to "Teams only" my MFA(2FA) is not working any more, what shall I do?

After migration to Teams Only without Public Telephony change authentication method or from landline number to mobile number.

Microsoft Multi-Factor Authentication - 2-Factor-Authentication - RAS - Docupedia (bosch.com)

Will "Contacts" be migrated to MS Teams from SfB automatically?

Yes, this will happen. Please have a look here about new contacts in Teams: https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1325189130#Chat&Activities-CanIcreatecontactlistslikeinSfB

How is the handling between Skype for Business and Teams when my account has been migrated already?

Watch this Video  DEMO about SfB and Teams Only interoparability!

My Skype status is not synchronized with my Teams status, so for many colleagues it seems like I am not available.

This is one of the reason we need to migrate to "Teams Only".

When a colleague calls me (via Skype) I am not able to share my screen or to turn on the camera. If I need this function, I have to stop the call and create a new Teams Meeting.

Watch this Video  DEMO about SfB and Teams Only interoparability!

When I send a chat message to a colleague or call them, and they already have installed Teams – but don’t use it that often – my message/call appears for them in Teams. But they still use Skype. So I am often wondering why they don’t answer me. There is no way for me to reach them via Skype which is still there mainly used messenger.
This is one of the reason we need to migrate to "Teams Only".
How can I apply for the authorization for screen recording? 

Please refer to this link for further information: https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/YO6iSw

When I join Skype meeting now, all my colleagues see this:

Even though I am using Skype for Business, however the chat function on my Skype is now missing.

I only receive Team messages.

That`s because of the usage of" Teams only".

Jabra Evolve 75 Headset, the microphone mute by moving the microphone up and down, does not work anymore. What to do?

Please change in the Jabra Device Settings the softphone from Skype to Teams.

What will happen to resource account that could not get Teams license after SfB end of life? 

Some accounts will get a license, from some of the accounts the SfB part will be removed (if not needed).

 NOTE There still will be a SfB server pool for special topics. It means some of accounts might still stay in SfB. Details are currently in preperation. 

What will happen with my voicemail after migration?

SfB voicemail will be lost after migration. You need to set up your voicemail in Teams again.

Hardphone

Question:Answer:
I use a hardphone in combination with my SfB number, should I migrate to Teams Only mode?

It's not recommended. After the migration your hardphone will not work anymore. The support of hardphones will start at a later time. 

Can I reuse my hardphone after the migration to Teams Only mode?

Only certified models will work with Teams, please refer to the link for Teams BD certified hardphones:

  • Conference Phones link
  • Desk Phones link
I am using a Teams compatible hardphone.  Can I upgrade my phone to Teams ?

We are running a small pilot, so you can participate in the pilot and provide us the feedback.

PREREQS

  • No intune/mobile PIM
  • Account already migrated to M365
  • Mailbox moved to Exchange Online
I would like to participate in pilot of hardphone, whom should I reach out?

Please use this FORM

Do Teams hardphones support Wi-Fi?
No, Teams hardphones require PoE/LAN physical network port.
If it is possible to custom a ringtone?
It is not possible, and, what is more, it depends on Microsoft Teams App.
Why do some devices have a dial pad?
It depends on the individual phone configuration.  To change this setting please raise an IT ticket.
Can I search for external contacts via Teams phone?
This feature has not been able to support yet, it depends on Microsoft.
Which requirements I need to fulfill?
Your user need to be Teams enabled. You can find more details here.
Will click2join work in Teams?
Yes. Teams phone comes with a special feature called “MeetingSignIn”, which is similar to Click2Join, but please note, that an account should have been migrated to Exchange Online first!
I would like to discuss on the specific models & certifications. Whom should I contact with discuss?
You can send a mail to AudioDevice.AudioDevice@bosch.com

Self-Service On-Premises Data Gateway


Important

Due to the configuration of data sources in the gateway by the users themselves we need to monitor the gateway cluster in terms of performance, stability and availability.

Please be also aware you can only use the Self-Service Gateway OR the Enterprise Gateway when mapping data sources in a single dataset, not both at the same time!

Introduction

The Microsoft on-premises data gateway allows users to safely connect their on-premise data sources with Power BI. 

With this pilot we want to enable our users to create and manage gateway data sources on their own and to reduce the time it takes for a Power BI report to be able to be configured for a scheduled refresh or to work in DirectQuery mode.

Prerequisites

In order to use the self-service on-premises data gateway, you need to have the following IDM role assigned to your user:

IT ApplicationPOWER BI CLOUD
Access RightPower BI Cloud - Self-Service On-Premises Data Gateway Connection Creator

Follow this link to open IDM→ IDM Welcome Page

The role request needs to be granted by the user's manager and additionally by the Power BI Platform team.




Info

Once the IDM role has been granted to you, it might take up to 2 hours for the role to be synced from IDM → BCD (Bosch Corporate Directory) → AAD (Azure Active Directory) and therefore until you can use it!

Terms and Conditions

It is important to understand that by adding data sources to the self-service gateway you are allowing data to leave the Bosch corporate network (BCN) and make it accessible by Microsoft Power BI in the Cloud.

  • The Power BI Cloud has been on-boarded for data that has been clarified as SC-2 or less only
    • It is not allowed to use data of SC-3 in the Cloud
  • You can only add data sources to the gateway that you have been granted the permission to do so by the master of data
  • If you grant access to one of the data sources that you created to other users, they will be able to map their data sets to your data source using your credentials and might be able to access/see data that they are not intended to see
  • It is your responsibility to make sure that the data source that you are adding to the gateway can be used with Power BI Cloud
  • The Power BI Cloud team is not responsible for any data sources added in the self-service
  • The Power BI Cloud team can see all data sources that you add to the self-service gateway
    • this does not include credentials
  • Upon request, the Power BI Team can inform the master of data of a data source if their data source has been added to the gateway and by whom
  • The Power BI Cloud team is monitoring the gateway cluster for any suspicious activity and reserves the right to remove data sources at any time to ensure performance and stability
  • Support by the Power BI Cloud team for data sources added to the self-service gateway is limited, especially during the pilot phase
  • Any data source not listed in the supported data sources might be possible to add and working, but is not supported by the Power BI Platform team
  • If you are merging cloud and on-premise data sources in a query inside Power Query Editor your Cloud data source needs to be configured in our Proxy4Server policy
    • currently this is only configured for salesforce.com and sharepoint online
  • During the pilot, availability and performance of the self-service gateway can not be guaranteed
  • Single sign-on (SSO) is NOT supported as this would require individual configuration on the server cluster to enable Kerberos authentication

How to use the self-service gateway

In this section we will describe how to use the self-service gateway once you have the appropriate access rights in IDM.

Supported Data Sources

At this time, the following connectors are supported:

  • Folder
  • File
  • SharePoint Online
  • Oracle (use tnsname as server to connect)
  • MySQL(https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/mysql-database)
  • SQL Server
  • Salesforce
  • Analysis Services (SSAS)
    • to set up SQL Server Analysis services you need to use a SysAdmin account (not the role administrator but an actual SysAdmin account on the server)
    • if you have access to this, you can use the self-service gateway
  • SAP BW
  • Web Intranet (Bosch sites)
  • MariaDB
  • Impala
  • InterSystem
  • Postgresql


Info

Data sources that do not require a driver installation on the gateway might be working but are not supported by us!

Planned Data Sources

The following data sources will be added to the supported data sources in the following weeks

Unsupported Data Sources

Data sources on this list are not supported and will not be working

  • Any data sources that require ODBC drivers installed and DSN configurations
  • Drivers that require SSO (Single Sign-on) setup
  • Cloud data sources if they are combined in the same query like an on-premise data source and are NOT in the supported data sources list
    • these data sources would require configuration in the Proxy4Server policy
  • SharePoint (2013)
  • Access DB
  • Python

Add a data source

There are two ways to add a data source to the self-service gateway. You can create the data source manually and then use it with your Power BI Dataset or you can add the data source from an existing gateway directly.

Manually add a data source to the self-service gateway

Important

You need the IDM access right mentioned in the Prerequisites in order to see and use the gateway


  1. From the page header in the Power BI service, select Settings  > Manage gateways.

  2. Select New at the top of the ribbon to add a new data source.

  3. Choose the gateway you want to create the connection on, by providing the Gateway cluster name, then select the Data Source Type. In this example, we'll choose SQL Server.

  4. Enter information about the data source.

    1. For Oracle, provide the Server TNS Name

    2. For SQL Server, provide the Server and Database


      Important

      Always use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN)! (i.e. de.bosch.com, emea.bosch.com etc.)

      Our server might not be able to access your data source if you are not using the FQDN

  5. Select an Authentication Method to use when connecting to the data source. For SQL Server, choose Windows or Basic (SQL Authentication). Enter the credentials for your data source.

    1. Basic authentication (login name and password)
    2. Windows authentication (user name and password from the Bosch Corporate Directory)


      Make sure to add your DOMAIN to the username, otherwise it will not work.

  6. Optionally configure the privacy level for your data source (doesn't apply to DirectQuery).

  7. Select Create. You see Created New data source if the process succeeds.

You can now use this data source to include data from your on-premise data source with your Power BI Datasets, Dataflows or Datamart.

Create data source directly from an existing dataset

Important

You need the IDM access right mentioned in the Prerequisites in order to see and use the gateway

  1. Inside your dataset settings, open the "Gateway connection" section and search for the little triangle next to the Self-Service gateway:
  2. Once you have clicked on the triangle, all data sources used in your dataset will be shown and you have the option to add them to the gateway
  3. After clicking on "Add to gateway" the "New data source" dialogue will show up with all necessary data source information pre-filled
  4. You can now follow the steps beginning at Step 4 of the previous chapter to finalize the data source creation in the gateway

Remove a data source

You can remove a data source if you no longer use it. Removing a data source breaks any dashboards and reports that rely on that data source.

To remove a data source, select the data source and then select Remove from top ribbon.

Use the data source for scheduled refresh or DirectQuery

After you create the data source, it's available to use with either DirectQuery connections or through scheduled refresh. You can learn more about setting up scheduled refresh in Configure scheduled refresh.

Note

Server and database names must match between Power BI Desktop and the data source added to the on-premises data gateway.

The link between your dataset and the data source in the gateway is based on your server name and database name. These names must match. For example, if you supply an IP address for the server name, in Power BI Desktop, you must use the IP address for the data source in the gateway configuration. If you use SERVER\INSTANCE in Power BI Desktop, you must use the same in the data source configured for the gateway.

If you have the IDM role (see prerequisites) and the server and database name match, you see the gateway as an option to use with scheduled refresh.


Warning

If your dataset contains multiple data sources, each data source must be added in the gateway. If one or more data sources aren't added to the gateway, you won't see the gateway as available for scheduled refresh.


FAQ

How much does it cost to use the self-service gateway?

Using the self-service gateway is free of charge for you

What kind of license do I need to use the self-service gateway?

Anybody at Bosch can use the self-service gateway! Even if you do not have a Pro-License you can publish reports into your own "My Workspace" and use the gateway to access on-premise data sources.

Why did you just start offering this self-service and why did we have to wait for so long?

Microsoft just recently released the ability to have users added as "Connection Creators" to a gateway. Previously, there was only the "Administrator" role which we cannot grant to the end-users.

Bosch Connect Editor


Tip: Press Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site

If you do not find the answers here, use the Bosch Connect forum in Bosch Connect.

General information

With Bosch Connect editor you can add your blog post and Wiki pages, as well prepare your content in Rich Content app. 

In June 2022 the random editor on Bosch Connect was changed from Textbox.io to TinyMCE (so far available for early adopters only) in order to reduce bugs while editing and to provide more features (i.a. new look and feel, more fonts and emoticons available). The comparison between TinyMCE and Textbox.io you can find here.

The current TinyMCE version is: TinyMCE. 6.6.0.


Editor features

If you've used a word processor such as Microsoft Word™ or Open Office™, then most of the functionality provided by TinyMCE will seem familiar. 


Main areas

The Editor is split into two main areas: the toolbar and the editing area. The editing area is where you type in your content, whereas the toolbar sits at the top, providing you with all the options and functionalities needed to style your page.

Under the editor you will find features belonging to Community App component as Advanced Settings and Publishing features. 



Basic styling features 

  • bold, italic, underlined text (the strike through you will find in Font menu feature);

  • permanent pen;

  • lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title case.



Text styles

When you expand Paragraph window, you'll find available text styles, i.a. different headings sizes. If you don't want to change your text style, leave the settings with "Paragraph" chosen. 



Font menu 

Use font feature menu to:

  • choose font;
  • adjust its size and line height;
  • set text and background colors;
  • choose superscript, subscript or strike through.  



Inserting extra content

Click on + sign to add extra elements to your content as:

  • Image

  • Links
  • Link to Connections Files (files saved on Bosch Connect)
  • Image
  • Table
  • Embed Bosch Tube Media
  • Special character
  • Horizontal line




Adding Anchor Links

An anchor (or bookmark) button is available in your editing toolbar that inserts the anchor directly into your HTML. You’ll find this anchor link selector next to the hyperlinking tool.

To add an anchor:

  • Click in the text box, or select the text, where you would like to place the anchor. This would be the section you would like to direct your learners to.
  • Click the anchor icon on the toolbar. A dialogue box appears.
  • Type an ID to identify the anchor. The ID is meant to help you identify how to link to the anchor in the next step. The ID should start with a letter, followed by only letters, numbers, dashes, dots, colons or underscores.




To link to the anchor:

  • Highlight the text you want to link and click the hyperlink icon on the toolbar.
  • Click the anchor drop-down and select the anchor ID that corresponds to the anchor you want to link to. When a learner clicks on the linked text, they will be taken to the anchor link.

     

Content alignment and lists

  • Align your content to: left, center, right or justify it;
  • Choose between bullet list, numbered list or insert checklist;
  • Increase or decrease indent (decrease indent turns active after increasing indent before);
  • Use block quote to present your content with quote indent. 



Formatting entry features

  • format painter;
  • clear formatting.

Emoticons

You can choose emoticons from various categories after clicking on smiley face icon. 



Working with code 

Any time you can change tabs in the editor to view:

  • Rich text - WYSWIG (=what you see is what you get);
  • HTML source.

and edit the content wherever you prefer. 

If you don't want to edit the code in HTML source, only add a piece of code, click on this icon to open a pop-up window, when you can insert your code. 

Please, do not paste your code directly to the editing area in Rich text mode. 





Expand more settings

Click on three dots icon to expand more toolbar features:



Language settings

  • text language;
  • text direction left to right;
  • text direction right to left. 


Find and replace

If your content is longer, you might want to use the find and replace feature to adjust it. 



Accessibility checker

This plugin allows you to check the HTML in the editor for various WCAG & Section 508 accessibility problems. It has an auto-repair feature that lets the user fix identified problems. Here you can find some interactive examples. 





Full screen mode

Press this icon to go to full screen mode. It's very useful, when you want to focus on writing. 


To close the full screen mode press Esc or move your mouse on the screen corners to display "closing X" sign. 




Settings menu

Here you can find some extra features as:

  • word count - counts words, characters (no spaces) and characters in document and in selected text;
  • spellcheck language - you can turn it off or choose from the following languages: English, English (UK), Danish, Dutch, Finish, French, German, Italian, Norwegian Bokmal, Portuguese, Portuguese (Portugal), Spanish or Swedish;
  • auto correct - randomly active; turn it on/off by clicking on it;
  • capitalization;
  • help - please be aware that support for plugins might redirect you to support center of TinyMCE for different version then applied on Bosch Connect. 





Preview

Before you save, the preview feature will help you to see what your content will look like.
