QuestionDescription/Answer
What is Teams Call Queue?

Teams Call Queue consists of two components: Auto Attendant and Call Queue. Used together, they can easily route callers to the appropriate person or department in your organization.

  1. Auto Attendant: Auto Attendants allow you to set up menu options to route calls based on caller input. Menu options for an Auto Attendant, such as "For Sales, press 1--For Services press 2--", let an organization provide a series of choices that guide callers to their destination quickly, without relying on a human operator to handle incoming calls.

The primary purpose of an Auto Attendant is to direct a caller to an appropriate person or department based on the caller's input to the provided menu options. Callers can be directed to a specific people within your organization, to call queues where they wait to talk to the next available agent or to voicemail. Different call routing options can be specified for business hours, off hours and holidays. Below, there are some features available in Auto Attendant listed:

  • Deliver corporate or informational greetings.
  • Provide custom corporate menus, which you can customize.
  • Search a directory for a name.
  • Enable callers to reach or leave a message for a person in your organization.
  • Support multiple languages for prompts, text-to-speech, and speech recognition.
  • Support specifying holidays and business hours.
  • Transfer calls to an operator, other users, call queues, and auto attendants.
  • Support shared voicemail for callers to leave a message for an organization.

    2. Call Queue: Call queues are waiting areas for callers. For situations where callers need to reach someone with a particular specialization, such as sales or service, rather than a specific person, you can use call queues to connect callers to the group of agents who can assist them. Callers are put on hold until an agent assigned to the queue is available to take their call.

Call queues allow you to route calls specifically when the total number of callers in the queue or waiting time exceeds the limits you specify. Calls can be routed to specific people, voicemail, other call queues or auto attendants. Below, there are some features available in Call Queue listed:

  • A greeting message.
  • Music while people are waiting on hold.
  • Redirection of calls to agents in mail-enabled distribution lists and security groups.
  • Configuration parameters such as queue maximum size, timeout, and call handling options.
  • Shared voicemail for callers to leave a message for an organization.

The example below shows an example of call routing using Auto Attendants and Call Queues.

What is Exchange Online Archive (EOA)?

General Information:

  • Exchange Online Archiving is not a long-term archiving solution, but an extension of the personal mailbox.

  • Microsoft Exchange Online Archiving (EOA) is a cloud-based Microsoft 365 archiving solution for large organizations (Not OnPremise).

  • Exchange Online Archive (EOA) is displayed to the user as an additional mailbox entry in the navigation pane.

An archive mailbox can be used only to store emails for a single user or entity for which a license has been applied. Using an archive mailbox to store emails from multiple users or entities is not allowed.

Important: Shared mailboxes cannot be created to allow data copies from multiple users in a shared mailbox (via the "Cc" or "Bcc" field or via a transport rule/forwarding) for the explicit purpose of archiving.

*2If LegalHold or Litigation-Hold is set for a mailbox, this setting is applied to both the mailboxes. Means: Primary/personal and the archive mailbox.
*3

System folders (Inbox, Sent Items, Calendar, Contacts) which are automatically created by the archiving function, get the retention policy from the personal mailbox.
Attention: If the retention is changed in one of the above system folders, they will be reset by the system.

What is EOA mailbox?

General Information:

  • Exchange Online Archiving provides users with an enhanced mailbox storage area with the Exchange Online Archive mailbox feature.

  • An archive mailbox is a special mailbox that appears with the user's primary mailbox folders in Outlook or Outlook on the Web.

  • Users can access the archive in the same way they access their primary mailbox folders. In addition, they can search their archives and primary mailboxes.

What is the size of the EOA mailbox?

General Information:

  • The size of the archive mailbox is initially 99GByte. Microsoft gradually increases the size by 10GByte when the limit of 90% is reached.
How can I save data to the EOA mailbox?

General Information:

  • Drag&Drop emails from the primary mailbox to the archive.
  • Right-click menu on the item and select Move to Folder.
  • Select archiving policies to automatically move email items from the primary mailbox to the archive mailbox.
  • Benefit: By reducing the mailbox size, the performance of the primary mailbox is improved.

Important:

  • It is not allowed to use auto-forwarding rules to copy messages to Exchange Online archiving for archiving.
  • An user's EOA mailbox is intended only for that user. Microsoft reserves the right to deny additional archive storage space in cases where a user's archive mailbox is used to store archive data for other users or in other cases of inappropriate use.
How to search for items in the EOA mailbox?

General Information:

  • A search in Outlook is not performed automatically in all connected mailboxes, but only in the selected mailboxes. Example:
  • If the personal mailbox is selected in the folder bar, a search is only performed in the personal mailbox.
  • If the Exchange Online Archive mailbox is selected in the folder bar, a search is only performed in the Exchange Online Archive mailbox.

Important:

  • To perform a search in the personal mailbox and Exchange Online Archive mailbox, "Search in all mailboxes" must be enabled in the search selection.
Why is the EOA mailbox not available in offline mode?

General Information:

The Exchange Online Archive Mailbox is not designed from Microsoft to use it in Offline Mode. 

How do I restore deleted items in the EOA mailbox?

General Information:

  • Users can recover items they have deleted from an email folder in their EOA mailbox. When an item is deleted, it is kept in the Deleted Items folder of the EOA mailbox. It is stored there until it is automatically moved by the user or automatically removed by retention policies.

  • After an item is deleted from the Deleted Items folder of the EOA mailbox, the item is retained in the Recoverable Items folder of the EOA mailbox for an additional 30 days before it is permanently deleted. Users can recover these items using the Recover Deleted Items feature in Microsoft Outlook or Outlook on the Web.

How to restore deleted EOA mailboxes?

General Information:

  • When user mailboxes are deleted, user archives are also deleted.

  • If the deleted archive mailboxes need to be restored, only Microsoft support team can perform this restoration.

Important:

  • Administrators have 30 days from the time a user's mailbox is deleted to request archive mailbox recovery from Microsoft.

  • After 30 days, the archive mailbox cannot be restored.

What are the retention settings in the EOA mailbox?

General Information:

  • Retention settings are made according to the same criteria as for the personal mailbox
  • Each user created folder with name do not match from primary mailbox  can be set to 10 years
  • The relevant date for deleting an item by the retention setting is the creation date --> not the archiving/moving to archive!
  • Possible retention settings:
    • RB - Default Retention Policy (Email Governance 10 Years).
    • Special RB - LegalHold

Important:

  • If an Archive Mailbox Folder has the same folder name like the folder in the personal mailbox, then the Archive Mailbox Folder inherited the retention policy from the personal mailbox folder.
  • Attention: System folders like Inbox, Deleted Items, Sent Items, Calendar, Contacts will always overwriten from the personal mailbox retentions.

How do I use EOA with the Outlook App for Mac?

General Information:

  • You can move (Drag&Drop) individual messages from Outlook for Mac to your archive mailbox one at a time (but you can't move or copy multiple items at once).

  • However, the most efficient way to ensure that your messages are archived is to apply archive and retention policies to Outlook Web App (OWA).

Important:

  • You can create inbox rules to automatically file messages in folders, assign categories to them, or redirect them to another mailbox.
  • However, these rules are not applied to your archive mailbox, and you cannot redirect messages to your archive mailbox using an inbox rule.
How do I search for items in the EOA mailbox using the Outlook App for Mac?

General Information:

  • If you want to search inside the EOA mailbox, select a folder in the EOA in the folder area/navigation pane.

What other compliance and security features are available for EOA?

Retention policies:

  • Exchange Online Archiving provides retention policies that help organizations reduce their obligations regarding email and other forms of communication. Using these policies, administrators have the ability to apply retention settings to specific folders in a user's inbox.
  • Exchange Online archiving offers two types of policies: archive and delete. Both types can be applied to the same item or folder. For example, a user can mark an email to be automatically moved to the personal archive after a specified number of days or deleted after another specified number of days.

Compliance archive and retention for potential litigation:

  • If litigation is anticipated, BOSCH is required to retain electronically stored information relevant to the case, including email. This action may occur before the details of a case become known, and the amount of data to be retained is often large. Bosch may retain all email related to a specific subject or all email for specific individuals.

In Exchange Online, you can use the compliance archive or retention for potential litigation to accomplish the following goals:

  • Enable retention of user mailboxes and their data in archives in an unchangeable form.
  • Retain mailbox items that could be deleted by users or automatic deletion processes. Ex: MRM (Messaging Records Management = Retention Policy)
  • Protect mailbox items from tampering, changes by a user or by automated processes by storing a copy of the original item.
  • Retain items indefinitely or for a specified period of time.
  • Retention is more transparent to the user because no MRM changes need to be made

Compliance eDiscovery:

  • Exchange Online Archiving supports Compliance-eDiscovery for searching mailbox content across an organization.
What security features exist in the EOA?

Encryption between local servers and Exchange Online archiving.

  • TLS is used to encrypt the connection between email servers to prevent spoofing and enable confidentiality of messages in transit.
  • TLS is also used to secure local email server traffic to Microsoft data centers for Exchange Online archiving.

Encryption between clients and Exchange Online archiving

For client connections to Exchange Online Archiving, security is enhanced using the following encryption methods:

  • SSL is used to secure Outlook, Outlook on the Web (OWA), and Exchange Web Services traffic by using TCP port 443.
  • Client connections to on-premises servers do not change with the introduction of Exchange Online Archiving.

Encryption: S/MIME and PGP

  • Exchange Online Archiving stores S/MIME (Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) messages. However, Exchange Online archiving does not host S/MIME functions or public keys, nor does it provide storage, management and directory services for keys, as all of these services are related to the on-premises Exchange infrastructure.
  • Similarly, Exchange Online Archiving stores messages encrypted using client-side, third-party encryption solutions such as Pretty Good Privacy (PGP).

Hinweise:

*1

Ein Archivpostfach kann nur zum speichern von E-Mails für einen einzelnen Benutzer oder eine Entität verwendet werden, für die eine Lizenz angewendet wurde. Die Verwendung eines Archivpostfachs zum Speichern von E-Mails von mehreren Benutzern oder Entitäten ist unzulässig.

Wichtig: Es können keine Shared Mailboxen erstellt werden, um Datenkopien von mehreren Anwendern in einer Shared Mailbox zu erstellen (über das Feld "Cc" oder "Bcc" oder über eine Transportregel/Weiterleitung) zum expliziten Zweck der Archivierung zu ermöglichen.

*2Wenn für ein Postfach LegalHold oder Litigation-Hold gesetzt wird, wird diese Einstellung sowohl auf das primäre/persönliche Postfach wie auch auf das Archivpostfach angewendet.
*3

Systemordner (Posteingang, Gesendete Objekte, Kalender, Kontakte) welche durch Archivierungsfunktion automatisch erstellt werden, erhalten die Retention Policy vom persönlichen Postfach.

Achtung: Wird in einem der oben genannten Systemordnern die Retention geändert, werden sie vom System wieder zurückgestellt.
Was ist das EOA Postfach?

Allgemein:

  • Exchange Online-Archivierung bietet Benutzern mit der Archivpostfachfunktion einen erweiterten Postfachspeicherbereich.
  • Ein Archivpostfach ist ein spezielles Postfach, das zusammen mit den primären Postfachordnern des Benutzers in Outlook oder Outlook im Web angezeigt wird.
  • Benutzer können auf das Archiv auf die gleiche Weise zugreifen, wie sie auf ihre primären Postfachordner zugreifen. Darüber hinaus können sie ihre Archive und primären Postfächer durchsuchen.
Welche Größe besitzt das EOA Postfach?

Allgemein:

  • Die Größe des Archivpostfaches beträgt initial 99GByte. Microsoft vergrößert die Größe schrittweise um 10GByte, wenn das Limit von 90% erreicht wird.
Wie kann ich Daten in das EOA Postfach speichern?

Allgemein:

  • Ziehen von E-Mails aus dem primären Postfach in das Archiv.
  • Menüpunkt bei Rechter Maustaste verschieben in Ordner
  • Anwählen der Archivierungsrichtlinien um E-Mail-Elemente automatisch aus dem primären Postfach in das Archivpostfach zu verschieben.
    Vorteil: Durch Verringerung der Postfachgröße wird die Leistung des primären Postfachs verbessert.

Wichtig:

  • Es ist nicht zulässig, Regeln zur automatischen Weiterleitung zu verwenden, um Nachrichten zur Archivierung zu Exchange Online-Archivierung zu kopieren.
  • Das Archivpostfach eines Benutzers ist nur für diesen Benutzer vorgesehen. Microsoft behält sich das Recht vor, zusätzlichen Archivspeicherplatz in Fällen zu verweigern, in denen das Archivpostfach eines Benutzers zum Speichern von Archivdaten für andere Benutzer oder in anderen Fällen unangemessener Verwendung verwendet wird.
Wie suche ich nach Elementen im EOA Postfach?

Allgemein:

Eine Suche im Outlook erfolgt nicht automatisch in allen angebundenen Postfächern, sondern nur in den angewählten Postfächern. Bsp.:

  • Ist das persönliche Postfach in der Ordnerleiste angewählt, so wird eine suche nur im persönlichen Postfach durchgeführt.
  • Ist das Exchange Online Archive Postfach in der Ordnerleiste angewählt, so wird eine suche nur im Exchange Online Archive Postfach durchgeführt.

Wichtig:

  • Um eine Suche im persönlichen Postfach und im Exchange Online Archive durchzuführen, muss bei der Auswahl „Suche in allen Postfächern“ aktiviert werden.
Warum ist das EOA Postfach nicht im Offline Mode verfügbar?

Allgemein:

Das Exchange Online Archiv Postfach ist nicht für die Verwendung im Offline-Modus von Microsoft vorgesehen.

Wie stelle ich gelöschte Elemente im EOA Postfach her?

Allgemein:

  • Benutzer können Elemente wiederherstellen, die sie aus einem E-Mail-Ordner in ihrem Archiv gelöscht haben. Wenn ein Element gelöscht wird, wird es im Ordner "Gelöschte Elemente" des Archivs aufbewahrt. Es wird dort so lange gespeichert, bis es vom Benutzer automatisch verschoben oder durch Aufbewahrungsrichtlinien automatisch entfernt wird.
  • Nachdem ein Element aus dem Ordner „Gelöschte Elemente“ des Archivs gelöscht wurde, wird das Element im Ordner „Wiederherstellbare Elemente“ des Archivs weitere 30 Tage lang aufbewahrt, bevor es endgültig gelöscht wird. Benutzer können diese Elemente mithilfe der Funktion „Gelöschte Elemente wiederherstellen“ in Microsoft Outlook oder Outlook im Web wiederherstellen.
Wie werden gelöschte EOA Postfächer wieder hergestellt?

Allgemein:

  • Wenn Benutzerpostfächer gelöscht werden, werden auch die Archive der Benutzer gelöscht.
  • Wenn die gelöschten Archivpostfächer wiederhergestellt werden müssen, kann nur das Microsoft-Supportteam diese Wiederherstellung durchführen.

Wichtig:

  • Administratoren haben ab dem Zeitpunkt, an dem das Postfach eines Benutzers gelöscht wird, 30 Tage Zeit, um die Wiederherstellung eines Archivpostfachs bei Microsoft anzufordern.
  • Nach 30 Tagen kann das Archivpostfach nicht mehr wiederhergestellt werden.
Wie sind die Retentioneinstellungen im EOA Postfach?

Allgemein:

  • Die Retentioneinstellungen erfolgen nach den selben Kriterien wie beim persönlichen Postfach
  • Jeder Ordner (ausser Systemordner) können auf 10 Jahre eingestellt werden
  • Das relevante Datum für das Löschen eines Objekts durch die Aufbewahrungseinstellung ist das Erstellungsdatum --> nicht das Archivieren/Verschieben ins Archiv!
  • Mögliche Retentioneinstellungen:
    • RB – Default Retention Policy (E-Mail Governance 10 Years)
    • Special RB – LegalHold

Wichtig:

  • Wenn ein Archivpostfach-Ordner den gleichen Ordnernamen wie der Ordner im persönlichen Postfach hat, dann hat der Archivpostfach-Ordner die Aufbewahrungsrichtlinie vom persönlichen Postfach-Ordner geerbt.
    Achtung: Systemordner wie Posteingang, Gelöschte Objekte, Gesendete Objekte, Kalender, Kontakte werden immer von den Aufbewahrungsrichtlinien des persönlichen Postfachs überschrieben.

Wie verwende ich EOA mit der Outlook App for Mac?

Allgemein:

  • Sie können einzelne Nachrichten von Outlook für Mac nacheinander in Ihr Archivpostfach verschieben (doch nicht mehrere Elemente auf einmal verschieben oder kopieren).
  • Die effizienteste Methode zum Sicherstellen, dass Ihre Nachrichten archiviert werden, ist jedoch die Anwendung von Archiv- und Aufbewahrungsrichtlinien für Outlook Web App (OWA).

Wichtig:

  • Sie können Posteingangsregeln erstellen, um Nachrichten automatisch in Ordnern abzulegen, ihnen Kategorien zuzuweisen oder an ein anderes Postfach umzuleiten.
  • Diese Regeln werden jedoch nicht auf Ihr Archivpostfach übertragen, und Sie können Nachrichten mithilfe einer Posteingangsregel nicht an Ihr Archivpostfach umleiten.
Wie suche ich Elemente mit der Outlook App for Mac im EOA Postfach?

Allgemein:

  • Wenn Sie im Archiv suchen möchten, wählen Sie im Ordnerbereich einen Ordner im EOA aus.
  • Sie können Ihr persönliches Postfach und Ihr Archivpostfach nicht gleichzeitig durchsuchen.
Welche weiteren Merkmale bzgl. Compliance & Security sind für EOA vorhanden?

Aufbewahrungsrichtlinien:

  • Exchange Online-Archivierung bietet Aufbewahrungsrichtlinien, die Organisationen dabei helfen, ihre Verpflichtungen hinsichtlich E-Mails und anderen Kommunikationsformen zu reduzieren. Mithilfe dieser Richtlinien haben Administratoren die Möglichkeit, Aufbewahrungseinstellungen für bestimmte Ordner des Posteingangs eines Benutzers anzuwenden.
  • Exchange Online-Archivierung bietet zwei Arten von Richtlinien: archivieren und löschen. Beide Typen können auf das gleiche Element oder den gleichen Ordner angewendet werden. Ein Benutzer kann beispielsweise eine E-Mail so markieren, dass sie nach einer bestimmten Anzahl von Tagen automatisch in das persönliche Archiv verschoben oder nach einer anderen festgelegten Anzahl von Tagen gelöscht wird.

Compliance-Archiv und Aufbewahrung für eventuelle Rechtsstreitigkeiten:

  • Wenn Rechtsstreitigkeiten zu erwarten sind, ist BOSCH dazu verpflichtet, die für den Fall relevanten elektronisch gespeicherten Informationen einschließlich E-Mail aufzubewahren. Diese Maßnahme kann eintreten, bevor die Details zu einem Fall bekannt werden, und die Menge der aufzubewahrenden Daten ist häufig groß. Bosch kann alle E-Mails zu einem bestimmten Thema oder alle E-Mails für bestimmte Personen aufbewahren.

In Exchange Online können Sie das Compliance-Archiv oder die Aufbewahrung für eventuelle Rechtsstreitigkeiten verwenden, um folgende Ziele zu erreichen:

  • Einschalten der Beibehaltung von Benutzerpostfächern und deren Daten in Archiven in unveränderbarer Form
  • Beibehalten von Postfachelementen, die von Benutzern oder automatischen Löschprozessen gelöscht werden könnten. Bsp.: MRM (Messaging Records Management = Retention Policy)
  • Schützen von Postfachelementen vor Manipulation, Änderungen durch einen Benutzer oder von automatischen Prozessen, indem eine Kopie des ursprünglichen Elements gespeichert wird
  • Beibehalten von Elementen auf unbestimmte Zeit oder über einen bestimmten Zeitraum
  • Das Beibehalten der Daten ist für den Benutzer transparenter, da keine MRM Änderungen gemacht werden müssen

Compliance-eDiscovery:

  • Exchange Online-Archivierung unterstützt Compliance-eDiscovery für das Durchsuchen von Postfachinhalten in einer Organisation.
Welche Sicherheitsfunktionen existieren in der EOA?

Verschlüsselung zwischen lokalen Servern und Exchange Online-Archivierung

  • TLS wird zum Verschlüsseln der Verbindung zwischen E-Mail-Servern verwendet, um Spoofing zu verhindern und die Vertraulichkeit von in der Übertragung befindlichen Nachrichten zu ermöglichen.
  • TLS wird auch zum Sichern des lokalen E-Mail-Serverdatenverkehrs an Microsoft-Rechenzentren für Exchange Online-Archivierung verwendet.

Verschlüsselung zwischen Clients und Exchange Online-Archivierung

Bei Clientverbindungen zu Exchange Online-Archivierung wird die Sicherheit anhand der folgenden Verschlüsselungsmethoden erhöht:

  • SSL wird zum Sichern von Outlook, Outlook im Web (OWA) und Exchange Webdienstdatenverkehr mithilfe von TCP-Port 443 verwendet.
  • Clientverbindungen zu lokalen Servern ändern sich mit der Einführung von Exchange Online-Archivierung nicht.

Verschlüsselung: S/MIME und PGP

  • Exchange Online-Archivierung speichert S/MIME (Secure/Multipurpose Internet-Mail Extensions/-Nachrichten. Exchange Online-Archivierung hostet jedoch keine S/MIME-Funktionen oder öffentliche Schlüssel und bietet auch keine Speicher-, Verwaltungs- und Verzeichnisdienste für Schlüssel an, da all diese Dienste mit der lokalen Exchange-Infrastruktur zusammenhängen.
  • In ähnlicher Weise speichert Exchange Online-Archivierung Nachrichten, die anhand von clientseitigen, Drittanbieter-Verschlüsselungslösungen wie Pretty Good Privacy (PGP) verschlüsselt wurden.

html_content:
Warning Message in Browser When Uploading a Directory (Folder) in OpenDXM

When uploading a directory (folder) in OpenDXM, your browser displays a warning message:  

"Upload [number of files] files to this site? This will upload all files from [directory name]. Only do this if you trust the site."


Just click on "Upload" and continue.


This prompt is a browser security feature.

There is no way to prevent this warning message from appearing or to at least prevent it appearing again and again for every upload to the same site.

Power BI Integration - oneIDM

This article describes how you can use oneIDM to manage access to your Power BI artefacts like Power BI Apps and workspaces.

Using oneIDM with Power BI is easy, but requires a bit of effort on your end for the initial setup. But once you have everything setup, you can easily and conveniently use the newly created oneIDM access rights with Power BI.

Introduction

The Power BI Platform team is providing an oneIDM application that you can use for your own oneIDM access rights named "POWER BI REPORTING".

You can easily find this application in the "User Self-Service" when searching for "Power BI Reporting" and add it to your list of applications.

This application is owned and managed by the Power BI Platform team but you can have your own oneIDM access rights added to this application and use it for your access management.

The Power BI Reporting application is using "idm2bcd" which will map an access right in this application with a security group in the Bosch Corporate Directory (BCD) and add/remove members to this security group if they have the access right granted/revoked in IDM.

This security group in the BCD can then be used like any other security group for access management to your workspaces, reports, power bi apps, etc. 


TODO: Graphic showing the relationship between a user, an oneidm access right, a security group in the bcd, the AAD and power bi


Process

In a nutshell, the following steps need to be done which are explained in more detail later on:

  1. Think of all the access rights that you need and that you want to use in Power BI
    1.  Short name of the access right
    2. Description of the access right
    3. technical name of the access right
  2. Create a ticket with CI Hotline to have the security groups for each access right created in the BCD
  3. Populate the  excel template for the access right import into the oneIDM application 
  4. Once the security groups are created, import the access rights into the oneIDM application
    1. Power BI Platform Team will approve if everything is technically correct
  5. Use the oneIDM access rights in your Power BI app, report, etc


Step 1 - Preparation of the access rights

As a first step you need to come up with all the access rights that you need and want to use with Power BI. The following information needs to be prepared:

NameDescriptionExample (for the "Lorem Ipsum" project)
Security Group nameThe IDM2BCD integration of oneIDM requires the creation of a security group that follows the following naming convention:
idm2bcd_xxx
The xxx is a free text that you can provide as you want. We do recommend the following naming convention though:
idm2bcd_pbireporting_xxx
where xxx should be a clear and unique description. You can only use letters, numbers and an underscore.		idm2bcd_pbireporting_LoremIpsumPowerBICloudDataset_Admin
Short DescriptionShort description of the access right that clearly indicates the purpose of the access right and the report/power bi application in questionLorem Ipsum Power BI Cloud Dataset - Admin
Long DescriptionLong description that clearly indicates the purpose of this access right and the report/power bi application in question. Lorem Ipsum Power BI Cloud Dataset - unrestricted access to all data for administrators only

Step 2 - Create a ticket with CI Hotline

The security groups in the BCD that will be mapped with your oneIDM access rights need to be created by the CI. For this you need to create a ticket and route it to the correct team. 

Link to the IT Service Portal "Create IDM2BCD Groups" 

Please click on the „Order for others” button and type in the following credentials: 

Afterwards please select the Power BI Reporting IT Application and insert your wished group suffix and click on “Add Group to Cart”. Please be aware that not including idm2bcd into the group suffix, because is already written in the left grayed space. 

Don't forget to click on Request.


Step 3 - Populating the Excel template for access right import in oneIDM

While you are waiting for the security group creation, you can already start preparing the Excel file that will be used for the access right import.

To do so, go to oneIDM and follow these steps:

  1. Navigate to the Access rights catalogue 
  2. Click on import access rights 
  3. Download the current Excel Template 

When you open the downloaded Excel file on your computer, insert the following informations to the first empty row: 


Column ACREATE/UPDATE
Column B

Insert your group suffix which you created in the previous step with idm2bcd_ before. 

IMPORTANT: This technical name needs to follow this naming convention exactly! Make sure it is matching your security group name 100%! 

Look on the following Screenshot for detailed description! 

Column CPower BI Reporting
Column DMOR department that will have to approve/revoke your access right
Column EChoose the appropriate workflow (description can be found in the header of the column)
Column F-JOptional (depending on your requirements)
Column K,L,M,NShort/Long Description of your access rights. You can either use English for all of them or provide a German version in the DE column as well.


IMPORTANT: You need to enter a reason why you are importing/modifying access rights (Field B6)

Once you are finished with the file, save it on your computer.

Step 4 - Import your access right(s) into oneIDM

In this step you will actually start the access right import process for your newly created oneIDM access rights

  1. In oneIDM, navigate to the Access Right Catalogue
  2. Click on "Import Access Rights"
  3. Click on Load and open the Excel file that you created that contains the new/updated access right
  4. Check if there are any errors in the validation section - you can only proceed if there are no errors
  5. Click on Import to initiate the access right import process

IMPORTANT

You can only import the access rights into IDM once the security groups have been created!

Do NOT try to import access rights unless you have received confirmation from the CI Hotline that your security groups have been created successfully!


Step 5 - Use the oneIDM Access right in Power BI

Once you receive the confirmation that your access right(s) have been successfully imported into oneIDM you can start using them in your Power BI application!

Just type in the name of the security group that you have created when you need to assign access in Power BI (Power BI App, workspace, dataset, etc.):

That's it! Congratulations on your first IDM2BCD integration with Power BI

FAQ

What's the cost for using this oneIDM integration with Power BI?

There is no cost for you when using the IDM2BCD integration and the Power BI Reporting application in oneIDM

Is there any limitation in the number of access rights that I can use with this oneIDM application?

No, you can create as many roles as you need

This is a lot of work for access management, do I need oneIDM?

The easiest way to do access management is by creating a security group in the IT Service Portal. Depending on your use-case it is up to you if you want to use oneIDM or the managed security group of the IT Service Portal

My user just got approved for my oneIDM access right but they still can't access my Power BI Content!

Before a user can use their newly acquired access right in Power BI, the following syncs need to occur:

  • Sync between oneIDM and the BCD (~30-60 minutes)
  • Sync between BCD and AAD (~30-60 minutes)

The same times apply if a user right has been revoked

How do I use Microsoft Bookings?

Bookings is an online service, so you don't need to download anything. Just go to the app chooser within the Microsoft 365 Web experience. Get Access

Will customers see my personal or business calendar?

Customers will only see the Bookings calendar that you publish online for the services, times, and staff that you choose.

Is Bookings supported in a federated or hybrid environment?

No. Bookings is a cloud-only application. It's not supported in a federated or hybrid environment.

Can I delete a previously created Bookings calendar?

No, this has to be done by an administrator. Please create a ticket (3311, itservicedesk@bosch.com).

For BSH Users: You can create "Service Call" by choosing IT Product > MS Bookings on BSH IT Service Portal.

Can I create more than one Bookings calendar under the same Microsoft 365 account and switch between them?

Yes. You can create and manage more than one Bookings calendar with one account. You can switch between them using the caret next to the business name in the Bookings Web app.

If I create a calendar and someone else has access to Bookings, would they be able to see my calendar?

The only people who have access to Bookings calendars that you create is anyone who has been added as staff, in either an Administrator or Viewer role. Tenant admins will be able to see a list of all Bookings mailboxes in Exchange and Azure AD.

How many staff members are allowed?

Bookings supports up to 100 staff members in a Bookings calendar.

Staff member is not able to access MS Bookings calendar

Please resend the confirmation mail, customer should accept with client (notebook). 
Mobile device is not supported for accepting confirmation mails.

Is it possible to book for another user?

In MS Bookings it´s possible to book as a proxy, in Bookings with me it´s not possible.
Just enter the name and the e-mail address of the user.

Do I have to add the data protection information and/or users has to give their consent in accordance to GDPR?

There is no need to give consent as this is already covered by Exchange (only name and email address will be processed like in an Outlook appointment).
If there are special requirements in your case, you can configure this under "Customer data usage consent".

Where can I see the consent?

Consent will not shown separatly, booking without accepting the conditions is not possible

Is it possible to send SMS instead of Mails?

This function was deactivated, because for sending SMS a special license is required and SMS sending is currently only available in a few countries.

What is Miro

Miro is an online collaborative whiteboard platform that enables distributed teams and users to work effectively together, from brainstorming with digital sticky notes up to planning and managing complete agile workflows.

With Miro, users can take advantage of a full set of collaboration capabilities, make cross-functional teamwork effortless, and organize meetings and workshops by planning whole presentations, share content and using many more advanced whiteboard features.

It empowers design, development, and engineering teams to align and innovate in a platform that makes it all possible in real-time. They can create concepts, map user stories or even plan full customer journeys. At the end it enables the users to focus on their creative processes by providing the right toolset.

As Miro lives by working with others it also offers an easy interface towards External partners.

During the subscription term, user may access and use the service only for its internal business purposes in accordance with the documentation, including any usage limits in an order. This includes the right to copy and use the software as part of users authorized use of the service.

Miro feed

Miro feed is an in-product notification center, that aggregates the most important updates from your team, such as mentions, comments, invites and requests. On your board, feed can be found on the board menu in the top right corner.

All the updates are organized by boards. Your most recent updates are listed first (all the updates are shown in reverse chronological order).

All new updates are on the Unread tab. Once you reply in threads, accept requests, or take other actions on updates, they will be moved to the All updates tab and stored for 30 days. If you need to get back to something later, simply mark updates as unread to bring them back to the Unread tab.

Bosch colors and brand font

Miro cards

Miro cards provide you with a structured way to add more details and make things like planning or story mapping easier. Cards are simply containers for information, which can be used for different purposes: text, tasks, etc.


To start using the tool:

  • Drag the card icon from the sidebar and drop it anywhere on the board
  • Select the card icon and click on the board
  • Use D hotkey

You can also convert any sticky note, text box, or shape into a card by clicking on it and selecting card icon.


Editing cards:

Cards are blue and empty by default, but you can choose a color from the palette and fill card background, change the card length and height, add up to 8 tags to each card, assign tasks to board participants, add links, or dates. All the changes can be made both in closed and in expanded cards, except links (only in closed).

  • To add more custom colors to your cards, click the plus icon on the palette. 
  • Add and remove tags by simply clicking them. Use tags for searching and filtering your cards.
  • Change the card size by dragging the white dots and rotate it by dragging the arrow icon.
  • To add text to the card heading, select it and start typing. You can input up to 6,000 text symbols in the card description.
  • To expand the card, click on the Expand icon either on the top right corner of the card or on the pop-up menu.
  • To format the text of the description, use the formatting toolbar. NOTE Formatting text and changing the text size in the heading of the card is not possible.

  • To delete a card, select it, click the three dots on the context menu, and choose Delete. Or simply press backspace.


Chat

  1. To start the chat, click on the chat icon on the top-right collaboration toolbar. 

       2. Write messages and hit Enter to send them just like you would in any other messengers. Don't forget to @mention your team members to quickly draw them into a conversation. 

       3. In case you need to edit your message, simply click on it, change the text of the message, click Save or hit Enter. You can also delete it by clicking the Trash icon near your message.


Charts

  1. Click charts on the toolbar, select a chart type, and click it or drag it to the board.


      2. Select the object to open the context menu, click the three dots, and click Edit or double-click the object to enter the editing mode.

    3. Choose the name and customize the legend to make your chart more informative. Enable and disable Title and Legend toggles. You can also clear all notes in one click.

    4. To delete a row, select all cells of a row, click the Trash icon, and choose Delete row.


NOTE

  • You can only add positive values to charts
  • You cannot change the color of the chart elements


How to add an organizational chart
  1. Open the Miro board where you wish to create the organizational chart.
  2. Go to the creation toolbar on the left side of your board.
  3. Click on More apps (+) and search ‘Org chart’.

       4. Click Org chart to create a draft org chart on the board. 

       5. Click on the draft org chart to open the context menu, then click Import CSV to upload your organizational data. Select one of two options: Update org chart to refresh existing data, or Create new org chart to create one from scratch. 

       6. Miro will automatically process your data and fill in the org chart accordingly. 



Connection lines

Connection lines allow you to link objects on the board. This is helpful for building diagrams and flowcharts.


  1. To create a line, select connection line on the toolbar or use the hotkey L. You can also select an object and click one of the blue dots around it to draw a line.

     2. Change arrowheads, the line type (straight, orthogonal, curved), thickness, color, etc. on the context menu.

NOTE

  • To draw a straight horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line, start drawing a line and hold Shift.
  • To disable snapping to other objects hold Ctrl (for Windows) or Cmd (for Mac).
  • If you want to create a specific path for the line, you can do so by working with the blue and white bullet points on the line. To remove extra bends and turns and reset a line, simply double-click the white bullet points.
  • To disconnect a line and attach it to another object, drag the line end. 
  • To delete a connection line, select it, click three dots on the context menu, and click Delete (or simply hold Backspace/Delete).
  • You can add shapes, cards, and other objects on connection lines. Select a connection line and choose Insert shape on the context menu. Make sure that there is enough space between two connected objects.
  • You can use text labels - to do that double-click any connection line or click +T in the context menu to start entering the text. Move the text along the line by dragging it. You can change the text size, color on the context menu and fix it horizontally or let the text follow the line curves. To delete the text, select it and press Delete on the keyboard.
  • You can connect shapes, cards, sticky notes, text blocks, and other objects (but not frames) with connection lines. Select an object and drag the blue dot.

If you drag a line and attach it to a non-center blue dot, the line will cross the objects if you move them.

  • To create a connection line with arrowheads on both ends select the line, choose None on the context menu, and add the arrowhead.


Comments

To create a comment:

  1. Choose Comment on the toolbar or press C hotkey. Click the spot where you would like to post it, type in your comment, @mention someone if needed, and press Enter.

Comments can be attached to any widget on the board - post a comment right on the object and it will belong to this object (NOTE This doesn't apply to frames). 

You can attach an existing comment to an object by dragging it to the desired location.


      2. You can also create a comment by selecting the option on an object's context menu.


     3. You can also add comments to messages in notes by simply clicking the small comment icon next to the message.



You can mark any comment thread as Resolved to hide it and focus your attention where it’s most needed:

You can also add a reaction by clicking the emoji icon next to a comment.

NOTE If you want your resolved comments to be visible on the board, choose Show resolved option in the comments panel in the board overview. 


To edit a comment you've left in a thread, simply click it, make the necessary changes and choose Save.


If you want to delete a comment from the board, click the three-dot menu and choose Delete.

NOTE:

  • If you don't see the option to delete a comment, make sure to switch to the select mode and open the comment again.
  • here is no way to delete all or multiple comments from the board simultaneously.


You can choose the color of the comment icon to highlight important threads for your collaborators or to specify the status of your message (for example, blue for ideas, green for discussions, etc.).


To keep a comment open for the current session, choose the Pin option in the three-dot menu. By pinning several threads you can keep multiple comment threads open simultaneously on your board.


Comments panel is located in the bottom left board overview. This panel displays all your mentions and comments in one place and allows you to see instant notifications when someone leaves a comment or mentions you. 

Choose Read all if you want to mark all new comments as read.

To hide comments on your board click hide comments button in the bottom-left corner of the panel. To show the hidden comments click the same icon.

Interactive presentations

Managing presentation frames

Miro frames are the slides of your presentation. You can manage your frames by clicking on the sidebar icon in the lower left-hand corner of your Miro board. This will open up the Frames panel. From there you can set the order of frames by simply clicking and dragging the frames on the sidebar. 

You can rename a frame by clicking on the field below the frame. If you click on the three dots next to a frame's name, you’ll also have more options to hide the frame, export the frame, add another frame, copy the frame link, and delete the frame. 

How to start presentation

Click on the arrow next to the Present button in the top-right corner of your board and select one of the present options. 

If you directly click Present, the presentation mode will depend on whether you have frames. If you’ve added frames to your presentation you’ll present in Frames mode. If not, you’ll present in Board mode.

You can exit presentation mode by pressing Escape on your keyboard, or by clicking Stop in the toolbar at the bottom of your screen.



How to add presenter notes

You can add presenter notes to your frames. They will appear in a separate window that's only visible to you.

There are two ways to access your presenter notes: 

Access presenter notes from the boardAccess presenter notes while in presentation mode

In the bottom left corner of the board, click the Open frames icon. Next to the Present button, click the three dots (...) and select Presenter notes.

In the presentation toolbar on the bottom of your screen, click the Preferences icon, and select Presenter notes.  

Collaboration with the audience

When you launch your interactive presentation, you can collaborate with your audience by starting a collaboration app. Simply click the Activity apps icon at the bottom of the screen and select Timer, Voting, Private mode or Talktrack.


From Activity apps icon you can also manage participant tools during the presentation.



Handing off a presentation

If it's a big meeting with multiple speakers, you can hand off the presentation to another speaker:

  1. In the presenters toolbar at the bottom of your screen, access the list of people in the presentation. 
  2. Select a user and click Handoff.

The original presenter will transition to the audience view and the new presenter will be able to control the presentation. The audience will be notified that there is a new presenter.

NOTE  Instead of waiting for a hand-off, you can take over a presentation at any time. 

  1. In the toolbar at the bottom of your screen, open the list of people in the presentation. 
  2. Click Take over and select a user to take over from. 

Audience view

As soon as the presenter launches the presentation, the other participants on the board will see a modal with the option to join.

When participants join, they’ll be guided by the presenter's view. They can move around the board and switch back to the presenter’s view by clicking Return to presenter.

The presentation experience remains interactive: participants can use reactions or raise their hand by selecting the corresponding options on the bottom toolbar.

On the left-hand creation toolbar they can use tools allowed by the presenter.



Finishing the presentation

As the presenter clicks Stop on the bottom toolbar, all board collaborators are switched to the standard board view.

Will guests have access to the board after the meeting?

Exporting board

You can save your board as an image, PDF, or CSV file in the board export menu.

NOTE When you export your board as a PDF, all frames are exported as a single file.


Limitations

  • Miro board export may be restricted for users in the board content settings
  • Edge (version < 79) supports Vector export only

  • Bitmap images on the board are compressed during the upload, whereas objects created in Miro (shapes, stickers, text, links, etc.) will keep their quality


Saving a board backup

Available only for board owners and co-owners!


  1. To create a backup, open a board and click on the Export button on the board menu. Choose the Download board backup option and follow the on-screen instructions.

You can also save a backup from your dashboard: open a board's menu by clicking the three dots and choose the option.


       2. To restore a board from a backup, go to the dashboard and click Upload from backup. A dialogue box will appear, where you will be able to choose your *.rtb board backup file. After you confirm your choice, a new board with the same content will be created in the team. The board title will include Restored.



Managing boards


Moving boards between teams

To move a board between teams, you must:

  • own the board
  • be a member of both teams
  • none of teams are confidential.


  1. Go to your dashboard to see all boards in a team
  2. Hover over the card of the board you want to move
  3. Click the three dots 
  4. Choose Move to team 
  5. A pop-up will open. Select a new team from the dropdown. The list will include all the teams you have access to
  6. Click Move

NOTE If any board collaborators are not part of the team where the board is moving, you’ll see a denied access message.

There are two ways to see which user emails will lose access to the board after you move it. If the number of users is less than 10, you can see the email list by clicking View users emails in the Denied access message. If the number is greater than 10, there will be a link to download the email list. 

You can also choose Move anyway and add collaborators to the board again after it's moved. 


Templates gallery

You can use a lot of ready-made templates to create your board. 

  1. Go to your Miro dashboard
  2. Select Templates

      3. Select the template you want to use

Create and Manage a Miro Team

🔎 TIP: Use Ctrl + F to find the content you are searching for on this site.

Creation of a new Miro Team

Info

Miro Teams can be ordered via MS Forms order form.


Please read the following information carefully to ensure proper creation of your Miro Team:

  • A meaningful name should be used
  • The requesting user (future primary admin of the Team) needs to be provided with NTUserID@bosch.com
  • A secondary Team admin is needed to ensure data lifecycle - this user needs to be provided with NTUserID@bosch.com
  • An Access Right Owner (ARO) - previously called Master of Role (MoR) - needs to be defined - this needs to be a correct organizational unit in Bosch (e.g. BD/WPA-UCS) 
  • The Team type needs to be decided: "Internal", "Confidential" or "External" - this will impact feature availability and sharing/collaboration options within the Team in Miro later on, but please note, that for collaboration with externals there is a dedicated training needed 

Please have a look at our Miro Team Types comparison and general rules for Miro Teams

For External Team creation check HERE


To start the creation of your Miro Team please use this Team Creation Orderform.

Fill out the order forms required information carefully - requests not fulfilling the requirements will be ignored!

Once you sent the request please wait for a confirmation email in your inbox!

Managing a Miro Team


User types
UserDescription
Team admin
  • Can create boards, projects, content and teams (via order forms).
  • Can assign access rights to projects and boards
  • Can share boards, projects, content
  • Can invite new members to the Miro Team

Team member/ Externals with ECI

  • Can create boards and content
  • Can share accessable boards based on board settings
  • Can embed boards into Microsoft Teams

Guest

Only available for External Miro Teams. Details here.    



How to check who is a team admin
  1. Go to a team settings

     2. Click on Users. Here you will be able to see roles in a team.



How to assign a team admin role

NOTE Only team members can be an admin.

  1. Go to your Team settings by clicking on the expansion next to the team`s name.
  2. Click on Team users.
  3. Click the three dots next to the user and choose Grant Team Admin.

To remove team admin role → click on Revoke Team Admin.




Inviting to a team 

After creating a team you will be automatically added there as a Team Admin. Then you can add new members to your team.

  1. In your Miro client select a team, to which you want to add a user.
  2. Click on it and then on Users.

     3. To add a member, just click on Add team members button in the right corner.

     4. Here you can search for an user via Bosch NTUsers e-mail address (e.g. abc1fe@bosch.com) → you can enter many addresses at once. You can also click on Add users from Company to select an user from the list.


     5. Click on Send invitations.


Inviting to a board

Something different is inviting users to a particular board in your team. HERE you can check, how to do it.



Building a team structure

To built your team structure you can add selected users (see the point above). In Team users section you can see basic information about your team members such as: role, licence type, number of their teams and last activity. If you click on three dots next to the user name, you can check user info, grant Team Admin rights or delete an user from a team.

Team users section can be found by clicking on the name of a team → Users




Managing team profile

Select a team → click on its name → select Team profile


In this section you can easily change a team name, add a team logo, leave or delete a team.




How to change Master of Role (MoR) in an existing Miro team

The Master of Role is responsible for the data and must be an organizational office. In the order form you should enter a valid organizational office name. A single user ID is therefore not possible. Only a single organizational office will be accepted, for example “BD/WPA-UCS1”.

Please NOTE that changing MoR isn`t possible on your own → if you need to change it, you have to create an IT ticket.




Team permissions

To set or change permissions select team name → click on Permissions

In this section you can define:

  • how members can see and join your team,
  • how members can access and share your team, team boards or projects,
  • who can give permissions to copy content and copy it,
  • if you want enable co-owner role,
  • use labels to tag boards into categories.



Managing projects in the team

Projects are essentially folders of boards with the option to manage user access for a smaller group of people within a team. Projects help you organize your boards and make them easier to find and share. In other words, a project is a group of boards that you can share with your teammates all at once.


FeatureDescription
Creating projects

Click the +Add button in the left sidebar to create a new project. Set the name for the project and feel free to add members and boards.

Changing project details
The creator of a project and the participants invited as co-owners and editors can invite other people and add existing boards to the project. New boards can be created by any participant. Only the project owner and co-owners can rename the project and toggle the Anyone in your team can view boards in this project setting. 
Adding members to projects

Project members can:

  • access all boards within the project, both present and all newly created or added to the project
  • create boards within the project
  • add existing boards to the project
  • be notified of all changes in all boards within a project

NOTE Only team members can be invited to projects.


→ To add team members to a project, click the Add Members button in the project settings.


→ You can also select project name and use +button next to your profile picture.


→ Select members from the list and set the access level for them (editor, commenter, or viewer). Select Notify members if you need to send notifications. Click Done.

Changing the project owner
  1. Open the project settings by clicking on the name of the project.
  2. Open the menu next to the name of the owner-to-be.
  3. Choose Is owner in the user's menu.

When you transfer a project to another user, it doesn’t change a board owner for the project boards. 

Reassigning roles and ownership and removing members

If you would like to change the participant's role or remove them:

  1. Open the project settings by clicking on its name.
  2. Open the menu next to their name.
  3. Choose the new role (editor, commenter, viewer, or owner) or click to Remove them.

NOTE A removed member may still retain access to project board by team or company access.

Adding boards to a project

There are several ways project members who are also the board editors can move boards to a project:

  • to add several boards to one project at once, click the Add boards button in the project settings,
  • open the board’s information card by clicking on its name and select the project to attach the board to,
  • on the dashboard, click the three dots on a board and choose Move to project.
Moving boards to another project or removing it

You can move a board to another project or remove it the same ways you add a board to a project. Open the settings and from the project names list choose another name or choose None. This can be done in two ways:

  • from the board’s information card (click on board name) → Move
  • from the dashboard by clicking the three dots and choosing Move to project
Starred projects
Make your most frequently used projects more accessible by clicking the star icon next to the project name. As soon as you add at least one project to starred, the Starred projects section appears on the left of your dashboard above all Projects. You can expand and collapse Starred projects at any time.
Sharing project
A project may be shared with the whole team in one click by its owner or co-owner. To do that just open the project menu by clicking on its name and enable Anyone in your team can view boards in this project option.




You can find relevant information also in the following sections:

  • Work with Miro
  • Miro FAQ

If you couldn't find an information, ask your question in the dedicated forum

Miro FAQ

To users in China

Please be aware of performance issues when using Miro in China. These issues are being worked on.



General Miro FAQ


ProblemSolution
I am already a Miro user. Can I automatically use Bosch Central Miro environment?

Yes. Your access depends on which user profile you use. If you are using NT User Profile (e.g. abc1fe@bosch.com) 

I want to start working with Miro. Where to start?
Check detail here.
I`m a BSH user. Can I use Bosch Central Miro?

Yes. Check details here.

How much does Miro cost?
Check details here.
Can I collaborate outside Bosch Central Miro?

Yes, but if you are using an account outside Bosch Central Miro, you need to take under consideration, that Bosch Miro Team isn`t responsible for external environments so isn`t able to support you.

To prevent future complication please use NTuser@bosch.com.

I have two Miro accounts. Which one to use?
Note, that only NT User Profiles are supported in Bosch Central Miro, so you should use an account with such a profile.
How to move boards between profiles?

Your profile in Miro is your NT ID (AQO1COB@BOSCH.COM), and all teams you create or are invited to can be found under this profile. Some users may have more than one Miro profile registered with different emails. 

If the board is located in a paid or Education team and you would like to move it to Bosch Central Miro, simply save the board backup and upload it to that team.

  1. Open your dashboard
  2. Hover over the card of the board you want to move
  3. Click the three dots
  4. Click Download board backup
  5. The .rtb file will be saved to your device
  6. Log in to your second Miro profile
  7. Switch to the team where you want to move the board
  8. Scroll down to Projects, and click Upload from backup
  9. The file picker will open
  10. Choose the .rtb backup file you previously saved and click Open. The board will then be available from your dashboard.
I can't log in

Please check, if you have successfully get the access and received the confirmation e-mail. If not, go through the process once more.

Endless loading when signing in
  • Log in on a different browser.
  • Log in using your browser’s private (incognito) mode. If the issue is not reproduced in incognito mode/another browser, clear your browser cache.
I can’t access a Miro board
  • Request access by clicking on the blue button on the pop-up. The request will be sent to the board owner.
  • Make sure that you’re using the correct link to access the board. If the board link is correct, the board was most likely deleted more than 90 days ago or together with a team.
  • If you created the board and no longer have access, it’s possible that you were removed from the team where the board is stored. 
I’m no longer able to edit a Miro board
  • Try to duplicate the board and try again.
  • Your access level may have been changed in the board sharing settings. Request editing access from the board owner. You can do this by clicking Request editor rights in the top right corner of the board.

I lost my board 

  • If you're a member of multiple Miro teams, try switching between your teams on the left sidebar of your dashboard. Then click Boards in this team to see all boards in a specific team.

  • You can also use search to locate a board.

You may need to apply the Owned by anyone filter to make sure you’re viewing all boards. Filters can also help you narrow your search into boards you own and boards owned by everyone else.

  • You can try restoring the board from Trash.
Can I restore a deleted board?

Yes, but NOTE you can do it only within 90 days. 

You can restore deleted board using the board link. 

You can try finding the board link by typing your board name:
    • in your browser address bar,
    • in your browser history search,
    • in your email search.

Once you’ve found the link and opened it in your browser, you’ll see a message that the board has been deleted. 

Click restore the board and you’ll be redirected to your Miro dashboard - there you’ll be able to open the recovered board.

How to restore a deleted board from trash?

Yes, but NOTE

  • you can do it only within 90 days,
  • it`s only available for full licence users (If you’re on a free licence you can restore deleted board using board link - check the above point)

  1. Make sure you’re viewing the right team.

  2. Open Trash to see any deleted boards.

   3. Hover over the deleted board thumbnail. You’ll see the option to Restore and how many days you have left, as well as who deleted it. 
   4. Click Restore and the board will appear on your dashboard in All boards. 

Can I restore a board from a past user?

If a user was removed from the team and their boards were deleted, ask your Miro admin to help you. They’ll be able to see the deleted boards in the trash and can restore the board within 90 days of being deleted.

The team admin will become the owner of the restored board. 

I lost my content
  • Open the board and click the Open sidebar icon on the bottom-left corner. In the opened board overview, click the Board history icon. If you see the missing content, in most cases you can easily restore it by clicking the restore icon.

  • Try checking the mini-map. The mini-map is located in the bottom right corner of your board and gives you an overall view of your content, so if something snuck out of frame you’ll be able to spot it there. 

  • It’s possible that you were removed from the team where your board was located and lost your board access. If the board has not been deleted, you can follow the board link and request access from the current owner. 
Export button is missing on my board
Reach out to the board owner and ask them to enable the option for you in the Share window > Sharing settings > Permissions. The owner/co-owner needs to select which category of users can copy the board content.
Images/PDFs are blurry on the exported document
  • Set the board zoom to 100% and let the images/PDFs render before exporting the board
  • The uploaded image/PDF may be too complex or large for export. To downsize the file, convert the image/PDF to PNG format and replace it on the board. Then export the board again
What does team deletion mean?
Deleting your team results in deleting all boards and templates saved in the team. You cannot undo this action. Before deleting the team you may want to transfer your boards to other teams, save backups, or export them, and ask your team members to do the same.
Why I'm getting Miro prompts to upgrade my account?
The option given to upgrade your account's subscription is because the Team you are currently in is a Team outside our Central Environment. If you move the boards/ contents to a Team in our Environment, you can delete the external Team and enjoy working with your full feature set.
Do I need to create a Miro team? 
Depends on your needs. Note, that content like boards or projects are a part of a team - this is needed to ensure content still will be accessible and team is manageable when e.g. admin leaves the company.  So effectively you need a team to be able to work - this can be a team you own or someone else owns. This is designed similar to MS Teams rooms where the same rule applies.
I am not able to create boards

You also need a team in which you can then create the boards. -> Create and Manage a Miro Team

I can see only "Welcome to Bosch" team.
All boards must be created in a team, other than "welcome to Bosch Miro" team, owned and managed by at least two users and have a responsible MoR. Without a team no boards/ content can be created. In case you want to work with Miro please request a team.
I've worked with Miro in the past. Is it possible to get all my Miro boards into my SSO account?
This can be achieved by ordering an internal team in the central environment and then moving the boards to this particular team by adding your central user profile as an owner of the existing boards and using "Move to team" function.
If I have a board which is not team hosted (older free license), is there a possibility to transfer the board to an official team hosted ?

In case this board is owned externally by the same profile (NTUser based profile) you should be able to move the board to an Internal Team (in Confidential Teams this is not possible). You can also use a board backup file which you can download and upload in a central Team. Please note that e.g. public links and permissions most likley break when migrating the board.

NOTE If you did not change your e-mail address before ordering, you can either invite your UPN user to the external team/board, make him an owner and move or use the backup method.


FAQ for Miro team admins


ProblemSolution
I want to be promoted to Miro team admin. How can I do that?

Reach out to the current team Admin and ask them to change your role. If you don't know who the current Admin is, open Team or Company Settings > Active users to find out and Team settings > Team users > Contact Team admin.

How to grant admin rights to a teammate?
To grant team admin rights to a team member, open team Settings and switch to Active users, click the three dots next to user and choose Grant team admin rights.
How to revoke team admin rights to the corresponding/counterpart admin?

To revoke the admin rights to a corresponding/counterpart team admin, open team Settings and switch to Active users, click the three dots next to user and choose Revoke team admin rights.

I want to delete my profile (while being team admin). What happens to my team after that?
  • If you are the only member there, the team will be deleted together with your profile.
  • If there are other members, the team will stay and your profile will simply be removed from it and then deleted.
  • If you are the only admin in the team, then after your profile's removal the first team member alphabetically will become the new admin. 
There are several users in the team who left the company. How can I remove them from the team?
Users who leave the company and are removed in the azure AD will be deactivated in Miro automatically and lose their access. 
How can we cancel licenses of users who are leaving company?
The subscription will be stalled when the NT ID is deleted/ users leave organization.
Is there a desktop app for Miro?

Yes. It is already available via ITSP.
